S 级 肝转移 转化研究 基础机制 IF 33.3
靶向中性粒细胞胞外诱捕网抑制结肠癌肿瘤坏死与转移
Targeting Neutrophil Extracellular Traps to Inhibit Colon Cancer Tumor Necrosis and Metastasis.
Cancer Discovery · 2026-11 · Gazzara ER, Adrover JM, Dziadowicz SA, Liu AW, Han S, Aminzada Z, et al.
研究背景：肿瘤坏死通常被视为肿瘤生长的被动结果，但作者提出其可能是可干预的治疗靶点；本研究探讨中性粒细胞胞外诱捕网（NET）驱动的肿瘤坏死在结直肠癌转移中的作用。
核心结果：人CRC中坏死与转移性疾病独立于肿瘤大小相关；单细胞RNA测序和空间转录组显示坏死周围程序与转移进展相关，患者循环中性粒细胞增多（包括NET预激活和CD177低表达亚群），瘤内血管NET聚集体邻近坏死区；在MMR proficient小鼠模型中，遗传和药物抑制NET可减少肿瘤坏死、降低转移并增强化疗疗效。
意义与启示：该研究将NET驱动的肿瘤坏死确立为CRC转移的主动促进因素，提示NET抑制可作为结直肠癌（含肝转移）的潜在治疗策略，并为联合化疗提供新思路。
评分明细：设计 18/30 · 验证 10/15 · 机制 14/15 · 影响力 20/20 · 契合度 18/20 = 80/100 ｜ 等级理由：研究结合单细胞测序、空间转录组和小鼠模型，机制深入但尚处临床前阶段，暂未改变临床实践。

B 级 肝转移 转化研究 多组学与生信 IF 14.1
AARS1介导的GLUD1 K503乳酰化通过转录后重编程驱动结直肠癌转移
AARS1-Mediated GLUD1 K503 Lactylation Drives Colorectal Cancer Metastasis Through Post-Transcriptional Reprogramming.
Advanced Science (weinheim, Baden-wurttemberg, Germany) · 2026-11 · Qian J, Shen J, Su G, Jiang J, Zhu Y, Chen Y, et al.
研究背景：结直肠癌预后高度取决于是否发生转移，Warburg效应导致的乳酸蓄积可引发赖氨酸乳酰化（Kla），但非组蛋白Kla在CRC转移中的作用尚不清楚。
核心结果：整合肝转移灶与配对原发灶的乳酰化组和蛋白质组分析，鉴定GLUD1为促进CRC转移的关键乳酰化蛋白；乳酸增强GLUD1 K503位点乳酰化，促进YBX1与ELAVL1互作，提高CXCL8和SLC7A11 mRNA转录后稳定性，增强转移潜能；GLUD1乳酰化与远处转移及不良预后显著相关，结构筛选发现坎格雷洛四钠可有效抑制GLUD1-K503la，在细胞系、PDO及体内模型中均显示强效。
意义与启示：揭示AARS1介导的GLUD1 K503乳酰化通过转录后重编程驱动CRC转移的新机制，GLUD1-K503la可作为预后生物标志物和治疗靶点，坎格雷洛四钠为潜在靶向药物，为课题中乳酰化修饰调控转移及药物干预研究提供直接依据。
评分明细：设计 22/30 · 验证 12/15 · 机制 14/15 · 影响力 9/20 · 契合度 18/20 = 75/100 ｜ 等级理由：多组学结合体内外验证和药物筛选，机制深入但尚处临床前阶段，暂不足以改变实践。

S 级 综合及其他 系统综述/Meta IF 7.1
超越细胞毒化疗：阿司匹林与结构化运动降低结直肠癌复发
Beyond cytotoxic chemotherapy: Aspirin and structured exercise to reduce colorectal cancer recurrence.
European Journal of Cancer (oxford, England : 1990) · 2026-11 · Sabbagh R, Sharma N, Sinicrope FA
研究背景：II-III期结直肠癌根治性治疗后复发仍是主要致病和致死原因，即使接受辅助化疗的患者亦如此；近年随机试验提示阿司匹林与结构化运动可能进一步降低复发风险，但缺乏系统证据整合。
核心结果：ALASCCA III期试验显示，对携带PI3K通路变异的切除后结肠或直肠癌患者，低剂量阿司匹林治疗3年使复发风险降低约50%，确立了生物标志物指导的辅助阿司匹林策略；CHALLENGE试验显示，辅助化疗后启动的3年结构化运动方案改善了II/III期结肠癌患者的无病生存和总生存。机制上阿司匹林通过抑制COX/前列腺素信号、血小板-肿瘤相互作用及PI3K相关通路发挥抗肿瘤作用，运动则经代谢信号、全身炎症和抗肿瘤免疫起效，二者可能共同汇聚于炎症、肿瘤微环境和免疫监视。
意义与启示：该研究为生物标志物导向的辅助阿司匹林和结构化运动作为细胞毒化疗之外的辅助策略提供了随机证据，支持对CRC患者检测体细胞PI3K通路变异并将结构化运动纳入术后生存者管理；二者机制互补，也为联合评估阿司匹林与运动的协同效应提供了依据，对本课题探索非细胞毒辅助治疗及联合干预具有重要启示。
评分明细：设计 25/30 · 验证 12/15 · 机制 10/15 · 影响力 5/20 · 契合度 18/20 = 70/100 ｜ 等级理由：基于两项3期RCT的综述，证据等级高，直接支持生物标志物指导的阿司匹林和运动干预，可能改变临床实践。

B 级 转化研究 基础机制 IF 14.1
大分割放疗诱导肿瘤源性APOC2驱动炎性单核细胞分化增强结直肠癌抗肿瘤免疫
Hypofractionated Radiotherapy Elicits Tumor-Derived APOC2 to Drive Inflammatory Monocyte Differentiation and Potentiate Anti-Tumor Immunity in Colorectal Cancer.
Advanced Science (weinheim, Baden-wurttemberg, Germany) · 2026-11 · Xu Q, Wang H, Li M, Zou Z, Liu L, Zheng L, et al.
研究背景：大分割放疗（HFRT）联合免疫化疗有望克服微卫星稳定（MSS）局部晚期直肠癌的免疫抵抗，但其重塑肿瘤免疫微环境的机制尚不明确。
核心结果：研究发现HFRT诱导肿瘤细胞分泌APOC2：HFRT下调ATF3、解除其对APOC2启动子的抑制；APOC2激活脂蛋白脂肪酶、增加游离脂肪酸生成、增强I型干扰素信号，并促进Ly6A+炎性单核细胞分化。治疗后血清APOC2水平较高的患者更易获得病理完全缓解（pCR）。
意义与启示：该研究揭示了HFRT通过APOC2-脂肪酸代谢-I型干扰素轴驱动炎性单核细胞分化、增强抗肿瘤免疫的新机制，提示血清APOC2可作为HFRT联合免疫化疗疗效的预测生物标志物，并为MSS直肠癌的免疫增敏策略提供潜在靶点。
评分明细：设计 18/30 · 验证 10/15 · 机制 14/15 · 影响力 9/20 · 契合度 17/20 = 68/100 ｜ 等级理由：机制研究结合临床队列验证，发现血清APOC2与pCR相关，具转化潜力但尚需前瞻验证。

B 级 转化研究 基础机制 IF 14.1
KRT16通过内皮间质转化诱导房颤：多癌种共享机制及肠癌启示
KRT16 From Diverse Tumors Induces Atrial Remodeling and Fibrillation via Endothelial-to-Mesenchymal Transition.
Advanced Science (weinheim, Baden-wurttemberg, Germany) · 2026-11 · Zhan G, Yang X, Xue G, Li J, Wang X, Dong H, et al.
研究背景：抗癌治疗会增加房颤（AF）发生率，但多种癌症是否可不依赖抗癌治疗、通过共同机制直接促进房颤尚不明确。本研究探讨乳腺癌、肺癌和结直肠癌等恶性肿瘤对心房重构与房颤的直接作用及其共享分子机制。
核心结果：回顾性临床分析显示，治疗前乳腺癌、肺癌和结直肠癌女性患者房颤患病率显著升高，且不依赖抗癌治疗；原位荷瘤小鼠模型同样表现出房颤诱发率增加，并伴心房扩大、纤维化和电重构。整合转录组分析与TCGA数据发现，内皮-间质转化（EndMT）是多种癌症相关房颤的共享心房重构通路；角质蛋白16（KRT16）作为多种恶性肿瘤共享的循环因子，在心房内皮细胞中蓄积，通过抑制AnxA2 Tyr23磷酸化促进其异常膜滞留，进而经AnxA2依赖的TGF-β1/Smad信号激活EndMT。沉默肿瘤细胞KRT16或内皮敲低AnxA2，可显著减轻荷瘤小鼠的EndMT、心房纤维化及房颤易感性。
意义与启示：该研究揭示多种癌症可通过KRT16驱动的EndMT直接诱导心房重构和房颤，为肿瘤相关房颤提供了共享机制解释和潜在治疗靶点；对结直肠癌肝转移患者，提示应关注KRT16/AnxA2-EndMT轴介导的心律失常风险，并可作为干预候选方向。
评分明细：设计 22/30 · 验证 10/15 · 机制 14/15 · 影响力 9/20 · 契合度 12/20 = 67/100 ｜ 等级理由：多癌种回顾性临床分析结合动物模型与机制解析，发表于高影响力期刊，但尚处临床前阶段，暂不改变实践。

B 级 转化研究 基础机制 IF 14.1
DLAT棕榈酰化拮抗SYVN1泛素化调控结直肠癌铜死亡敏感性
Palmitoylation of DLAT Licenses Cuproptosis by Antagonizing SYVN1-Dependent Ubiquitination in Colorectal Cancer.
Advanced Science (weinheim, Baden-wurttemberg, Germany) · 2026-11 · Cai J, Shi M, Li X, Zhang J, Zhang L
研究背景：铜死亡是一种铜依赖性的细胞死亡方式，在癌症治疗中具有潜力，但调控细胞对铜死亡敏感性的机制尚不清楚。本研究通过翻译后修饰（PTM）抑制剂筛选，在结直肠癌中鉴定S-棕榈酰化是铜死亡敏感性的必需决定因素。
核心结果：研究发现DLAT是棕榈酰化的主要底物，在保守的C488位点被修饰；C488棕榈酰化通过空间位阻阻止E3泛素连接酶SYVN1催化DLAT的K48连接多泛素化，从而稳定DLAT蛋白。ZDHHC1被鉴定为DLAT的棕榈酰转移酶，铜应激稳定TFE3，使其入核结合ZDHHC1启动子并直接激活转录。AAV介导的ZDHHC1递送使患者来源异种移植（PDX）肿瘤对铜离子载体elesclomol敏感，抑制肿瘤生长。
意义与启示：揭示了铜感应信号级联（TFE3-ZDHHC1-DLAT棕榈酰化）调控铜死亡脆弱性，确立ZDHHC1介导的脂化作为增敏结直肠癌铜基治疗的治疗靶点，为结直肠癌（含肝转移）的铜死亡靶向策略提供了新思路。
评分明细：设计 18/30 · 验证 10/15 · 机制 15/15 · 影响力 9/20 · 契合度 14/20 = 66/100 ｜ 等级理由：机制研究深入但尚处临床前阶段，未改变当前临床实践。
66/ 100
B 级 转化研究 基础机制 IF 14.6
靶向FOLR1抗体偶联药物逆转结直肠癌免疫逃逸并增强抗PD-1疗效
Targeting cancer immune evasion with anti-FOLR1 antibody-drug conjugate potentiates anti-PD-1 efficacy in colorectal cancer.
Science Translational Medicine · 2026-11 · Chen S, Liu Q, Ye S, Yu J, Xie Y, Yuan Y, et al.
研究背景：结直肠癌中MHC-I抗原提呈缺失导致免疫逃逸和免疫检查点阻断（ICB）耐药，本研究通过CRISPR激活筛选寻找可逆转该过程的治疗靶点，鉴定出叶酸受体α（FOLR1）为关键负调控因子。
核心结果：FOLR1在CRC肿瘤中异质性表达而在癌旁正常组织中检测不到，其高表达预示ICB应答差、肿瘤干性增强及患者预后不良；功能实验显示FOLR1促进CRC干性相关特性并塑造CD8+ T细胞功能受损的免疫抑制性肿瘤微环境。靶向FOLR1的抗体偶联药物（ADC）可增强抗PD-1疗效，逆转免疫逃逸。
意义与启示：FOLR1既是CRC预后与ICB疗效的预测标志物，也是通过ADC形式增敏抗PD-1治疗的潜在靶点，为MHC-I缺失型CRC的免疫联合治疗提供了新策略，提示可将FOLR1-ADC与PD-1抑制剂联合用于结直肠癌（含肝转移）的临床转化研究。
评分明细：设计 18/30 · 验证 8/15 · 机制 14/15 · 影响力 10/20 · 契合度 16/20 = 66/100 ｜ 等级理由：临床前机制研究，基于CRISPR筛选与功能验证，提出ADC联合免疫治疗新靶点，尚需临床验证。

B 级 系统治疗 系统综述/Meta IF 10.5
VEGF与PD-(L)1双靶向在胃肠道肿瘤中的生物学、临床格局与治疗前沿
Co-targeting VEGF and PD-(L)1 in gastrointestinal cancers: biology, clinical landscape, and therapeutic frontiers.
Cancer Treatment Reviews · 2026-11 · Laliotis G, Pourbahrighesmat S, Tojjari A, Saeed A
研究背景：胃肠道肿瘤大多对免疫检查点抑制剂耐药，持久获益仅见于dMMR/MSI-H、PD-L1富集的胃食管腺癌及肝细胞癌；VEGF驱动的免疫排斥微环境为血管生成与PD-(L)1轴联合靶向提供了机制依据。
核心结果：atezolizumab联合bevacizumab已在HCC确立标准地位（IMbrave150）；III期STELLAR-303中zanzalintinib（VEGFR/MET/TAM多激酶）联合atezolizumab首次在MSS结直肠癌中带来基于免疫检查点的总生存获益。双特异性抗体方面，ESMO 2026公布的III期HARMONi-GI1显示ivonescimab联合吉西他滨/顺铂较durvalumab联合化疗改善OS（中位14.9 vs 12.1个月，HR 0.75），但为仅限中国人群的中期分析且获益局限于肝内胆管癌。
意义与启示：VEGF/PD-(L)1共靶向在MSS结直肠癌和胆道癌中已获III期验证，支持将其作为肝转移等免疫排斥型CRC的联合策略方向；但现有证据尚不能区分获益源于免疫协同还是单纯抗血管生成，课题设计应纳入与抗VEGF/检查点双药联用的头对头比较，并探索双抗类药物的疗效预测标志物。
评分明细：设计 18/30 · 验证 10/15 · 机制 12/15 · 影响力 7/20 · 契合度 18/20 = 65/100 ｜ 等级理由：综述整合多项III期试验（STELLAR-303、HARMONi-GI1）证据，但非原始研究且双特异性抗体证据尚早，暂不直接改变实践。

B 级 转化研究 基础机制 IF 9.1
多基因工程成纤维细胞仿生囊泡用于肿瘤多模态靶向与免疫重编程
Multigene-engineered fibroblast-derived biomimetic vesicles for cancer multimodal targeting and immune reprogramming.
Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America · 2026-11 · Tan Y, Bai L, Zhang LF, Luo M, Wan Q, Liu Y, et al.
研究背景：仿生囊泡在肿瘤治疗中面临生物安全性、可扩展性和疗效等临床转化瓶颈，且肿瘤靶向效率不足。本研究旨在揭示肿瘤归巢的关键分子机制，并构建多基因工程化成纤维细胞来源的仿生囊泡以实现广谱肿瘤靶向和免疫重编程。
核心结果：研究鉴定出趋化因子轴（CXCL12/CXCR4）和整合素（αVβ3）协同介导的“趋化招募-黏附锚定”级联效应，并以此为基础构建了共表达CXCR4、iRGD、PD-1和CD47的工程化成纤维细胞纳米囊泡（X-Fb-MNVs）。该囊泡在乳腺癌、肝癌、胰腺癌和结肠癌PDX模型中均实现强效广谱靶向；CD47修饰减少了肝脏蓄积和吞噬清除，降低了脱靶效应。负载diABZI STING激动剂后，系统同时激活T细胞和先天免疫，逆转ICB耐药，实现83.3%生存率、90天无肿瘤复发及长期免疫监视，而游离diABZI组无小鼠存活。

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Intestinal spirochetosis (IS) is an uncommon condition that is often asymptomatic and detected incidentally but may occasionally present with chronic diarrhea. We report a case of IS incidentally identified in the adjacent non-neoplastic mucosa of a rectal adenoma specimen resected by cold snare polypectomy. We present a case of a man in his 50s who was referred for a positive fecal occult blood test and had a history of chronic diarrhea. Colonoscopy revealed a 5-mm sessile polyp in the upper rectum, which was removed by cold snare polypectomy. Histopathological examination showed a tubular adenoma. In addition, routine hematoxylin and eosin staining revealed a characteristic false brush border on the adjacent non-neoplastic colorectal epithelium, consistent with IS. A detailed medical interview subsequently revealed chronic diarrhea for more than 10 years and prolonged close contact with a pet dog. Treatment with metronidazole (1500 mg/day for 10 days) resulted in resolution of the diarrhea. This case highlights the importance of careful histopathological examination and detailed history-taking in patients with IS.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Arginase is overexpressed in many advanced cancers, which can deplete arginine in tumors to promote immunosuppression. Arginase inhibition may enhance the efficacy of standard chemotherapy regimens by increasing arginine levels and modulating arginine-mediated immune function. INCB001158 is a potent and selective arginase inhibitor that was assessed in combination with chemotherapy. This was an open-label, nonrandomized, phase 1/2 dose-escalation/expansion study in adults with advanced or metastatic solid tumors. INCB001158 was administered orally twice daily (bid) in combination with chemotherapy (mFOLFOX6, gemcitabine/cisplatin, or paclitaxel). Phase 2 tumor-type cohorts were colorectal cancer, biliary tract cancer (BTC), ovarian cancer (OC), gastroesophageal cancer, and endometrial cancer. Primary end points included safety, tolerability, and overall response rate (ORR). Fifty-four patients were enrolled in phase 1 and 95 in phase 2. No dose-dependent adverse event trends were observed. Recommended phase 2 dose of INCB001158 was 100 mg bid. Two phase 2 expansion cohorts met criteria for Simon 2-stage expansion: patients with BTC treated with INCB001158 100 mg bid plus gemcitabine/cisplatin, and patients with platinum-resistant OC treated with INCB001158 100 mg bid plus paclitaxel. The overall response rate was 24.2% (8/33 patients, all partial responses) in the BTC cohort and 16.7% (1/24 complete response and 3/24 partial responses) in the OC cohort. Pharmacodynamic increase in arginine levels was observed systemically in blood plasma and locally detected by mass-spectrometry images of tumor tissue. INCB001158 was generally well tolerated and associated with increases in arginine levels and responses in the BTC cohort, suggesting that combination regimens with chemotherapy may provide clinical benefit for some patients.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
This review evaluates the integration of PET-computed tomography (CT) in the management of esophageal, gastric, and colorectal malignancies. While anatomical imaging remains the standard for T-staging, PET-CT provides superior accuracy in identifying occult metastases and monitoring therapeutic response. The article also covers the prognostic utility of semiquantitative PET metrics, such as standard uptake value, metabolic tumor volume, and total lesion glycolysis. The potential of novel tracers such as fibroblast activation protein inhibitors to address limitations of fluorodeoxyglucose in specific circumstances is also discussed. Ultimately, PET-CT allows precision in oncology by refining diagnostic accuracy and individualizing therapeutic interventions.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Gastrointestinal (GI) cancers rank among the most common and lethal malignancies, and most are immunologically "cold," showing limited baseline sensitivity to immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs). Radiotherapy (RT) can boost antitumor immune responses and may convert some of these tumors into more treatment-responsive forms. This gives RT-ICI combinations a solid biological justification. However, clinical evidence supporting this approach in GI cancers remains limited relative to that in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma and non-small cell lung cancer. So far, the strongest data come from esophageal/gastroesophageal junction cancer and rectal cancer. In esophageal cancer, combining PD-1 blockade with neoadjuvant or perioperative chemoradiotherapy (CRT) results in substantial pathological responses. Furthermore, adjuvant PD-1 therapy after neoadjuvant CRT and R0 resection improves disease-free survival in patients with residual disease. In rectal cancer, adding PD-1 blockade to total neoadjuvant therapy (TNT) protocols increases pathological response rates and supports organ-preservation strategies. Hepatobiliary studies suggest high intrahepatic control and meaningful conversion-to-curative potential with RT-ICI, whereas pancreatic and other GI sites are represented mainly by early-phase, heterogeneous studies. RT dose, fractionation, and treated volume all significantly affect efficacy and safety across GI cancer sites. Treatment-related lymphopenia has become a significant challenge, prompting greater emphasis on lymphocyte-sparing treatment planning. Overall, RT-ICI combinations are safe and feasible, but a reliable survival advantage has not been established to date. Progress will depend on larger, well-powered randomized trials with standardized RT timing, prespecified patient-reported and functional outcomes, and biomarker strategies to identify which approaches truly improve long-term outcomes.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Hydrogen sulfide (H2S) is an endogenous gasotransmitter. The effect of H2S in colorectal cancer depends on the balance between its biosynthesis and mitochondrial clearance via sulfide:quinone oxidoreductase. In colorectal cancer, the upregulation of cystathionine β-synthase and suppression of sulfide:quinone oxidoreductase lead to increased H2S levels. H2S primarily acts through persulfidation, a reversible redox modification that regulates metabolic reprogramming, redox homeostasis, and cell fate. Moderate levels of H2S promote proliferation, angiogenesis, and immune evasion, whereas supraphysiological levels of H2S induce oxidative cell death. This review analyzes H2S dysregulation in colorectal cancer, the role of persulfidation in reshaping metabolic networks and the tumor microenvironment, and its potential as a biomarker. We also summarize therapeutic strategies, including cystathionine β-synthase inhibitors, H2S-responsive nanotheranostics, and combinations thereof, that target H2S-driven metabolic and immune vulnerabilities. Although still in the early stages, the H2S/persulfidation axis has translational value, and warrants further investigation.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Cancer screening programmes apply uniform criteria irrespective of inherited risk. Polygenic risk scores (PRSs) have been proposed as a promising tool to stratify individual cancer risk and tailor screening strategies. However, whether PRS-informed strategies improve health outcomes compared with current practices remains uncertain. We aimed to synthesise the available evidence on the projected clinical utility of PRS-stratified cancer screening across six malignancies. We searched PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science from inception to March 15, 2026, for studies evaluating PRS-stratified screening for breast, colorectal, prostate, lung, gastric, or cervical cancer. Eligible outcomes included cancer-specific mortality, life-years gained (LYG), quality-adjusted life-years (QALYs), overdiagnosis, and false-positive rates. Risk of bias was assessed using the ISPOR-AMCP-NPC questionnaire for modelling studies and ROBINS-I for observational studies. Certainty of evidence was appraised using the GRADE framework. Of 20,Simulated 100 million 058 records identified, 25 studies were included (22 decision-analytic modelling studies, 3 observational studies) covering five malignancies; no eligible studies were identified for cervical cancer. Modelled PRS-stratified strategies were projected to improve QALYs for breast, colorectal, gastric, and lung cancer, whereas results for prostate cancer were heterogeneous. Modelled mortality reductions were projected for colorectal, gastric, and lung cancer, although evidence for the latter two rested on single studies. For breast cancer, modelled mortality outcomes were inconsistent and dependent on comparator intensity. For prostate cancer, modelling studies primarily projected reductions in overdiagnosis rather than mortality improvement. Across all cancer sites, the absolute magnitude of incremental benefit over non-stratified screening was modest. Harms increased in high-risk groups receiving intensified surveillance. The certainty of evidence was rated very low for all outcomes across all cancer types, driven by serious risk of bias and very serious indirectness, reflecting limited transferability across populations and healthcare systems. PRS-stratified screening shows consistent but modest potential to improve the efficiency of cancer screening, particularly for breast, colorectal, and prostate cancer, although the certainty of evidence remains very low. PRS-stratified screening should remain investigational pending validation through prospective trials powered for clinical endpoints, conducted in ancestrally diverse populations, and incorporating equity-sensitive implementation frameworks. ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Feasibility evaluation of lung cancer screening (LCS) using low-dose computed tomography for high-risk individuals has been recommended in the EU. Unlike other cancer screening programs, LCS eligibility depends on the individuals' smoking history. However, the size, health status, and screening behavior of the eligible population across the EU remain poorly characterized. We used the European Health Interview Survey (EHIS)(wave 3, collected mostly in 2019) to estimate the number of individuals aged 50-80 eligible for LCS in the EU under two criteria: the United States Preventive Services Task Force (USPSTF) 2021 guidelines and the risk-based PLCOm2012 model (six-year-risk≥1.51%). We assessed health status and adherence to established cancer-screening programs (colorectal, breast, cervical) of LCS-eligibles using mixed-effects regression. An estimated 25.38million individuals(16.16% of 50-80-year-olds) met the USPSTF2021 criteria in 2019, while 16.42million(10.45%) were eligible under risk-based criteria, with substantial inter-country-variation. Screening-eligibles reported poorer health, including higher prevalence of chronic respiratory and cardiovascular conditions. They also showed 24-29% lower adherence to existing cancer screening programs. Our findings highlight the need for country-specific LCS strategies that consider both eligibility criteria and healthcare capacity. More intensive and targeted strategies to encourage participation will be essential.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Gastroesophageal adenocarcinoma (GEA) is a major cause of global cancer-related deaths. A first-line standard of care for advanced GEA is FOLFOX, with the addition of immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) in patients with a programmed death-ligand 1 (PD-L1) combined positive score of ≥1. However, overall survival remains poor. There is a strong mechanistic rationale for cooperativity between anti-vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) antibodies and ICIs across cancers. Ivonescimab is a bispecific antibody that simultaneously targets programmed cell death protein 1 and VEGF, with evidence of safety and efficacy in colorectal, hepatocellular, and lung cancers. This single-arm, multi-institutional, phase II study seeks to evaluate ivonescimab in combination with FOLFOX as a first-line therapy in GEA. Adults with locally advanced unresectable or metastatic human epidermal growth factor 2 (HER2)-negative GEA are eligible. Positive PD-L1 expression is not required for eligibility. We plan to enroll 40 patients. Ivonescimab 20 mg/kg and FOLFOX are given on day 1 and day 15 of a 28-day cycle. Treatment will continue until disease progression, withdrawal of consent, or death. The primary objective is to define the efficacy of ivonescimab in combination with FOLFOX as measured by the 6-month progression-free survival rate. Translational correlative studies are planned to explore tumor and immunologic determinants of response.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
RAS gene mutations play a major role in the development and progression of cancer. According to recent data, mutations in the RAS gene are responsible for nearly 30% of all cancer cases worldwide. Among these, KRAS mutations account for more than 85% of all RAS mutations and are particularly prevalent in aggressive malignancies, including colorectal cancer (CRC), non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC), and pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC). In this manuscript, we provide a detailed discussion of the RAS signaling cascades and their regulatory mechanisms. The catalytic region of RAS proteins, which comprises the P-loop, Switch I and Switch II regions, and RAS-effector interaction surfaces, exhibits a high degree of structural conservation across the different RAS isoforms. Sotorasib was the first covalent KRAS inhibitor to receive regulatory approval and acts by irreversibly binding to the cysteine residue at position 12 (Cys12). In this manuscript, we discuss in detail targeted RAS inhibitors, including adagrasib (MRTX849), fulzerasib (IBI351), garsorasib (D-1553), glecirasib (JAB-21822), and divarasib (GDC-6036). Finally, we focus on recent advances in RAS inhibitor patents from 2019 to the present, with particular emphasis on thiazole, benzothiazole, quinazoline, and other emerging chemical scaffolds.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Mood and anxiety disorders are common in cancer survivors, and are associated with worse outcomes; however, systematic identification of high-risk patients remains limited, despite screening and intervention guidelines. A systematic review and meta-analysis were conducted to identify risk factors for mood and anxiety disorders, including diagnoses and clinically significant symptoms, in adult cancer survivors. PubMed, Web of Science, Embase, PsycINFO, and Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials were searched for cohort and case-control studies published from January 2000 to November 2024 that evaluated cancer-related, sociodemographic, lifestyle, and psychosocial risk factors in adults with breast, lung, colorectal, prostate, stomach, liver, or pancreatic cancer. Random-effects models with robust variance estimation pooled relative risks (RRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) for factors assessed in ≥5 studies. Fifty of the 53 eligible studies were included in the meta-analysis. Consistent risk factors included high tumor stage (vs. low; n = 28; RR, 1.55; 95% CI, 1.21-1.97), more physical comorbidities (vs. fewer; n = 36; RR, 1.57; 95% CI, 1.34-1.84), prior psychiatric history (high vs. low burden; n = 13; RR, 4.85; 95% CI, 2.77-8.50), female sex (vs. male; n = 19; RR, 1.52; 95% CI, 1.32-1.75), underweight body mass index (vs. normal; n = 6; RR, 1.93; 95% CI, 1.55-2.44), unmarried status (vs. married; n = 25; RR, 1.35; 95% CI, 1.14-1.58), and current smoking (vs. never; n = 12; RR, 1.27; 95% CI, 1.12-1.46). Suggestive associations, although less consistent in sensitivity analyses, were observed for high tumor grade, more extensive surgery, low income, low education, and low social support. Several clinical and social factors were associated with increased risk of mood and anxiety outcomes in adult cancer survivors. These findings may support risk-based psychiatric screening and early intervention in resource-limited oncology settings.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Transplant oncology is generating systematic reviews faster than it is generating independent primary evidence. This imbalance matters because multiple meta-analyses may appear to provide replication while repeatedly pooling the same patients, centers, and prospective programs. The problem is most visible in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) and colorectal liver metastases (CRLM). In HCC, recent umbrella reviews already acknowledge overlapping meta-analytic evidence and variable methodological quality. In CRLM, several contemporary syntheses report materially different 5-year overall survival estimates despite drawing from a small evidence base dominated by a limited number of transplant programs: a broad 16-study analysis reported 53%, a salvage-focused 23-study review 49.4%, and a prospective-only four-study synthesis 62%. These differences may reflect eligibility criteria, study design, era, and patient selection as much as true clinical heterogeneity; without a citation matrix, the contribution of repeated cohorts cannot be quantified. Cholangiocarcinoma and neuroendocrine liver metastases illustrate a different problem: premature pooling of biologically distinct subgroups or sparse series rather than redundancy of mature review literatures. In this methodological perspective, which does not itself perform a formal overlap analysis, we argue that transplant oncology needs evidence-synthesis stewardship. Before another meta-analysis is performed, investigators should determine whether the field needs a new primary synthesis, an overlap-aware umbrella review, or no additional pooling at all. We propose a framework in which corrected covered area, pairwise overlap assessment, AMSTAR 2 appraisal, and explicit cohort-lineage mapping are applied routinely when reviews share concentrated primary evidence, and we offer a worked example and indicative overlap ranges to guide whether a new synthesis is warranted.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Perineural invasion (PNI) is known as a pathological indicator of aggressive tumor behavior and is associated with poor survival in colorectal cancer (CRC). Although individual biological features associated with PNI have been reported, the relationship between PNI and neural cell attraction and stromal features within the tumor microenvironment remains incompletely understood. We aimed to characterize the clinical, genomic, immune, stromal, vascular, and neural features associated with PNI-positive CRC. Clinical and transcriptomic data from 179 CRC patients in The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA) were analyzed. PNI status was morphologically determined from pathological records, yidlding 45 PNI-positive and 134 PNI-negative cases. Gene set enrichment analysis (GSEA) using Hallmark gene sets characterized transcriptomic differences. Genomic features, immune cell composition, consensus molecular subtypes (CMS), stromal and vascular features, and neural features were compared between groups. PNI-positive CRC was associated with advanced T category, distant metastasis, advanced stage, and worse progression-free survival. There was the enrichment of proliferation-related pathways, including E2F targets, the G2M checkpoint and MYC target pathways, in PNI-positive CRC. However, genomic differences were limited, with higher homologous recombination deficiency and PNI-positive CRC is characterized by a coordinated mesenchymal and stromal phenotype accompanied by angiogenic and neural features, with relatively limited genomic and immune differences. These findings provide a biological framework that may help explain the aggressive clinical behavior of PNI-positive CRC.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Ki-67 is widely investigated for its role in assessing colorectal cancer aggressiveness, prognosis, and treatment response. High Ki-67 is associated with poor differentiation and advanced stage, yet there is no consensus on the optimal cutoff value that defines clinically meaningful expression. p53 overexpression was also correlated with high Ki-67. This study aimed to evaluate the effect of neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy (nCRT) on Ki-67 and p53 expressions in rectal adenocarcinoma, explore their association with pathological tumor response using different Ki-67 cutoff thresholds, and assess their relationship with clinicopathological features. A total of 45 patients with rectal adenocarcinoma treated with standard nCRT followed by surgery at a cancer center (from June 2023 to June 2024) were retrospectively included. Pre- and post-nCRT biopsy and resection specimens were immunostained for Ki-67 and p53. Two pathologists evaluated expression levels. Paired Ki-67 expression significantly decreased after nCRT (mean reduction: 32.9%, P < 0.001). A greater decline, especially at ≥ 50% and ≥ 70% cutoff thresholds, was associated with better TRS. Higher baseline Ki-67 was associated with lymphovascular invasion (P < 0.001). p53 showed only modest reduction and was not significantly associated with pathological tumor response. Changes in Ki-67 expression following nCRT were associated with pathological tumor response, whereas pre-treatment Ki-67 and p53 expressions were not. Larger prospective studies are needed to validate these findings and further define the clinical utility of Ki-67 in rectal adenocarcinoma.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Family with sequence similarity 83 member D (FAM83D) is a member of the FAM83 protein family characterized by a conserved domain of unknown function 1669 domain. Initially recognized for its role in mitotic spindle organization and cell-cycle regulation, FAM83D has increasingly emerged as a cancer-associated protein. FAM83D is frequently upregulated in multiple malignancies, including lung, hepatocellular, ovarian, breast, gastric, colorectal, esophageal and pancreatic cancer. Elevated FAM83D expression is associated with tumor progression, lymph node metastasis, epithelial-mesenchymal transition, therapeutic resistance and worse clinical outcomes. Mechanistically, FAM83D may promote malignant phenotypes by regulating cell-cycle progression, interacting with casein kinase 1 isoforms, kinesin family member 22 and F-box/WD repeat-containing protein 7, and modulating oncogenic pathways such as MAPK/ERK, PI3K/AKT/mTOR, Wnt/β-catenin and TGF-β/SMAD signaling. There may be an association between FAM83D and the tumor immune microenvironment, although direct mechanistic evidence remains limited. Clinically, FAM83D may have value as a diagnostic or prognostic biomarker and as a potential therapeutic target. However, the majority of available evidence comes from public database analyses, retrospective tissue studies and preclinical models, while large-scale prospective validation and standardized detection methods are lacking. The present review summarizes the biological features, expression patterns, functional roles, regulatory mechanisms, clinical implications, limitations and future research directions for FAM83D in cancer.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
DNA polymerase ε (POLE) proofreading-deficient variants (POLE-pds) are rare in metastatic colorectal cancer (mCRC) but may predict high sensitivity to immune checkpoint inhibitors. Tumors invading the hollow viscera can develop fistulas due to treatment-induced necrosis. However, immunotherapy-associated ureteral fistulas may present atypically. The current study describes the case of a 52-year-old male patient with mCRC harboring the POLE P286R mutation. After second-line therapy failure, the patient received penpulimab plus anlotinib. Following four treatment cycles, the patient developed unexplained ascites and peritoneal thickening, which were initially considered to potentially indicate disease progression or immune-related adverse events. A ureteral tumor fistula was identified 3 months later; the ascites-to-serum creatinine ratio (3.4:1) and resolution after nephrostomy confirmed urinary leakage. Notably, the patient achieved sustained clinical complete remission for >2.5 years without further antitumor therapy. Ureteral fistulas presenting as ascites are a diagnostically challenging complication during treatment with immunotherapy. Early recognition and conservative management via nephrostomy can be effective and patients with POLE-pd mCRC can achieve durable remission despite such complications. Trial registration no. NCT04970914; date of registration, July 21, 2021.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Ulcerative colitis (UC) is a chronic relapsing inflammatory bowel disease characterized by large-intestinal mucosal ulceration and persistent inflammation, which manifests as bloody diarrhea and abdominal pain and may elevate colorectal cancer risk. Polysaccharide-based hydrogels are attractive candidates for local rectal therapy of UC owing to favorable biocompatibility; however, their therapeutic performance is compromised by short lesion residence time caused by continuous intestinal peristalsis. Herein, we fabricated a muco-adaptive multifunctional hydrogel (B-ODT/CM@PF) constructed via dual-dynamic cross-linking of boronate-diol ester bonds and Schiff-base imine bonds for local treatment of UC. The carboxymethyl chitosan component contributes to rapid local hemostasis and epithelial barrier repair, whereas boron-complexed oxidized dextran confers broad-spectrum bactericidal capacity by disrupting bacterial membrane integrity. Benefiting from boronate-diol interactions, paeoniflorin (PF) is anchored within hydrogel networks to realize inflammation-triggered sustained release. The released PF targets the TLR4-NF-κB signaling axis to drive macrophage M2 polarization and mitigate excessive intestinal inflammatory responses. Moreover, B-ODT/CM@PF rescues the integrity of the intestinal mucosal barrier by inhibiting MLCK activation and preserving tight-junction proteins expression, further ameliorating colitis manifestations. Collectively, this dual-crosslinked bioadhesive hydrogel achieves synergistic functions including mucosal adhesion, hemostasis, antibacterial activity, immunomodulation and barrier reconstruction, providing a promising strategy for local treatment of UC.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
The prognosis of patients with colorectal cancer (CRC) largely depends on whether metastasis occurs. The Warburg effect leads to lactate accumulation and potential lysine lactylation (Kla), thereby promoting tumor initiation and progression. However, the role of non-histone Kla in CRC metastasis remains poorly understood. In this study, integrated lactylome and proteome profiling of liver metastases (LM) and paired primary tumors (PT) from patients with metastatic colorectal cancer (mCRC), together with multi-omics analyses and in vitro and in vivo validation, identified GLUD1 as a key lactylated protein that promotes CRC metastasis. Moreover, GLUD1 lactylation was significantly associated with distant metastasis and poorer prognosis in patients with CRC. Mechanistically, lactate enhanced lactylation of GLUD1 at lysine 503 (K503), which facilitated the interaction between YBX1 and ELAVL1 and increased the post-transcriptional stability of CXCL8 and SLC7A11 mRNAs, thereby enhancing the metastatic potential of tumor cells. In addition, structure-based screening identified cangrelor tetrasodium as a potent inhibitor of GLUD1-K503la, and this compound showed robust efficacy in cell lines, patient-derived organoids (PDOs), and in vivo models. Collectively, these findings identify GLUD1-K503la as a key driver of CRC metastasis and highlight its potential clinical value as both a prognostic biomarker and a therapeutic target.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Cuproptosis is a copper-dependent form of cell death with therapeutic potential in cancer; yet the mechanisms controlling cellular susceptibility to this process remain poorly understood. Here, through a PTM inhibitor screen in colorectal cancer (CRC), we identify S-palmitoylation as a required determinant of cuproptosis sensitivity and DLAT as the principal substrate, modified at the conserved C488 residue. Palmitoylation at C488 stabilizes DLAT by preventing its proteasomal degradation. Mechanistically, this lipidation sterically blocks the E3 ubiquitin ligase SYVN1 from catalyzing K48-linked polyubiquitination of DLAT. We identify ZDHHC1 as the cognate palmitoyltransferase for DLAT and show that copper stress stabilizes TFE3, which then translocates to the nucleus and directly activates ZDHHC1 transcription by binding its promoter. Therapeutically, AAV-mediated ZDHHC1 delivery sensitizes patient-derived xenograft (PDX) tumors to the copper ionophore elesclomol, suppressing tumor growth. Our findings reveal a copper-sensing signaling cascade-from TFE3 through ZDHHC1 to DLAT palmitoylation-that governs cuproptosis vulnerability, and establish ZDHHC1-mediated lipidation as a therapeutic target for sensitizing CRC to copper-based therapies.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Cancer metabolic reprogramming is a hallmark of malignancy, within which ketone body metabolism, particularly β-hydroxybutyrate (BHB), has garnered significant attention due to its complex and paradoxical roles in tumor biology. This review systematically examines the multifaceted functions of BHB in cancer, spanning molecular mechanisms to clinical translation, and synthesizes the conflicting evidence regarding its tumor-suppressive and tumor-promoting effects. We first explore the potential of BHB as a diagnostic, prognostic, and predictive biomarker, where its differential abundance across cancers such as colorectal and pancreatic cancer underscores its context-dependent nature. We then examine the underlying molecular mechanisms that account for these opposing effects. A key focus of this review is the integration of recent advances in combination therapies involving BHB alongside chemotherapy, targeted therapy, immunotherapy, and physical treatments, highlighting its emerging potential as a promising sensitizer for combination regimens. Finally, we systematically outline the core controversies and challenges in the field, attributing the diversity of BHB effects to heterogeneity in tumor metabolic phenotypes, molecular subtypes, and the tumor microenvironment. By constructing a framework that integrates mechanistic diversity, clinical evidence, and combination therapeutic strategies, this review underscores the imperative to shift from a "one-size-fits-all" paradigm toward precision stratification based on tumor metabolic phenotypes, thereby providing a theoretical foundation for the development of safe and effective BHB/ketogenic diet-based combination therapies.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Liver metastasis is the most common site for metastasis, occurring in up to 60% of cases, with the 5-year OS rate being <5%. Current clinical studies have shown that CRC patients with liver metastases have poor outcomes when receiving immunotherapy. However, there are no comprehensive studies that explore the actionable mutations and signaling pathways in metastatic CRC with liver-only involvement, particularly using large next-generation sequencing (NGS) panel data combined with clinical case information. Due to the challenge of enrollment work, this study included clinical and mutational characteristics of patients with liver-only metastasis (N = 72) and those with lung or peritoneal-only metastasis (N = 26). Two external comparison cohorts with mutational characteristics were obtained from cBioPortal and used for external comparison; survival data were available for one of them. Liver-only metastasis in CRC was predominantly in males (66.67%) and is notably characterized by a high left-sided occurrence (55.56%, 40/72). Only three patients with liver-only metastatic CRC were TMB-high (TMB-H), and two were microsatellite instability-high (MSI-H), with no cases found in those with lung or peritoneal-only metastasis. The most commonly mutated genes in liver-only metastatic CRC included TP53 (83%), APC (76%), KRAS (50%), and BRAF (14%), with BRAF and KRAS mutations being mutually exclusive. Moreover, genes in the hepatocellular carcinoma pathway were significantly enriched; the same pathway was also enriched when the lung or peritoneal-only cohort was analyzed separately, so it is not specific to liver metastasis. In univariable analysis, left-sided primary tumor approached significance (P = 0.051), and BRAF- and TSC2-mutated tumors were associated with poorer overall survival (OS; P = 0.00062 and P = 0.031, respectively). After Benjamini-Hochberg correction of the 29 univariable comparisons, only BRAF remained significant (q = 0.018), whereas TSC2 did not (q = 0.45). In the multivariable model, BRAF mutation remained independently associated with poorer OS (HR 3.2, 95% CI 1.6-6.4; P = 0.0012), whereas the TSC2 association (P = 0.025, based on 4 altered patients) is reported as exploratory. A total of 120 treatment-sensitive driver mutations and 41 drug-resistant mutations were identified, averaging 2.24 per patient. The dominant drug-resistant mutations-KRAS/NRAS-were associated with resistance to cetuximab and panitumumab (Level R1). Therefore, KRAS/NRAS status should be determined before treatment and monitored for acquired resistance mutations during therapy, because it determines eligibility for anti-EGFR therapy. This study provides insights into the molecular characteristics of CRC with liver-only metastasis and identifies a candidate prognostic biomarker that requires independent validation. These analyses illustrate how mutation data can be translated into candidate treatment options.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Additional biomarkers are needed to improve prognostic assessment and support individualized clinical management in colorectal cancer (CRC). This study aimed to identify exosomal proteins enriched in specimen-derived blood and explore their prognostic relevance in CRC. Specimen-derived blood (sdBlood) was collected immediately after removal of colorectal cancer specimens during radical resection. Exosomes were isolated using a commercial extraction kit, and exosomal proteins were quantified by liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry. Functional enrichment analyses were performed for significantly upregulated proteins. Prognostic associations were explored using tumor-tissue gene expression and survival data from a publicly available CRC dataset. Larger volumes of sdBlood were obtained from ascending and transverse colon cancer specimens than from descending colon cancer specimens (12.77 ± 2.72 mL and 11.10 ± 2.59 mL vs. 5.28 ± 1.96 mL, respectively; P < 0.001). CEA levels and the abundance of eight exosomal proteins (H2AC20, TXN, SERPINF2, HSPB1, SERPINB3, DSP, H2BC21, and S100A7) were significantly higher in sdBlood than in peripheral venous blood. Functional enrichment analyses identified vesicle-related components, including the vesicle lumen and secretory granule lumen, as well as focal adhesion and amoebiasis-associated pathways. In the public tumor-tissue dataset, higher expression of H2AC18 (HIST2H2AA3), H2BC21 (HIST2H2BE), and SERPINB3 was associated with poorer overall survival; the other genes showed no significant survival associations. sdBlood-derived exosomes contain proteins at higher levels than those found in peripheral venous blood and may provide a useful source of candidate CRC biomarkers. Their prognostic value at the exosomal protein level requires further validation.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
The role of statins and aspirin in modulating tumour response to total neoadjuvant therapy (TNT) in advanced rectal cancer remains unclear. This study evaluates the impact of these medications on overall complete response (oCR) to TNT in patients with advanced rectal cancer. This multicentre, retrospective cohort study included patients with advanced rectal cancer treated with TNT with curative intent at five South Australian hospitals between 2019 and 2026. Medication use (statins and aspirin) was extracted from electronic medical records prior to TNT initiation. The primary outcome was the oCR rate, encompassing clinical complete response (cCR) and pathological complete response (pCR). Secondary outcomes included overall survival (OS), cancer-specific survival (CSS), disease-free survival (DFS) and local recurrence-free survival (LRFS). Of 360 patients receiving TNT, 95 (26.4%) used statins and 30 (8.3%) used aspirin. No significant differences in oCR rates were observed between statin or aspirin users and non-users (51.9% vs. 40.8%, p = 0.068; 43.3% vs. 43.6%, p = 0.974, respectively). Similarly, no significant differences in cCR or pCR rates were observed for either statin or aspirin use. On logistic regression, achievement of oCR was not significantly associated with statin use (OR, 1.55; 95% CI, 0.97-2.48) or aspirin use (OR, 0.99; 95% CI, 0.47-2.10). Cox regression revealed no significant associations between statin or aspirin use and OS, CSS, DFS or LRFS. Neither statin nor aspirin use was independently associated with improved tumour response to TNT in advanced rectal cancer.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
CRC is the fourth most common cancer diagnosed in the United States today. The cancer develops in an adenoma-type polyp and takes more than five years to develop cancerous change. Removal of the polyp will prevent the development of cancer. The National Program for Quality Indicators in Medicine was founded in 2012 and, over the years, has reached a continuous measurement of 65 indicators. The PDR index was chosen because of the relationship between the rate of colonoscopies in which at least one polyp )PDR) was found, and the development of CRC after a colonoscopy that was considered normal. The current study aims to evaluate the participation of gastroenterology units of hospitals in Israel in the two years of PDR measurement and the relationship to various factors, while comparing service providers. A retrospective study that relies on data from the national program as published for the measurement years 2022 and 2023. PDR data were analyzed in 32 general hospitals. The national target reached was calculated, and they were compared. In these years, 87,813 and 90,499 colonoscopies were performed in all departments for all the indications (except those detailed in "Methods"), respectively. The PDR range in 2022 was between 23% and 47%, and in 2023 between 19% and 47%. In 2022, 8 hospitals reached or exceeded the 42% rate, and in 2023, 10 hospitals. 20 hospitals improved, dropped by 5, and there was no change in 5. The national achievement was 37% in 2022 and 38% in 2023 (P = 0.03277). PDR improved over time. There is room to improve the quality of colonoscopies in Israel to increase their effectiveness in preventing CRC. There is a need to develop a strategy to improve PDR rates while taking into account various process factors.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Although sentinel lymph node mapping has become the standard approach for surgical staging in early-stage endometrial cancer, systematic pelvic lymph node dissection (PLND) continues to play an important role in selected patients with intermediate- and high-risk disease. A 66-year-old woman with preoperatively diagnosed early-stage uterine serous carcinoma (p53-positive) underwent single-port robotic staging surgery, including simple hysterectomy, bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy, pelvic and para-aortic lymph node dissection, and partial omentectomy. The procedure was completed without intraoperative complications. A standardized, anatomy-based approach using reproducible anatomical landmarks facilitated safe and systematic en bloc PLND. Suspension of the vesicohypogastric fascia (umbilical artery) provided stable exposure of the retroperitoneal space, while the articulating snake-like instruments of the SP platform enabled precise traction and countertraction, facilitating meticulous dissection throughout the procedure. Final histopathological examination confirmed stage IIC uterine serous carcinoma. The patient subsequently received adjuvant paclitaxel-carboplatin chemotherapy and remains disease-free at the latest follow-up. The SP platform enables standardized, anatomy-based, en bloc PLND while adhering to fundamental oncologic principles. The anatomical concepts and technical strategies may facilitate reproducible surgical practice and may be applicable across multiple specialties in pelvic oncology.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Primary sclerosing cholangitis (PSC) is a rare cholangiopathy characterized by multifocal inflammation and fibrostenotic remodeling of the bile ducts, cholestasis, and increased risks of cholangiocarcinoma and colorectal cancer. No pharmacological therapy has yet improved transplant-free survival. Clinical care therefore depends on accurate phenotyping, surveillance, treatment of biliary and intestinal complications, and timely liver transplantation. Population-based and clinical studies define the epidemiology, risk factors, presentation, diagnosis, and management of PSC. Studies of human biospecimens, including microbiome and metabolomic analyses, describe biological changes associated with the disease, whereas organoid and animal models are used to investigate potential mechanisms. The available evidence links genetic susceptibility and PSC-associated inflammatory bowel disease to cholangiocyte injury, immune activation, disturbed bile acid homeostasis, and microbial alterations. At the bile duct interface, cholangiocyte senescence and barrier dysfunction may interact with microbial exposure and immune-cell recruitment to promote periductal fibrosis. PSC is therefore more plausibly viewed as a multicellular process than as the consequence of a single microbial, immune, or bile acid pathway. Whether dysbiosis and altered bile acid profiles contribute to disease development or instead reflect established PSC remains unresolved. Concomitant inflammatory bowel disease, medication use, biliary obstruction, and previous biliary interventions further complicate causal inference. Longitudinal human studies may distinguish early drivers from secondary changes. Mechanistic findings should ultimately improve patient phenotyping, surveillance, endoscopic management, and selection for targeted trials. Such trials will require biologically informed designs and endpoints that capture durable clinical benefit.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Appendectomy is among the most frequently performed operations in children, and acute appendicitis remains one of the most common pediatric surgical emergencies worldwide. For more than a century, the appendix was regarded as a vestigial structure whose removal carried no lasting consequence, an assumption that underlies the long-standing default of operative management of appendicitis. Two developments now invite reexamination of that assumption: the growing use of nonoperative management for uncomplicated appendicitis, and an expanding body of evidence arguing the appendix is immunologically active and serves as a reservoir for the gut microbiome. This review synthesizes current data on the long-term implications of appendectomy in the pediatric population. We first examine the appendix as a functional organ-its immunologic role, its function as a microbiome reservoir, and its participation in the gut-brain axis. We review its proposed associations with inflammatory bowel disease, systemic autoimmune disease, and Parkinson disease, followed by its oncologic relevance with respect to appendiceal neuroendocrine tumors and colorectal cancer. Much of the evidence is observational, derived from adults, and contradictory. Appendectomy for appropriate indications remains safe and effective, but increasing understanding of the appendix's biology and consequences of its removal may be helpful with shared decision-making.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Diffuse pleural mesothelioma (DPM) is an aggressive, most commonly asbestos-related malignancy with limited therapeutic options. HER2-directed antibody-drug conjugates active against HER2-low tumors have renewed interest in HER2 assessment across malignancies, yet no DPM-specific HER2 scoring system exists and the impact of applying tumor-specific guidelines to DPM is unknown. We evaluated HER2 expression by immunohistochemistry, with FISH confirmation, in 53 consecutive DPM patients, and compared classification when the breast, gastric, and colorectal scoring guidelines were applied in parallel to the same cases. HER2 membrane staining was detected in 9 cases (17.0%), consistently faint-barely perceptible, incomplete, and segmental (median 5% of neoplastic cells), with no overexpression or amplification. The identical staining pattern yielded markedly discordant scores: most cases were classified as "0″ under breast criteria but as "1+" under gastric and colorectal criteria. HER2 expression was confined to epithelioid components. These findings show that, in the absence of a validated DPM-specific scoring system, HER2 guidelines are not interchangeable, a methodological caveat with direct implications for biomarker comparability and for interpreting "HER2-low" status in the era of next-generation antibody - drug conjugates.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Colorectal cancer is a major global health concern, highlighting the need for early and accurate detection to improve treatment outcomes. Existing screening techniques are often expensive, invasive, or lack sensitivity, especially for asymptomatic individuals. Genetic mutations, like Tumor Suppressor Protein (TP53), K-Ras protein (KRAS) and Adenomatous Polyposis Coli (APC), play crucial roles in Colorectal cancer development, while demographic factors, like age, sex, ethnicity, and family history, significantly influence risk. Incorporating genetic and demographic data might improve early and non-invasive diagnosis. Current diagnostic techniques ineffectively combine genetic and demographic factors, which limits the accuracy of early detection. Hence, there is a need for predictive modules to improve screening and personalized risk assessment. To overcome these limitations, Fractional Bitterling Fish Optimization-based Hierarchical Convolutional Neural Network (FBFO_HCNN) is proposed for diagnosing Colorectal cancer based on genetic mutations and demographic factors. This research involves two types of input data, namely, gene and demographic data. First, the gene selection process is performed using gene expression data with the Fractional Bitterling Fish Optimization (FBFO). Then, augmentation is done using the bootstrapping method, which is considered as output-1. Similarly, demographic data is utilized in the data normalization phase is executed by Peldschus normalization. After that, FBFO is designed for the feature selection process, and the bootstrapping method is employed for the data augmentation process, which provides output-2. Lastly, diagnosis of Colorectal cancer is done by Hierarchical Convolutional Neural Network (HCNN) by considering both outputs, where HCNN is tuned using the FBFO algorithm. Experimental results demonstrate that FBFO_HCNN achieved superior values for Accuracy, True Negative Rate (TNR), True Positive Rate (TPR), and False Omission Rate (FOR) of 96.656%, 96.678%, 95.412%, and 3.796%.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Early remission in inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) is increasingly recognized for providing long-term prognostic benefits, despite limited supporting data. We examined the prognostic value of histological remission within 12 months of diagnosis. A nationwide cohort study of 14 019 Swedish IBD patients diagnosed in 1990-2022. These patients underwent ileo-colorectal biopsies showing histological remission or inflammation within 1-<12 months post-diagnosis. We estimated adjusted hazard ratios (aHRs) for treatment failure (IBD-related surgery, hospitalization, third corticosteroid dispensation, or second-line advanced therapies), colorectal cancer (CRC), and death until 2023. We adjusted for sociodemographic characteristics, comorbidities, IBD phenotype, and medication history. Early histological remission was more prevalent in patients with higher educational attainment or those diagnosed since 2000, but less common in childhood-onset (<18 years) and elderly-onset (≥60 years) IBD. Average follow-up extended to 13.7 years. Compared to early remission, histological inflammation within 12 months was linked to an increased risk of treatment failure (aHR = 1.47, 95% CI = 1.39-1.54), particularly hospitalization (aHR = 1.46, 95% CI = 1.39-1.54) and second-line advanced therapy (aHR = 1.60, 95% CI = 1.34-1.91). Histological inflammation (vs early remission) was also linked to a heightened CRC risk (aHR = 1.65, 95% CI = 1.21-2.24), with similar risks in Crohn's disease (CD: aHR = 1.66, 95% CI = 0.94-2.93) and ulcerative colitis (UC: aHR = 1.77, 95% CI = 1.20-2.60). Mortality risk was elevated in CD (aHR = 1.21, 95% CI = 1.01-1.45) but not UC (aHR = 0.96, 95% CI = 0.85-1.08). Associations were similar for corticosteroid-free histological remission within 6 and 12 months. Sustained histological inflammation (vs remission) 12 months after IBD diagnosis predicted a higher risk of treatment failure and CRC, indicating that early histological remission may improve long-term disease prognosis.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Gynaecological surveillance is offered in Lynch syndrome despite limited evidence for its clinical effectiveness. Invasive gynaecological investigations often cause pain and distress, but experiences vary and little is known about the psychological burden of repeated testing. We evaluated the lived experiences of annual gynaecological surveillance in women with and at risk of Lynch syndrome. Recruitment occurred via hospital clinics, social media, and Lynch Syndrome UK. Participants completed a semi-structured questionnaire by telephone. Quantitative data were summarised descriptively. Free-text responses were recorded verbatim, coded inductively and grouped thematically, with outputs reviewed by a second researcher. Overall, 104 women participated: 93 had confirmed Lynch syndrome and 11 had a strong family history of Lynch syndrome cancers (median age: 41 years). Median pain scores were 7/10 for outpatient hysteroscopy (IQR 6-9) and endometrial biopsy (IQR 6-10), versus 3/10 for pelvic examination and transvaginal ultrasound scan (both IQR 2-4). Among participants undergoing annual surveillance (75/104), 74 (98.6%) found surveillance reassuring, but 44 (58.6%) reported surveillance-related anxiety. 51 (68%) said they attended all scheduled surveillance visits. Free-text responses identified anticipatory procedural distress and cancer worry, particularly fear of adverse findings. Participants described surveillance as necessary given the limited non-surgical alternatives. Although regular gynaecological surveillance provides reassurance, it imposes considerable physical, psychological and practical burdens. Addressing this requires a dual approach: immediate optimisation of pain management and psychological support within current clinics, alongside a long-term shift toward non-invasive diagnostic innovations to fundamentally transform the healthcare experiences of high-risk cohorts.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
To develop a machine-learning model combining multiparametric MRI-derived intratumoral heterogeneity (ITH) scores with clinical features for preoperative prediction of microsatellite instability (MSI) in rectal cancer and to explore MSI-associated molecular features. This retrospective study enrolled 464 rectal cancer patients from three centers, including training (n = 198; MSI-H, 26), internal validation (n = 110; MSI-H, 12), and external validation (n = 156; MSI-H, 23) cohorts. Three-dimensional ITH scores were derived from T2WI and DWI. Logistic regression identified independent clinical predictors. Six machine-learning algorithms were used to construct clinical, ITH, and combined models. Performance was assessed using AUCs with 95% confidence intervals, calibration curves, decision-curve analysis, and SHAP. TCGA transcriptomics, PPI analysis, and immunohistochemistry in 10 local samples were used for molecular exploration. Age, tumor length, location, and N stage were independent predictors. The combined model achieved AUCs of 0.865 (95% CI, 0.828-0.899), 0.839 (95% CI, 0.775-0.895), and 0.785 (95% CI, 0.729-0.835) in training, internal, and external cohorts, respectively. In external validation, it was comparable to the clinical model (AUC = 0.790; BH-adjusted P = 0.076), and the ITH-only model performed poorly (AUC = 0.548). SHAP identified tumor location, T stage, and ITH features as major contributors. Transcriptomics identified 378 differentially expressed genes, and PPI analysis suggested AKT1 as a hub candidate. IHC showed higher AKT1 H-scores in MSS tumors (143.60 ± 26.14 vs. 76.74 ± 38.43; P = 0.008). The model showed favorable training/internal performance but moderate external performance without clear incremental value. Larger prospective multicenter cohorts are needed. Transcriptomic and pilot IHC analyses suggest possible AKT1 expression differences between MSI-H and MSS rectal cancers.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Rectal prolapse is increasing in prevalence as the population ages. It can cause a wide variety of symptoms, including fecal incontinence severely impacting a patient's quality of life. Given that hemorrhoidal disease is often misdiagnosed as rectal prolapse, it is important for surgeons to be familiar with key symptoms, appropriate physical exam, and work-up. With improvements in anesthesia care and minimally invasive surgery, the options for a more durable repair have expanded for patients who are older with multiple medical comorbidities. This article aims to review the diagnosis, work-up, and evolution of surgical management of rectal prolapse. This will aid surgeons in making the correct diagnosis and assisting their patient's informed decision making regarding surgical repair.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
This study aimed to comprehensively analyze the burden of cancer attributable to dietary risk factors in China from 1990-2023 and explore age-and sex-specific patterns to inform targeted prevention strategies. Using data from the Global Burden of Disease (GBD) 2023 study, we evaluated China's diet-attributable cancer burden using absolute death counts, disability-adjusted life years (DALYs), age-standardized mortality rates (ASMRs), and age-standardized DALY rates (ASDRs). Estimated annual percentage changes (EAPCs) were computed to characterize temporal trends. In 2023, dietary risks were responsible for 168,740.24 (95% UI: 58,919.72-314,396.91) deaths and 4,096,470.77 (95% UI: 1,338,318.09-7,634,577.27) DALYs from the included diet-attributable cancers. Between 1990 and 2023, the overall ASMR (EAPC = -3.09, 95% CI: -3.28--2.90) and ASDR (EAPC = -3.28, 95% CI: -3.47--3.10) for these cancers demonstrated a decreasing trend, with colorectal cancer (CRC) accounting for the largest diet-attributable cancer burden. Diets high in red meat, low in milk, and low in whole grains were the three leading risk contributors, and stratified analyses revealed a markedly higher burden among males and older adults. Although age-standardized rates (ASRs) of diet-attributable cancer in China have declined over the past three decades, the absolute disease burden remains substantial. Suboptimal dietary patterns characterized by high red meat intake together with inadequate milk and whole grain consumption continue to drive this burden, particularly among males and older adults, underscoring the urgent need for targeted public health interventions for dietary adjustments in these high-risk groups.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Alternative multiport robotic systems from manufacturers other than Intuitive Surgical are being adopted for colorectal cancer procedures, yet how their outcomes compare with the established da Vinci platform remains unclear. PubMed, Web of Science, Scopus, and CENTRAL were searched through August 2026 for randomised trials and comparative observational studies of alternative multiport robots versus da Vinci for colorectal cancer surgery. Random-effects risk ratios (RRs) and mean differences were stratified by platform and resection site; RoB 2, ROBINS-I and GRADE were applied. Twelve studies (one randomised trial; 1,144 participants: 557 alternative platform, 587 da Vinci) evaluated six platforms; hinotori was assessed in six studies and four platforms in one study each. Five cohorts were at serious risk of bias. Console time was 29.38 min longer with alternative platforms (95% CI 17.87 to 40.89; low certainty; mainly hinotori). Total operative time was 20.04 min longer (95% CI 8.81 to 31.28), but heterogeneity and small-study effects made this very uncertain (trim-and-fill estimate 7.24 min, - 4.20 to 18.69). Morbidity estimates were imprecise: Clavien-Dindo grade ≥ II complications RR 1.17 (0.91 to 1.51), grade ≥ III RR 0.86 (0.44 to 1.69), and anastomotic leak RR 1.35 (0.47 to 3.89; 17 events). Certainty was very low for all other outcomes. Alternative multiport robots appear feasible for colorectal cancer surgery but may prolong console time. Their comparative safety and pathological quality relative to da Vinci remain uncertain, and current data do not establish equivalence or non-inferiority. Adequately powered, platform-specific prospective comparisons with predefined non-inferiority margins are required.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Imbalance in copper ion homeostasis is closely associated with the development and progression of various cancers, yet its dynamic regulatory mechanisms and targeting value in colorectal cancer remain unclear. This study reveals the relationship between endogenous metabolites and copper-dependent proliferation in CRC, identifying the histone deacetylase SIRT6 as a critical hub regulating copper homeostasis and determining cell fate. SIRT6 knockout promotes copper-dependent proliferation but simultaneously sensitizes CRC cells to cuproptosis. Mechanistically, SIRT6 epigenetically suppresses the transcription of SLC31A1 by deacetylating H3K9/K56, thereby limiting intracellular copper accumulation and inhibiting cuproplasia. On the other hand, SIRT6 directly binds to and deacetylates the transcription factor MTF1, inhibiting its ubiquitination-mediated degradation and enhancing its transcriptional activity, consequently promoting the expression of metallothioneins. MT1A/MT2A remodel subcellular copper distribution through copper chelation, reducing mitochondrial copper load and conferring resistance to cuproptosis. Importantly, the combined application of the SIRT6 inhibitor OSS_128167 and the copper ionophore Elesclomol demonstrated significant synergistic anti-tumor efficacy in patient-derived xenograft models. To identify risk factors for antimicrobial resistance (AMR) in seven pathogen-antimicrobial combinations in patients with cancer and cancer survivors. ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Tumor microenvironment interactions are crucial for driving inflammation, proliferation, and metastatic potential in cancer. Genomic and microenvironmental alterations disrupt gene expression networks, where transcription factors play a pivotal role in oncogenic signaling. While the NF-κB pathway typically drives the expression of pro-inflammatory cytokines and inflammasome components (such as NLRP3), the hypoxic response mediated by HIF-1α promotes angiogenesis via VEGF recruitment. This study investigates how colorectal adenocarcinoma (HT29) and carcinoma (HCT116) cells modulate the inflammatory and hypoxic responses of gastric epithelial cells (GES-1) via paracrine factors released in conditioned medium (CM). Our findings reveal that despite a downregulation of NF-κB and inflammasome components in CRC-CM-treated GES-1 cells, there was a significant upregulation of IL1B, HIF1A, and HIF1B transcripts. Notably, we observed a striking upregulation of Caspase-4 (CASP4) mRNA. Together, these data demonstrate that colorectal cancer cells alter the transcriptional profile of hypoxia-associated genes in normal epithelial cells by upregulating HIF-1α and HIF-1β mRNA levels, alongside a massive induction of CASP4 transcripts.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Gastrointestinal (GI) cancers have been a largely disappointing arena for immune-checkpoint inhibition, with durable benefit confined to mismatch-repair-deficient (dMMR/MSI-H) disease, PD-L1-enriched gastroesophageal adenocarcinoma, and hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). A shared feature of many resistant GI tumors is a vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF)-driven, immune-excluded microenvironment, providing a mechanistic rationale for co-targeting angiogenesis and the PD-(L)1 axis. The clinical foundation for this strategy has now been established across GI malignancies: atezolizumab plus bevacizumab became standard of care in HCC (IMbrave150), and the combination of zanzalintinib with atezolizumab delivered the first immune-checkpoint-based overall-survival benefit in microsatellite-stable (MSS) colorectal cancer in the phase 3 STELLAR-303 trial - providing phase 3 support for multikinase (VEGFR/MET/TAM-family)/checkpoint co-targeting in a disease long considered immune-refractory, and supporting the VEGF/checkpoint hypothesis without establishing that the benefit is attributable to VEGF-pathway inhibition specifically. These successes have catalyzed the development of single-molecule VEGF/VEGFR × PD-1/PD-L1 bispecific antibodies, which aim to consolidate and potentially improve upon the co-targeting paradigm through cooperative binding, conditional tumor selectivity, and simplified pharmacology. Ivonescimab (AK112) is the most clinically advanced agent and carries the broadest GI portfolio, spanning colorectal, gastroesophageal, hepatobiliary, and pancreatic programs; pumitamig (BNT327/PM8002) and SSGJ-707 (PF-08634404) anchor parallel registrational efforts. In biliary tract cancer, the randomized phase 3 HARMONi-GI1 trial - presented at ESMO 2026 - showed that ivonescimab plus gemcitabine/cisplatin improved overall survival over durvalumab plus gemcitabine/cisplatin (median 14.9 versus 12.1 months; HR 0.75), the first positive phase 3 result for the class in a GI cancer, albeit from an interim analysis in a China-only population with benefit confined to intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma; the remaining pivotal programs (HARMONi-GI2/GI3, ROSETTA) are ongoing. The biological warrant and cross-tumor signals are compelling, but GI-specific efficacy and safety for the bispecific class remain early, geographically concentrated, and confounded by comparator choice; no bispecific-validated biomarker yet exists. HARMONi-GI1 establishes superiority over checkpoint-plus-chemotherapy in one disease; the trials now needed are those comparing the bispecific with the co-administered anti-VEGF/checkpoint doublet, which alone can determine whether single-molecule co-targeting delivers a genuinely immunological gain or merely a superior anti-angiogenic effect.

Rural patients often bypass local hospitals for surgical care, but the frequency and impact of bypass among colorectal cancer patients are unclear. We studied rural Medicare beneficiaries aged 65-99 undergoing colorectal cancer surgery (2016-2023). Hospital bypass was defined as surgery at a hospital >20 min farther than the nearest surgical facility. Regression models evaluated associations with postoperative outcomes. Among 58,373 patients, 38% bypassed their nearest hospital. Bypass was more common for proctectomy than colectomy (48.8% vs 35.4%). Among rectal cancer patients, bypass was associated with lower 30-day mortality and similar complication and readmission rates. Among colon cancer patients, bypass was associated with higher complication and readmission, and lower mortality rates. Efforts to improve access to specialized care while strengthening local surgical capacity may help optimize outcomes.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Use of glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs) for diabetes and obesity is increasing, but effects on uncommon or long-latency cancers are uncertain. We synthesised meta-analytic evidence for overall and site-specific cancer risk and assessed methodological quality, overlap, outcome-level certainty, and credibility. We searched PubMed, Embase, and the Cochrane Library from inception to 30 June 2026 for meta-analyses of GLP-1RAs or the dual GIP/GLP-1 receptor agonist tirzepatide and incident cancer. Randomised and observational evidence was considered separately; review-level estimates were not recombined. We assessed methodological confidence with AMSTAR 2, overlap with corrected covered area (CCA), outcome-level certainty with a GRADE-informed algorithm, and association credibility with Ioannidis criteria. We included 38 meta-analyses from 2012 to 2026. The most comprehensive placebo-controlled randomised evidence (48 trials, 94 245 participants, median follow-up 70 weeks) showed no statistically significant association with thyroid cancer (odds ratio [OR] 1·37, 95% CI 0·82-2·31; 1 fewer to 9 more cases per 10 000 treated), pancreatic cancer (0·84, 0·53-1·35), colorectal cancer (1·11, 0·75-1·65), or breast cancer (0·95, 0·60-1·49), and no overall cancer increase (OR 1·05, 0·98-1·13 across 50 trials). Thyroid and agent-specific haematological signals were inconsistent or based on sparse events; between-review discordance for thyroid and colorectal cancer was largely attributable to comparator restriction, choice of estimator, and handling of zero-event trials rather than to differences in cancer ascertainment. Observational syntheses suggested lower hepatocellular carcinoma risk (hazard ratio 0·60, 95% CI 0·41-0·88), but four reviews had very high overlap (CCA 50·0%). Outcome-level certainty was moderate for five outcomes, low for 11, and very low for five; none was high. No association met class I or II credibility criteria. Randomised evidence shows no evidence of a material increase in overall or site-specific cancer risk over currently observed trial durations (median about 70 weeks, maximum about 5 years), and cancer concerns alone do not justify withholding indicated GLP-1RA treatment. Small, rare, long-latency, dose-specific, or agent-specific effects cannot be excluded, and the evidence cannot address exposure beyond approximately five years, well short of the 8-10 years generally required to evaluate cancer incidence. Observational protective associations should not support causal or cancer-prevention claims. None.

Ulcerative colitis (UC) and granulomatosis with polyangiitis (GPA) are distinct autoimmune disorders, and their coexistence is rarely reported. Furthermore, long-term malignant complications in patients with both conditions have been infrequently described. Consequently, long-term management strategies and surveillance for intestinal cancer risk in patients with concomitant UC and GPA remain poorly defined. A male patient initially diagnosed with extensive UC sequentially developed sacroiliitis and subsequently GPA during a 13-year disease course, confirmed by renal and cutaneous involvement. The patient was diagnosed with long-standing extensive ulcerative colitis, granulomatosis with polyangiitis, sigmoid colon adenocarcinoma, and rectal adenocarcinoma. The patient received long-term maintenance therapy with glucocorticoids and underwent laparoscopic radical rectal cancer resection combined with total colectomy and permanent ileostomy, followed by adjuvant XELOX (oxaliplatin plus capecitabine) chemotherapy. The patient tolerated the chemotherapy well, with only grade 1 gastrointestinal adverse events and no severe myelosuppression. He is currently undergoing regular adjuvant chemotherapy and continues standardized multidisciplinary long-term outpatient surveillance. This case highlights the cumulative risk of concurrent autoimmune comorbidities and malignant transformation in long-standing UC, while emphasizing the diagnostic and therapeutic challenges associated with multisystem overlapping inflammatory disorders. It also adds to the limited body of literature describing the coexistence of inflammatory bowel disease, antineutrophil cytoplasmic antibody-associated vasculitis, and rectal adenocarcinoma.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Anti-EGFR therapy improves outcomes in patients with RAS wild-type metastatic colorectal cancer (mCRC), but acquired resistance frequently emerges, and its mechanisms are heterogeneous. This report describes 2 patients with RAS wild-type mCRC who developed acquired resistance to anti-EGFR therapy. Case 2: human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (HER2) overexpression (immunohistochemistry 3+) was identified in the primary tumor on molecular reassessment after progression. Case 1 received cetuximab plus mFOLFOX6 followed by cetuximab-based maintenance; after progression, molecular analysis of the liver metastasis detected a Kirsten rat sarcoma viral oncogene homolog mutation, anti-EGFR therapy was discontinued and switched to FOLFIRI plus bevacizumab, and the patient subsequently underwent liver metastasectomy, with quarterly liquid biopsies for monitoring. Case 2 received cetuximab plus mFOLFOX6 followed by cetuximab plus 5-fluorouracil; after HER2 amplification was confirmed, treatment was switched to trastuzumab plus pertuzumab combined with chemotherapy, and surgery was deferred. At the last follow-up, case 1 had stable disease with undetectable RAS-mutated circulating tumor DNA after metastasectomy and continued chemotherapy. Case 2 showed gradual disease progression despite HER2-directed therapy and required further-line treatment. These 2 cases illustrate that acquired resistance to anti-EGFR therapy is a dynamic and heterogeneous process rather than a single event, and they support repeated molecular profiling of metastatic lesions to guide subsequent treatment selection.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）

Complete data-independent acquisition analysis output quantified 11,528 protein groups, of which 9,097 were included in the statistical analysis. The retained matrix had an overall missing-data rate of 8.59%, and the mean protein-wise coefficients of variation were 8.45% for pooled quality-control samples and 7.57% for technical replicates. Primary Welch testing identified 293 colorectal and 325 gastric nominal candidate proteins at |log2 fold change| > log2(1.2) and P < 0.05. Moderated limma analysis with Benjamini-Hochberg correction across all 9,097 proteins identified 11 colorectal and 6 gastric candidates with q < 0.05. In an analysis performed without imputation or outlier truncation, 92.8% and 92.0% of the respective candidate sets retained the direction of change, whereas 78.8% and 76.6% retained both the fold-change and nominal P-value thresholds. The candidate proteins showed exploratory recurrence of lipid-, insulin-, and peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor-related pathways, whereas public multi-omics data provided pathway-level context rather than gene-level validation. Overall, the study provides a high-throughput archival-tissue proteomics workflow and a robustness framework for interpreting detection-sensitive candidate proteins.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Tumor necrosis is associated with poor prognosis in colorectal cancer (CRC) yet is generally viewed as a passive consequence of tumor growth rather than a therapeutic target. We demonstrate that necrosis correlates with metastatic disease in human CRC independently of tumor size. Single-cell RNA sequencing and spatial transcriptomics of primary CRC and colorectal liver metastases revealed that peri-necrotic programs are associated with metastatic progression. Patients with CRC exhibited increased circulating neutrophils, including NET-primed and CD177-low neutrophils with reduced extravasation capacity. Consistent with these findings, intravascular NET aggregates localized adjacent to necrotic regions in human CRC specimens. In a mismatch repair-proficient mouse model of CRC, neutrophil infiltration and NET formation increased during tumor progression, whereas genetic and pharmacologic NET inhibition reduced tumor necrosis, decreased metastasis, and enhanced chemotherapy efficacy. Together, these findings identify NET-driven tumor necrosis as an active promoter of CRC metastasis and support NET inhibition as a therapeutic strategy.
