ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Gastrointestinal physiology varies across the 24-h day as central and peripheral clocks coordinate metabolism, epithelial renewal, mucosal immunity, barrier permeability, motility, and microbial activity. Disrupted temporal organization is associated with metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease, inflammatory bowel disease, colorectal cancer, and hepatocellular carcinoma. This narrative review integrates molecular mechanisms with clinical evidence, distinguishing experimental causality from observational associations. Chrononutrition examines interactions between eating patterns and circadian biology, including meal timing, frequency, regularity, and eating-window duration. Human studies support effects of meal timing on peripheral rhythms, but improvements in metabolic markers do not consistently exceed those achieved by calorie restriction. Sleep disturbance predicts disease activity in some inflammatory bowel disease cohorts, whereas preliminary sleep-intervention trials have not established prevention of relapse. Chronomodulated chemotherapy illustrates both potential benefits and implementation barriers, including sex-dependent outcomes and the need for programmable infusion systems. Chronotype, an individual's preference for earlier or later sleep and activity, may modify the feasibility of temporal interventions. Translation requires adequately controlled trials that assess biological phase, disease activity, nutritional safety, adherence, and clinically meaningful outcomes alongside standard care.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Transgender women face a substantially higher risk of anal cancer- about 5.5 times that of cisgender individuals- largely due to higher rates of anal HPV infection. Despite this elevated risk, data on screening in this population are scarce, and formal screening guidelines were not established until 2024. To address gaps in understanding screening engagement, the factors and barriers to high‑resolution anoscopy (FAB HRA) study used a sequential explanatory mixed‑methods design to examine how transgender women with abnormal cytology make decisions about completing HRA. Participants were recruited from a clinic that offers gender affirming care to transgender communities. In the qualitative phase, Black transgender women, predominantly living with HIV (n = 16), completed semi-structured interviews using a phenomenological qualitative approach. The interview guide was developed using a constant comparative approach, and the data were analyzed using thematic analysis. Qualitative findings identified four primary influences on engagement in screening: knowledge and awareness of anal cancer risk; physical and emotional comfort and safety during procedures; the quality of patient-provider relationships; and the role of community norms and support. The findings articulate the importance of individual, interpersonal, and structural factors in the decision-making process for transgender women in anal cancer screening and HRA procedures. These insights underscore the need for culturally responsive, community-informed strategies to improve anal cancer prevention and care for transgender women and other marginalized populations.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Quality indicators (QIs) are central to safe delivery of cytoreductive surgery with hyperthermic intraperitoneal chemotherapy (CRS-HIPEC), yet program-level benchmarking across tumor types is scarce. To describe the structure, process, and outcome QIs of a single-center CRS-HIPEC program (2014-2024) and to assess temporal trends in cytoreduction completeness, early mortality, length of stay (LOS), renal safety, and multidisciplinary team (MDT) integration against contemporary international benchmarks. A retrospective cohort study of consecutive CRS-HIPEC procedures (2014-2024) was conducted at a Polish tertiary center. Prespecified QIs included complete or near-complete cytoreduction (CC-0/1), 30- and 90-day mortality, LOS, LOS > 10 days, unplanned reoperation, 30-day readmission, MDT uptake, and acute kidney injury (AKI; defined using Kidney Disease: Improving Global Outcomes (KDIGO) serum creatinine criteria). Time trends were displayed with Shewhart charts and funnel plots; Wilson's 95% confidence intervals (95% CIs) were used for proportions. Among 319 procedures (colorectal cancer (CRC) 111; ovarian cancer 87; mesothelioma/other 57; low-grade appendiceal mucinous neoplasm/pseudomyxoma peritonei (LAMN/PMP) 52; gastric cancer 12), the CC-0/1 rate was 93.4% overall (CRC 96.4%; LAMN/PMP 100%; ovarian cancer 90.8%; gastric cancer 91.7%; mesothelioma/other 86.0%). Thirtyand 90-day mortality were 0.6% and 1.6%, respectively; tumor-specific 30-day mortality ranged from 0% to 1.9%. Median LOS fell from 8.6 to 7.4 days (2014-2018 vs 2019-2024), and LOS > 10 days declined from 25.0% to 13.2%. Peritoneal cancer index (PCI) correlated weakly with LOS (Spearman's ρ = 0.13, p = 0.019), while AKI occurred in 70/308 (22.7%, 95% CI: 18.4-27.7), predominantly stage 1; AKI did not differ by cisplatin exposure (26.0% vs 21.2%, p = 0.389). The proportion of procedures with documented MDT discussion increased to approx. 20-33% after 2018. Over 11 years, a single-center CRS-HIPEC program achieved high-quality cytoreduction with low early mortality and a reduction in LOS, meeting or exceeding contemporary QI standards. Incorporating AKI and MDT uptake into routine audit supports comprehensive, program-level benchmarking.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Translesion synthesis (TLS) promotes DNA damage tolerance and contributes to chemotherapy resistance by enabling replication across damaged DNA templates. REV1, a central TLS regulator, is a potential therapeutic target to enhance the efficacy of genotoxic chemotherapy. Here, we investigated the therapeutic consequences of pharmacologic and genetic REV1 targeting in colorectal cancer (CRC) and evaluated the sensitivity of patient-derived CRC organoids to the REV1 inhibitor JH-RE-06. JH-RE-06 enhanced oxaliplatin sensitivity in HCT116 cells and 5-fluorouracil (5-FU) sensitivity in HT-29 cells, whereas reciprocal combinations produced limited sensitization, indicating treatment-and cellular context-dependent responses. siRNA-mediated REV1 depletion similarly enhanced chemotherapy sensitivity, supporting REV1 involvement in these responses. MNNG sensitivity assays and MLH1 expression analyses did not reveal consistent treatment-associated changes in mismatch repair function, while targeted HPRT1 sequencing identified no detectable sequence alterations in the region examined. Chemosensitization was not accompanied by consistent increases in caspase-3/7 activation under the conditions tested. REV1 inhibition also caused LC3-II accumulation and, after prolonged inhibitor exposure, reduced β-tubulin abundance, indicating additional autophagy-associated and cytoskeletal responses. In two patient-derived CRC organoid models, JH-RE-06 exhibited single-agent growth-inhibitory activity, with mean IC50 values of 2.01 and 1.4 µM, respectively. Together, these findings demonstrate context-dependent chemosensitization and organoid growth inhibition following REV1 targeting, suggesting that its therapeutic consequences may extend beyond canonical TLS-mediated DNA damage tolerance. Targeting REV1 enhances sensitivity to specific chemotherapeutic agents in colorectal cancer cells and inhibits growth of patient-derived colorectal cancer organoids. REV1 inhibition is also accompanied by LC3-II accumulation and reduced β-tubulin abundance, revealing cellular responses beyond conventional measures of DNA damage and mutagenesis. These findings identify treatment-dependent therapeutic vulnerabilities and suggest that the consequences of REV1 targeting may extend beyond its established role in translesion synthesis, supporting further investigation of REV1-directed therapeutic strategies in colorectal cancer. Chemotherapy resistance remains a major obstacle to effective treatment of colorectal cancer (CRC). This study identifies REV1 as a potential therapeutic target, showing that pharmacologic and genetic REV1 targeting enhances oxaliplatin sensitivity in HCT116 cells and 5-fluorouracil (5-FU) sensitivity in HT-29 cells, while reciprocal combinations show limited additional sensitization. Furthermore, patient-derived CRC organoids demonstrate single-agent sensitivity to REV1 inhibition at low-micromolar concentrations, supporting its activity across distinct tumor-derived models. REV1 inhibition is also associated with LC3-II accumulation and reduced β-tubulin abundance, suggesting additional cellular responses that may influence therapeutic outcomes. Together, these findings provide a preclinical rationale for investigating REV1-directed therapies in CRC and underscore the importance of identifying tumor-specific determinants of chemotherapy response and sensitivity to REV1 inhibition.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
People living with human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) are increasingly surviving into older age due to the effectiveness of antiretroviral (ARV) therapy (ART), creating a growing population in whom age-related changes may influence treatment outcomes. Although aging is known to affect drug disposition, the molecular mechanisms by which aging alters ARV pharmacology remain incompletely understood, particularly within tissue compartments, including the rectosigmoid region of the colon, that serve as sites of HIV transmission and persistence. To address this knowledge gap, we used proteomics by liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry (LC-MS) to evaluate the impact of age and HIV status on proteins and pathways relevant to ARV disposition in peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMC) and rectosigmoid colon tissue obtained from young (18-50) HIV-seronegative adults, older (65-80) HIV-seronegative adults, and older virally suppressed people living with HIV. We found that aging and HIV infection differentially influenced proteins predominantly within nucleos(t)ide reverse transcriptase inhibitor (NRTI) pathways, in rectosigmoid tissue and PBMC. HIV- associated effects to the proteome were more prominent in PBMC, whereas aging produced broader alterations in ARV disposition-related proteins in rectosigmoid tissue, including proteins involved in drug transport, intracellular drug activation, dephosphorylation, and nucleotide homeostasis. Several age-associated changes were further influenced by biologic sex, suggesting that aging may not affect ARV disposition uniformly across populations. To place these findings within a broader context, pathway analyses were performed that identified extensive tissue-specific remodeling associated with aging and HIV infection involving drug disposition, immune regulation, cellular metabolism, and disease-related pathways. Notably, aging was associated with alterations in pathways relevant to nucleotide metabolism and gastrointestinal tissue function, suggesting that processes beyond traditional drug transport and metabolism pathways may contribute to variability in ARV disposition with advancing age. Together, these findings identify aging as an important modifier of pathways that regulate ARV disposition within compartments relevant to HIV transmission and persistence. While the clinical consequences of our findings are unknown, these data provide a mechanistic foundation for future studies investigating whether age-associated changes influence the effectiveness of ART and HIV pre-exposure prophylaxis in older adults. Adults over 50 years of age comprise a rapidly growing proportion of both HIV treatment and prevention populations, yet the biological effects of aging on antiretroviral drug disposition remain poorly understood. We demonstrate that aging, sex, and HIV status differentially alter proteins and pathways involved in antiretroviral transport, activation, and nucleotide homeostasis, with the most pronounced effects occurring in colorectal tissue, providing a mechanistic foundation for future studies of HIV therapeutics in aging populations.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Spatial transcriptomics (ST) is increasingly used to map clonal architecture within tumors, yet methods for analyzing cancer ST data are difficult to evaluate because real tumors lack ground truth for copy-number alterations (CNAs), subclonal identity, and malignant cell fraction. Existing ST simulators model normal tissue and do not represent tumor evolution, CNA-driven expression, or the spatial organization of malignant subclones. We present OncoSpot, a cancer-aware simulator of Visium-like spot-based ST data. OncoSpot combines a spatial evolutionary scaffold from DEMON, CNAs generated along the resulting clonal phylogeny with CNAsim, cancer-type-specific malignant transcriptional programs, and spatially clustered nonmalignant cell types, and aggregates cells into spots with known malignant fraction, subclone, and copy-number profiles. We demonstrate OncoSpot on high-grade serous ovarian carcinoma, colorectal cancer, and hepatocellular carcinoma, which represent three distinct modes of tumor evolution. Simulated subclones were spatially clustered and showed stronger phylogeny-space concordance than those generated by scCube under matched subclone populations. Benchmarking CopyKAT, CancerFinder, Clonalscope, and RCTD revealed cancer-dependent performance: Clonalscope recovered copy-number signals more accurately in ovarian and colorectal cancer, whereas CopyKAT performed better in hepatocellular carcinoma, reflecting both the assumptions of each method and the copy-number landscapes of the three cancers. OncoSpot's ground truth also exposed a failure mode in Clonalscope's malignant spot identification, in which tumor and normal labels were inverted, and allowed us to trace its cause. These method-dependent behaviors would be difficult to detect in real data. OncoSpot provides a framework for benchmarking CNA inference, subclone detection, malignant spot identification, and normal spot deconvolution, and its modular design and guidelines allow extension to additional cancer types. OncoSpot is freely available at https://github.com/compbio-mallory/OncoSpot .

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Enhanced Recovery After Surgery (ERAS) pathways have transformed perioperative care in elective colorectal surgery, but the clinical value of individual anesthetic interventions remains uneven. This state-of-the-art narrative review integrates current evidence across seven domains: general anesthetic technique and depth, opioid-sparing and regional analgesia, neuromuscular blockade and reversal, intraoperative fluid and hemodynamic management, lung-protective ventilation and oxygenation, prevention of postoperative nausea and vomiting, and perioperative temperature management. Recent colorectal-specific randomized trials, evidence syntheses, and current guidelines were prioritized. The evidence supports multimodal opioid-sparing analgesia, quantitative neuromuscular monitoring with complete reversal, avoidance of both fluid overload and clinically relevant hypovolemia, lung-protective ventilation with individualized oxygen administration, risk-adapted multimodal antiemetic prophylaxis, and active maintenance of normothermia. By contrast, clinically meaningful superiority is not consistently established for a single general anesthetic technique, universal opioid-free anesthesia, deep neuromuscular blockade as a recovery strategy, routine goal-directed hemodynamic therapy in all patients, routine recruitment maneuvers, or fixed oxygen and temperature targets. The central clinical implication is that ERAS should standardize recovery goals rather than mandate identical anesthetic techniques. Anesthetic plans should therefore be individualized according to patient vulnerability, surgical approach, and perioperative risk, while future trials should prioritize standardized patient-centered recovery outcomes over isolated physiological surrogates.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
The effective absorption of oral chemotherapy drugs in the intestines is of vital importance for enhancing their therapeutic effects. Natural plant-derived compounds, in specific, their diversities in type, structure, and function, might offer opportunities to modulate gut microbiota metabolites for enhancing colorectal cancer therapy. Guided by this thinking, synergistic self-assembly of natural products, namely Xyl-CA/Sin nanoparticles (NPs), was engineered by integrating the prebiotic xylan (Xyl) with chlorogenic acid (CA) and sinomenine (Sin). Xyl protects the formulation during gastric transit and promotes targeted accumulation in colorectal tumors. Upon exposure to the acidic tumor microenvironment (TME), the NPs release CA and Sin, enabling their therapeutic actions. In colorectal cancer (CRC) models, CA triggers tumor cell pyroptosis, while Sin reshapes macrophage polarization and elevates the microbial tryptophan metabolite indole-3-acetic acid (3-IAA). Acting synergistically, 3-IAA and CA suppress glutathione peroxidase 3 (GPx3) and glutathione peroxidase 7 (GPx7), leading to reactive oxygen species (ROS) accumulation and autophagy inhibition. This cascade restrains tumor growth, induces immunogenic cell death (ICD), and stimulates antitumor immunity. Overall, this study presents a microbiota metabolite-driven strategy through the application of natural plant-derived bioactive compounds to potentiate chemotherapy and establishes a concise, multimodal framework for antitumor therapy based on natural products.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
DNA mismatch repair (MMR) immunohistochemistry (IHC) is widely used for Lynch syndrome screening and selection of patients for immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI) therapy. Standardized companion diagnostic (CDx) testing and interpretation frameworks support consistent patient classification. We evaluated routine clinical-record MMR IHC results against the Food and Drug Administration-approved CDx, VENTANA MMR RxDx Panel (Roche Diagnostics), and examined focal staining and reduced-protein testing strategies. This retrospective multicentre study included 1443 resection specimens from five hospitals in China: colorectal carcinoma (CRC; n = 402), endometrial carcinoma (EC; n = 413), gastric carcinoma (GC; n = 367) and other solid tumours (n = 261). Concordance between historical clinical-record MMR status and the CDx classification varied by tumour type. The highest agreement was observed in CRC and GC, whereas EC and the heterogeneous other-tumour subgroup showed the lowest positive per cent agreement (95.81%) and the lowest negative per cent agreement (92.98%), respectively. Third-panel assessment of 34 discordant cases supported the VENTANA classification in 31 cases, while the three remaining cases were unresolved without orthogonal molecular testing. Subclonal loss was identified in 74 of 525 dMMR cases (14.1%; most in MSH6 and MLH1), highlighting interpretative complexity beyond a binary framework. Reduced two-protein testing, although operationally attractive, may miss clinically meaningful dMMR cases: the best-performing PMS2/MSH6 combination was estimated to miss 33 dMMR cases when assessed against the VENTANA four-protein classification. These findings support full-panel MMR assessment and adherence to CDx-specific interpretation guidance to improve confidence in patient selection for ICI therapy.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Glyceraldehyde-3-phosphate dehydrogenase (GAPDH) is a multifunctional protein that participates in cancer metabolism, apoptosis, DNA repair, angiogenesis, and immune regulation beyond its canonical glycolytic role. However, how distinct post-translational modifications (PTMs) coordinate GAPDH functional transitions and determine its diverse biological roles in cancer remains incompletely understood. In this review, we summarize current advances in GAPDH PTMs, including methylation, phosphorylation, acetylation, ubiquitination, S-nitrosylation, serotonylation, crotonylation, lactylation, and succinylation, with emphasis on modification sites, regulatory enzymes, cellular contexts, and functional consequences. We propose a PTM-driven molecular switching model in which different cellular stimuli induce specific GAPDH modifications to regulate its enzymatic activity, subcellular localization, and protein interactions. Representative mechanisms include Src-mediated Tyr41 phosphorylation promoting DNA repair and 5-fluorouracil resistance in colorectal cancer, K254 and K160 acetylation regulating glycolytic activity and apoptosis through distinct cellular contexts, Parkin-mediated ubiquitination controlling mitophagy and metabolic reprogramming, and Gln262 serotonylation enhancing CD8

The progression of ulcerative colitis (UC) to colorectal cancer (CRC) represents a major clinical challenge. Glucocorticoids (GCs) are widely used for the treatment of UC and also are included in therapeutic regimens for CRC. The transcriptional mechanisms through which GCs regulate inflammation and tumourigenesis via the glucocorticoid receptor (GR) remain incompletely understood. GR Impaired GR dimerisation attenuated colon inflammation, as reflected by improved epithelial barrier integrity and reduced expression of pro-inflammatory genes. Tumourigenesis followed a biphasic pattern, with delayed tumour onset but accelerated tumour growth at later stages. Transcriptomic analyses revealed a distinct inflammatory signature in GR GR dimerisation differentially contributes to the anti-inflammatory and tumour-related GC effects, thereby uncoupling the control of colitis from the regulation of tumour progression, highlighting potential limitations of selectively targeting GR monomer activity in therapeutic regimens.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Whether local availability of cancer-operating surgeons is independently associated with population cancer outcomes beyond deprivation and rurality remains unclear. We evaluated gastrointestinal/hepatopancreatobiliary (GI/HPB) cancer outcomes in U.S. counties with and without local surgical access. This cross-sectional ecological study linked the 2025 CMS Doctors and Clinicians file with NCI/CDC State Cancer Profiles, Area Deprivation Index, 2023 Rural-Urban Continuum Codes, and 2020 Census populations across all 3,144 U.S. counties (331 million residents). A GI/HPB surgical desert was defined as no in-county general surgeon, surgical oncologist, or colorectal surgeon. The primary outcome was age-adjusted colorectal cancer mortality. Population-weighted linear models adjusted for deprivation, rurality, region, and incidence. Overall, 1,430 counties (45%), encompassing 26.6 million residents, were surgical deserts; 13.5 million affected residents lived in metropolitan counties. Colorectal cancer mortality was 3.65 per 100,000 higher in deserts before adjustment and remained 0.75 per 100,000 higher after adjustment (95% CI, 0.45-1.04; P<.001). Adjusted excess mortality was also observed for pancreatic (0.47) and hepatobiliary (0.37) cancers; the pooled five-site excess was 0.58 per 100,000 (95% CI, 0.44-0.71). Among surgeon-present counties, surgeon density was not associated with mortality (0.004 per surgeon per 100,000; 95% CI, -0.012 to 0.021; P=.61). Deserts also had higher case fatality for colorectal, pancreatic, and hepatobiliary cancers and later-stage diagnosis for HPB/upper-GI cancers, but not colorectal cancer. GI/HPB surgical deserts were independently associated with higher cancer mortality. The absence of local surgical access, rather than surgeon density once present, may identify a systems-level target for regional cancer-care planning.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
To evaluate the effects of a resident-nurse collaborative discharge education program on quality of discharge teaching, readiness for hospital discharge, stoma self-efficacy, stoma-specific quality of life, complications, unplanned readmission, and length of hospital stay among colorectal cancer patients with stomas. The intervention comprised a five-stage collaborative education protocol (joint assessment, resident-led cognitive teaching, nurse-led skills training, joint pre-discharge teach-back, and reinforced remote follow-up). All 120 participants (100%) completed the trial. The intervention group demonstrated significantly higher Quality of Discharge Teaching Scale (QDTS) total scores (median 147.0 vs. 100.0, p < 0.001), readiness for hospital discharge (84.17 ± 8.66 vs. 68.68 ± 7.65, p < 0.001), stoma self-efficacy (T3: 87.76 ± 1.07 vs. 75.25 ± 0.68, p < 0.001), and stoma quality of life (T3: 58.27 ± 0.55 vs. 52.04 ± 0.36, p < 0.001). Complication rates at T3 were 1.7% vs. 21.7% (p < 0.001), and unplanned readmission at T3 was 1.67% vs. 10.00% (p = 0.045). No significant difference was found in length of hospital stay (p = 0.538). A resident-nurse collaborative discharge education model substantially improved transitional outcomes for colorectal cancer stoma patients, enhancing cognitive understanding, self-efficacy, and quality of life while reducing complications and readmissions, without extending hospital stay.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Liver-synchronous colorectal cancer (CRC) metastases occur in 15-25% of patients with colorectal cancer. Curative intent typically combines systemic chemotherapy with complete resection of both the primary tumor and liver lesions. Minimally invasive liver surgery has been associated with reduced morbidity, but evidence on simultaneous robotic resection of CRC primary tumors and synchronous liver metastases remains limited. Here, we report our institutional experience with simultaneous robotic resections using a standardized operative setup and coordinated colorectal and hepatobiliary surgical teams. Data from consecutive patients undergoing robotic simultaneous resection for CRC liver metastases (Jan 2023-Dec 2025) were prospectively collected and retrospectively analyzed. The study descriptively assessed the feasibility of a standardized double docking approach. Perioperative, 90-day postoperative, pathological and early oncological outcomes were recorded. In the study period, 158 patients underwent liver resections; simultaneous robotic resections for CRC liver metastasis were completed in 18 patients. The median patient age was 66 years (interquartile range (IQR) 53-73). Most patients received oxaliplatin-based neoadjuvant chemotherapy, achieving partial response in the majority. Robotic surgery was performed without intraoperative complications or conversions. Median operative duration was 519 (IQR 420-627) minutes, with a median liver transection time of 50 (IQR 30-75) minutes and median total docking time of 13 (IQR 10-15) minutes. Median estimated blood loss was 175 (IQR 100-362.5) mL and no intraoperative transfusions were required. Postoperatively, complications occurred in 8 patients, with 4 (22.2%) experiencing severe complications (Clavien-Dindo > 2). No 90-day mortality occurred. The median length of stay was 8 days (IQR 5.7-14.2). No R1 resection occurred for the primary tumor. R1 liver resection occurred in 16.7% of patients: all cases were R1 vascular. At a median follow-up of 2 years no death occurred, the median disease free survival (DFS) was 22 months (IQR 7-30). Out of 3 patients with R1 vascular liver resection, one experienced a lung and liver recurrence, the other two were disease free. This study showed that standardized simultaneous robotic resection for synchronous CRC liver metastases was feasible in experienced robotic centers. Despite several limitations, perioperative and oncological outcomes may be considered in line with the reported liver surgery literature. Larger multicenter studies are needed to confirm potential advantages and refine patient selection criteria.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Large-scale safety data for newly introduced bevacizumab biosimilars in routine oncology practice remain limited. As part of post-marketing safety evaluations under the Risk Management Plan in Japan, we evaluated the risk of venous thromboembolism (VTE) associated with a bevacizumab biosimilar (CTNK) and compared the findings with those for a reference biologic (Avastin®) in Japanese patients with cancer. In this retrospective cohort study using a large-scale hospital-based claims database (Medical Data Vision) in Japan, we identified new users of bevacizumab diagnosed with colorectal, breast, or ovarian cancer or glioblastoma between November 2020 and February 2025. Patients were classified into the biosimilar group or the reference biologic group. The primary outcome was the incidence of VTE, evaluated using a multivariable Cox proportional hazards model. Exploratory safety outcomes, including bleeding/hemorrhage and infections, were also assessed. A total of 8599 eligible patients (1967 in the biosimilar group and 6632 in the reference biologic group; male versus female patients, 45.60% and 41.74% versus 54.40% and 58.26%, respectively; median age, 69.0 years in both groups) were included in the primary analysis. The overall incidence of VTE was 2.36%. The adjusted hazard ratio for VTE in the biosimilar group compared with that in the reference biologic group was 0.82 (95% confidence interval, 0.57-1.19; P = 0.30), indicating no significant difference. This finding was consistent across subgroups stratified by target cancer type or by VTE history. Furthermore, the incidence of exploratory safety events was comparable between the two treatment groups. This retrospective cohort study showed no evidence of increased VTE risk with the bevacizumab biosimilar or major safety differences between the bevacizumab biosimilar and the reference biologic in Japanese patients with cancer, providing reassuring real-world evidence supporting the safe use of the bevacizumab biosimilar in routine clinical practice. Graphical abstract available for this article. Japan Registry of Clinical Trials identifier, jRCT2031250738, retrospectively registered on February 13, 2026.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Laparoscopic surgery relies on stable camera navigation, while shortages of surgeons and assistants have increased the need for multidisciplinary approaches to surgical support. In Japan, clinical engineers (CEs) can perform camera operation during endoscopic surgery after completing a training program designated by the Minister of Health, Labour, and Welfare. We retrospectively evaluated perioperative outcomes of laparoscopic colorectal cancer surgery with CE-assisted versus surgeon-assisted camera operation. We retrospectively reviewed 59 patients who underwent laparoscopic colorectal cancer surgery at a single institution between February 2024 and September 2025. Camera operation was performed by surgeons in 23 patients and by CEs in 36 patients. Operative time, blood loss, postoperative complications, and postoperative hospital stay were compared between the groups. Camera operator assignment was not randomized and depended on operating room staffing and CE availability. No significant differences were detected between the surgeon-assisted and CE-assisted groups in operative time, blood loss, postoperative complications, or postoperative hospital stay. In the CE-assisted group, camera operation was performed by CEs who had completed the designated training program, with real-time verbal instruction from the operating surgeon during surgery. In this single-center retrospective cohort, no significant differences in perioperative outcomes were detected between CE-assisted and surgeon-assisted camera operation. These findings support the feasibility of CE participation in laparoscopic camera operation under appropriate training and intraoperative supervision. However, the limited sample size does not permit definitive conclusions regarding safety or equivalence.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Precision oncology has profoundly transformed the management of digestive malignancies, making predictive biomarker testing an integral component of routine pathology practice. Beyond identifying actionable molecular alterations, pathologists now face the challenge of selecting appropriate testing strategies, preserving limited tissue, ensuring analytical quality and integrating increasingly complex biomarker data into multidisciplinary therapeutic decision-making. This review provides a practical overview of clinically actionable biomarker testing across digestive cancers, focusing on current testing strategies, methodological challenges and tumour-specific applications. We discuss the complementary roles of immunohistochemistry, in situ hybridisation and molecular techniques, together with practical aspects of tissue stewardship, pre-analytical optimisation, tumour heterogeneity and biomarker re-testing. Particular emphasis is placed on integrating predictive biomarkers into routine diagnostic workflows while maintaining analytical robustness and clinical relevance. Current biomarker requirements are reviewed across the major digestive tumour types, including upper gastrointestinal, colorectal, small bowel, hepatocellular, biliary and pancreatic cancer, as well as gastrointestinal stromal tumours, highlighting both organ-specific biomarkers and emerging tumour-agnostic approaches. The review also addresses contemporary frameworks for clinical actionability, multidisciplinary interpretation of molecular findings and future developments, including comprehensive genomic profiling, liquid biopsy, digital pathology and artificial intelligence. By integrating methodological principles with tumour-specific applications, this review highlights the central role of the pathologist in delivering high-quality precision oncology and provides practical guidance for implementing predictive biomarker testing in routine clinical practice.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Circulating exosomal miR-21 has been investigated as a potential biomarker for colorectal cancer (CRC), but its low abundance poses challenges for highly sensitive detection. We report a signal-on, label-free electrochemical biosensor that integrates target-initiated duplex-specific nuclease (DSN)-assisted cyclic cleavage, Cas12a/crRNA trans-cleavage, Cu-doped Zr-UiO-66 (Cu/Zr-MOF) nanozyme catalysis, and DNA tetrahedron-based interfacial engineering for exosomal miR-21 detection. miR-21 triggers the DSN-Cas12a cascade, in which activated Cas12a cleaves 5'-hydroxyl single-stranded extensions from electrode-bound DNA tetrahedra, generating short 5'-phosphate strands. These strands bind Cu/Zr-MOF via Zr-O-P coordination, and the intrinsic nanozyme activity of Cu/Zr-MOF catalyzes TMB oxidation to produce electrochemical signals. Under optimized conditions, the biosensor shows a linear range of 50 aM-10 pM and a detection limit of 4.7 aM, with excellent selectivity against mismatched sequences and interfering miRNAs. It also distinguishes CRC patients from healthy controls, consistent with RT-qPCR. This strategy provides a robust signal-on and label-free approach for highly sensitive detection of circulating exosomal miR-21 in CRC patients, demonstrating its potential for liquid biopsy applications.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Systemic malignancies may influence cerebral metabolism without direct intracranial involvement, but whether different tumor types are associated with distinct regional and network-level patterns remains uncertain. This retrospective study included 342 patients (219 men and 123 women) with colorectal, esophageal, gastric, or lung cancer, or lymphoma, who underwent Analysis of variance identified regional differences among tumor groups, and several Tukey-adjusted pairwise comparisons were significant. Age and sex showed broader associations than surgery or treatment. Global metabolic patterns substantially overlapped across tumor types, without clear separation. Covariance networks differed in topology and hub distribution. In the full cancer cohort, lung cancer had sparse connectivity and the greatest number of hub regions, whereas esophageal cancer showed high local clustering without hubs. The no-intervention tumor groups and nontumor controls also showed different network topology and hub distributions. Brain metabolic covariance network analysis provides information on interregional metabolic organization alongside regional SUVR comparisons and global metabolic pattern analysis. The network findings require further validation.

意义与启示：该研究建立人源化转基因猪代谢病模型，揭示代谢应激下结肠屏障、免疫、线粒体自噬及菌群代谢协同改变，为肠癌及肝转移的代谢-菌群机制研究提供大动物平台。

展开英文原题摘要与原文链接
ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Metabolic disorders are increasingly associated with intestinal dysfunction and colorectal diseases, yet the pathological characteristics and underlying mechanisms of intestinal injury under metabolic stress remain poorly understood. Here, we established a transgenic (TG) Bama pig model by CRISPR/Cas9-mediated knock-in of three humanized susceptibility genes and subjected the pigs to a high-fat, high-sugar diet (HFHSD) for 4, 8, or 12 months to investigate metabolic disorder-associated colonic dysfunction. HFHSD intervention induced marked alterations in serum biochemical parameters and disrupted colonic mucosal architecture, characterized by glandular disorganization and crypt distortion. Colonic tissues from TG pigs exhibited reduced populations of goblet cells, CD8⁺ T cells, and CD79A⁺ B cells, accompanied by pronounced activation of mitophagy, indicating impaired epithelial barrier integrity and mucosal immune homeostasis. In parallel, microbial diversity and IgA levels were reduced in the colonic contents of TG pigs, accompanied by an increased abundance of potentially pathogenic bacteria, particularly Escherichia-Shigella. Metabolomic profiling of colonic contents further revealed significant alterations in the intestinal metabolic landscape, including decreased levels of isobutyric acid and isovaleric acid and an increased level of myristic acid, a metabolite associated with autophagy-related processes. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that metabolic disorders are associated with coordinated alterations in colonic mucosal integrity, mucosal immunity, mitochondrial quality control, gut microbiota, and intestinal metabolism. The humanized TG Bama pig model provides a clinically relevant large-animal platform for investigating the pathophysiology of metabolic disorder-associated colonic diseases and may facilitate the development and preclinical evaluation of therapeutic strategies targeting intestinal dysfunction.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
As many genetic conditions present with cutaneous features, the dermatologist plays a pivotal role in identifying skin lesions that are suggestive of systemic conditions, predisposing patients to the development of internal malignancies and other potentially morbid systemic conditions later in life. An example is the Birt-Hogg-Dubé syndrome, which can present with primarily upper body cutaneous lesions and where patients have a higher risk of pneumothorax and renal cell carcinoma. Such patients with Muir-Torre syndrome can present with characteristic sebaceous neoplasms and have an increased risk of colon and genitourinary tract cancers. Individuals with Cowden syndrome present with cutaneous lesions and can develop malignancies of the colon, breast, and thyroid at higher rates than does the general population. This is exemplified by Gardner syndrome in which patients can develop mucocutaneous osteomas and epidermal cysts and where they are almost 100% susceptible to the future development of colon cancer at an early age. Dermatologists are responsible for becoming knowledgeable of these disease entities to facilitate timely diagnosis and the initiation of cancer screening protocols to reduce overall morbidity and mortality.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Recurrence remains a major cause of morbidity and mortality after curative-intent treatment of stage II-III colorectal cancer (CRC), including among patients receiving adjuvant chemotherapy. Recent randomized trials demonstrate that aspirin and structured exercise can further reduce recurrence risk and improve patient outcomes. Two phase 3 randomized trials provide evidence for extending adjuvant strategies beyond cytotoxic chemotherapy in CRC. In ALASCCA, 3 years of low-dose aspirin reduced recurrence by approximately 50% among patients with resected colon or rectal cancer harboring PI3K-pathway alterations, establishing a biomarker-guided approach to adjuvant aspirin therapy. In CHALLENGE, a 3-year structured exercise program initiated after adjuvant chemotherapy improved disease-free and overall survival in patients with resected stage II or III colon cancer. Mechanistically, aspirin may exert antitumor effects through inhibition of cyclooxygenase and prostaglandin signaling, platelet-tumor interactions, and PI3K-related pathways, whereas exercise may act through metabolic signaling, systemic inflammation, and antitumor immunity. Despite distinct anti-tumor mechanisms, both interventions may converge on inflammation, the tumor microenvironment, and immune surveillance. ALASCCA and CHALLENGE trials provide randomized evidence supporting biomarker-directed aspirin and structured exercise as additional adjuvant strategies in patients with CRC. These study findings support testing for somatic PI3K-pathway alterations to identify patients who may benefit from adjuvant aspirin, and support incorporation of structured exercise into survivorship care after CRC resection. Their distinct mechanisms, and potentially complementary biological effects also provide a rationale for evaluating aspirin and exercise in combination.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Oxaliplatin proves ineffective in the treatment of colorectal cancer (CRC) due to the acquired drug resistance during the treatment period. Combination therapy represents an effective strategy in the treatment of cancer, including CRC, which can effectively overcome drug resistance and reduce side effects. Herein, this study aims to clarify the role and mechanism of ropivacaine in improving the sensitivity of CRC to oxaliplatin. The combination of ropivacaine and oxaliplatin exhibited significantly enhanced cytotoxicity, apoptosis, generated a considerable amount of reactive oxygen species (ROS) and caused a loss of mitochondrial membrane potential (MMP) through the mitochondrial-dependent apoptosis pathway and endoplasmic reticulum stress both in HCT-116 cells and HCT-116/OXA cells. Moreover, the combination of ropivacaine and oxaliplatin effectively suppressed the expression of SLC7A11, Nrf2, GPX4, p62 and LC3BII in HCT-116 cells and HCT-116/OXA cells, suggesting that it can trigger cell death by inducing ferroptosis and autophagy. Interestingly, in xenograft model of HCT-116/OXA, the combination of oxaliplatin and ropivacaine enhances antitumor efficacy while reducing the toxicity of oxaliplatin. Our preliminary results demonstrated that the combination of oxaliplatin and ropivacaine represents a potential therapeutic strategy for overcoming oxaliplatin resistance in CRC.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Peritoneal carcinomatosis (PC) is a frequent pattern of tumor dissemination across multiple malignancies, including colorectal, gastric, ovarian, and pancreatic cancers, and is associated with poor prognosis and limited survival. Although cytoreductive surgery (CRS) with or without hyperthermic intraperitoneal chemotherapy (HIPEC) has improved outcomes in selected patients, its indication remains restricted, leaving a substantial proportion of patients without curative options, and recurrence rates remain high even after treatment. Therefore, the development of novel therapeutic strategies is urgently needed. Chimeric antigen receptor T (CAR-T) cell therapy has emerged as a promising approach, achieving remarkable success in hematological malignancies and gaining increasing attention in solid tumors. Several tumor-associated antigens, including CEA, CLDN18.2, GUCY2C, EpCAM, and mesothelin, have been investigated across different tumor types, showing encouraging preclinical and early clinical results. In particular, similar to HIPEC, regional delivery strategies such as intraperitoneal administration may enhance tumor targeting, improve cell trafficking, and increase therapeutic efficacy in peritoneal disease. However, CAR-T cell therapy in PC faces important challenges inherent to solid tumors, including antigen heterogeneity, limited tumor trafficking and infiltration, and a hostile tumor microenvironment characterized by dense stromal barriers and immunosuppressive conditions, which ultimately limit its efficacy. Overcoming these barriers is essential to optimize therapeutic outcomes. This review summarizes the current evidence on CAR-T cell therapy in major solid tumors associated with PC, highlighting key targets, administration strategies, and clinical outcomes, while addressing the main limitations and emerging strategies to improve its clinical application, as well as future perspectives for its integration into multimodal treatment approaches.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Mucinous colorectal adenocarcinoma (MAC) accounts for approximately 10% of all colorectal cancers and is defined by the presence of extracellular mucin in more than 50% of the tumour volume. The prognosis of MAC compared with non-mucinous colorectal adenocarcinoma remains debated, with reported outcomes influenced by tumour stage, location and molecular characteristics. MAC is frequently diagnosed at a more advanced stage, exhibits increased lymph node involvement and a greater tendency towards peritoneal metastases, and has been associated with reduced response to neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy, particularly in rectal cancer. Moreover, mucinous differentiation is associated with distinct clinicopathological, molecular and epigenetic features, including higher frequencies of microsatellite instability (MSI), CpG island methylator phenotype (CIMP) and BRAF mutations. Nevertheless, current clinical guidelines do not provide separate treatment recommendations for this histological subtype, and management remains guided by disease stage, resectability and established molecular biomarkers. In this review, we explore the current literature to summarise the epidemiology and prognosis, distinct clinicopathological features, molecular characteristics, diagnostic techniques and management of MAC, including recent advances in surgical treatment, targeted molecular therapy and immunotherapy. As our understanding of the molecular biology of mucinous colorectal adenocarcinoma continues to evolve, advances in molecular profiling may facilitate more precise risk stratification and the development of targeted and personalised treatment approaches.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
The development of phototherapeutics with tunable localization and controllable therapeutic mechanisms is critical for precision oncology but remains challenging. While indocyanine green (ICG) is a clinically approved near-infrared (NIR) dye for phototherapy, its intrinsic limitations, such as poor photostability, lack of organelle selectivity, and suboptimal phototherapeutic efficacy, have necessitated extensive efforts toward functional modification, yet effective molecular-level optimization remains limited. Herein, we report a novel carboxyl-number engineering strategy that regulates the subcellular distribution of P6-series photosensitizers from individual organelles (mitochondria/lysosomes) to broad multi-organelle networks. The optimal candidate, P6-3COOH, features a potent condition-dependent bimodal therapeutic mechanism. In the dark, it inherently orchestrates p53-associated apoptosis. Exposure to an 808 nm near-infrared laser triggers a multi-organelle-driven activation of cell death pathways, leading to tumor cell ablation primarily through efficient photothermal heating, while reactive oxygen species generation may serve as a secondary complementary mechanism that further contributes to the anticancer effect. In HCT116 xenograft mice, local tumor temperatures increased to ∼48 °C within 10 min under 808 nm irradiation. Furthermore, in vivo imaging and therapeutic studies demonstrate a favorable tumor-to-background fluorescence contrast, robust phototherapeutic efficacy (∼79.9% tumor growth inhibition), and favorable short-term tolerability. Collectively, this work provides a new molecular design strategy for spatiotemporal multi-organelle targeting and offers a valuable functional material platform for localized colorectal cancer phototherapy.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Surgical planning for colorectal liver metastasis (CRLM) is crucial for achieving curative resection. The advent of artificial intelligence and automatic image segmentation has made 3D holograms readily available for surgical planning. Conventional patient imaging can now be converted into interactive 3D models and displayed in augmented reality (AR). This multicentre, observational study evaluated the impact of 3D visualisation on surgical planning for CRLM. 46 surgeons from 21 liver surgery centres in nine countries assessed eight complex CRLM cases. Each case included CT portal venous phase images and a 3D hologram displayed in AR, created using an automatic segmentation tool and quality assessed by radiologists. Surgeons completed four surveys covering experience, initial CT-based management, post-3D review management, and perceived benefit. Among the participants (33 consultants, 13 residents), 24% worked in centres performing 50-100 resections per year, and 70% in centres performing over 100 per year. The 3D holograms changed resectability assessments in 20% of cases (8% from inoperable to operable; 12% from operable to inoperable). Management decisions between neoadjuvant therapy and surgery changed in 21% of cases, and 22% of surgeons modified their surgical approach. Most surgeons (96%) found the technology easy to use, valuing it for complex cases (61%), tumour board discussions (83%), and teaching (98%). 3D holographic imaging can influence CRLM management decisions. The technology is acceptable to liver surgeons with multiple potential clinical applications. Prospective, randomised studies are needed to evaluate its clinical implementation and impact on patient outcomes.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Bridge-to-surgery approaches relieve obstruction before elective resection, but most evidence concerns self-expanding metal stents and pools outcomes across stages. Diverting stoma is a relevant alternative where stenting is restricted, yet stage-specific DS-BTS versus ER comparisons remain limited. To evaluate the stage-specific comparative effectiveness of diverting stoma as a bridge to surgery (DS-BTS) versus emergency resection (ER) in obstructive colorectal cancer. We performed a nationwide target trial emulation using the linked Taiwan National Health Insurance Research Database and Cancer Registry (2016-2022; follow-up through 2023). The primary comparison was DS-BTS versus ER among patients with obstructive colorectal cancer undergoing primary tumor resection. The primary outcome was 90-day all-cause mortality. Inverse probability of treatment weighting was applied within each stage cohort, with propensity-score matching for sensitivity. Among 17,162 patients, the primary comparison included 1135 DS-BTS and 14,594 ER patients. Associations were stage- and endpoint-dependent. In stage IV, DS-BTS was associated with lower 90-day mortality than ER (weighted OR, 0.60; 95% CI, 0.39-0.94) without long-term benefit. In stage III, DS-BTS was associated with worse long-term mortality (3-year weighted HR, 1.30; overall weighted HR, 1.36). In stage I-II, 3-year mortality was higher (weighted HR, 1.33), while overall mortality did not differ significantly. DS-BTS showed stage-dependent, endpoint-specific associations in obstructive colorectal cancer, with a short-term survival benefit in stage IV, but worse long-term mortality in stage III. These findings argue against uniform bridge-to-surgery use and support selective, stage-specific management.

Aerobic exercise has been associated with better outcomes in colorectal cancer, but its effects on antitumor immunity within the tumor are unclear. We asked whether aerobic exercise altered the tumor microenvironment in a murine colorectal cancer model and whether CD8 Female BALB/c mice bearing subcutaneous CT26 tumors were randomized to sedentary control, sequential exercise, or concurrent exercise. Tumor growth, body weight, and survival were recorded. Tumors were analyzed by RNA sequencing, proteomics, qPCR, ELISA, and flow cytometry, and immune-cell composition was estimated from transcriptomic data. ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Background Colonoscopy surveillance for colorectal cancer (CRC) is invasive, burdensome and costly for patients with inflammatory bowel disease (IBD). Aim To reduce colonoscopy frequency, we assessed the potential of faecal volatile organic compounds (VOCs) as non-invasive biomarkers to detect colorectal dysplasia in IBD. Methods Exploratory study in which patients with IBD collected faeces in the three months before surveillance colonoscopy. Faecal VOCs were analysed using field asymmetric ion mobility spectrometry followed by machine learning pipelines. Mucosal remission was defined as Mayo 0-1 (ulcerative colitis), SES-CD 0-2 (Crohn's Disease) or Rutgeerts i0-i1 (postoperative Crohn's disease). Results Among 46 included patients (median 57 years, 54% male, 63% ulcerative colitis), 14 patients had dysplasia at colonoscopy, which was mostly low-grade and did not involve CRC. During mucosal remission (the ideal setting for surveillance), faecal VOCs detected colorectal dysplasia with 100% sensitivity at 50% specificity. Irrespective of mucosal activity - which would be unknown at the time of future faeces sampling - colorectal dysplasia was detected with 93% sensitivity at 38% specificity. Conclusions Faecal VOCs may have potential to detect (early stage) colorectal dysplasia in IBD. Our results serve as a stepping stone for large validation studies that also consider accuracy for advanced dysplasia, patient acceptability, and confounders - in an effort to reduce colonoscopy burden in IBD.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Without prophylactic colectomy, the lifetime colorectal cancer risk in familial adenomatous polyposis (FAP) patients approaches 100%. Even after surgery, adenomas frequently develop in the residual intestinal mucosa, underscoring the need for effective chemopreventive agents. Here, we evaluated the chemopreventive effect of lithium on adenoma initiation. This single-arm, phase II trial enrolled FAP patients aged 18-35 years without history of colectomy. In an 18-month protocol, participants received daily lithium carbonate for 6-12 months. Colonoscopies with biopsies of normal mucosa were conducted at baseline, 6, 12 and 18 months. The primary endpoint was the number of APC-deficient pre-malignant clones over time, assessed by tracing mutant clones via marker gene expression. Secondary endpoints included adenoma burden, safety and tolerability. Investigators were blinded during analyses. In total, 12 FAP patients underwent baseline colonoscopy, the full analysis set included 11 patients who received at least one study dose. Across all participants, no significant change in clone frequency was observed (χ2 = 5.09, df = 3, p=0.165). Moreover, no significant effect on adenoma burden was detected. Lithium was well tolerated, with only grade 1-2 adverse events, mostly gastrointestinal (nausea and diarrhoea: n=3, 27.27%). This is the first trial to trace and inhibit mutant clone expansion as efficacy endpoint by boosting normal tissue fitness, aimed at preventing adenoma formation. Although lithium had no effect on the expansion APC-deficient pre-malignant clones or adenoma burden after six months, aberrant clones were detected in histologically normal mucosa, demonstrating the feasibility of tracing early tumorigenesis in humans. Trial registration: ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT05402891).

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Retrospective studies and analyses of RCTs showed that surgical quality of mesorectal excision affects oncological outcomes of rectal cancer patients. Objective of this study was to determine the impact of mesorectal excision quality on local recurrence and overall survival in rectal cancer patients. MEDLINE was searched till April 1, 2024, with MeSH terms: rectal cancer/neoplasm, total mesorectal excision, TME, rectal cancer surgery, macroscopic assessment/evaluation, quality/adequacy/completeness of surgery/mesorectum/resection specimen, prognosis, and outcome for randomized clinical trials, prospective and retrospective cohort studies reporting oncological outcomes and quality of the mesorectal excision. The main outcome and measures were local recurrence and overall survival. TME quality was classified into three grading categories (complete or mesorectal resection (MRR); nearly complete or intramesorectal resection (IMR); incomplete or muscularis propria resection (MPR)). Of 438 records screened and an additional three studies by cross-referencing, 15 articles with 11,285 individual patients were identified. Median age of included patients was 63, 55 (range 21, 0-95, 0). Pooled incidence of good (MRR), intermediate (IMR), and insufficient (MPR) TME quality was 65, 6%, 22, 8%, and 11, 6%, respectively. Insufficient TME quality was associated with locally advanced tumors. No difference in TME quality was observed between patients with and without neoadjuvant therapy. Pooled analysis showed lower odds for LR and higher odds for OS in patients with good TME quality, which is also shown in a subgroup analysis of neoadjuvantly treated patients. In conclusion, this meta-analysis confirms that good TME quality is associated with lower risk for local recurrence and higher probability for overall survival, an association that persisted also in neoadjuvantly treated patients. These findings suggest that neoadjuvant therapy will not compensate for suboptimal surgical quality; however, given the substantial heterogeneity across the included studies and the limited availability of data on contemporary treatment regimens, they should be regarded as hypothesis-generating rather than definitive.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Colorectal cancer (CRC) screening is underutilized in underserved populations, contributing to racial, ethnic, and socioeconomic disparities in CRC incidence and outcomes. In February 2025, UMMA Health, a federally qualified health center in Los Angeles that serves predominantly low-income Hispanic/Latino and Black patient populations, transitioned from fecal immunochemical testing (FIT) to triennial stool DNA-FIT (sDNA-FIT) kits. After implementation, screening rates declined from the previous median of 43.6% in February 2025 to 27.9% by August 2025, prompting a qualitative evaluation of patient experiences with the new workflow. From July to November 2025, we conducted a focus group discussion and individual semistructured telephone interviews. We recruited 15 study participants by telephone call or text message, including 4 focus group participants and 11 interviewees. Participants were English- and Spanish-speaking patients aged 45 to 75 years with an sDNA-FIT order. Interviews were conducted in English or Spanish, according to patient preference, with an interpreter as needed, and explored experiences with test kit completion, outreach, and access to results. Transcripts were analyzed by using workflow-based process mapping and thematic analysis. All but 2 participants completed their kits. Patients who did not complete kits were more difficult to recruit in part because they seemed unaware of the CRC screening process. Moreover, a substantial drop-off occurred between the number of kits that were returned (n = 13) and the number of patients who accessed their results (n = 5). Patients reported difficulty navigating online result portals, uncertainty about expected follow-up communication, and anxiety due to inaccessible results. The results of the qualitative workflow analysis suggested that standardization of access to results and proactive outreach via text message campaigns may improve CRC screening rates in this patient population.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Colorectal cancer (CRC) represents a major global health burden, ranking as the third most common malignancy. The transition from benign polyps to metastatic CRC highlights the need for novel therapeutic strategies. Advances in epidemiology and molecular biology have enhanced our understanding of CRC risk factors and tumor dynamics, supporting precision medicine to improve patient outcomes. This review analyzes CRC through epidemiology, molecular mechanisms, and therapeutic innovations, emphasizing advanced drug delivery systems for precision targeted treatment and the shift from conventional to individualized oncology. Key biomarkers such as kirsten rat sarcoma (KRAS) viral oncogene homolog, neuroblastoma RAS (NRAS) viral oncogene homolog, B-Raf proto-oncogene (BRAF), human epidermal growth factor (HER2), neurotrophic tyrosine receptor kinase (NTRK) and microsatellite instability (MSI)-H play crucial role in guiding treatment. Despite the potential of targeted therapies, obstacles including tumor microenvironment and resistance still exist. Emerging nanoparticle and lipid-based systems may address these challenges. Future research should focus on clinical translation, optimizing delivery methods, and identifying new biomarkers to enhance personalized CRC treatment.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Although post-treatment FDG-PET/CT is frequently obtained following definitive chemoradiation (CRT) for locally advanced anal canal cancer (LAACC), its prognostic utility remains uncertain. We hypothesized that quantitative PET/CT metrics would be associated with overall survival (OS) and that pre-treatment metabolic parameters would provide greater prognostic information than post-treatment metabolic response. We conducted a retrospective cohort study of patients with LAACC who underwent definitive CRT and both pre-treatment and post-treatment fluorodeoxyglucose (FDG) PET/CT. Quantitative PET metrics were extracted, including mean SUL, total lesion glycolysis (TLG), metabolic tumor volume (MTV), maximum SUL, and peak SUL. OS was estimated using the Kaplan-Meier method. Associations between PET-derived variables and OS were evaluated using univariable Cox proportional hazards regression, with optimal cutoffs identified using maximally selected rank statistics (MaxStat). Forty-five patients were included (median age 57.7 years), with post-treatment PET/CT performed at a median of 4.4 months following CRT. Lean body mass (HR 3.10, 95% CI 1.01-9.50; p = 0.049) and pre-treatment primary tumor mean SUL (HR 4.93, 95% CI 1.40-17.37; p = 0.013), size (HR 4.01, 95% CI 1.22-13.17; p = 0.022), TLG (HR 3.68, 95% CI 1.11-12.14; p = 0.033), and peak SUL (HR 3.31, 95% CI 1.02-10.72; p = 0.046) were associated with OS in exploratory univariable analyses. Post-treatment, higher weight (HR 4.94, 95% CI 1.06-22.96; p=0.041; cutoff 60.42 kg; N=45) and lean body mass (HR 4.82, 95% CI 1.06-21.90; p=0.042; cutoff 44.50 kg; N=44) were associated with worse OS. No post-treatment PET-derived metabolic parameters met the nominal threshold for statistical significance. Among patients with higher baseline metabolic activity, greater reduction in mean SUL following CRT demonstrated a nonsignificant trend toward improved OS. Pre-treatment FDG-PET/CT metabolic parameters demonstrated stronger associations with OS than post-treatment metabolic parameters in this exploratory cohort. Baseline tumor metabolic activity may provide useful prognostic information in patients with LAACC, warranting validation in larger prospective studies.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Conversion of minimally invasive surgery often adds operative time and may lead to complications. The aim was to develop a preoperative prediction model for conversion and identify predictive risk factors in minimally invasive colorectal cancer resections, to be used in consideration and counselling preoperatively. An observational study based on data from national Swedish registries (CRCBaSE, 2019-2021). Logistic regression models were used to predict conversion, with variable selection based on statistical performance. Model discrimination, calibration, and uncertainty were evaluated using the Brier score, AUC, calibration plots, and bootstrap resampling. External validation was performed in the Danish Colorectal Cancer Registry (2016-2020). Minimally invasive surgery was performed on 7,811 patients. Seven preoperative predictors were identified as risk factors of conversion: body mass index (BMI), clinical T stage, age, previous abdominal surgery, sex, robotic approach, and left-sided tumour location. Risk of conversion increased with advanced T stage, left-sided tumours, prior abdominal surgery, extremes of BMI, and age up to 80 years, whereas robotic surgery and female sex reduced the risk of conversion. A 7-variable model was created and achieved an AUC of 0.730 in the Swedish test set but demonstrated reduced discrimination and calibration on internal validation (AUC 0.681). External validation in a Danish national cohort confirmed consistent directions of the predictors but showed further reduced predictive performance (AUC 0.608). Internal validation did not maintain adequate discrimination or calibration, and neither did the external validation. Several variables showed consistent associations with conversion and may be regarded as candidate predictors.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Ostomy reversal is a frequently performed procedure in colorectal surgery and is often considered suitable for surgical training. However, evidence regarding the impact of surgeon training level on postoperative outcomes remains limited. This study aimed to evaluate outcomes after ostomy reversal performed by residents versus consultant surgeons through a combined single-center analysis and systematic review with meta-analysis. A retrospective, single-center observational study was conducted, including 255 patients who underwent loop ileostomy or loop colostomy reversal between 2012 and 2024. Postoperative outcomes were compared between procedures performed by residents and consultants. The observational study was conducted and reported in accordance with STROBE guidelines. In addition, a systematic review and meta-analysis were carried out according to PRISMA guidelines to assess outcomes after loop ileostomy reversal stratified by surgeon training level. The primary outcomes were overall and major postoperative morbidity. In the single-center cohort, postoperative outcomes after ostomy reversal were largely comparable between residents and consultants. Residents more frequently performed direct stoma closure and had shorter operative times, and their patients were discharged sooner. Major postoperative morbidity was significantly higher in consultant-performed ileostomy reversals, likely reflecting greater procedural complexity. The meta-analysis of available comparative studies, including 1,196 patients (resident: n = 419; consultant: n = 777), demonstrated that resident-performed loop ileostomy reversal was not associated with inferior outcomes. In contrast, resident-performed stoma reversal was associated with lower rates of overall postoperative morbidity (OR = 0.59; 95% CI, 0.46-0.76; p < 0.0001) and major postoperative morbidity (OR = 0.66; 95% CI, 0.44-0.99; p = 0.04), whereas complication-specific outcomes did not differ significantly between groups. Notably, serious risk of bias and low certainty of evidence were detected. Resident-performed ostomy reversal appears safe and feasible when conducted within a structured and supervised training environment. Findings from both the single-center analysis and the meta-analysis support integrating stoma reversal procedures into surgical residency training.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Alcohol consumption is known to be a significant risk factor for cancer. In 2025, the US Surgeon General recommended adding cancer risk warning labels to alcoholic beverages, emphasizing the need for increased awareness. However, national-level data describing long-term trends in alcohol-attributable cancer mortality, including variation by age, sex, and geographic region, remain limited. This study aims to evaluate trends in alcohol-attributable cancer mortality in the USA. This was a population-based observational trend analysis using data from the Global Burden of Disease database. We analyzed age-standardized mortality rates (ASMRs) and the percentage of ASMR attributable to heavy alcohol use-defined as consumption exceeding the theoretical minimum risk exposure level, in the USA from 1990 to 2023. We evaluated ASMR for all cancers combined, followed by ten specific cancers. Results (per 100,000 population) were stratified by sex, location (50 states and Washington DC), and age-groups (20-54, 55 years and older). Joinpoint regression was performed using Monte Carlo permutation testing to select the optimal model; EAPCs were reported with 95% confidence intervals and two-sided p values. All rates are reported per 100,000 population. Alcohol-attributable cancer deaths in the USA doubled from 1990 (11,361) to 2023 (23,126). Mortality rates were higher in the 55 years and older age-group (19.2; 95% CI, 12.8-28.7) versus 20-54 years (2.4; 1.4-3.4), and in males (6.4; 3.8-9.7) versus females (2.1; 1.4-3.0). The percentage of mortality attributable to alcohol increased across most cancer types, age groups, and sexes, with liver cancer demonstrating the greatest increase in alcohol-attributable (113.9%). In 2023, liver (12.7; 11.2-14.4) and breast (2.4; 0.9-5.9) cancers had the highest alcohol-related mortality rates in 55 years and older males and females, respectively; in ages 20-54, colorectal (0.9; 0.4-1.4) in males and breast (0.9; 0.5-1.4) in females were highest. State-wise, the District of Columbia recorded the highest (M: 9.8; 6.0-14.1; F: 3.5; 2.2-5.2), while Utah had the lowest (M: 3.9; 2.4-5.9; F: 1.4; 0.9-2.0) ASMR. Alcohol-attributable cancer mortality has increased in the USA, with a disproportionate burden observed in males and 55 years and older individuals. Our findings highlight the critical need for targeted prevention efforts and increased awareness to address the rising impact of alcohol consumption on cancer-related mortality. No funding received for this study.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Colorectal endoscopic submucosal dissection (ESD) sometimes remains technically challenging. Although various traction-assisted techniques have been developed, many require scope withdrawal or additional preparation, which may limit procedural efficiency and reproducibility. We developed the radial crane method (RCM), a multipoint traction technique designed to provide stable and sustained radial traction during ESD. RCM uses a reopenable clip preassembled with 4 commercially available traction devices. The clip is placed on the contralateral side of the lesion, and each loop is fixed to 4 peripheral points around the lesion to generate centralized radial traction. We demonstrate the feasibility and effectiveness of this method in a case of colorectal ESD. An 84-year-old woman with a 30-mm elevated rectal adenocarcinoma underwent ESD using RCM. Four-point radial traction enabled stable, multidirectional exposure of the submucosal layer, facilitating precise dissection under a clear field of view. En bloc resection was achieved safely and efficiently within 25 minutes without adverse events. RCM provides stable and sustained radial traction using commercially available devices without additional modification. This simple and reproducible technique may enhance visualization and procedural efficiency during colorectal ESD in selected challenging lesions.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Squamous cell carcinoma is one of the most common aerodigestive malignancies, while colorectal cancer is one of the most prevalent cancers worldwide. Although these cancers share similar risk factors, synchronous presentation is rare. We report the case of a woman who successfully underwent a total laryngectomy and right hemicolectomy during a single operative session. She presented with a three-month history of dysphonia and weight loss. Laryngoscopy revealed a suspicious vocal cord lesion, confirmed on a positron emission tomography (PET) scan. Incidentally, PET also demonstrated a colonic lesion. Colonoscopy confirmed a synchronous caecal tumour. As a result of clinical deterioration, she required emergent admission for dyspnoea and necessitated a tracheostomy. Following multidisciplinary team discussion, a decision was made to proceed with simultaneous laryngectomy and right hemicolectomy. The postoperative course was unremarkable. This case highlights the importance of multidisciplinary collaboration and careful preoperative planning in managing synchronous malignancies.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
An 80-year-old man with ulcerative colitis underwent computed tomography colonography (CTC) for colorectal cancer surveillance. Mild pain was experienced during rectal catheter insertion. CTC demonstrated extensive extraperitoneal gas and portal venous gas involving both hepatic lobes. Blood was noted on digital rectal examination, but the patient had no abdominal pain or clinical signs of sepsis. He was managed conservatively with antibiotics, bowel rest, and close observation. He remained asymptomatic, afebrile, and haemodynamically stable, with an uncomplicated recovery and discharge on Day 3. Rectal catheterization during CTC can result in rectal perforation, and extensive portal venous gas may occur as a consequence of pressure-related insufflation in the absence of bowel ischemia or septic pylephlebitis. The presence of portal venous gas should therefore be interpreted in the context of the clinical presentation rather than considered an indication for intervention by itself. In clinically stable patients, recognition of a pressure-related mechanism may support conservative management and avoid unnecessary invasive intervention.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Allostatic load is an emerging stress biomarker capturing immune, cardiovascular, and metabolic dysregulations. We evaluated associations between allostatic load and mortality after colorectal cancer (CRC) diagnosis, comparing allostatic load to metabolic syndrome to determine if including additional domains beyond metabolism strengthens associations with mortality. Southern Community Cohort Study participants who developed incident CRC after enrollment (2002-2009) were included; most self-identified as Black (69%) and report <$15,000 annual household income (55%). Enrollment samples were analyzed for immune, metabolic, and cardiovascular biomarkers. A standard metabolic syndrome definition was used (3/5 traits); most (N=1007) had available information to calculate metabolic syndrome. To calculate allostatic load, biomarkers above clinical risk cutoffs were summed; counts above median indicated high allostatic load (4/10 traits). A subsample of 303 had additional information to calculate allostatic load. Mortality was ascertained through 2020 via National Death Index linkage. Multivariate-adjusted Cox models estimated hazard ratios and 95% confidence intervals (HR[95%CI]). High allostatic load was associated with higher risk of all-cause (1.81[1.25-2.62]) and CRC-specific mortality (HR:1.81[1.07-3.07]). The latter attenuated after controlling for health behaviors (HR:1.57[0.91-2.70]). Metabolic syndrome was not associated with mortality (all-cause: 1.06[0.88-1.28]; CRC-specific: 1.08[0.83-1.40]). Allostatic load may be a clinically actionable biomarker to readily identify cancer patients with comorbidity.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Tregs significantly shape the colorectal cancer (CRC) immune microenvironment, yet the roles of specific Treg-associated genes remain poorly understood. Treg-related genes were screened from scRNA-seq data (GSE161277), followed by expression and prognostic validation in several independent cohorts (TCGA, GSE87211, GSE44076, and GSE17538). GSEA and CellChat characterized regulatory pathways and intercellular communication. MED10 expression was verified in CRC tissues and cell lines by qRT-PCR and western blotting. Functional assays (CCK-8, colony formation, wound healing, flow cytometry) evaluated MED10's impact on tumor behavior. Finally, the in vivo relevance of MED10 to tumor growth and immune microenvironmental changes was assessed using a syngeneic mouse model. MED10 was identified as a critical Treg-related gene in CRC, with high expression correlating with shortened survival. GSEA revealed that high MED10 expression was associated with enrichment of the Wnt/β-catenin signaling pathway. Furthermore, intercellular communication analysis suggested that elevated MED10 expression may be associated with increased interaction strengths between cell populations, potentially contributing to the remodeling of an immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment. In vitro functional assays revealed that MED10 knockdown significantly impaired CRC cell proliferation and migration while inducing apoptosis. MED10 knockdown also reduced Wnt/β-catenin transcriptional activity, which was partially restored by LiCl treatment. Finally, in vivo, MED10 silencing suppressed tumor growth and was accompanied by reduced Treg infiltration and enhanced effector T-cell activity. MED10 is associated with CRC progression, Wnt/β-catenin signaling alterations, and a Treg-enriched immunosuppressive immune context, supporting its potential value as a prognostic indicator and candidate therapeutic target.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Metastasis of colorectal carcinoma (CRC) to the parotid gland is exceptionally rare, with only a few cases reported in the literature. We describe a 70 year old woman previously treated for sigmoid adenocarcinoma who developed a painful right parotid mass three years after hemicolectomy and adjuvant XELOX chemotherapy. Fine needle aspiration confirmed metastatic sigmoid colon adenocarcinoma through characteristic immunohistochemical markers, including CDX 2 and Villin positivity. A review of the 8 reported cases (including the current one) shows the disease occurs in patients at a mean age of 63 years (range, 34 to 83). There is no gender or side predilection. The overall features indicate that parotid metastasis from CRC typically occurs with widespread disease and carries a poor prognosis. Diagnosis is challenging because parotid metastases often mimic primary salivary gland tumours clinically and radiologically, making immunohistochemistry essential for distinguishing intestinal adenocarcinoma from primary salivary malignancies. Reported outcomes remain poor, reflecting advanced systemic disease at presentation. This case emphasises the need to consider metastatic CRC in the differential diagnosis of new parotid masses in patients with a history of colorectal malignancy. Early recognition, accurate diagnosis through imaging and histopathology, and multidisciplinary management are crucial. This case highlights the importance of considering metastatic CRC in the differential diagnosis of parotid masses in patients with a known primary malignancy.
