ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
This study compared the long-term results of patients submitted to laparoscopic and open right colectomy under the principles of complete mesocolic excision (CME) and central vascular ligation (CVL) for right colon cancer. This is a long-term follow-up update of our previously published series comparing laparoscopic and open right CME/CVL colectomy for colon cancer. It is a retrospective comparative study of prospectively collected data of all patients submitted to right colectomies in a tertiary referral center between January 2012 and December 2018. A 1:1 propensity score matching algorithm was applied based on age, gender, American Society of Anesthesiologists, cardiac, respiratory, and other comorbidities, emergency, R, T, and N status. Survival analysis included the performance of multivariable Cox regression analysis. Overall, 82 patients were included. Regarding the primary outcome, 5-year overall survival (OS) of the open and laparoscopic arms was 81.5% and 78.4%, respectively ( Our results suggest that laparoscopic CME/CVL right colectomy is at least as good as open regarding long-term oncological results.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Upper tract urothelial carcinoma (UTUC) is a rare malignancy with complex clinical behavior, particularly in patients with hereditary cancer syndromes such as Lynch syndrome. In the absence of universal tumor testing for mismatch repair deficiency or microsatellite instability, personal or family history of Lynch syndrome-associated cancers (PFHLAC) may serve as a surrogate marker for identifying patients at risk. This study aims to characterize the clinical features and oncological outcomes of UTUC in patients with PFHLAC. We conducted a multicenter retrospective cohort study of 1,893 patients who underwent radical nephroureterectomy (RNU) for UTUC between February 2000 and February 2021 across 7 U.S. institutions. Patients were stratified based on the presence or absence of PFHLAC. Clinical, pathological, and treatment-related variables were compared. Oncologic outcomes (bladder recurrence, extravesical recurrence, all-cause mortality, and cancer-specific mortality) were modeled using Cox proportional hazards with adjustment for clinical, surgical, and pathologic covariates. Of the total cohort, 223 patients (11.7%) had PFHLAC. These patients were younger at surgery (70 years vs. 72 years, P < 0.001), more likely to be female (45.3% vs. 32.1%, P < 0.001), and exhibited higher rates of multifocal tumors (30.9% vs. 24.4%, P = 0.038), nodal involvement (cN1 or N2 11.5% vs. 10.7%, P = 0.031), and lymphovascular invasion (34.1% vs. 28.8%, P < 0.001). They frequently received neoadjuvant chemotherapy (NAC) (32.3% vs. 19.4%, P < 0.001). On Cox modeling, PFHLAC was not associated with increased risk of recurrence or all-cause mortality but had lower risk of cancer-specific mortality (HR 0.59, P = 0.044). UTUC in patients with PFHLAC demonstrates distinct clinical and pathological features, with reduced risk of cancer-specific mortality. Routine screening for Lynch syndrome using clinical criteria, immunohistochemistry, and confirmatory genetic testing may improve identification and management of high-risk patients. These findings support the need for personalized approaches and further prospective studies in this population.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
In colorectal cancer, universal screening for defective mismatch-repair (dMMR) enables identification of individuals with Lynch syndrome and provides treatment-relevant prognostic and predictive information. The outcome of universal dMMR screening was evaluated in a population-based cohort of 3164 colorectal cancers diagnosed in Sweden during 2022-2025. Implementation was successful with 98% of the colorectal cancers assessed for dMMR, which was identified in 21% of the tumours. Reflex testing for BRAF mutations was performed in 92% of the tumours with combined MLH1 and PMS2 loss. However, the subsequent diagnostic pathway showed gaps. Of patients with dMMR patterns suggestive of Lynch syndrome, 50% were referred for genetic counselling and 45% underwent genetic testing. Disease-predisposing germline MMR variants were identified in 25% of the patients undergoing genetic testing. Real-world data from this population-based cohort demonstrate successful implementation of universal dMMR diagnostics but reveal an incomplete diagnostic pathway with missed opportunities to reduce morbidity and mortality through preventive measures and surveillance.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Although the short- and mid-term safety of transanal total mesorectal excision is well documented, concerns regarding atypical recurrences make robust ten-year oncological data necessary. This study evaluates long-term safety and surgical quality using strict, rectal-specific Textbook Outcome criteria. This is a retrospective analysis of 234 consecutive patients operated on between 2013 and 2021. The Dutch ColoRectal Audit criteria defined a successful outcome. Kaplan-Meier and multivariable Cox regression analyses evaluated overall survival, disease-free survival, and cancer-specific survival. Median follow-up was 98 months (reverse Kaplan-Meier), 62 patients had a potential follow-up of ten years, of whom 30 remained at risk at 120 months. A successful outcome was achieved in 64.1 percent of patients, primarily hindered by postoperative complications and readmissions. The cumulative incidence of local recurrence, with death as a competing event, was 5.6% (95% CI 3.0-8.6) at 3 and 5 years. After adjustment for age, ASA class and clinical stage in a multivariable Cox regression analysis, achieving a Textbook Outcome was associated with lower all-cause mortality at a borderline level of statistical significance (aHR 0.61, 95% CI 0.37-0.99; p = 0.046), but not independently with cancer-specific survival (aHR 0.57, 95% CI 0.28-1.18; p = 0.131) or disease-free survival (aHR 0.74, 95% CI 0.47-1.18; p = 0.211). Stage IV disease was the only independent predictor of cancer-specific survival, and age and stage IV were independent predictors of disease-free survival. Transanal total mesorectal excision was associated with favorable long-term oncological outcomes and acceptable local control. The rectal-specific composite outcome serves as a useful framework for auditing surgical quality. It was associated with overall survival after adjustment, but not independently with cancer-specific or disease-free survival; these exploratory findings do not establish causality.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Deep mural injury (DMI) is a recognized adverse event (AE) of colorectal endoscopic submucosal dissection (ESD), but which patients require surgery after endoscopic closure is poorly defined. We aimed to define its incidence, risk factors, and outcomes. This single-center retrospective cohort included colorectal ESDs performed between July 2015 and November 2024. DMI was identified and graded (Sydney classification) from procedure reports and images by two expert endoscopists, with adjudication by a third. The primary endpoint was urgent surgical intervention; secondary endpoints were post-procedural AEs and technical outcomes. DMI risk factors were assessed by multivariable logistic regression. Among 710 lesions, 131 (18.5%) had DMI, of which 116 (88.5%) were Sydney III-V; all were closed endoscopically. Urgent surgery was required in 6 (4.6%) DMI versus 1 (0.2%) non-DMI patient (p<0.001). Post-procedural AEs were more frequent with DMI (26.7% vs 3.1%; p<0.001), including post-polypectomy syndrome (17.6% vs 1.7%; p<0.001). All delayed perforations and surgeries among DMI cases occurred with Sydney III-V injury. Technical success was comparable (en-bloc 84.0% vs 83.9%, p=1.000; R0 78.2% vs 80.9%, p=0.522). Lesion size, prior manipulation, submucosal fibrosis, and significant intraprocedural bleeding were independently associated with DMI. In exploratory analyses, left colon location and CT contrast leak were associated with surgery. DMI during colorectal ESD increases post-procedural AEs but does not compromise technical success, and most cases are managed conservatively after closure. Surgical risk is concentrated in Sydney III-V injuries; left colon DMI and CT contrast leak warrant prospective validation as risk markers.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Colorectal cancer (CRC) incidence is rising among younger populations, yet age-associated differences in prognosis and molecular characteristics remain incompletely understood. This study compares survival outcomes between early-onset CRC (EOCRC) and late-onset CRC (LOCRC) and explores age-associated molecular and immune characteristics. We identified CRC patients diagnosed between 2000 and 2021 from the SEER database. Survival was compared using Kaplan-Meier curves. Cox regression was used to assess prognostic associations, while competing-risk analyzes were performed using cumulative incidence functions and Fine-Gray regression. Diagnostic-period stratification and an age group × diagnostic period interaction analysis were also conducted. Findings were externally validated in two independent patient cohorts. To explore age-associated molecular heterogeneity, transcriptomic profiling and functional enrichment analyzes were additionally performed using data from The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA) database. Immune cell infiltration and functional status were evaluated using CIBERSORT and single-sample Gene Set Enrichment Analysis (ssGSEA), respectively. A total of 29,576 EOCRC and 164,359 LOCRC patients were analyzed. EOCRC patients demonstrated significantly better overall survival than LOCRC patients. Multivariable analysis identified associations of sex, race, grade, T stage, N stage, M stage, and tumor size with survival. The survival advantage of EOCRC was consistently observed across subgroups stratified by anatomical subsite and treatment type, and was also observed in external cohorts. The adjusted HR for LOCRC versus EOCRC decreased from 1.89 (95% CI, 1.85-1.94) in 2000-2010 to 1.51 (95% CI, 1.46-1.57) in 2011-2021 (P for interaction < 0.001). In competing-risk analysis, LOCRC was associated with a higher adjusted subdistribution hazard of CRC-specific death (SHR = 1.19, 95% CI, 1.16-1.22). Transcriptomic analysis of 53 EOCRC and 262 LOCRC patients identified 1,099 differentially expressed genes involved in membrane potential regulation, nucleosome organization, neuroactive ligand-receptor interaction, neutrophil extracellular trap formation, and cell adhesion molecules. Immune cell infiltration and functional scoring revealed comparable immune cell abundance and individual immune functional signature scores between groups; however, the effector/exhaustion ratio was significantly lower in EOCRC (P = 0.033), indicating an age-associated difference in the relative enrichment of cytotoxicity- and exhaustion-related gene signatures. Pathway analysis further revealed enrichment of the HALLMARK_KRAS_SIGNALING_DN and HALLMARK_MYOGENESIS gene sets in EOCRC. EOCRC was associated with better overall survival than LOCRC, although the magnitude of this association varied across diagnostic periods. Transcriptomic analyzes identified age-associated differences in KRAS-related, differentiation-associated, and immune functional gene signatures. The clinical and prognostic significance of these molecular and immune differences requires further investigation.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Colon cancer progression involves coordinated changes in epithelial cells and the tumor microenvironment, yet the transcriptional organization, associated regulatory programs and candidate vulnerabilities of epithelial cell states remain unclear. Multi-cohort single-cell RNA sequencing data were integrated with inferred copy-number variation, pseudotime, regulon and spatial transcriptomic analyses. Ligand-receptor interactions were inferred to characterize state-associated communication. Geneformer-based in silico perturbation, virtual screening and molecular dynamics simulations were performed to nominate candidates for functional investigation. ZC3HC1 knockdown, overexpression and rescue were assessed in HCT 116 cells using EdU, cell-cycle, apoptosis and migration/invasion assays. Multiplex immunofluorescence examined epithelial and immune-marker distributions in tumor sections. An epithelial-state-informed prognostic model was developed using nested selection within TCGA-COAD and evaluated in GEO cohorts with fixed training-derived thresholds. Epithelial cells formed three transcriptional states with distinct expression and regulatory programs. State 3 was enriched for ILF2-, NFYB-, MLX-, CTCF- and HMGA1-associated regulons. Fibroblasts were the dominant signaling source, whereas T cells had the highest incoming communication strength and State 3 showed candidate CypA, COLLAGEN and CD99 expression associations; spatial analyses further showed co-occurrence of collagen ligands with SDC1, SDC4, CD44 and integrin receptor complexes. ZC3HC1 knockdown in HCT 116 cells reduced EdU incorporation, increased G0/G1 accumulation and apoptosis, and diminished migration and invasion; rescue partially restored these phenotypes. Multiplex staining illustrated contrasting myeloid and T-cell distributions around PanCK-positive regions. Virtual screening nominated DB12168 as a candidate ZC3HC1-interacting compound. The epithelial-state-informed risk model showed cohort-dependent prognostic performance, and its associations with immune exclusion and angiogenesis were exploratory. Epithelial transcriptional states in colon cancer are associated with distinct regulatory programs and stromal expression patterns. Functional assays implicated ZC3HC1 in HCT 116 cell phenotypes, and virtual screening nominated DB12168 for binding studies, while the epithelial-state-informed risk model provides a framework for retrospective prognostic evaluation.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Predicting Kirsten rat sarcoma viral oncogene homolog (KRAS) mutation status in colorectal cancer (CRC) from routine hematoxylin and eosin (H&E)-stained whole-slide images (WSIs) may provide a cost-effective complement to molecular testing. However, existing multiple instance learning (MIL) methods typically treat WSIs as unordered collections of image patches, leaving heterogeneous morphological patterns inconsistently organised across patients. We propose TCAMIL (Two-stage Cluster-aware Aligned Multiple Instance Learning), a weakly supervised computational framework for organising slide-specific histomorphological patterns into globally aligned phenotype representations. TCAMIL first performs morphology-driven within-slide clustering to identify local phenotype units and then aligns these units across slides to construct a shared cross-slide morphological phenotype space. The resulting phenotype identities are encoded and integrated with tile-level representations through phenotype-guided hierarchical aggregation for slide-level KRAS mutation prediction. In patient-level 10-fold cross-validation on the Gansu cohort (n=349), TCAMIL achieved a mean AUC of 0.7917 and an ACC of 0.7158, outperforming representative MIL baselines. Under a strict out-of-distribution evaluation protocol, the model was directly applied to the independent Scottish SurGen cohort (n=350) without retraining or fine-tuning, achieving the highest external AUC of 0.6566, ACC of 0.6442, and F1-score of 0.4929 among the compared methods. Further analysis of globally aligned phenotype units showed that model attention was preferentially concentrated within a restricted subset of morphologically coherent glandular, epithelial, and tumour-stroma interface patterns. TCAMIL provides a structured framework for morphology-aware molecular prediction from routine histopathology by organising heterogeneous WSI morphology into cross-slide comparable phenotype units. The results suggest that cross-slide morphological phenotype organisation can support interpretable weakly supervised KRAS mutation prediction from CRC WSIs. The code is available at: https://github.com/YiShi-123/TCAMIL.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Malnutrition and metabolic dysregulation are common among patients undergoing gastrointestinal cancer surgery and are associated with adverse postoperative outcomes. While perioperative nutritional supplementation has been associated with improved early postoperative recovery, its association with long-term oncologic survival remains unclear. This is a secondary survival analysis of PROGRESS, a single-center, double-blinded, placebo-controlled feasibility randomized controlled trial conducted between 2018 and 2020 in Ontario, Canada. Adults undergoing elective resection for gastrointestinal malignancies were randomized 1:1 to perioperative nutritional supplementation (protein, immuno-nutrition, and carbohydrate-loading solutions) or placebo. Progression-free survival (PFS) and overall survival (OS) were assessed up to 60 mo using Kaplan-Meier methods and Cox proportional hazards regression. Of 71 enrolled patients, 56 were included in the final analysis (30 placebo, 26 intervention). Recurrence occurred in 36.7% of the placebo group and 57.7% of the intervention group (P = 0.116); mortality occurred in 46.7% and 46.2%, respectively (P = 0.969). Five-year PFS was 46.7% (placebo) versus 42.3% (intervention), and 5-y OS was 53.3% versus 53.8%, with no statistically significant differences. Notably, the intervention group had a more favorable tumor distribution (fewer pancreatic cancers, more colorectal cancers), yet no survival advantage was observed. Perioperative red blood cell transfusion was independently associated with worse PFS (hazard ratio 5.35, 95% confidence interval 2.30-12.44) and OS (hazard ratio 7.83, 95% confidence interval 3.13-19.58); tumor location and the number of positive lymph nodes were also associated with OS. Perioperative nutritional supplementation was not associated with improved long-term survival in this heterogeneous gastrointestinal cancer cohort, consistent with recent evidence suggesting limited additional benefit of immune-enhanced formulations over standard nutritional support. However, this study demonstrates the feasibility of incorporating long-term survival end points into perioperative nutrition trials and underscores the importance of adequate stratification by tumor type and procedure type in future definitive studies.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Colorectal cancer (CRC) may develop through the conventional adenoma-to-carcinoma sequence or alternative routes of carcinogenesis, accompanied by changes in epithelial cell states and remodeling of the tumor microenvironment, yet its core driving mechanisms and therapeutic options remain unclear. This study integrated single-cell, bulk transcriptomic, and spatial transcriptomic datasets for comprehensive bioinformatics analyses, followed by validation in CRC cells and clinical samples using immunohistochemistry. Epithelial cells showed the most pronounced transcriptional and cell-communication remodeling during adenoma-to-carcinoma progression, with marked expansion of tumor-related subpopulations including tumor epithelial cells, stem-like tumor cells, and proliferating tumor cells. Multi-omics integration identified tissue inhibitor of metalloproteinase 1 (TIMP1) and claudin-23 (CLDN23) as core genes closely linked to inflammatory, immune, and metabolic pathways. Ruxolitinib was predicted to target the TIMP1/CLDN23 regulatory network, and in vitro experiments confirmed that it downregulated TIMP1, upregulated CLDN23, and suppressed CRC cell proliferation. Functional assays further showed that TIMP1 promoted while CLDN23 inhibited CRC cell proliferation and migration, and that the two genes may act cooperatively through their shared downstream molecule selenium-binding protein 1 (SELENBP1). These findings suggest an epithelial-centered mechanism of adenoma-to-CRC progression, identify TIMP1 and CLDN23 as molecules with diagnostic, prognostic, and therapeutic potential, and provide preliminary support for repurposing Ruxolitinib in CRC.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Colorectal cancer (CRC) ranks third in global cancer incidence and second in mortality. However, reliable diagnostic and prognostic CRC biomarkers remain elusive. To identify potential biomarkers, proteomic profiling was performed on tumor and adjacent non-tumor tissues (n = 20) using a hybrid TIMS quadrupole time-of-flight mass spectrometer. Candidate proteins were analyzed on preoperative plasma of stages II and III CRC patients (n = 71) and healthy controls (n = 22) by ELISA. Plasma levels of platelet factor 4 (PF4) showed high sensitivity in discriminating CRC patients from controls (unadjusted AUC 0.942; age-adjusted model AUC 0.999), while combined PF4, G protein-coupled receptor class C group 5 member A (GPRC5A), and aminomethyltransferase (AMT) markers give the best diagnostic performance for CRC patients with 95% sensitivity and 100% specificity. In patients with normal CEA values (n = 55), combined PF4/AMT and PF4/GPRC5A measurements gave 65.5% and 41.8% sensitivity with 100% specificity (P < 0.001, respectively). Moreover, a strong trend of recurrence was observed in patients with abnormal plasma levels of PF4/GPRC5A (P = 0.075). In conclusion, combined analysis of PF4, GPRC5A and AMT in the plasma are novel diagnostic markers for locally advanced CRC patients. Combined PF4/GPRC5A assay could be an alternative marker panel for CEA-normal CRC patients with prognostic implication.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Anti-epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) rechallenge is a standard therapeutic option for patients with RAS/BRAF wild-type (WT) metastatic colorectal cancer (mCRC) who benefited from prior anti-EGFR-based regimens. Circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA)-guided molecular selection improved efficacy, but routine testing and real-world evidence remain limited. REalCHALLENGE is a retrospective study aiming at assessing the activity of real-world anti-EGFR rechallenge versus other standard-of-care (SoC) treatments in microsatellite stable (MSS), RAS/BRAF WT mCRC patients profiled by ctDNA. The primary endpoint was overall response rate (ORR), while secondary endpoints included disease control rate (DCR), progression-free survival (PFS), and overall survival (OS). Hyperselection integrating archival solid tissue profiling to ctDNA profiling was also investigated. 104 patients were included: 69 (66%) ctDNA RAS/BRAF WT and 35 (34%) mutants. Among ctDNA WT, anti-EGFR rechallenge led to higher ORR compared with SoC (29% vs 0%, p = 0.003), and DCR (68% vs 42%, p = 0.049). A trend toward longer median PFS was observed (4.7 vs 2.9 months, p = 0.06), alongside with improved OS (21.9 vs 11.1 months, p = 0.04). In ctDNA mutant patients, outcomes were comparable between groups. In hyperselected non-mutant patients, anti-EGFR rechallenge led to improved ORR (34.4% vs 0%; p = 0.006), PFS (4.98 vs 2.59 months; p = 0.02) and OS (22.20 vs 11.18 months; p = 0.02). No new safety signals emerged. Anti-EGFR rechallenge confirmed meaningful activity in ctDNA RAS/BRAF WT MSS mCRC patients in a real-world setting, particularly in a hyperselected population integrating ctDNA and solid tissue profiling. These findings support the value of molecular profiling to optimize selection for anti-EGFR rechallenge.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
These updated national guidelines were developed jointly by the Saudi Gastroenterology Association, Saudi Society of Colon and Rectal Surgery, Saudi Society of Gastrointestinal Oncology, and Saudi Society of Family and Community Medicine, and provide evidence-based recommendations for colorectal cancer (CRC) screening in Saudi Arabia, superseding the 2015 national guidelines. This update incorporates new epidemiological data from Saudi Arabia, including updated incidence estimates, polyp prevalence studies, colonoscopy quality audit data, and national screening uptake surveys, to provide a comprehensively evidence-anchored and locally contextualized framework. A national multidisciplinary group formulated 25 key Population, Intervention, Comparison, Outcome (PICO) questions across seven domains. Systematic literature searches were performed from inception to March 2026. Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation (GRADE) evidence profiles were prepared for critical outcomes, and recommendations were developed through an iterative consensus process requiring ≥80% agreement for strong recommendations. The Task Force strongly recommends implementing an organized national CRC screening program for all asymptomatic average-risk adults aged 45 to 75 years. Biennial fecal immunochemical testing (FIT) is recommended as the primary population-based screening modality. Colonoscopy every 10 years is a recommended alternative. All positive FIT results must be followed by timely, high-quality colonoscopy. Specific recommendations are provided for high-risk groups. High-certainty evidence from multiple randomized trials and large-scale implementation studies demonstrates that organized CRC screening substantially reduces CRC-specific mortality and incidence. A phased, FIT-based national implementation strategy is recommended, tailored to Saudi epidemiology, population preferences, and healthcare infrastructure, with iterative quality improvement as new evidence emerges.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Computer-aided detection (CADe) improves adenoma detection in broad randomized-trial populations, but its incremental value may diminish when baseline colonoscopy performance is already high. We evaluated whether CADe improves advanced neoplasia detection in contemporary high-detection practice. PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, CENTRAL, Scopus, Google Scholar, ClinicalTrials.gov, and WHO ICTRP were searched from inception through September 2026. Randomized trials were eligible when control-arm adenoma detection rate (ADR) was at least 35%; FIT-only trials were analyzed separately. Advanced adenoma detection rate (AADR) and advanced colorectal neoplasia detection rate (ACNDR) were primary outcomes. Random-effects models used restricted maximum likelihood with modified Hartung-Knapp inference. Risk of bias was assessed using RoB 2 and certainty using GRADE. The protocol was prospectively registered in PROSPERO (CRD420261495680). No external funding was received. Forty-eight unique randomized trial families were included. In routine high-detection trials, no statistically significant improvement in AADR was demonstrated (17 trials; RR, 1.018; 95% CI, 0.921-1.125; I² = 0%). CADe reduced whole-colon tandem adenoma miss rate (6 trials; RR, 0.473; 95% CI, 0.363-0.618) and increased overall ADR (28 trials; RR, 1.137; 95% CI, 1.082-1.194). The ADR effect was not clear when control ADR was at least 50% (RR, 1.039; 95% CI, 0.964-1.120). Sessile serrated lesion detection increased (RR, 1.284; 95% CI, 1.125-1.465). Advanced-neoplasia estimates were limited by sparse compatible reporting. In high-detection colonoscopy settings, CADe substantially reduces adenoma misses and improves overall adenoma and sessile serrated lesion detection, demonstrating benefits beyond advanced neoplasia detection. Although a statistically significant improvement in advanced adenoma detection was not demonstrated, the potential long-term clinical benefits of improved lesion recognition remain uncertain. ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
The aim of this study was to investigate the relationship between malnutrition, diagnosed using GLIM criteria, and SF-36 General Health score among patients with colorectal (CRC) and other digestive cancers and to evaluate the combined prognostic association of malnutrition and QoL with survival at 90 days and 1 year after discharge. In a prospective cohort of 519 cancer patients, nutritional status was assessed using MUST and GLIM criteria. QoL was measured with the SF-36 and EuroQol questionnaires, and functional status with the Barthel Index. Survival was estimated using the Kaplan-Meier method, and Cox regression identified prognostic factors. Patients were 62% male with a mean age of 67.9 years; 23.51% were moderately and 21.97% severely malnourished. The most prevalent diagnosis was CRC (65.5%). Patients had moderate functional status and QoL scores at admission. Mortality was 12.5% at 90 days and 27% at 1 year. Combined low SF-36 General Health score and malnutrition was associated with 90-day mortality (HR = 6.03, p < 0.001), followed by low SF-36 General Health score without malnutrition (HR = 3.4, p < 0.05). Longer hospital stay and medical complications were associated with increased mortality, while surgery was associated with lower mortality (HR = 0.38, 95% CI 0.19-0.76, p < 0.001). At 1 year, age, CCI, stage IV cancer, and complications remained key mortality-associated factors. The impact of SF-36 General Health score was weaker than at 90 days but combined poor SF-36 General Health score and malnutrition remained significant. Models showed strong discrimination (C-Index > 0.80). Combined assessment of GLIM-defined malnutrition and self-reported general health may help identify hospitalised patients with digestive cancer who are at increased risk of post-discharge mortality. Whether interventions based on this risk stratification improve outcomes requires prospective interventional evaluation. ClinicalTrials.gov as ID NCT04188990. Registration date: 2 December 2019.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Community-based education may reduce disparities in breast and colorectal cancer (BC/CRC) screening, particularly among individuals with limited English proficiency (LEP) and lower educational attainment. We evaluated whether the Synergistic Partnership for Enhancing Excellence in Cancer Health (SPEECH) BC/CRC education program improved knowledge of screening recommendations and whether gains differed across participant subgroups in the U54 Community Outreach Core (COC) cohort serving high-risk and under-resourced communities. Among 453 participants (median age, 57.7 years; 69.3% female), 41.7% had LEP and 33.6% had less than a high school education. Insurance and primary care access were high (86.3% and 85.2%), yet screening rates remained modest (CRC, 42.4%; mammography, 54.2%). Among 395 participants with matched pre/post surveys, knowledge improved significantly after SPEECH education (all p < 0.0001): correct CRC screening age increased from 38.7% to 83.3%, mammography screening age from 40.3% to 69.6%, and TP53 knowledge from 56.2% to 89.9%. High composite knowledge scores increased from 39.0% to 89.6%. Knowledge gains differed significantly across education levels for CRC, TP53, and total knowledge. Participants with LEP demonstrated greater gains in knowledge than those without LEP. A brief community education program substantially improved cancer screening knowledge, particularly among participants facing educational and language barriers. Despite high healthcare access, screening remained suboptimal. Pairing education with patient navigation and longitudinal follow-up may help translate knowledge gains into improved screening participation and clarify whether it can lead changes in screening behavior.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Early-onset colorectal cancer (EOCRC, < 50 years) is rising sharply. The obesity paradox, where overweight correlates with better outcomes despite obesity being a risk factor, has been reported in colorectal cancer (CRC), mainly for overall survival, but its relevance to recurrence and to EOCRC specifically remains unclear. We investigated the association between body mass index (BMI) at diagnosis and risk of recurrence in EOCRC compared to average-onset colorectal cancer (AOCRC, ≥ 50 years). This retrospective cohort study at Sahlgrenska University Hospital included 1821 patients who underwent radical surgery with curative intent for colorectal adenocarcinoma between 2011 and 2019, comprising 158 patients with EOCRC and 1663 with AOCRC. Cox models of recurrence were adjusted for tumour stage and location and stratified by differentiation. BMI was modelled with restricted cubic splines, and overall association and nonlinearity were assessed with likelihood-ratio tests (LRTs). In EOCRC, BMI was associated with recurrence (LRT p = 0.048), with a lower hazard among patients in the overweight range, although the test for nonlinearity was not significant (p = 0.08). In AOCRC, no significant association was observed (LRT p = 0.88). The interaction between BMI and cohort was not statistically significant (p = 0.11). BMI at diagnosis was associated with recurrence in EOCRC but not in AOCRC. The observed pattern may be consistent with an obesity paradox in EOCRC. Larger studies incorporating prediagnostic weight and body composition are needed to confirm these findings.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Chromosomal instability (CIN) is a hallmark of cancer that drives tumor evolution. Recent studies suggest that CIN contributes to cancer cell dissemination and metastasis formation. Here, we assessed this relationship in a panel of human cancer cell lines. Single nucleotide polymorphism (SNP)-based allele-specific copy number analysis was used to determine the weighted genome instability index (wGII) as a measure of CIN in 24 cancer cell lines. Immunofluorescence microscopy was performed to assess micronucleus (MN) formation, cGAS activity, RelB activity, and mitotic chromosome missegregation. Western blotting was employed to analyze for epithelial to mesenchymal transition (EMT). We established a comprehensive panel of 24 cancer cell lines across four tumor entities (colorectal, lung, pancreatic, and prostate cancer) with a wide metastatic potential spectrum to systematically investigate the role of CIN in metastasis. Although CIN and whole-genome doubling (WGD) were highly prevalent, the wGII did not correlate with mitotic chromosome missegregation rates, MN formation, cGAS-STING signaling, or metastatic potential score of the analyzed cell line panel. Furthermore, neither activation of non-canonical NF-κB signaling nor our EMT-marker based score was associated with increased metastatic potential, indicating that these parameters do not predict metastatic potential. Our study demonstrates that commonly used parameters of genomic instability and EMT do not correlate with the metastatic potential of well-established human cancer cell lines. Improved methods for the reliable assessment of ongoing CIN in tumor cells and three-dimensional cell culture models might be utilized to further analyze the impact of CIN on tumor invasion and metastasis.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
AMP-410 achieves potent antitumor efficacy with high therapeutic index and favorable tolerability in murine tumor models. It is a conditional bifunctional VEGF-4-1BB biologic designed to simultaneously neutralize VEGF and activate 4-1BB signaling, delivering a localized and dual-action approach to immunotherapy. By leveraging VEGF-dependent activation of 4-1BB, AMP-410 preferentially enhances immune responses within the tumor microenvironment, minimizing systemic toxicity while amplifying innate and adaptive immunity. In human 4-1BB transgenic mice bearing syngeneic tumors (MC38 colorectal carcinoma and B16F10 melanoma), AMP-410 promoted rapid M1 macrophage differentiation and enhanced progenitor-exhausted (Pex) T-cell signatures, suggesting coordinated activation of innate and adaptive compartments. At later stages, AMP-410 sustained macrophage antitumor activity and a continued expansion of Pex cells, consistent with long-term immune engagement. Localized activity was indicated by clonal T-cell expansion within tumors with minimal draining lymph node exchange. Compared with the systemic 4-1BB agonist urelumab in syngeneic tumor models, AMP-410 provided superior long-term protection with reduced exhaustion and improved hepatic tolerability. In head-to-head testing against a VEGF-PD-1 bispecific, AMP-410 achieved robust tumor suppression and survival benefits without systemic IFNγ surges. To establish translational relevance, VEGF concentrations were measured in tumor interstitial fluid from patients with cancer. VEGF levels were consistently two to four orders of magnitude higher in tumors than in matched serum, supporting the clinical opportunity of VEGF-restricted 4-1BB activation. Together, these studies position AMP-410 as a promising next-generation immunotherapy for both monotherapy and combination settings, with the potential to overcome key limitations of existing checkpoint- and 4-1BB-based approaches. Localizing 4-1BB activity to VEGF-rich tumor microenvironments may expand the therapeutic window of 4-1BB costimulation, promoting strong antitumor immunity while limiting systemic immune activation and liver inflammation.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
The cost-effectiveness of the Enhanced Recovery After Surgery (ERAS) programme has been well-documented. However, to date, no study has evaluated the economic impact of the ERAS programme specifically among colorectal cancer (CRC) patients undergoing laparoscopic surgery. A historical retrospective cohort study was conducted at the National Cancer Institute of Thailand. CRC Patients undergoing elective laparoscopic surgery between 2021 and 2025 were included in this study. Median cost differences and their 95% confidence intervals (CIs), in Thai Baht (THB), comparing the ERAS and non-ERAS groups were estimated using a median regression model. Subgroup analyses were conducted according to the different reimbursement schemes. A total of 359 patients with CRC were included. The ERAS programme yielded a - 13,992.23 THB total cost reduction, compared with non-ERAS (95% CI [THB]: -19,781.74, -8202.72). A -2235.27 THB reduction in uncovered costs was observed when comparing the ERAS group to the non-ERAS group (95% CI [THB]: -3902.39, -568.16), with significantly lower uncovered costs noted in the Civil Servant Medical Benefit reimbursement schemes. The ERAS group had a significantly shorter length of stay compared to the non-ERAS group. No statistically significant differences in pain scores or adverse events were observed between the two groups. The ERAS programme is cost-saving for CRC patients undergoing laparoscopic surgery and should be routinely implemented in clinical practice. Further studies should be conducted to explore core implementation outcomes.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Whether advanced therapies should be continued before elective surgery for Crohn's disease remains uncertain because of concerns regarding postoperative infectious and anastomotic complications. We evaluated the association between preoperative advanced therapy use and postoperative anastomotic complications. We conducted a retrospective cohort study of patients with Crohn's disease undergoing elective colectomy or proctectomy in the 24-center NSQIP-Inflammatory Bowel Disease Collaborative from 2021-2024. Advanced therapy use within 60 days before surgery was compared with no advanced therapy. The primary outcome was anastomotic leak and/or organ space surgical site infection (AL/OSSI) within 30 days. Inverse probability of treatment weighting with institutional clustering was used to adjust for baseline differences. Among 1,150 patients, 740 (64%) received advanced therapy. After weighting, AL/OSSI occurred in 2.43% of patients receiving advanced therapy vs 6.46% without advanced therapy (absolute risk difference -4.03%; RR 0.38, 95% CI 0.19-0.75; p=0.01). No statistically significant differences were observed in superficial surgical site infection, deep incisional surgical site infection, or wound dehiscence. Firth penalized logistic regression demonstrated a concordant association (OR 0.46, 95% CI 0.24-0.90; p=0.02). Point estimates favored advanced therapy across examined subgroups, with no statistically significant interactions. Preoperative advanced therapy use was associated with lower 30-day AL/OSSI without statistically significant increases in other reported infectious or wound complications among patients with Crohn's disease undergoing elective colorectal surgery. These findings support the safety of preoperative advanced therapy continuation while warranting confirmation of the observed association with improved anastomotic outcomes.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Dihydroartemisinin (DHA), an active derivative of artemisinin, has anti-tumour potential, but its immunomodulatory effects in Colorectal Cancer (CRC) remain insufficiently defined. We investigated whether DHA suppresses CRC phenotypes in association with JAK2/STAT3 inhibition and altered immune-checkpoint- marker expression. HCT116 and RKO CRC cells were evaluated using CCK-8, colony formation, wound healing, Transwell migration, live/dead staining, qRT-PCR, western blotting, and pharmacological rescue assays. A total of 20 male C57BL/6 mice (6-8 weeks old; 22-25 grams) with AOM/DSS-induced CRC were allocated to control and DHA-treatment groups (n = 10 per group) to assess tumour burden, pathway-associated markers, checkpoint-marker expression and CD8+ cell presence in tumour tissue. DHA reduced JAK2/STAT3 signalling and PD-L1/CD47 expression; these effects were partly counteracted by Coumermycin A1. in vivo, DHA reduced tumour burden, improved histological differentiation, reduced Ki-67, JAK2/STAT3, PD-L1 and CD47 staining, and was associated with increased intratumoural CD8+ cell staining. DHA suppresses CRC progression in the models studied and modulates JAK2/STAT3-associated immune-evasion markers. These data support further preclinical evaluation of DHA as a potential adjunctive strategy for CRC.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Systemic sclerosis (SSc), or scleroderma, is a multisystem disorder characterised by cutaneous and visceral fibrosis, uncommonly presenting as scleroderma renal crisis (SRC), a life-threatening complication involving renal failure, microangiopathy and hypertension. Paraneoplastic SSc is a rare manifestation of malignancy. We report an unusual case of radiologically suspected colorectal cancer recurrence presenting with paraneoplastic SSc complicated by SRC in a 61-year-old female treated for stage IIIC colorectal adenocarcinoma 22 months earlier. Serology revealed elevated antinuclear and anti-RNA polymerase III antibodies with thrombotic microangiopathy. Computed tomography demonstrated findings suspicious for malignancy recurrence. Given rapid onset, advanced age and suspected cancer recurrence, paraneoplastic SSc was favoured following multidisciplinary consultation. Due to poor performance status and renal dysfunction, best supportive care was pursued. Anticancer therapy and tissue biopsy were deferred. Paraneoplastic features did not resolve, and the patient died six months after presentation. This case underscores the need for further research into malignancy-associated autoimmunity.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Anastomotic leak (AL) is among the most feared complications of gastrointestinal surgery, but its psychological consequences are poorly characterised. Embase, PubMed, and Scopus were searched to June 2026 for studies of adults undergoing gastrointestinal anastomosis that reported psychological or mental health-related quality-of-life outcomes by leak status. Findings were synthesised without meta-analysis using vote counting based on the direction of effect, with risk of bias assessed by the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale and certainty by GRADE and GRADE-CERQual. Twenty-six studies (more than 5800 patients) were included. Within 12 months of surgery, AL was associated with worse global quality of life in 8 of 8 studies with an extractable direction, worse role and social function in 6 of 7, and worse emotional function in 5 of 7; in the largest prospective cohort, AL was associated with clinically relevant deterioration at 6 months (odds ratio 3.65, 95% CI 1.62 to 8.21). Beyond 12 months, most comparisons still favoured patients without leak, but differences were small and imprecise, emotional findings were mixed, and the only study using a dedicated distress scale found no excess distress. Bowel dysfunction was the most consistent harm. Certainty was low for early functional impairment and bowel dysfunction and very low for psychological distress and later outcomes. Anastomotic leak appears to impose a psychological burden concentrated in the first postoperative year. Structured screening during this period is a reasonable practical consideration, and a leak-specific patient-reported outcome measure is needed.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Platelets, traditionally recognized as core components of the coagulation system, have emerged as critical regulators in the multistep progression of colorectal cancer (CRC) beyond their hemostatic functions. Accumulating evidence demonstrates that platelets orchestrate a multidimensional network to promote CRC initiation, proliferation, invasion, metastasis, and immune escape through direct interactions with tumor cells, modulation of the tumor microenvironment, and regulation of angiogenic processes. Two key platelet surface molecules, P-selectin (CD62P) and C-type lectin-like receptor-2 (CLEC- 2), serve as central hubs in these pro-tumorigenic cascades: CD62P mediates platelet-tumor cell aggregation, extravasation, and immunosuppressive macrophage polarization, while CLEC-2 interacts with its ligand podoplanin (PDPN) to drive platelet activation, tumor cell epithelial-mesenchymal transition, and cancer-associated thrombosis. In-depth research into their mechanisms of action is of great significance for the development of targeted therapeutic drugs for colorectal cancer.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
In vivo pretargeting based on the inverse electron-demand Diels-Alder reaction between a trans-cyclooctene (TCO)-modified monoclonal antibody (mAb) and a radiolabeled tetrazine (Tz) is a highly effective approach for reducing radiation burden in nuclear imaging and therapy. However, the large size and slow pharmacokinetics of full-length immunoglobulins greatly hinder their bloodstream clearance. To circumvent this limitation of pretargeting, much effort has been put towards developing masking or clearing agents: molecules designed to be injected prior to the radioligand to rid the bloodstream of excess circulating TCO-mAbs via clearance organs. Yet even with the use of previously established clearing agents, high levels of TCO-mAb still remain in circulation. Moreover, some of these agents could lead to aggregate formation in the lungs or clogs in the bloodstream. Recently, a novel class of cell-surface protein degraders called lysosome-targeting chimeras (LYTACs) have been reported to simultaneously bind hepatocytic-expressed asialoglycoprotein receptor (ASGPR) and a harmful, disease-relevant protein, internalizing the latter for lysosomal degradation. Herein, we present a novel ASGPR-targeted tetrazine-bearing LYTAC  TriGalNAc-Tz (LYTAC-Tz)  as a clearing agent for pretargeting. First, the essential components of the pretargeted system were synthesized: LYTAC-Tz, a TCO-modified variant of the mAb CC49 (TCO-CC49), and an 111In-labeled DOTA-bearing Tz ([111In]In-DOTA-Tz). Then, LYTAC-Tz was evaluated in vivo for its efficacy as a clearing agent for pretargeting in a murine model of colorectal cancer. SPECT-CT images and ex vivo biodistribution data revealed that LYTAC-Tz resulted in lower blood activity levels than control cohorts along with higher tumor-to-blood ratios. Healthy organs boasted low activity levels (excluding the kidneys, which showed uptake due to their rapid excretion of excess radioligand). Ultimately, this work illustrates that LYTAC-Tzs are effective clearing agents and could be beneficial for reducing radiotoxicity in pretargeted systems.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Distant-stage incidence and cancer-specific mortality describe different aspects of cancer burden. We compared their long-term population trends across 10 solid cancers in the United States. Age-adjusted distant-stage incidence from the Surveillance, Epidemiology, and End Results (SEER) Program 17 Registries database (SEER17) and national cancer-specific mortality were analyzed for 2004-2023 using Joinpoint regression. Primary incidence models omitted 2020; mortality models retained 2020. Both endpoints were also analyzed over a common 2004-2019 window. Endpoint direction was defined from the 95% confidence interval for average annual percentage change (AAPC). Relative survival and incidence-based mortality were complementary analyses. Among 5,545,600 incident cancers, 1,060,790 were diagnosed at distant stage. Breast cancer, prostate cancer, and melanoma had increasing distant-stage incidence with declining mortality; lung and colorectal cancers declined in both endpoints; pancreatic, liver and intrahepatic bile duct, and uterine cancers increased in both; and kidney and renal pelvis and stomach cancers had no clear incidence change with declining mortality. All 10 paired patterns were unchanged in the common 2004-2019 window. One- and 3-year distant-stage relative survival increased for all cancers, and all 20 primary survival contrasts remained significant after Benjamini-Hochberg adjustment. The relation between distant-stage incidence and cancer-specific mortality differed by cancer site and was unchanged in a common pre-pandemic window. Distant-stage incidence is best interpreted alongside, rather than as a substitute for, population mortality.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Bipolar disorder affects 1.3 million people in the United Kingdom. People with bipolar disorder are less likely, than the general population to attend and/or complete cancer screening. To explore the barriers and facilitators towards thinking about, and/or completing cervical, breast and colorectal screening by people with bipolar disorder. Semi-structured interviews with 27 people living with bipolar disorder in the North-East and Cumbria (January 2023 to June 2023). Deductive thematic analysis was completed using the constructs of Normalisation Process Theory (NPT). NPT was used to ensure recommendations from the study were developed through an implementation lens. Participants with bipolar disorder highlighted how their mental health influenced their decision to complete cancer screening, or not. Most participants understand what screening was and why it was important to complete screening. However, they described barriers such as anxiety, forgetfulness and fear in completing screening. As well as systemic barriers such as appointments not being at a good time, unfamiliar screening locations and discomfort in waiting rooms were also specifically highlighted for cervical and breast screening. Whilst for colorectal screening, home testing kits were seen as useful, participants felt unsupported in completing the kit, and feared completing the kit wrongly. The identification of barriers and facilitators to cancer screening has highlighted a clear need to increase awareness and providing tailored support for people with bipolar disorder. Offering multiple screening options could further improve screening participation among the group.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
To evaluate the utility of transabdominal ultrasound in children with colorectal pathology (anorectal malformation, functional constipation and Hirschsprung's disease) to assess the outcome of bowel management. Collect data to calculate age-dependent cut-offs of the transrectal diameter (TRD) in children with faecal load. Prospective cohort study with subgrouping for a-/symptomatic patients and a healthy control group. Derived control group for adjusting sex-ratio in patients with Hirschsprung's disease (4:1 ratio for male to female). 380 patients during a 31-month period were included. The transrectal diameter was measured routinely during the bowel management program after 1/3/6 months. Treatment options were oral laxatives, transanal irrigation or combination of both. For calculation of an age-dependent TRD cut-off, receiver operating characteristic, linear regression and locally estimated scatterplot smoothing were determined. The cut-off value was chosen based on a positive likelihood ratio > 10. Diagnostic accuracy was evaluated by the area under the curve, sensitivity and specificity. In the symptomatic subgroups of all cohorts the median values of TRD were significantly elevated compared to asymptomatic subgroups or control groups (p < 0.001). Successful bowel management had a large to very large effect on the TRD (Cohen's d = 1.05 - 1.81) and mean values were significantly lower (p = 0.015 - 0.001). TRD and age showed a minor association with a non-linear positive trend without significant influence after age stratification. Receiver operating characteristics determined a collective cut-off for all cohorts of 2.985 cm in children ≥ 1 year old (positive likelihood ratio = 36.09; sensitivity = 81.92 %; specificity = 97.73 %; area under the curve = 0.91 (95%-CI 0.87 - 0.94); accuracy = 88.67 %). Measuring the TRD is a radiation-free alternative method to assess faecal loading and monitoring response to bowel management in patients with colorectal pathology. TRD was consistently increased in symptomatic patients and decreased following successful treatment. Diagnostic thresholds were close to 3 cm across all cohorts, with good diagnostic performance. This study extends patient cohorts for transabdominal ultrasound and supports further multicentre validation of a standardized ultrasound protocol. Not applicable.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Colorectal cancer (CRC) survivors experience persistent challenges that negatively affect health-related quality of life (HRQoL). While mobile health (mHealth) may offer a useful approach to survivorship care, limited user involvement and scarcity of structured programs in developing countries remain barriers. This study aimed to co-design and evaluate the feasibility of an mHealth survivorship program for CRC survivors following primary treatment. A mixed-methods study was conducted in two phases. Phase 1 utilized a user-centered design framework involving 12 co-designers across nine online sessions to develop and refine the FORYOU mHealth program. Phase 2 was a pilot randomized controlled trial (RCT) with 30 CRC survivors to assess feasibility and preliminary effectiveness of the 12-week program, measured by HRQoL outcomes. In phase 1, the co-designed program indicated above-average usability (System Usability Scale ≥ 68) and adequate acceptability (E-Acceptability Scale ≥ 24). In phase 2, the adherence rate was 73.3%; participants in the intervention group completed an average of 5.4 out of 6 sessions and accessed the app 9.7 times. Although no significant between-group difference was observed in overall HRQoL, exploratory findings were mixed. The intervention favored the subscale functional well-being (P < 0.05; g = 1.34), whereas the control group favored the secondary outcome, fatigue. These preliminary findings require cautious interpretation. The co-designed mHealth program was usable and acceptable, and the pilot RCT was feasible among CRC survivors after primary treatment. Exploratory findings suggested possible benefits in selected outcomes, but these preliminary findings require confirmation in a larger adequately powered trial. This co-designed mHealth survivorship program showed encouraging engagement among CRC survivors after primary treatment, with exploratory findings suggesting potential effects on selected survivorship outcomes. Trial registration NCT07158671 on ClinicalTrials.gov. Registered on September 8, 2025.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Depression is common among colorectal cancer (CRC) survivors and may involve heterogeneous symptom domains. We examined age- and sex-related differences in indicators of motivational anhedonia, consummatory anhedonia, and negative affect during survivorship and compared them with a frequency-matched normative population. Data were obtained from 471 CRC survivors in the population-based PROCORE study. Indicators were assessed 12 and 24 months after diagnosis. Linear mixed-effects models examined associations of age, sex, and their interaction over time. A frequency-matched normative sample (n = 260) served as a comparison group. Overall symptom levels were comparable between CRC survivors and normative participants, except for higher HADS-D scores among survivors at 24 months. Significant Age × Sex interactions were observed for all three indicators. Motivational and consummatory anhedonia indicators increased with age among men but not women, whereas emotional functioning improved with age among women but not men, indicating more negative affect among younger women. Direct Group × Age × Sex tests showed differences for emotional functioning at both assessments and for the consummatory anhedonia indicator at 24 months, but not for motivational anhedonia. Motivational anhedonia increased over time among women of mean age; the other indicators did not change significantly. Age and sex were associated with different patterns across depression-related symptom indicators. Replication is needed, particularly among younger CRC survivors and survivors with clinically significant depressive symptoms. IMPLICATIONS FOR CANCER SURVIVORS: Symptom-level assessment may help characterize heterogeneity in psychological adjustment after CRC, although further research is needed before informing screening or care.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Colorectal cancer (CRC) requires robust biomarkers and therapeutic targets. This study aimed to identify secretome-associated genes with diagnostic, prognostic, and tumor-suppressive relevance in CRC, focusing on GUCA2B (uroguanylin). We integrated single-cell transcriptomics, pseudobulk differential expression, machine learning (ML), multi-omics, and in vitro functional assays (HCT-116 cells). ML consensus feature selection across four algorithms identified 20 shared features from 850 downregulated genes; eight genes, including GUCA2B, were selected by all four models, forming the finalized signature. GUCA2B was markedly reduced in CRC epithelium. A frozen eight-gene logistic model showed an apparent (training-set) AUC of 0.998 in TCGA-COADREAD and maintained discrimination in three independent cohorts (AUC = 0.881-0.974). Reduced GUCA2B expression correlated with adverse survival, promoter hypermethylation, and altered immune infiltration. In vitro, GUCA2B restoration induced intrinsic apoptosis (increased BAX, decreased BCL2), reduced viability, and impaired migration; because GC-C/cGMP dependence was not tested, these effects constitute receptor-mechanism-agnostic proof of concept. In conclusion, GUCA2B represents a candidate epithelial-restricted CRC biomarker and tumor-suppressive gene. While the frozen multi-gene model shows promise for diagnostic stratification and GUCA2B restoration demonstrates preliminary tumor-suppressive activity, the small discovery set (n = 23 pseudobulk samples), moderate feature-selection stability, and single-cell-line validation necessitate cautious interpretation. Prospective clinical validation and in vivo multi-model studies are required before diagnostic or therapeutic application.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Thyroid metastases from colorectal cancer (CRC) are extremely rare and pose a clinical challenge because of their resemblance to primary thyroid neoplasms. Their recognition is essential to avoid diagnostic delays and optimize treatment. We present 3 cases diagnosed at a single center, identified through an institutional review spanning more than 30 years. Two cases were synchronous and 1 was metachronous. Fine-needle aspiration (FNA) demonstrated diagnostic limitations, requiring histologic confirmation in all cases through immunohistochemical positivity for SATB2 and CDX2. Surgical treatment, within a multidisciplinary approach, proved feasible and safe in all patients. These findings highlight the need to include metastatic thyroid involvement in the differential diagnosis of thyroid nodules in patients with a history of malignancy.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Right-sided bowel localizations of deep infiltrating endometriosis (DIE) may be under-recognized preoperatively and are sometimes addressed concomitantly during planned left-sided colorectal surgery. We aimed to assess whether concomitant right-sided bowel procedures are associated with increased early major postoperative morbidity. Retrospective cohort study based on a prospectively maintained institutional database. High-volume tertiary referral endometriosis center (IFEMEndo, Clinique Tivoli-Ducos, Bordeaux, France). Consecutive women undergoing left-sided colorectal surgery for DIE between January 2021 and July 2025. Left-sided colorectal surgery alone (left-only group, n = 898) versus left-sided colorectal surgery with concomitant right-sided bowel procedures (left+right group, n = 160). A total of 1,058 women were included. Early major postoperative morbidity (Clavien-Dindo grade ≥IIIb within 30 days) occurred in 22/160 (13.8%) patients in the left+right group versus 66/898 (7.3%) in the left-only group (p = 0.007), with earlier onset in the combined group (mean postoperative day 9 ± 12 vs. 15 ± 23; p = 0.034). Early pelvic septic complications were also more frequent after left+right surgery (16.3% vs. 8.6%; p = 0.003). In models adjusted for age, BMI, smoking, and prior abdominal surgery, ileocecal resection (ICR) was associated with major morbidity (adjusted OR [aOR] 2.25, 95% CI 1.13-4.21; p = 0.01) and early pelvic septic complications (aOR 2.60, 95% CI 1.29-4.91; p = 0.005). Adjusted absolute risk of septic complications increased from 8.7% (95% CI 6.6-10.9%) without right-sided procedures to 16.3% (8.2-25.9%) with ICR and 22.0% (0.0-44.4%) with two or more right-sided procedures (n = 13). The association between ICR and major morbidity varied significantly according to the extent of left-sided surgery (interaction p = 0.022), with a pronounced association when ICR was added to conservative procedures and an attenuated, non-significant association when added to segmental resection. In women undergoing left-sided colorectal surgery for DIE, concomitant right-sided bowel procedures were associated with higher crude early major morbidity and pelvic septic complications. The association between ICR and major morbidity differed according to the left-sided surgical context, being pronounced with conservative procedures and attenuated with segmental resection. These findings support individualized risk counseling and should be interpreted cautiously given the small number of events in some subgroups.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Endoscopic mucosal resection (EMR) is an effective and safe technique for the management of non-pedunculated colorectal polyps and plays a critical role in colorectal cancer prevention. Traditionally, hot EMR, which incorporates electrocautery after lifting the lesion with submucosal injection, has been the standard approach for resection of larger and more complex lesions. However, increasing recognition of the risks associated with thermal injury-particularly delayed bleeding, perforation, and post-polypectomy syndrome-has driven growing adoption of cold EMR, which relies on mechanical transection without electrocautery. Over the past decade, expanding evidence has demonstrated that cold EMR is highly effective for a wide range of colorectal lesions, particularly sessile serrated lesions (SSLs) and non-pedunculated adenomas up to 20 mm in size, while offering a superior safety profile with lower risk of delayed bleeding and perforation. Hot EMR remains an important and widely utilized resection technique for large (≥20 mm) adenomatous lesions because of its effectiveness, broad availability, and lower recurrence rates compared with cold EMR, although ESD may provide superior en bloc resection and lower recurrence in selected lesions. This narrative review synthesizes current data comparing cold and hot EMR with respect to indications, efficacy, safety, recurrence, and surveillance strategies, and provides a practical, lesion-specific framework for clinical decision-making.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Surgery is the standard treatment for localised colorectal cancer, but its benefit-risk balance is heterogeneous in frail older adults. Evidence describing outcomes when frail patients decline surgery and are managed non-operatively remains limited. This study aimed to describe survival, palliative interventions and healthcare utilisation in frail patients with localised colorectal cancer managed non-operatively within a structured geriatric-oncology pathway. This single-centre prospective cohort study included consecutive adults with non-metastatic colon or rectal cancer and a positive PRISMA-7 frailty screen between 2017 and 2024. Patients underwent comprehensive geriatric assessment, including IF-VIG frailty severity stratification. Outcomes were primarily described among patients who elected non-operative management; a contemporaneous frail surgical cohort was included for contextual comparison. Among 1028 patients assessed for curative-intent treatment, 115 screened positive for frailty: 74 (64.3%) were managed non-operatively and 41 (35.7%) underwent surgery. Mean follow-up was 24.5 months. In the non-operative cohort, 65 of 74 patients (87.8%) died, with a mean overall survival of 28 months. Compared with the surgical cohort, non-operative management was associated with higher mortality (87.8% vs 65.8%; p = 0.008) and shorter survival (28 vs 50 months; p < 0.001). Palliative interventions were required in 62.2% of non-operative patients. Emergency department attendance and hospital admission rates were 0.81 and 0.65 per patient-year, respectively. In frail older adults with localised colorectal cancer, non-operative management after declining surgery was common and associated with shorter survival, frequent palliative interventions and measurable healthcare utilisation. Frailty severity stratification may support realistic surgical decision-making and goal-concordant treatment selection.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Early urinary catheter removal after total mesorectal excision(TME) reduces urinary tract infections but increases the risk of acute urinary retention. Evidence on perioperative use of alpha-blockers in rectal cancer surgery remains limited. This study evaluated whether perioperative Alfuzosin or Silodosin reduces urinary re-catheterization after minimally invasive TME for rectal cancer. A prospective multicentre cohort study(2021-2025) included male patients undergoing minimally invasive TME with low colorectal or coloanal anastomosis. Patients received either Alfuzosin (10 mg daily, day -3 to day +3), Silodosin (8 mg daily, day 0 to day +4), or no alpha-blocker (controls from the GRECCAR 10 trial). The primary endpoint was urinary re-catheterization within hospital stay. Secondary endpoints were catheterization duration, urinary and overall morbidity, and length of hospital stay. Of 311 patients(Alfuzosin, n = 100; Silodosin, n = 100; controls, n = 111), urinary re-catheterization occurred in 4%, 8% and 14%, respectively. Alfuzosin significantly reduced the risk compared with controls (p = 0.016), whereas silodosin had no effect (p = 0.199). Urinary morbidity was lower in both alpha-blocker groups(9% and 8% vs. 18%). Median catheterization duration was 1, 2, and 4 days, and hospital stay was shorter with alpha-blockers (6 and 8 vs.10 days, p < 0.001). In multivariate analysis, Alfuzosin was associated with lower odds of urinary re-catheterization compared with controls (OR 0.27), while diabetes mellitus increased risk (OR 2.68). Perioperative alfuzosin was independently associated with lower urinary re-catheterization rates after minimally invasive TME and may support early catheter removal within enhanced recovery pathways, though randomized evidence is needed.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
National guidelines recommend cross-sectional imaging and serum carcinoembryonic antigen (CEA) assessment for rectal cancer staging. However, the frequency of complete staging immediately before proctectomy remains unclear. We evaluated preoperative staging completion and associated hospital characteristics. This retrospective observational study used 100% Medicare claims to identify patients aged 65-99 years undergoing elective proctectomy for rectal cancer (2016-2023). The primary endpoint was completion of four guideline-recommended staging components within 90 days before surgery. Completion within 180 and 270 days and associations with hospital characteristics were also assessed. Among 10,726 patients treated at 1,584 hospitals, only 20.3% underwent complete staging within 90 days before proctectomy. Individual component completion rates were 57.3% for abdominal imaging, 66.1% for chest imaging, 47.5% for pelvic imaging, and 56.4% for serum CEA. Complete staging increased to 45.0% within 180 days and 51.8% within 270 days. Completion within 90 days was more likely at National Accreditation Program for Rectal Cancer-accredited, teaching, nonrural, and higher-volume hospitals. Only one in five Medicare patients undergoing proctectomy for rectal cancer had all four staging components documented within 90 days before surgery, with substantially higher completion over longer assessment windows. Variation by hospital characteristics identifies potential targets for quality improvement. These findings support clearer guidance on the timing of preoperative staging and standardized assessment of staging completion.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Despite advances of biomimetic vesicles in cancer therapy, clinical challenges such as biosafety, scalability, and therapeutic efficacy remain significant hurdles. To address these limitations, we reveal the critical tumor-homing motifs of cancer cell membrane vesicles: a synergistic "chemotactic recruitment-adhesion anchoring" cascade effect, especially chemokine axes (e.g., CXCL12/CXCR4) and integrins (e.g., αVβ3). In this study, we identify autologous fibroblasts as an ideal "chassis" cell for engineering biomimetic carriers. Using this platform, we construct multigene-engineered fibroblast-derived nanovesicles (X-Fb-MNVs) coexpressing critical chemokine receptor CXCR4 and adhesion ligand iRGD, as well as PD-1 and CD47 protein, which achieved robust and broad-spectrum tumor targeting across breast, liver, pancreatic, and colon cancer PDX models. Significantly, CD47-modified X-Fb-MNVs reduced hepatic accumulation and phagocytic clearance, thereby minimizing off-target effects in vivo and improving tumor targeting efficiency. By loading diABZI STING agonist into X-Fb-MNVs with overexpressed PD-1, our system activates both T cell and innate immunity, reversing ICB resistance and achieving 83.3% survival with no tumor recurrence and long-term immune surveillance over 90 d, whereas no mice survived with free diABZI treatment. By merging multimodal targeting, immune reprogramming, and scalable production into a single platform, X-Fb-MNVs represent a remarkable biomimetic system with transformative potential for a wide-spectrum cancer immunotherapy.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Participation in Australia's National Bowel Cancer Screening Program (NBCSP) remains low in some ethnic minority communities. Support from adult children may help overcome barriers, particularly for parents with chronic disease. To examine the association between parental chronic disease and adult children's encouragement of, and practical help, with parents' colorectal cancer (CRC) screening, and variation by ethnicity. In April 2025, a quota-based cross-sectional online survey of 1,025 adult children in Australia (Anglo-Australian, n = 210; Chinese, n = 205; Vietnamese, n = 200; Arab, n = 198; Indian, n = 212) assessed (1) encouragement of their parents to use the faecal immunochemical test (FIT) (n = 1,025) and (2) practical help to their parents with completing the FIT among those whose parent had completed screening (n = 719). Parental chronic disease was defined as offspring-reported longstanding health conditions. Separate multivariable logistic regression models were fitted for each outcome, and ethnicity-by-chronic disease interactions were interpreted using adjusted predicted probabilities. Parental chronic disease was associated with higher odds of encouragement (OR = 2.06, 95% CI 1.47-2.87) and practical help (OR = 2.05, 95% CI 1.39-3.04). Compared with Anglo-Australians, Chinese, Arab, and Indian participants had consistently higher adjusted probabilities of both outcomes across parental chronic disease categories. Vietnamese participants showed the largest within-group increase in both outcomes when parental chronic disease was present. Adult children's support was higher among ethnic minority groups than among Anglo-Australians and most strongly associated with parental chronic disease among Vietnamese participants. Integrating family-engaged screening support within chronic disease care and tailoring approaches for specific communities may reduce inequities in CRC screening participation.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Obesity and type 2 diabetes (T2D) increase colorectal cancer (CRC) risk, yet the mechanisms linking systemic metabolic dysfunction to carcinogenesis are usually considered independently. I propose that metabolic disease can act as an ecosystem engineer, altering the selective conditions in which neoplastic cells emerge and evolve. Nutrient availability, adipose dysfunction, metabolic-epigenetic coupling, immunometabolic rewiring, microbial remodeling, and bile acid metabolism interact across the colonic environment, redistributing metabolic fitness among epithelial, immune, and microbial populations. These interactions may establish a self-reinforcing ecosystem that favors metabolically adaptable clones and reduces constraints on their persistence. Metabolic dysfunction may thus alter which cellular populations can most effectively exploit available resources and evade antitumor surveillance. This hypothesis predicts that tumors with similar molecular characteristics may exist within biologically distinct environments according to the host metabolic state, and therefore could show differential responses to immune activity and therapy. Integrating systemic metabolic parameters, including adiposity distribution, insulin resistance, glycemic control, circulating metabolites, and microbial features, with molecular tumor classification could reveal distinct CRC ecological states and host-tumor dependencies. Such metabolic stratification could generate opportunities for personalized prevention and therapy by identifying vulnerabilities that remain obscured by current tumor-centric classification.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Restorative proctocolectomy with ileal pouch-anal anastomosis (IPAA) is the gold-standard treatment for ulcerative colitis and familial adenomatous polyposis. Pelvic radiation for co-existing malignancies has been associated with pouch complications, yet guidance is still limited. This review synthesized current evidence on effects of pelvic radiation in patients with IPAA. A systematic search of Embase, MEDLINE, and Scopus was conducted in February 2025 using IPAA and pelvic-radiation terms. Eligible studies included patients who underwent IPAA and received pelvic radiation before or after surgery, and reported a pouch-related clinical outcome. Twelve studies (2004-2024) met inclusion criteria, comprising 101 patients who received radiation (83 external beam radiation therapy [EBRT], 18 brachytherapy). The pooled pouchitis rate was 28% (95% CI, 24%-34%). Complications were more common when radiation was delivered after IPAA than before: pouchitis occurred in 53.7% versus 7.7%, and pouch failure in 39.0% versus 3.8%. Brachytherapy was associated with numerically lower pouchitis (16.7% versus 25.3%) and pouch failure (11.1% versus 18.1%) rates than EBRT; however, differences were not statistically significant. Pelvic radiation in patients with IPAA is associated with adverse outcomes. Radiation timing and modality should be considered when balancing oncologic benefit against pouch function.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Venous thromboembolism (VTE) is a significant source of morbidity in patients undergoing colectomy and proctectomy for colorectal adenocarcinoma. However, the association between cancer stage and VTE risk is unclear. We aimed to describe the association between colorectal cancer stage and post-operative VTE among patients undergoing resection for colorectal cancer. Utilizing the 2022-2023 American College of Surgeons National Surgical Quality Improvement Program database, a retrospective cohort study was conducted. A multivariable logistic regression analyzed the association between VTE and cancer stage with adjustments for covariates. Of 18,830 patients fitting inclusion criteria, 4,418 (23%) had stage I adenocarcinoma, 6,509 (35%) had stage II, 6,402 (34%) had stage III and 1,501 (8%) had stage IV; while 302 (2%) experienced postoperative VTE. On univariate analysis, patients with stage II, III and IV cancers had higher VTE rates than patients with stage I (stage I: 0.9%, stage II: 1.7%, stage III: 1.8%: stage IV 2.5%; p < 0.001). In the multivariable analysis of VTE risk, patients with stage II, III and IV cancer had higher odds of VTE relative to patients with stage I cancer (OR for stage II vs. I: 1.57; 95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.08, 2.27; p = 0.017; OR for stage III vs. I: 1.77; 95% CI: 1.22, 2.55; p = 0.002; OR for stage IV vs. I: 1.73, 95% CI:1.07, 2.79; p = 0.025). Resectable colorectal cancers at higher stages are associated with increased risk of VTE. Understanding the differences in risk can help clinicians make more informed and targeted treatment plans for patients undergoing colectomy or proctectomy for locoregional adenocarcinoma.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Long-term fecal continence and bowel habit outcomes remain a significant challenge in pediatric colorectal surgery. This study evaluated long-term functional bowel outcomes in patients treated for Hirschsprung disease (HD) and Anorectal Malformations (ARM) using the standardized Rintala Bowel Function Score, identifying key clinical predictors of favorable outcomes. A retrospective cross-sectional study was conducted at St. Paul's Hospital Millennium Medical College, Addis Ababa, Ethiopia, among children who underwent definitive surgical repair for HD and ARM between January 2018 and December 2022. Functional bowel outcomes were evaluated using the Rintala Bowel Function Score (0-20 scale), with a score ≥ 17 defined as a clinically favorable outcome. Multivariable logistic regression was utilized to assess predictive factors. A total of 136 patients were included: 94 with HD and 42 with ARM. In the HD cohort, the presence of associated congenital anomalies and colonic excision proximal to the splenic flexure were major negative predictors of bowel function, reducing the probability of a favorable outcome from 66 to 22% (p = 0.007) and from 75 to 28% (p = 0.008), respectively. In the ARM cohort, 100% of patients with low-severity malformations achieved favorable outcomes compared with 54.5% of those with high/intermediate-severity malformations (p = 0.004). While anatomical severity appears to be an important factor influencing bowel function outcomes in ARM, associated systemic anomalies and the extent of colonic excision were also associated with poorer bowel function in children with HD. These findings highlight the potential importance of structured, long-term postoperative follow-up, with particular attention to children at higher risk of functional bowel problems.
