ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Laparoscopic abdominoperineal resection (LAPR) is widely assumed non-inferior to open APR (OAPR), yet existing evidence derives from small retrospective series or randomised trials that pre-labelled patients as "definite APR" before surgery-thereby sacrificing any opportunity for intra-operative sphincter preservation and compromising patient autonomy. This post-hoc emulation of the LASRE trial compared successful resection rates and 3-year oncological outcomes between LAPR and OAPR using a "randomise-to-route, decide-at-surgery" design that preserves sphincter-saving options. Adults with rectal cancer ≤ 5 cm from the dentate line enrolled in the multicentre LASRE RCT (22 Chinese Centres, 2013-2018) were randomised 2:1 to laparoscopic or open resection; the final decision to perform APR was made intra-operatively. The primary endpoints were successful resection (complete or near-complete total mesorectal excision plus a circumferential resection margin ≥ 1 mm) and 3-year local recurrence (LR). Sensitivity analyses comprised as-treated and conversion-excluded sets, multivariable adjustment, and formal interaction testing. Of 321 patients whose final operation was APR (215 LAPR, 106 OAPR), baseline characteristics were balanced except age (58 vs 57 years, P = 0.048) and clinical stage I (43.7% vs 29.3%, P = 0.012). Successful resection was achieved less frequently with LAPR (89.1% vs 96.6%, P = 0.038). Three-year LR was higher after LAPR (8.1% vs 1.9%; HR 4.445, 95% CI 1.027-19.240; P = 0.029), and this association persisted in as-treated and conversion-excluded sensitivity analyses (HR 4.66 and 4.52, respectively), whereas 3-year disease-free survival (76.3% vs 73.4%; HR 0.888, 95% CI 0.558-1.413; P = 0.616) and overall survival (89.3% vs 89.5%; HR 1.019, 95% CI 0.494-2.102; P = 0.959) did not differ. LAPR reduced blood loss (50 vs 100 mL, P < 0.001), 30-day morbidity (13.7% vs 24.5%, P = 0.017) and perineal wound infection (6.2% vs 13.2%, P = 0.034). In this post-hoc analysis, even among credentialed surgeons, LAPR was associated with short-term recovery benefits but lower successful-resection rates and a higher observed rate of 3-year local recurrence. These findings represent a local-control signal rather than definitive evidence of overall oncological inferiority, and require validation before any change in practice. Parent trial: ClinicalTrials.gov NCT01899547.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Colorectal cancer (CRC) is the second leading cause of cancer death in the United States, with persistent disparities in screening rates. We examined racial and ethnic disparities in provider recommendations for CRC screening tests and screening uptake among U.S. adults eligible for screening using cross-sectional data from the 2019, 2021, and 2023 National Health Interview Survey (NHIS). Participants included adults aged 50-75 in 2019/2021 and 45-75 in 2023 (N=39,771). Primary outcomes were self-reported provider recommendation in the past 12 months and up-to-date status with guideline-concordant screening. In fully adjusted models accounting for socioeconomic factors and insurance, Hispanic (aOR, 0.68; 95% CI, 0.56-0.82), non-Hispanic Black (aOR, 0.81; 95% CI, 0.67-0.98), and non-Hispanic Asian adults (aOR, 0.50; 95% CI, 0.38-0.66) were significantly less likely than non-Hispanic White adults to receive recommendations. Odds of being up to date were lower for Hispanic (aOR, 0.84; 95% CI, 0.75-0.93), Asian (aOR, 0.59; 95% CI, 0.51-0.68), and American Indian/Alaska Native adults (aOR, 0.73; 95% CI, 0.55-0.96). Difference-in-differences analysis confirmed that the 2021 recommendations change increased provider recommendations by 13.4 percentage points among 45-49 year-olds. Persistent disparities in recommendation patterns highlight the need for targeted interventions to improve equity.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Higher cardiorespiratory fitness (CRF) is associated with a lower risk of cancer and mortality after diagnosis. However, mortality data are generally not specific to cancer sites or causes of death, limiting insights into the underlying mechanisms and opportunities for targeted prevention and survivorship strategies. This study aimed to examine the association between CRF and site-specific cancer incidence and mortality after diagnosis in men. This cohort study used data from the Cooper Center Longitudinal Study (1971-2018) linked to Medicare claims (1999-2019). CRF was estimated using a maximal treadmill test. The associations between CRF and site-specific cancer incidence and death after cancer for the leading cancer sites in men (colorectal, lung, and prostate) were estimated using multivariable illness-death models and proportional hazards regression with Gompertz baseline hazards. Among 28,612 men with a mean Medicare follow-up of 7.9 years to cancer incidence, 4,998 colorectal, lung, and prostate cancers were identified. Higher CRF was associated with a lower risk of colorectal (HR: 0.91 per metabolic equivalent of task [MET]; 95% CI: 0.87, 0.96) and lung cancer (HR: 0.81 per MET; 95% CI: 0.77, 0.85), but not prostate cancer. During a mean follow-up of 7.1 years to death after diagnosis of colorectal, lung, or prostate cancer, 1,549 deaths were identified. High- (vs. low-) fit men with colorectal, lung, or prostate cancer had a 33-41% lower likelihood of all-cause mortality, including a generally lower risk of death from cardiovascular disease and other non-cancer causes. Achieving higher CRF levels may contribute to cancer prevention and longer survival after diagnosis. Interventions that increase CRF through physical activity may improve health across the cancer control continuum.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Cryoablation is a minimally invasive thermal ablation modality that destroys tumor cells through intracellular ice crystal formation and osmotic injury. Although it offers theoretical advantages, its application in recurrent papillary thyroid cancer (PTC) remains limited, and the radiologic-pathologic findings of treatment response have not been well characterized. A 55-year-old male patient with biopsy-proven recurrent PTC in the left supraclavicular fossa and a history of total thyroidectomy, neck dissection, and advanced colorectal cancer underwent a single-session ultrasound-guided cryoablation. The 20-minute procedure was completed without complications. Immediately post-ablation, the lesion volume increased by over 200% with marked hypoechogenicity and obliteration of abnormal feeding vessels on microvascular imaging. Pathology demonstrated disrupted tumor cell membranes, necrotic changes, and myxoid peritumoral stromal alteration, consistent with direct and indirect injuries caused by cryoablation. At the first-month follow-up, repeat biopsy showed no viable tumor, with subacute inflammatory infiltrates, histiocytic aggregates, and progressive fibrosis. On ultrasound, a volume reduction rate of 71.4% was achieved at one month follow-up and 97.1% at three months follow-up. This case report provides the first radiologic-pathologic findings of both immediate and delayed effects of cryoablation in recurrent PTC, supporting its role as a promising minimally invasive palliative therapy.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
The prognostic significance of programmed cell death ligand 1 (PD-L1) in colorectal adenocarcinoma remains unclear. We evaluated the clinicopathological and prognostic relevance of the PD-L1 combined positive score (CPS). This single-center retrospective cohort included 124 patients with histopathologically confirmed colorectal adenocarcinoma; PD-L1 was assessed by CPS. Disease-free survival (DFS) and overall survival (OS) were evaluated using Kaplan-Meier methods and parsimonious Cox regression, and early recurrence within 12 months of curative-intent treatment with a truncated Cox model. Higher CPS was significantly associated with nodal stage (p = .012), lymphovascular invasion (p = .006), and tumor necrosis (p = .047). CPS correlated very strongly with immune-cell PD-L1 (rho = 0.945, p < .001) and strongly with tumor-cell PD-L1 (rho = 0.853, p < .001). CPS >5 remained associated with favorable DFS in a prespecified parsimonious multivariable model (adjusted hazard ratio [HR], 0.17; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.04 to 0.75; p = .019). No PD-L1 metric was significantly associated with OS; however, CPS showed a numerically favorable but non-significant trend (adjusted HR, 0.17; 95% CI, 0.02 to 1.30; p = .088). In the exploratory early recurrence analysis, CPS >5 was associated with a lower risk of early recurrence in a model adjusted only for nodal stage (adjusted HR, 0.21; 95% CI, 0.05 to 0.94; p = .042). PD-L1 CPS may serve as a complementary, hypothesis-generating prognostic marker in colorectal adenocarcinoma, particularly for disease-free survival. However, the lack of mismatch repair (MMR)/microsatellite instability (MSI) data prevents definitive conclusions regarding an MMR/MSI-independent prognostic effect. Further validation in larger, prospectively collected, multicenter cohorts with comprehensive molecular annotation is required.

Colorectal cancer (CRC) remains a global threat that has yet to be conquered, and this challenge is compounded by the rising worldwide incidence of early-onset CRC (EO-CRC), diagnosed before age 50. Most EO-CRC cases are sporadic and microsatellite-stable, and their etiology has yet to be fully elucidated. "Mutational epidemiology," which applies whole-genome sequencing to decode mutational signatures imprinted in tumor genomes, has emerged as a powerful tool for tracing carcinogen exposures. A key discovery is colibactin, a genotoxic metabolite produced by Escherichia coli and other Enterobacteriaceae carrying the pks pathogenicity island, which generates unique mutational signatures, SBS88 and ID18. Large-scale CRC genomic surveys, including the Mutographs Cancer Grand Challenge, show that regions with higher CRC incidence carry greater colibactin-signature burden, and that Japanese patients, particularly those with EO-CRC, show the highest prevalence worldwide, approximately 50%. ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Covalent organic frameworks (COFs) offer an attractive platform for organizing nanophotosensitizers into ordered architectures for improving photodynamic therapy (PDT). However, the photochemical performance of conventional porphyrin-based frameworks has largely been constrained by their limited optical absorption at longer wavelength and inefficient generation of reactive oxygen species (ROS). Herein, we report the first highly crystalline nanoscale COFs (nCOFs) incorporating reduced porphyrin units, chlorins, and bacteriochlorins, which exhibit markedly modulated light absorption photophysical activity and PDT efficacy. Chlorin- and bacteriochlorin-based nCOFs (Ctp and Btp) were prepared via imine condensation of high-purity monomers under oxygen- and light-free conditions at room temperature, affording long-range crystalline order while preserving the intrinsic optical properties of the reduced chromophores. Compared to porphyrin-based COF, Btp exhibited pronounced bathochromic shifts with strong absorption in the 640-750 nm region and substantially enhanced ROS generation under 705 and 808 nm laser irradiation. In Ctp- and Btp-mediated PDT, the photocytotoxicity toward MC38 cancer cells was significantly enhanced, with potent antitumor efficacy in a murine colorectal tumor model. This study establishes reduced porphyrin as a viable building block for highly crystalline COFs and highlights the potential of ordered chromophore engineering for expanding the photochemical functionality of nCOFs.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
The global burden of colorectal cancer(CRC)is rising. Early diagnosis and treatment are crucial for improving survival. Although advances in endoscopic techniques have improved the evaluation of tumor characteristics and invasion depth, no single method can accurately determine lesion depth in all cases. Therefore, this study aims to develop a more accurate approach for identifying patients suitable for endoscopic treatment. A total of 339 patients with 387 superficial CRC lesions were enrolled at Liaocheng Hospital, China. Lesions were classified as superficial cancer (high-grade dysplasia, mucosal carcinoma, or submucosal invasion < 1000 μm) or deep submucosal cancer (> 1000 μm). Demographic, tumor, treatment, and complication data were collected. For patients with multiple lesions, the single most advanced lesion (the index lesion), prioritizing depth of invasion and tumor size, was selected for analysis. Associations between potential risk factors and invasion depth were assessed using univariate and multivariate logistic regression analyses. A nomogram was then developed to construct and validate a predictive model for deep submucosal invasion. Among the 339 patients, altered bowel habits (25.37%) and abdominal pain (22.42%) were the most frequently reported clinical symptoms. Significant differences in tumor size, gross morphology, JNET classification, and pit pattern classification were observed between the superficial cancer group and the deep submucosal cancer group (P < 0.05). Multivariate logistic regression analysis demonstrated that a tumor diameter > 20 mm (P = 0.001, OR = 8.652, 95% CI: 2.415-30.981), an infiltrative JNET pattern (P < 0.001, OR = 6.843, 95% CI: 2.215-21.142), and an infiltrative pit pattern (P = 0.002, OR = 7.125, 95% CI: 1.985-25.568) were independently associated with deep submucosal invasion in superficial CRC. A nomogram incorporating these factors was developed as an exploratory predictive model. Lesions displaying a tumor diameter > 20 mm, infiltrative JNET, and infiltrative Pit pattern are strongly associated with deep submucosal infiltration in superficial colorectal carcinoma. The exploratory nomogram incorporating these three factors shows potential as a non-invasive screening tool; however, caution should be exercised, and external validation is required before broad clinical application.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
A flexible three-dimensional surface-enhanced Raman scattering (SERS) platform using a 4-mercaptophenol (4-MP)-modified glass fiber filter membrane (GFF@4MP) for label-free colorectal cancer (CRC) serum discrimination. Silver nanoparticles were uniformly immobilized onto NaCl-modified porous scaffolds. The 4-MP modifier optimized the interfacial microenvironment and provided specific binding sites, improving target adsorption within SERS "hot spots", reducing non-specific interference, and enhancing spatial uniformity (RSD = 7.63%). For clinical serum analysis (internal cohort: 30 CRC/30 healthy controls; external cohort: 21 CRC/21 healthy controls), the GFF@4MP substrate yielded highly discriminative SERS spectra. Coupled with machine learning, the support vector machine (SVM) model achieved an internal test accuracy of 93.3% (95% CI: 89.2-97.5%; AUC = 0.99) and maintained a robust external validation accuracy of 85.5% (95% CI: 81.7-89.0%; AUC = 0.92). This interfacial chemical modification strategy enhances SERS stability in complex biofluids, providing a reliable tool for minimally invasive CRC screening.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Despite evidence supporting the role of teleconsultation for surveillance of colorectal cancer (CRC) patients, implementation remains challenging. This study examined the perception, receptibility and acceptance of the care delivery models amongst elderly CRC patients. This mixed methods study involved a self-administered survey on 100 patients who were asked to rank their preferred communication method (physical hospital/general practitioner consultation, telephone and video call) for the various CRC care scenarios (pre-operative counselling, post-operative review, delivering normal/abnormal histology, imaging or blood test/scan results). Semi-structured interviews were conducted with 18 patients to explore reasons for acceptance and non-acceptance. Chi-square analyses revealed that patients were not accepting of teleconsultation for postoperative reviews of major conditions and delivery of abnormal test and/or scan results (all p < .05). However, there were no differences in teleconsultation acceptance for preoperative counselling and postoperative reviews of minor conditions, and more patients were accepting of teleconsultations for delivery of normal histology, imaging scan and blood test results (all p < .001). Content analysis showed that teleconsultation acceptance was mainly due to perceived equivalence in communication modalities as well as convenience, while non-acceptance was due to the limitations of telecommunication. It is evident that patients prefer a face-to-face physical consultation when their surveillance trajectories suggest more serious implications. However, our findings highlighted the opportunity for teleconsultations to be used selectively with particular patients and situations where patient outcomes remain normal. It remains uncertain if this hybrid model for CRC surveillance will be cost-effectiveness and acceptable.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Patient-derived tumor organoids (PDTOs) provide reliable and high-fidelity in vitro models for investigating the mechanisms underlying cancer development and progression, as well as exploring new therapeutic strategies. However, the establishment and culture of PDTOs largely rely on Matrigel, which possesses an ill-defined composition and non-tunable mechanical properties, thereby hindering the standardization, reproducibility, and clinical translation of organoid technology. In this study, a hyaluronic acid-based hydrogel incorporating cell adhesion sites and matrix metalloproteinase (MMP)-responsive degradability was designed for colorectal cancer (CRC) organoid culture. The hydrogel exhibited tunable stiffness within the range of 0.15-2.1 kPa and incorporated an MMP2-responsive peptide crosslinker, providing a favorable microenvironment for the growth of CRC organoids. Organoids cultured in the hydrogel retained the expression of key CRC molecular markers. Transcriptomic analysis further demonstrated that hydrogel-cultured organoids exhibited gene expression profiles highly comparable to those of organoids cultured in Matrigel. Furthermore, hydrogel-cultured organoids maintained their sensitivity to chemotherapy drugs. Collectively, this study provides a well-defined and mechanically tunable hydrogel system as a promising alternative to Matrigel for the culture of patient-derived CRC organoids.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Colorectal cancer (CRC) is a major public health issue in France. Although organized screening enables early detection and reduces the risk of death, participation rates remain below public health targets. Few studies have examined pharmacists' perspectives of CRC screening, even though they play an important role in promoting and distributing tests to eligible asymptomatic patients aged 50 to 74. Determining factors perceived by pharmacists as influencing their patients' participation in the CRC screening in pharmacies, to refine the recommendations intended for them. A mixed-method approach was conducted between May 2024 and March 2025, combining semi-structured telephone interviews and anonymous online questionnaires. Participants were pharmacists from across the Pays de la Loire region in western France. Thematic analysis was used to identify relevant factors from the qualitative data, and multivariable regression was subsequently performed to assess their associations with participation uptake. In total, 30 interviews and 391 questionnaires were completed. Qualitative results identified several factors structured into two groups: patient-related factors (socioeconomic status, health, practical and cognitive aspects) and pharmacy/pharmacist-related factors (work environment, organization and resources, and interprofessional skills). Quantitative analysis showed that higher socioeconomic status (β=104.7, p=0.04), greater confidence in self-care (β=32.3, p=0.02), and well-organized, accessible pharmacies (β=115.1, p=0.02) were associated with increased participation, while patient health problems (β=-19.4, p=0.04), practical barriers (β=-23.2, p=0.03), and limited pharmacists' skills (β=-81.9, p=0.01) were negatively associated. Pharmacists emphasized the importance of addressing emotional hesitation and concerns surrounding the procedure, alongside patient education and awareness, to improve participation in CRC screening. Pharmacists showed a high level of involvement in CRC screening. Strengthening targeted communication and proactive counselling based on patient profiles and implementing practical interventions tailored to pharmacies appear necessary. Such actions may close participation gaps in the future and advance CRC screening public health targets.

Gain/loss-of-function studies were performed in HT29/RKO cells and xenografts. IP-MS, co‑IP, immunofluorescence, cycloheximide chase, inhibitor assays, and ubiquitination assays defined the mechanism. CD8+ T cells were analyzed by flow cytometry and chemokines by ELISA. DUSP4 was preferentially expressed in BRAF V600E‑mutant CRC and associated with nodal (P = 0.005) and distant metastasis (P = 0.019), and shorter overall survival. High DUSP4 independently predicted mortality [HR=2.102, 95%CI 1.395-3.165, P < 0.001]. Overexpression promoted proliferation, migration, and xenograft growth; knockdown produced opposite effects. Mechanistically, DUSP4 reduced PTEN protein stability and activated PI3K-AKT. DUSP4 recruited E3 ligase TRIM27, promoting K48‑linked polyubiquitination and proteasomal degradation of PTEN. TRIM27 manipulation partially rescued DUSP4‑dependent phenotypes. In vitro, DUSP4-overexpressing CRC cells impaired CD8+ T cell function, as evidenced by decreased expression of IFN-γ, GZMB, and CD107a. DUSP4 overexpression was associated with downregulated CXCL9/16, IFN-γ, TNF-α, and IL-2, and upregulated IL-10, effects partially reversed by PTEN overexpression. DUSP4 is preferentially expressed in BRAF V600E-mutant CRC and independently predicts poor prognosis. It promotes tumor progression via a novel TRIM27-PTEN-PI3K-AKT axis, and modulates the immune microenvironment by impairing CD8+ T cell function. DUSP4 may serve as a candidate prognostic biomarker and warrants further investigation as a potential therapeutic target.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Blueberries have long been recognized as a functional food endowed with numerous health benefits. Although there is a growing body of literature evaluating the anticancer properties of blueberries, an updated critical evaluation is necessary to understand the full potential and translational impact of blueberries as sources of bioactive compounds with preclinical anticancer activity. This study provides a critical review of the current preclinical literature regarding the role of blueberries in cancer prevention and intervention, with an understanding of cellular and molecular mechanisms of action. The primary literature for this review was collected through major databases, including PubMed, ScienceDirect, Scopus, and Web of Science. The findings reveal that blueberries, rich in anthocyanins, flavanols, and phenolic acids, have been shown to modulate key signaling pathways, including nuclear factor-κB, phosphoinositide 3-kinase, protein kinase B, and mitogen-activated protein kinase.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
The prognostic significance of enlarged lateral pelvic lymph nodes (LPLNs) in patients with rectal cancer undergoing nonoperative management (NOM) remains unclear. This study evaluated whether pretreatment LPLN enlargement is associated with local regrowth or distant metastasis after NOM. The study retrospectively analyzed 77 patients with low rectal cancer who underwent NOM after radiotherapy-based neoadjuvant treatment between 2014 and 2025. Pretreatment LPLN enlargement was defined as a short-axis diameter of ≥ 7 mm on baseline magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). Local regrowth-free survival (LRFS) and distant metastasis-free survival (DMFS) were evaluated according to pretreatment LPLN enlargement. Pretreatment LPLN enlargement was present in 17 patients (22.1%). Among these patients, the median LPLN short-axis diameter decreased from 8 to 3 mm after treatment. During a median follow-up period of 55 months, local regrowth occurred in 15 patients (19.5%) and distant metastasis in 9 patients (11.7%). Pretreatment LPLN enlargement was not significantly associated with LRFS (hazard ratio [HR], 1.39; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.38-4.05; P = 0.587) but was associated with poorer DMFS (HR, 4.70; 95% CI, 1.24-19.01; P = 0.024). In an exploratory analysis treating local regrowth as a time-dependent covariate, pretreatment LPLN enlargement remained associated with distant metastasis (HR, 4.49; 95% CI, 1.20-16.84; P = 0.026). Pretreatment LPLN enlargement was associated with distant metastasis but not significantly associated with local regrowth in patients undergoing NOM despite substantial nodal regression after neoadjuvant treatment. Pretreatment LPLN enlargement may retain prognostic significance as a marker of metastatic potential in patients selected for NOM.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Large language models may support guideline screening and multidisciplinary tumour board preparation in gastrointestinal oncology, but their performance in postoperative treatment assessment remains insufficiently characterized. To evaluate guideline concordance, tumour board concordance, reproducibility, and discordance patterns of ChatGPT-generated postoperative treatment recommendations in gastrointestinal cancer. Single-centre exploratory cross-sectional study using retrospectively assembled clinical case vignettes assessed by a large language model (ChatGPT). Thirty adult patients with histologically confirmed pancreatic, gastric, or colorectal adenocarcinoma who underwent curative-intent surgery and subsequent multidisciplinary tumour board (MTB) review at a German tertiary referral centre (January 2025-January 2026) were included. Structured vignettes were entered into ChatGPT via a standardised prompt within a controlled guideline environment; each case underwent three independent runs (run-level) with majority voting to derive the decisive treatment recommendation (case-level). The primary outcome was concordance of ChatGPT recommendations with German guideline-based postoperative treatment recommendations on the case-level. Secondary outcomes included concordance with MTB recommendations, reproducibility, cross-guideline comparison, and qualitative characterisation of discordant recommendations (divided in minor or major deviation). ChatGPT-generated majority-vote recommendations were fully concordant with German guideline-based recommendations in 21 of 30 cases (70%). Concordance was higher in pancreatic and gastric cancer (8 of 10 cases [80%] each) than in colorectal cancer (5 of 10 cases [50%]). Multidisciplinary tumour board recommendations demonstrated the same overall concordance rate (21 of 30 cases [70%]). Concordance decreased in clinically advanced disease stages. Cross-classification demonstrated complete guideline concordance in both ChatGPT-generated and tumour board recommendations in 17 of 30 cases (56.7%), whereas major LLM discordance despite guideline-adherent tumour board recommendations was uncommon (1 of 30 cases [3.3%]). In exploratory run-level analysis, 23 of 90 outputs (25.6%) were discordant, comprising 14 (15.6%) major and 9 (10.0%) minor deviations. Complete agreement across repeated runs occurred in 61 of 90 case-guideline combinations (67.8%). ChatGPT-generated treatment recommendations showed relevant but variable concordance with guideline-based and multidisciplinary tumour board recommendations. Discordance clustered in clinically complex treatment situations, supporting a possible role for LLM-based systems in guideline screening and tumour board preparation while requiring expert physician oversight. ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Primary tumours of the jejunum and ileum are uncommon despite the distal small intestine representing most of the length and mucosal surface area of the gastrointestinal tract. Their relative rarity, limited endoscopic accessibility and often non-specific clinical presentation mean that many lesions are diagnosed only after symptoms, complications or surgical resection. This review summarises the principal tumour-forming conditions of the distal small intestine, including developmental heterotopias, hamartomatous and syndromic polyps, benign epithelial precursors, adenocarcinoma, neuroendocrine neoplasms, mesenchymal tumours and lymphoid proliferations. Emphasis is placed on malignant epithelial, neuroendocrine, stromal and haematolymphoid neoplasms, with discussion of their characteristic gross, histological, immunophenotypic and molecular features. Attention is given to diagnostic pitfalls, including pseudoinvasion in Peutz-Jeghers polyps, dysplasia arising in chronic inflammatory or immune dysregulation settings, differences of small intestinal adenocarcinoma from colorectal carcinoma, grading of neuroendocrine tumours and separation of aggressive intestinal T-cell lymphomas from indolent lymphoproliferative disorders. Integrated assessment using morphology, targeted immunohistochemistry and molecular testing is essential for accurate classification, prognostication and therapeutic stratification. Improved endoscopic, imaging and genomic approaches are likely to refine diagnosis and management of these challenging and anatomically remote neoplasms.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Cancer survivors have an elevated cardiovascular disease (CVD) risk. Existing evidence is often limited by cross-sectional designs or single-cancer focus, hindering systematic comparisons across different cancer types. We examined cancer type-specific patterns of association between cardiovascular risk factors and incident CVD. This nationwide cohort study utilized the Korea-Clinical Data Utilization Network for Research Excellence database, including 148,537 survivors of breast, colorectal, gastric, liver, or lung cancers (2012-2021). Primary outcome was incident CVD (ischemic heart disease [IHD] or stroke). Cause-specific Cox models were used to estimate adjusted hazard ratios (aHRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs), with death as a competing risk. Age, hypertension, and diabetes were significant predictors of incident CVD across all cancer types. Heavy smoking was associated with a high CVD risk in survivors of breast (aHR, 1.93; 95% CI, 1.29-2.89) and colorectal cancers (1.42; 1.26-1.60). Severe obesity (body mass index ≥ 30 kg/m²) was associated with a high CVD risk in survivors of breast (1.25; 1.07-1.47) and liver cancers (1.32; 1.03-1.69), and with incident IHD across all cancer types, but most strongly in liver and lung cancers. Incident stroke was more strongly associated with advanced tumor stage (aHR range, 1.59-2.13) than with obesity. Cardiovascular risk factor associations vary by cancer type and CVD subtype, supporting the use of tailored, cancer type-specific risk-reduction strategies in survivorship care. These findings provide an evidence base for cancer-specific cardiovascular risk stratification in survivorship care.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Smoking is associated with poor prognosis and distinct molecular alterations in CRC, but its prognostic significance across different treatment-exposed populations remains unclear. We comprehensively investigated the clinicopathological, genomic, and treatment-specific prognostic significance of smoking in CRC using large public datasets. Clinicopathological, genomic, treatment, and survival data were obtained from the MSK-CHORD 2024 and MSK-IMPACT 50K databases. Patients were classified as smokers or non-smokers. Associations between smoking history, genomic alterations, mutation clonality, and overall survival (OS) were evaluated. Independent prognostic factors were identified using multivariable Cox regression analyses. Smokers were older, more frequently male, and had poorer baseline performance status than non-smokers. Smoking was independently associated with worse OS in the overall cohort and among patients exposed to oxaliplatin-, irinotecan-, and EGFR-targeted therapies, but not among those exposed to VEGF-targeted therapy or immune checkpoint inhibitors. Genomic analyses demonstrated that BRAF mutations and FGFR1 copy number amplifications (CNAs) were significantly enriched in smokers, whereas TCF7L2 mutations were more frequent in non-smokers. Although the overall distribution of BRAF clonality categories differed significantly according to smoking status, this difference was not statistically significant among BRAF-mutant tumors. Smoking history was independently associated with poor prognosis in patients with CRC including among patients exposed to oxaliplatin-, irinotecan-, and EGFR-targeted therapies. Additionally, smokers exhibited distinct genomic characteristics, including higher frequencies of BRAF mutations and FGFR1 CNAs. These findings provide new insights into the clinical and molecular characteristics associated with smoking in CRC and warrant further validation in clinically annotated cohorts.

Prior gabapentin exposure did not significantly impact the incidence of postoperative delirium (OR 1.33 (0.86-2.05)) when the cohort was compared based on prior gabapentin exposure. The use of low dose gabapentin postoperatively is associated with lower incidence of delirium compared to absence of gabapentin. However, the absence of gabapentin in our study is a reflection of baseline vulnerability for delirium. Prior exposure to gabapentin had no influence on incident POD. ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
The expanding medical knowledge of tumour behaviour and advances in imaging, pathology, and therapeutic options require that TNM to be regularly updated. The 9th edition of the Union for International Cancer Control (UICC) TNM Classification of Malignant Tumours was published in 2025 [UICC 9th Edition (2025)] to take effect on January 2026. Updates are performed in collaboration with the AJCC. Not all sites were updated in the 9th edition and were planned to be revised later. The update of cancers of the colon and rectum is reported. The main changes are: clarification on what constituted regional or metastatic nodes (obturator nodes are regional for carcinomas of the rectum), that for low rectal cancer regional lymph nodes include superficial inguinal nodes, the inclusion of tumour deposit (TD's) - discrete tumour nodules in pericolic or perirectal fat as a stage descriptor, and subdivision of M1c into M1c1 (peritoneal only) and M1c2 (peritoneal with other sites). Stage was also updated and details are given below. To distinguish these new revisions from the UICC 9th Edition (2025), they will be designated as 'UICC 9th Edition (Revision 1, 2027)' and abbreviated as 'UICC-9.1.2027'.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Adjuvant chemotherapy (ACT) improves survival in patients with resected stage III and high-risk stage II colon cancer, yet its use in routine clinical practice remains variable. Real-world adherence to guideline-recommended ACT and factors influencing treatment use are not well defined at a population level. In this nationwide population-based study, data from the Netherlands Cancer Registry (2005-2020) were used to identify adults with nonmetastatic colon cancer who underwent surgical resection. Eligibility for ACT was defined as pT4N0 or node-positive disease (pT1-3N+ or pT4N+) according to Dutch guidelines and the available NCR variables. Adherence, defined as initiation of ACT when eligible, and factors associated with it were analyzed, including age, comorbidity, tumor characteristics, hospital type and region, and the urgency of the primary tumor resection. Among 44,471 patients, 22,050 (49.6%) were pathologically eligible for ACT, of whom 12,748 (57.8%) initiated treatment. Among ineligible patients, 2.6% received ACT. Non-adherence was strongly associated with advanced age (29.9% of patients ≥75 without comorbidities received ACT), comorbidity, female sex, right-sided tumors, and non-elective surgery (all p < 0.001). Younger patients were more likely to receive ACT despite pathological ineligibility (p < 0.001). Adherence also varied by hospital type, with lower adherence in teaching and academic hospitals compared with general hospitals (p < 0.001). In this nationwide cohort, guideline-recommended ACT was frequently not delivered to pathologically eligible patients. Adherence was influenced by several patient, tumor and hospital characteristics, highlighting factors associated with variation in guideline-based ACT receipt among colon cancer patients.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
The incidence of early-onset colorectal cancer (eoCRC; <50 years) is rising. Previous studies suggested that eoCRC patients have poorer outcomes than older adults. Whether this reflects distinct tumor biology or differences in stage at diagnosis and treatment patterns remains unclear. We compared clinicopathological features, treatment, and survival of eoCRC with average-onset (ao) and older-onset (oo)CRC in a nationwide cohort. Clinicopathological data of all patients diagnosed with colorectal adenocarcinoma in the Netherlands from 1 January 2016 through 31 December 2022 were retrieved from the Netherlands Cancer Registry (NCR). Patients were categorized as eoCRC, aoCRC (50-69 years), and ooCRC (≥70 years). Multivariable regression and matched analyses were performed to account for established prognostic factors and predictors of treatment response. Among 80,551 patients with CRC, 3917 (5%) were eoCRC, 34,499 (43%) were aoCRC, and 42,135 (52%) were ooCRC. EoCRC patients more often presented with advanced disease (stage III or IV) and left-sided colon or rectal cancer. Five-year relative survival (RS) for eoCRC, aoCRC and ooCRC patients was 70%, 77%, and 69%, respectively (crude excess hazard ratio [EHR] for eoCRC vs. aoCRC 1·32 [95% CI 1·24-1·41]). In patients with mismatch repair proficient (pMMR) stage IV disease, eoCRC was associated with better RS than aoCRC (EHR 0·87 [95% CI 0·80-0·94]), concurrent with more intensive first-line systemic therapy. After matching for disease characteristics and treatment, RS was similar between eoCRC and aoCRC (EHR 1·02 [95% CI 0·91-1·14]), whereas ooCRC patients retained worse survival. The poorer crude survival observed in eoCRC is largely associated with more advanced disease at diagnosis, rather than evidence of intrinsically distinct tumor biology. After accounting for established prognostic factors and factors predicting treatment response, survival of eoCRC and aoCRC patients is similar, challenging the notion that eoCRC constitutes a separate biological disease entity. ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Primary prostatic signet-ring cell carcinoma (SRCC) is exceedingly rare, requiring exclusion of other primaries. A 45-year-old man presented with dysuria and gross hematuria despite a serum PSA of 0.21 ng/mL. Biopsy showed a locally advanced Gleason 5 + 5 adenocarcinoma with signet-ring differentiation and extracellular mucin. Immunohistochemistry revealed an atypical PSA-negative, intestinal-marker-positive phenotype; extended work-up excluded urothelial, colorectal, renal, Müllerian, and gastrointestinal primaries. He received docetaxel, abiraterone/prednisone, intermittent androgen deprivation, and dose-escalated radiotherapy. Local disease remained stable despite bone and nodal lesions suggesting progression. Very low PSA does not exclude prostatic carcinoma; diagnosing this rare entity requires broad clinicopathologic and immunohistochemical evaluation.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Colorectal cancer (CRC) treatments cause immunosuppression, increasing susceptibility to opportunistic infections. Microsporidia are intracellular fungi, but their role during CRC treatment remains unclear. This longitudinal study investigated Microsporidia dynamics in CRC patients and healthy controls. Stool, sputum, and saliva samples were collected from 150 CRC patients preoperatively and at first and third postoperation months, and from 148 healthy controls. Microsporidia were evaluated by microscopy and species-specific real-time PCR, and clinical associations were analyzed. Microsporidia DNA was detected by PCR in 15 of 150 CRC patients (10.0%) preoperatively, compared with 2 of 148 healthy controls (1.35%; p = 0.002), whereas all samples were negative by microscopy. Enterocytozoon bieneusi was the most frequently detected species. A higher detection frequency was observed in patients with advanced-stage disease. During follow-up, the prevalence of Microsporidia DNA was 1.3% (2/149) at the first postoperative month and 6.8% (10/148) at the third postoperative month, when most patients were receiving chemotherapy. In conclusion, Microsporidia DNA was detected more frequently in CRC patients than healthy individuals. Increased postoperative detection may reflect chemotherapy-associated immunosuppression. Molecular screening may facilitate the detection of Microsporidia DNA during CRC follow-up. Further studies are warranted to clarify the potential role of Microsporidia in CRC.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
To identify the types of cancer and the corresponding screening methods evaluated in randomized controlled trials (RCTs), with a primary focus on situating oral cancer screening within the RCT-based body of evidence. This review followed the PRISMA-ScR guidelines. PubMed, Web of Science, Embase, Scopus, LILACS, ProQuest, and Google Scholar were searched without date restrictions for studies in English, Spanish, or Portuguese. Eligible studies were RCTs primarily evaluating cancer screening methods (clinical, imaging, endoscopic, laboratory, molecular/serological, or self-examination). Data were synthesized as means and frequencies. Nine cancer types and 33 distinct screening methods were identified across 97 cancer screenings in 91 RCTs spanning 57 years. Oral cancer ranked last, with only one RCT evaluating a single method, oral visual inspection, the fewest of any cancer type. By comparison, colorectal cancer was the most frequently investigated (n = 22/22.7%), followed by breast cancer (n = 21/21.6%) and lung cancer (n = 18/18.6%), with five, six, and four screening methods evaluated, respectively. These findings map the RCT landscape in cancer screening, revealing marked disparities in evidence across cancer types and identifying oral cancer as the most limited. Further RCTs are urgently needed to strengthen the evidence base and support effective oral cancer screening programs.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Anticancer therapy increases the incidence of atrial fibrillation (AF), the most common sustained cardiac arrhythmia worldwide. However, whether multiple cancers directly promote AF independently of anticancer therapy through shared mechanisms remains unclear. Here, retrospective clinical analyses revealed significantly increased AF prevalence in pre-treatment female patients with breast cancer (BC), lung cancer (LC), and colorectal cancer (CRC), independent of anticancer therapy. Consistently, orthotopic tumor-bearing mouse models exhibited enhanced AF inducibility accompanied by atrial enlargement, fibrosis, and electrical remodeling. Integrated transcriptomic analyses, combined with the TCGA datasets, identified endothelial-to-mesenchymal transition (EndMT) as a shared atrial remodeling pathway underlying tumor-associated AF across multiple cancers. Mechanistically, keratin 16 (KRT16) acted as a shared circulating factor across multiple malignancies. KRT16 accumulated in atrial endothelial cells and promoted EndMT through annexin A2 (AnxA2)-dependent activation of TGF-β1/Smad signaling. KRT16 promoted abnormal membrane retention of AnxA2 by suppressing Tyr23 phosphorylation, thereby sustaining profibrotic signaling and atrial remodeling. Genetic silencing of KRT16 in cancer cells or endothelial knockdown of AnxA2 markedly attenuated EndMT, atrial fibrosis, and AF susceptibility in tumor-bearing mice. Our findings demonstrate that multiple cancers directly induce atrial remodeling and AF through a shared mechanism centered on KRT16-driven EndMT, identifying this pathway as a potential therapeutic target.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Effective pain management after surgery is crucial for recovery following laparoscopic colorectal resection in enhanced recovery after surgery (ERAS) programs. While the transversus abdominis plane (TAP) block is commonly used, it may not fully address visceral pain. The quadratus lumborum (QL) block might provide better coverage for both somatic and visceral pain due to its ability to spread to the thoracolumbar fascia and paravertebral space. This study aims to compare the clinical outcomes of QL versus TAP blocks in laparoscopic colorectal surgery. The main outcome was total opioid use within 24 h. Secondary outcomes included early pain scores, time until the first rescue analgesic was needed, postoperative nausea and vomiting (PONV), length of stay, surgical complications, and side effects related to the blocks. We conducted a systematic literature search using PubMed, Cochrane CENTRAL, Web of Science Core Collection, and Scopus from database inception to 27 July 2025 for randomized controlled trials (RCTs) comparing QL and TAP blocks. Two reviewers independently screened the studies, extracted data, and assessed quality using the Cochrane Risk of Bias 2 tool. We calculated pooled estimates using a random-effects model and evaluated the reliability of the evidence on the basis of the grading of recommendations, assessment, development, and evaluation (GRADE) framework. Four RCTs (n = 419) met the inclusion criteria. Compared with the TAP block, the QL block led to lower opioid use within 24 h (MD [mean difference] -8.92 mg morphine equivalents; 95% CI -11.57 to -6.28) and reduced pain scores both at rest MD -0.25 (-0.37 to -0.21) and during movement MD -0.40 [-0.52 to -0.29]. Operative time numerically favored the QL block, but the pooled difference was not statistically significant. The rates of PONV (OR 0.54; 95% CI 0.25-1.19) and dizziness (OR 0.60; 95% CI 0.22-1.63) were not significantly different between the two groups. The evidence was rated high for PONV and operative time, and moderate for opioid consumption, pain at rest, pain during movement, and dizziness, reflecting downgrades for imprecision and, for opioid consumption and pain during movement, substantial-to-high heterogeneity (I In laparoscopic colorectal surgery, the QL block shows better opioid-sparing effects and lower pain scores at rest and during movement than the TAP block. Operative time numerically favored the QL block but did not differ significantly between groups. Importantly, it does not lead to more adverse effects. These findings suggest that the QL block may be a useful opioid-sparing option within ERAS-based perioperative care, although larger multicenter RCTs are needed before routine preference over the TAP block can be firmly recommended.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Acute diverticulitis (AD) is characterized by the inflammation of one or more mucosal diverticula. Previous guidelines for AD included follow-up colonoscopy to detect cancer, but advancements in high-resolution computed tomography (CT) have challenged the importance of such colonoscopies in recent years. Complicated AD is thought to have a higher risk of being associated with colorectal cancer (CRC), and thus a follow-up colonoscopy is still recommended for these patients; however, for patients who do not experience complications, the lower risk of CRC, added healthcare costs, and risks for bowel perforation during colonoscopy may outweigh the benefits. This study aims to assess whether the number of follow-up colonoscopies for AD can be safely reduced without increasing the risk of missed cancer or adenoma in our population. To do this, we investigated the intraluminal findings of patients who underwent a follow-up colonoscopy after a CT-confirmed AD using a retrospective cohort study approach for patients who received their diagnosis at the Hôpital Montfort emergency department. A total of 146 patients were separated into either uncomplicated (n = 102) or complicated (n = 44) AD groups, with demographic and clinical data being collected from electronic medical records for statistical analyses. The studied patients had no instances of CRC found by colonoscopy, further supporting a more conservative use of follow-up colonoscopies for AD. As a result, we believe that healthcare professionals should consider individual risk assessments over a universal post-diverticulitis endoscopic examination policy.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Malignant ovarian germ cell tumors (OGCTs) account for only 2-5% of ovarian cancers, and familial clustering of germ cell tumors in the ovaries and testes is rare. Lynch syndrome confers elevated colorectal, endometrial, and ovarian cancer risk, but germ cell histologies are not well recognized within its tumor spectrum. A 41-year-old woman presented with abdominal pain. Imaging demonstrated an 11.4 × 6.4 × 10.4 cm mass involving both adnexa with small-volume ascites and elevated tumor markers, including CEA, CA-125, AFP, and LDH. She underwent robotic-assisted hysterectomy, bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy, pelvic and para-aortic lymphadenectomy, partial omentectomy, and staging biopsies. Pathology showed FIGO stage IA yolk sac tumor with intestinal/glandular differentiation. Immunohistochemistry demonstrated diffuse SALL4, patchy glypican-3, focal AFP, mutant-pattern p53, and loss of MSH6 expression with retained internal controls. Germline testing identified a pathogenic MSH6 variant. Both of her brothers had been diagnosed with testicular seminoma, and her paternal grandmother had colon cancer. She completed four cycles of bleomycin, etoposide, and cisplatin and remains without evidence of disease. We report an ovarian yolk sac tumor arising in a woman with germline MSH6-associated Lynch syndrome and two brothers with testicular seminoma. The concordance between her germline variant and MSH6 loss within the tumor suggests the variant could affect tumorigenesis and raises the question whether germ cell tumors are an under-recognized component of the Lynch spectrum. A separate familial germ cell tumor susceptibility allele cannot be excluded. Cascade testing is strongly indicated but remains incomplete in this family, underscoring a persistent gap between identifying a hereditary cancer syndrome and delivering genetic services to relatives.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
As solid tumors progress, the tumor microenvironment becomes increasingly immunosuppressive, impairing cytotoxic T-cell activity and limiting the efficacy of immune checkpoint blockade. However, the mechanistic drivers of this immunosuppression remain poorly understood. Here, we identify a tumor-derived lipid-neutrophil-adenosine axis as a critical regulator of immune suppression in advanced colorectal cancer (CRC). We show that fatty acids enriched in tumor interstitial fluid reprogram neutrophils toward an immunosuppressive phenotype through PPARα activation, upregulation of CD39 and CD73, and adenosine generation, ultimately leading to T-cell suppression. AB928, a dual A2aR/A2bR adenosine receptor antagonist currently in clinical trials, restores T-cell proliferation, effector function, and tumor-killing capacity in vitro and in vivo. Importantly, AB928 synergizes with anti-PD-1 therapy to enhance survival in an immunotherapy-resistant autochthonous model of metastatic CRC. Thus, our findings define a metabolic immune evasion mechanism in the microenvironment and provide a rationale for targeting neutrophil-derived adenosine signaling to improve immunotherapy responses in CRC.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Innate sensing of endogenous double-stranded RNA and the ensuing interferon response are crucial for the efficacy of immune checkpoint inhibition. Microsatellite stable colorectal cancer characteristically lacks this response, remaining immune-refractory with undefined intrinsic regulators. Here, through an in vivo clustered regularly interspaced short palindromic repeats screen, we identify PTPN12 as a physiological barrier that suppresses double-stranded RNA sensing and interferon response. TRIM28 was identified as a direct PTPN12 substrate here; PTPN12 removes phosphorylation at Y370 to stabilize repressive complexes and silence transposable elements, while concurrently rewiring the adhesive cytoskeleton to disrupt the spatially organization of cytosolic double-stranded RNA required for efficient innate sensing. Pharmacological inducible PTPN12 knockdown inhibits pre-established tumor growth and overcomes immunotherapy resistance in vivo, recapitulating PTPN12 ablation-induced massive double-stranded RNA accumulation. Our findings reveal a role for PTPN12 in coupling epigenetic silencing with cytoskeletal surveillance, suggesting potential strategies to augment anti-tumor immunity and overcome immunotherapy resistance in microsatellite stable colorectal cancer.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Multiple systematic reviews and meta-analyses have established the benefits of computer-aided detection (CADe) among experienced endoscopists. The role of CADe among endoscopists who are still acquiring competence trainees in formal endoscopic training and independently practicing but less-experienced operators particularly its effect on right-colon adenoma detection, remains incompletely defined. We performed an updated systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials (RCTs) to evaluate the impact of CADe on adenoma detection by trainee and less-experienced endoscopists. We searched PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials, and ClinicalTrials.gov from inception through May 2026 for RCTs comparing CADe-assisted with standard colonoscopy performed by trainee or less-experienced endoscopists. The primary outcome was adenoma detection rate (ADR). Secondary outcomes were right-colon ADR (RADR), polyp detection rate (PDR), and advanced adenoma detection rate (AADR). Risk ratios (RRs) were pooled using DerSimonian-Laird random-effects models; heterogeneity was quantified with I Five RCTs enrolling 3,158 patients met the inclusion criteria. CADe significantly increased overall ADR (RR 1.17, 95% CI 1.07-1.29; P = 0.0012; I CADe-assisted colonoscopy increases adenoma detection by trainee and less-experienced endoscopists, with the largest relative effect for right-colon adenomas. Because the PIs cross the null and the certainty of evidence is moderate at best, these findings support further prospective evaluation of CADe as an adjunct to colonoscopy training rather than establishing that routine integration into fellowship curricula produces more competent independent endoscopists.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
This paper aims to explore the safety and efficacy of alfentanil in anesthesia for laparoscopic colorectal surgery. This study was designed as a prospective study at CR & WISCO General Hospital. Eighty elderly patients who underwent laparoscopic colorectal surgery between February 2023 and February 2025 were selected and randomly divided into an alfentanil group and a sufentanil group, with 40 patients in each group. The LIDCOrapid non-invasive hemodynamic monitor was used to record the heart rate (HR) and mean arterial pressure (MAP) of patients at five time points: pre-anesthesia baseline (T0), before tracheal intubation (T1), one minute after tracheal intubation (T2), three minutes after tracheal intubation (T3), and five minutes after tracheal intubation (T4). The incidence of intraoperative adverse reactions and the use of vasoactive drugs were recorded, and the recovery of patients after discontinuation of anesthetic drugs was compared. Compared with the alfentanil group, the MAP levels and HR in the sufentanil group fluctuated more significantly at T1, T2, and T3 (P < 0.05). The incidence of hypotension and the use of ephedrine were higher in the sufentanil group than in the alfentanil group (P < 0.05). The eye-opening time, orientation recovery time, and time to discharge from the post-anesthesia care unit (PACU) in the sufentanil group were longer than those in the alfentanil group (P < 0.05). Compared with sufentanil induction, alfentanil administration in laparoscopic colorectal surgery for elderly patients can more effectively reduce hemodynamic fluctuations, decrease the use of intraoperative active drugs, and ensure rapid awakening without increasing postoperative adverse reactions - that is, it provides a higher level of comfort.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) remains difficult to diagnose early and treat effectively. The related microRNAs miR-221 and miR-222 share a seed sequence, but their functions and clinical evidence should be evaluated individually. Pancreatic cancer models support miR-221/222-associated TIMP-2 repression and invasion, miR-222-mediated p57 regulation, and tumor-derived vesicular miR-222 effects on p27 expression and localization. Macrophage-derived extracellular vesicular miR-222-3p has also been implicated in gemcitabine resistance through TSC1-associated signaling. By contrast, the TRPS1-ZEB2 mechanism and the vesicular SPINT1-HGF liver pathway derive from breast and colorectal cancer studies, respectively, and remain extrapolations when discussed in PDAC. Circulating miR-221 has shown exploratory diagnostic associations, but results from general miRNA panels cannot be assigned to miR-221 or miR-222 individually. Tissue prognostic associations likewise do not validate circulating assays. A first-in-human study of the selective inhibitor LNA-i-miR-221 provides early safety and peripheral-blood pharmacodynamic evidence in a mixed advanced-cancer population that included pancreatic cancer; it does not establish PDAC-specific efficacy. Translation requires independent biomarker validation, molecule-specific target-dependence studies, and confirmation of effective pancreatic tumor delivery.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Helicobacter pylori is a recognized Group 1 carcinogen and the primary pathogenic driver of gastric adenocarcinoma. Although its role in gastric carcinogenesis is well characterized, its potential systemic oncogenic influence on extra-gastric digestive malignancies remains under clinical investigation. The main objective of this study was to assess whether anti-H. pylori seropositivity was associated with the presence of gastric or colonic neoplasms. A secondary, exploratory objective was to evaluate whether anti-H. pylori seropositivity was associated with the surgical outcome (R0 resection versus non-R0/non-curative surgery) in a separate series of patients operated on for digestive cancer. We conducted a retrospective cross-sectional study of 330 patients evaluated between February 2023 and May 2025 stratified by anti-H. pylori serological status, assessed using anti-H. pylori antibody testing. Logistic regression models were used to investigate associations between anti-H. pylori seropositivity and different types of neoplasms. An exploratory analysis included a separate series of 60 patients operated on for digestive cancer between April 2023 and December 2025. Anti-H. pylori seropositivity was associated with the presence of both gastric cancer (aOR 4.00, 95% CI 1.59-11.5, p = 0.005) and colon cancer (aOR 3.47, 95% CI 1.58-8.12, p = 0.003). The associations were consistent in sensitivity analyses, including Firth penalized regression. Occult gastrointestinal bleeding, a likely manifestation of the tumour, was more frequent in patients with colon cancer (17.3 % vs 7.7%; crude OR 2.50, 95% CI 1.20-5.26). In the surgical series of 60 patients who underwent surgery for digestive neoplasms, seropositivity was not associated with curative resection (OR for non-curative surgery 0.99, 95% CI 0.35-2.74). Anti-H. pylori seropositivity was associated with an increased prevalence of gastric and colonic neoplasia, with the strongest association observed for gastric cancer. Because serology does not confirm active infection and the study design was cross-sectional, these findings should be interpreted as associations rather than evidence of causality or preventive benefit from eradication therapy.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
The abdomino-perineal rectal resection (APRR) is associated with a significant rate of postoperative complications, many of them related to the pelvi-subperitoneal dead space that remains after the removal of the rectum. We performed a retrospective study on 21 consecutive patients operated in the Surgical Clinic - Mureş Clinical County Hospital / G.E. Palade University of Medicine, Pharmacy, Science, and Technology of Târgu Mureş, Romania between 01.01.2010 - 01.01.2022 in whom we used an omental flap (OF) for primary and secondary prophylaxis, as well as for the treatment of complications associated with the remnant space after APRR; all the procedures were performed using an open approach (median laparotomy) and the mobilization of the omentum was made according to the local anatomical situation. We encountered no case of flap ischemia (intraoperative evaluation at the end of the procedure and postoperative course). In the early postoperative period, we encountered one exitus through myocardial infarction and two wound suppurations; the time required for the regain of the intestinal transit ranged between 2 and 7 days, with a median of 3.5 days. At late follow-up (between 2 and 8 years) we encountered 5 deaths through distant metastases, 2 incisional hernias, 2 cases of local recurrence, and no reoperation for intestinal obstruction. Overall, we did not find any complication directly related to the use of the OF. The omentum remains a simple and quick solution for the prevention and solving of some of the complications associated with low rectal cancer surgery while its use does not seem to be associated with a significant supplementary morbidity.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
The capecitabine plus oxaliplatin (CapeOX) regimen is commonly used for adjuvant treatment and selected first‑line treatment settings in colorectal cancer. However, hematologic toxicities, such as leukopenia, neutropenia, anemia, and thrombocytopenia, may adversely affect treatment continuity, resulting in treatment delays, dose reductions, or treatment discontinuation. If these toxicities could be predicted based on pre-treatment blood test results and markers of inflammation and nutrition, it would lead to improved treatment continuity. In this study, we explored potential associations related to hematologic toxicities that occur at the end of the first cycle of CapeOX therapy. A retrospective analysis was conducted on 108 patients with colorectal cancer who began CapeOX therapy between September 2020 and October 2023. We evaluated hematologic toxicity (Grade ≥ 1) at the end of the first treatment cycle based on the Common Terminology Criteria for Adverse Events (CTCAE) version 5.0 and examined its association with pre-treatment blood test results, nutritional indices (PNIs), and inflammatory markers (systemic inflammation response index (SIRI), systemic immune‑inflammation index (SII), neutrophil‑to‑lymphocyte ratio (NLR), platelet‑to‑lymphocyte ratio (PLR), and lymphocyte‑to‑monocyte ratio (LMR)). We performed multivariate logistic regression analysis on factors showing significant differences and calculated cutoff values using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis. An SII value of ≤496.8 was identified as a significant pretreatment factor associated with the development of leukopenia. For hemoglobin reduction, age ≥68 years, red blood cell count ≤394 × 10⁴/μL, and hemoglobin (Hb) ≤11.7 g/dL were associated; for thrombocytopenia, lymphocyte count ≤12.41 × 10²/μL and SII ≤477.9 were significantly associated. The identified associations may help generate hypotheses for future prospective studies of pre‑treatment risk assessment and supportive‑care strategies. Evidence suggests that some of the hematologic toxicities associated with CapeOX therapy show exploratory associations with pre-treatment blood tests and markers of inflammation and nutrition. These exploratory associations may help inform future hypothesis‑generating research on pretreatment risk assessment and supportive‑care strategies.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
With the development of high-throughput sequencing technologies, microbiome data play an increasingly important role in pathological analysis and disease prediction. However, microbiome data are typically characterized by high dimensionality, small sample sizes, and compositional constraints, which present challenges to conventional statistical methods, particularly in studies of specific diseases with limited sample sizes. Motivated by these challenges, this paper develops an adaptive Bayesian transfer learning framework built upon the Bayesian Compositional Generalized Linear Mixed Model (BCGLMM). The proposed framework integrates a power-prior-based adaptive Bayesian transfer learning with BCGLMM, which enables information borrowing from a related source dataset while accounting for compositional constraints, phylogenetic relatedness among taxa, and dependence among samples in high-dimensional microbiome data. By adopting an adaptive transfer parameter, the framework can adjust the contribution of source information according to the compatibility between the source and target datasets, thereby improving robustness and reducing the risk of negative transfer. Systematic simulation studies show that the proposed Bayesian transfer learning methods generally achieve better predictive performance than target-only, pooled, and existing transfer-learning competitors, especially when the target sample size is limited and related source data are available. Compared with the fixed-transfer method, Adaptive BTL-CGLMM maintains more stable performance under increasing source-target discrepancy, different dimensions, varying sample sizes, and heterogeneous covariance structures. Real gut microbiome applications, including body mass index (BMI) prediction, type 2 diabetes (T2D) diagnosis, and colorectal cancer (CRC) diagnosis, further demonstrate that the proposed methods improve prediction by borrowing useful auxiliary information from related source datasets. The microbial taxa identified by Adaptive BTL-CGLMM are also consistent with existing biological findings, supporting the interpretability of the proposed framework. This study provides an adaptive Bayesian transfer learning framework for high-dimensional microbiome data analysis with limited target sample sizes. By enabling knowledge transfer under compositional constraints, the proposed method improves predictive performance and robustness across varying data settings, thereby enhancing phenotype prediction and disease diagnosis in small-sample microbiome studies.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
The global escalation of obesity and type 2 diabetes mellitus has driven a surge in gastrointestinal and hepatic pathologies, notably metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) and steatohepatitis (MASH). Incretin hormones, glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1), glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide (GIP), and glucagon, are pivotal regulators of the gut-liver-pancreas axis. We synthesized recent clinical trial data and real-world evidence evaluating the efficacy and safety of incretin-based multi-receptor agonists in metabolic and gastrointestinal diseases. Advanced multi-agonists (e.g., tirzepatide, retatrutide, mazdutide) demonstrate unprecedented metabolic efficacy, achieving significant body weight reduction, preserving relative lean mass, and reversing metabolic syndrome. In hepatology, these agents fundamentally alter disease trajectories; semaglutide, tirzepatide, and survodutide achieve MASH resolution without worsening fibrosis. Emerging data also suggest GLP-1 receptor agonists significantly reduce colorectal cancer incidence and lower the risks of surgery and hospitalizations in patients with inflammatory bowel disease. However, therapy is associated with gastrointestinal dysmotility and an increased risk of cholelithiasis, requiring careful clinical and perioperative management. Furthermore, discontinuation of therapy leads to rapid weight regain and a complete reversal of cardiometabolic benefits. Incretin multi-agonists represent a paradigm shift in gastroenterology and hepatology, offering definitive, disease-modifying interventions for the gut-liver axis. While highly effective, their chronic nature necessitates meticulous management of gastrointestinal tolerability and urgent health policy reforms to ensure long-term, equitable patient access.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Obesity is a known risk factor for colorectal cancer (CRC), yet its impact on the spatial organization of early epithelial transformation and immune remodeling remains poorly understood. Our goal was to translate spatial transcriptomic features of obesity-associated colorectal cancer into a functional landscape of epithelial, stromal, and immune cell interactions across both pre-neoplastic and tumor states. We employed a dual-platform spatial transcriptomics approach-GeoMx Digital Spatial Profiling and CosMx Spatial Molecular Imaging-to analyze 89 CRC patients (288 annotated regions) and 24 CRC patients (12 obese, 12 non-obese; 969 fields of view). This enabled high-resolution mapping of transcriptomic programs, immune composition, and cell-cell interactions across tumor, normal mucosa, adipose, and stromal compartments. In obese-normal mucosa, we identified a transcriptionally shifted epithelial state within morphologically intact mucosa, characterized by two distinct expression trajectories among 30 CRC-related genes. Notably, a subset of genes exhibited early transcriptional alterations in obese-normal tissue that were maintained throughout tumor development. As tumors progressed, obesity was associated with spatial immune remodeling characterized by localized enrichment of SPP1⁺ macrophages, increased SPP1⁺/pro-inflammatory macrophage ratios near cancer cells, and enhanced growth-factor and cytokine-mediated signaling. Obesity induces a two-phase reprogramming of colorectal tissue: first, by inducing early epithelial transcriptional reprogramming, and second, by fostering spatially restricted immune suppression in tumors. These insights offer mechanistic understanding and identify spatially defined targets for risk stratification and immunotherapy in obesity-associated CRC.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Surgical antibiotic prophylaxis (SAP) is essential for preventing surgical site infections, yet inappropriate perioperative antibiotic use remains a persistent stewardship challenge. Although SAP non-adherence is well documented, the behavioral and organizational mechanisms sustaining it remain poorly understood in Iranian surgical settings. This study assessed SAP adherence and explored factors shaping perioperative antibiotic prescribing and implementation. This explanatory mixed-methods study included a three-month retrospective assessment of SAP adherence followed by qualitative interviews. Adult patients undergoing elective colorectal and urologic surgeries in a tertiary university-affiliated hospital were included. SAP adherence was assessed using routinely collected hospital data based on indication, antibiotic selection, dose appropriateness, and duration. Antibiotic exposure was measured using length of therapy (LOT), days of therapy (DOT), and defined daily dose (DDD). Semi-structured interviews were then conducted with healthcare professionals to explore factors underlying the observed patterns of SAP non-adherence. Interview data were analyzed using directed content analysis guided by the Theoretical Domains Framework (TDF). Among 109 patients, only 10 (9.2%) met all SAP adherence criteria. Although indication was appropriate in all patients and dosing was appropriate in 105 patients (96.3%), non-adherence was mainly driven by inappropriate antibiotic selection and prolonged postoperative continuation. Antibiotics were continued beyond 24 h in 93 patients (85.3%), beyond 48 h in 82 (75.2%), and prescribed at discharge in 66 (60.6%). Antibiotic exposure was substantial, with median LOT, DOT, and total DDD of 4.0, 6.0, and 6.3, respectively. Fifteen interviews were conducted to explain these adherence patterns, identifying perceived infection risk, broad-spectrum prescribing norms, unclear responsibilities, workflow disruptions, professional responsibility concerns, patient expectations, and lack of structured antibiotic review as key drivers of persistent non-adherence. SAP non-adherence was common and extended beyond the decision to prescribe prophylaxis. Improving SAP practice requires stewardship interventions that address prescribing culture, perioperative workflow, and structured postoperative antibiotic discontinuation.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Patients often present at advanced stages of early-onset rectal cancer (EORC), which is becoming more common. Within a year following rectal resection, some patients experience early adverse outcomes (EAO), such as severe complications, recurrence, or death; however, there is currently no validated postoperative risk-stratification tool for this population. Current prognostic models concentrate on individual endpoints rather than the composite adversity spectrum that is pertinent to younger patients because they were mostly established in older cohorts. This work sought to create and externally validate a model for detecting EORC patients at greater risk of EAO using a stacking ensemble machine learning approach with SHAP interpretability in order to guide individualized postoperative surveillance and adjuvant therapy decisions. In this two-center retrospective cohort study, 648 EORC patients from Center A (2020-2025) constituted the development cohort and 102 patients from Center B (2024-2025) the external validation cohort. Eleven individual machine learning models and a two-layer stacking ensemble (combining three base learners with logistic regression meta-learner) were trained. Model performance was assessed by area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), calibration, and decision curve analysis. Boruta feature selection identified eleven important predictors, with pathological T stage (pT), lymphovascular invasion (LVI), and pathological TNM stage (pTNM) contributing most to model predictions. The stacking ensemble outperformed all 11 individual models, achieving AUCs of 0.91 (95% CI 0.88-0.93) in the training set, 0.89 (95% CI 0.85-0.94) in the internal validation set, and 0.83 (95% CI 0.76-0.91) in the external validation cohort, with a Brier score of 0.1104 and sustained net benefit on decision curve analysis. An interactive web calculator was deployed for individualized risk assessment. An interpretable stacking ensemble model integrating SHAP analysis and a web-based calculator showed promising predictive performance for EAO following EORC surgery. Designed for postoperative use once pathology data are available, the model provides a comprehensive risk estimate to guide surveillance intensity and interdisciplinary adjuvant therapy decision-making.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
The gut microbiota plays a critical role in modulating both the efficacy and toxicity of radiotherapy in patients with colorectal cancer (CRC). This review synthesizes current evidence on the bidirectional interaction between the gut microbiome and radiotherapy, highlighting the mechanisms through which microbial communities influence radiosensitivity and treatment-related adverse effects. Specific microbiota-derived metabolites, such as short-chain fatty acids and methylglyoxal, can enhance the radiotherapeutic response by exacerbating DNA damage, promoting immunogenic cell death, and activating antitumor immunity. Conversely, dysbiosis may contribute to radioresistance and exacerbate radiation-induced enteritis by impairing intestinal barrier function and amplifying inflammatory responses. Therapeutic strategies targeting the gut microbiome-including probiotics, prebiotics, antibiotics, and fecal microbiota transplantation-show promise in improving radiotherapy outcomes and mitigating toxicity. However, its clinical application remains limited by issues of safety, variability in individual microbiome composition, and lack of standardized protocols. Further high-quality clinical trials are essential to validate these interventions and advance personalized microbial modulation approaches in CRC radiotherapy.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
In Latin America, colorectal cancer is the third most common cancer among men and fourth most common cancer among women. Ecuador has experienced an upward trend in CRC incidence and mortality, highlighting the need to strengthen population-based prevention and early detection strategies. Previous studies in Ecuador recommended more comprehensive evaluations of CRC screening reach, effectiveness, and continuity of care. The study used an explanatory sequential mixed methods research design and collected data using quantitative surveys and individual interviews to explore perceived barriers and facilitators to CRC screening in Quito, Ecuador. For the survey data, bivariate analyses were performed to compare differences on CRC screening history (1 = yes; 2 = no). Categorical variables were compared using chi-square tests, and continuous variables, including scale variables, were compared using two sample t-tests. Independent variables based on previous work and that were identified to be related to CRC screening history in the bivariate analysis were then entered into a multivariable logistic regression model. Qualitative interview participants were asked about perceived causes of CRC, ways to reduce risk, the appropriate age to begin screening, and what types of CRC screening they had heard about or undergone. Content analysis was used to code the transcripts and generate themes from the interviews. Quantitative and qualitative findings were integrated at several stages. Bivariate analysis showed that individuals who had undergone screening had higher scores on negative beliefs about cancer (11.11 vs. 9.90; p=.03). CRC screening self-efficacy remained a significant independent variable in the multivariable model, showing that lower self-efficacy was associated with a lower probability of screening uptake (OR = 0.78; 95% CI: 0.61-0.99; p=.04). Qualitative analysis revealed that participants were unsure about the criteria for screening, the appropriate age to begin testing, and the differences between available screening tests. Some participants mentioned receiving CRC screening information through their healthcare providers, but they generally perceived public communication about the topic as limited. One finding from the study identified opportunities for stool-based testing during annual physical exams. The study also identified opportunities for improved communication in partnership with providers and patients to increase awareness of CRC prevention.
