ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Obesity and metabolic dysfunction are increasingly prevalent in patients with diverse gastrointestinal and liver diseases and contribute to disease progression, treatment response, and long-term clinical outcomes. In parallel, the therapeutic landscape for obesity has expanded rapidly, with growing use of incretin receptor agonists (RA), including glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP1)-RA, bariatric surgery, and endoscopic bariatric therapies. Understanding how these weight-loss interventions influence gastrointestinal disease activity, safety, and malignancy risk is essential for clinical decision-making. This narrative review synthesizes current evidence on the effects of obesity as well as weight-loss therapies across a spectrum of gastrointestinal and liver conditions, including metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD), inflammatory bowel disease (IBD), gastroesophageal reflux disease, celiac disease, gastrointestinal malignancies, and dumping syndrome. We summarize data from randomized trials, observational cohorts, and meta-analyses evaluating clinical outcomes, disease activity, adverse events, and cancer risk. In MASLD, GLP1-RA and bariatric surgery improve hepatic steatosis and steatohepatitis without aggravation of fibrosis. Fibrosis outcomes are most strongly influenced by sustained weight loss and improvements in insulin resistance. In IBD, obesity (particularly increased visceral fat) may negatively impact response to biologics; however, observational data suggest that GLP1-RA are not associated with increased IBD disease activity and may be associated with favorable clinical outcomes in selected patients with obesity. Bariatric surgery-particularly sleeve gastrectomy-may improve IBD control in carefully selected patients. Data on endoscopic bariatric therapies in IBD are limited but may be effective in selected patients. Gastrointestinal malignancies have increased prevalence in obesity, including esophageal, pancreatic, liver, and colorectal cancers. Current randomized and observational data do not demonstrate consistently increased cancer risk with GLP-1 based therapies, while bariatric surgery may be associated with reduced risk of selected obesity-related cancers. Evidence linking endoscopic bariatric therapies to malignancy risk is currently lacking. Dumping syndrome is a complication of bariatric surgery, but has not been reported following endoscopic bariatric therapies, likely due to delayed gastric emptying. Collectively, weight-loss therapies are increasingly important in the management of gastrointestinal and liver diseases. Ongoing studies and longer-term follow-up are needed to clarify durability of benefit, procedure-specific risks, and optimal patient selection for GLP-1 based therapies.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Tumor protein p53 (p53) plays a dual role in cancer under hypoxia, promoting cell cycle arrest and apoptosis, whereas facilitating survival. P53 can either suppress or cooperate with HIF1α to regulate hypoxia-driven transcription and metabolic adaptation. However, the precise molecular mechanisms by which p53 modulates hypoxia-induced tumor progression and therapy resistance in colorectal cancer remain unclear. In this study, we report that the expression of collapsin response mediator protein 4 (CRMP4) is highly expressed in CRC cells carrying wild-type p53 under hypoxic conditions and can be compromised by p53 or HIF1α knockdown. Wild-type p53 robustly enriches in four binding domains on the CRMP4 promoter. HIF1α fails to bind to the CRMP4 promoter in the presence of p53 knockdown. Disruption of the p53 binding region on the CRMP4 promoter or disruption of a key peptide in the formation of p53 tetramers by CRISPR-Cas9 both lead to the destruction of the promoter-proximal interaction, thereby weakening HIF1α binding. The positive correlation between this p53-driven DNA promoter-proximal interaction and the expression of CRMP4 is also validated in colorectal adenocarcinoma in vivo. Overall, our findings determine that CRMP4 is up-regulated in CRC cell lines with wild-type p53 upon hypoxia exposure; p53 is necessary for CRMP4 expression, whereas HIF1α determines how much CRMP4 is expressed; p53 as a tetramer interacts with four binding domains at the CRMP4 promoter, and facilitates DNA interaction to accommodate HIF1α, thereby enhancing CRMP4 expression in a novel epigenetic manner in CRC responding to hypoxia.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Metastatic pancreatic adenocarcinoma remains one of the most treatment-refractory malignancies. Although MBTA immunotherapy, consisting of mannan-BAM, Toll-like receptor ligands, and an agonistic anti-CD40 antibody, effectively eradicates primary tumors and induces systemic antitumor immunity, its efficacy against large established metastatic lesions remains limited. We hypothesized that therapeutic outcomes could be improved by combining MBTA with interventions targeting biological vulnerabilities of metastatic tumors. A bilateral Panc02 pancreatic adenocarcinoma model was employed to mimic primary tumors and established distant lesions. MBTA was administered intratumorally into primary tumors, while metastatic lesions were targeted using systemic or local interventions affecting glutamine metabolism, apoptosis, or tumor-cell membrane integrity. Combinations with immune checkpoint inhibitors and anti-TGF-β antibody were evaluated in a bilateral MC38 colorectal adenocarcinoma model. Treatment of primary tumors with MBTA generated a systemic antitumor response that significantly delayed the growth of distant tumors and prolonged survival but rarely induced complete responses. Therapeutic efficacy was enhanced by combining MBTA with the glutamine antagonist prodrug LTP607, the Smac mimetic LCL161, or intratumoral administration of the membrane-disruptive peptide LTX-315, each producing durable complete responses in a subset of animals. Direct treatment of both primary and distant tumors with MBTA further improved cure rates, which were additionally increased by blockade of the CD47-SIRPα axis. In contrast, immune checkpoint inhibitors and anti-TGF-β antibody provided minimal additional benefit when combined with MBTA. These findings suggest that MBTA-induced systemic immunity alone may be insufficient for eradication of large established metastatic lesions. However, therapeutic strategies targeting intrinsic vulnerabilities of metastatic tumors substantially enhance antitumor efficacy. Collectively, the results support the development of MBTA-based combination therapies for advanced metastatic cancer.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Enhanced Recovery After Surgery (ERAS) pathways and combined mechanical and oral antibiotic bowel preparation (MBP + OAB) have improved outcomes in colorectal surgery by reducing infectious complications and anastomotic leakage. However, their impact on anastomotic bleeding (AB) remains unclear. We conducted a prospective observational study including consecutive patients undergoing elective colorectal resection with primary anastomosis between 2012 and 2025 at a tertiary center. A modified ERAS pathway incorporating systematic MBP + OAB was progressively implemented. Predictors of AB were identified using Elastic Net penalized regression and multivariable logistic regression. Temporal trends were assessed using interrupted time series and change point analyses. A total of 1547 patients were included. Following implementation of the modified ERAS pathway, anastomotic leakage decreased (10.7% vs. 7.9%), whereas AB increased significantly (2.1% vs. 5.8%, p < 0.001). Most bleeding events were minor and did not require transfusion or invasive treatment. In multivariable analysis, MBP + OAB was associated with increased AB (OR 3.74, 95% CI 1.98-7.05), and ileocolic anastomosis was also associated with increased risk (OR 2.26, 95% CI 1.22-4.18). Temporal analyses identified a structural change after formal standardization of MBP + OAB, followed by a sustained increase in AB incidence. However, severe anastomotic leakage, reoperation, and postoperative mortality decreased. Implementation of systematic MBP + OAB was associated with an increased incidence of predominantly minor anastomotic bleeding. Ileocolic anastomosis was also associated with increased bleeding risk, whereas perioperative DOAC therapy may contribute to risk in selected patients. Surgical teams should factor these modifiable and anatomical elements into risk stratification models.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Colorectal cancer (CRC) remains a leading cause of cancer mortality with few effective targeted therapies. Kinesin family member 11 (KIF11), a motor protein essential for mitotic spindle assembly, is frequently overexpressed in multiple cancers. We hypothesized that nitidine chloride (NC), a natural benzophenanthridine alkaloid with documented anti-tumor activity, might suppress CRC by targeting KIF11.Molecular docking predicted a strong interaction between NC and KIF11 (- 9.0 kcal/mol). RNA sequencing, quantitative RT-PCR, and immunohistochemistry confirmed that NC treatment markedly downregulated KIF11 expression. Meta-analysis across public datasets showed consistent KIF11 mRNA overexpression in CRC (standardized mean difference [SMD] = 1.33; AUC = 0.87), while in-house immunohistochemistry on 416 clinical specimens demonstrated even stronger protein-level elevation (AUC = 0.99) that correlated with larger tumor size and deeper invasion. Single-cell RNA sequencing and spatial transcriptomics further revealed that KIF11 is preferentially expressed in proliferative malignant epithelial cells. Through CRISPR-based knockout screening and lentiviral silencing, KIF11 depletion impaired the growth or viability of the examined CRC cell models. Public ChIP-seq data suggested RAD21 occupancy near the KIF11 regulatory region, whereas reciprocal co-immunoprecipitation supported an association between the RAD21 and KIF11 proteins. Among genes co-expressed with KIF11,a pronounced enrichment was observed in pathways governing cell-cycle progression. Following KIF11 knockdown, transcriptomic profiling showed reduced expression across cell-cycle, DNA-replication, and chromatin-cohesion programs, alongside a reciprocal increase in amino-acid metabolism and stress-response genes. At the functional level, KIF11 depletion suppressed cell proliferation and induced G2/M-phase arrest. Taken together, these in vitro and limited xenograft data indicate that NC restrains CRC growth chiefly through the RAD21-KIF11 axis; KIF11 represents a promising preclinical target, though comprehensive systematic in vivo pharmacodynamic and translational animal validation remains absent in the current study and requires further independent investigation.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs) exhibit substantial heterogeneity in colorectal cancer (CRC), yet the upstream tumor-derived signals associated with their state remodeling during disease progression remain incompletely defined. Through integrative analysis of multi-cohort single-cell transcriptomics, proteomics, and bulk RNA sequencing data, we identified tumor-derived midkine (MDK) as a stage-associated candidate signal linked to CAF remodeling in CRC. MDK cell-type specificity and stage-associated expression, together with CAF composition and stage-dependent remodeling, were evaluated in two large colorectal cancer single-cell RNA-sequencing cohorts, with the principal findings cross-validated between cohorts and further integrated with bulk transcriptomic, proteomic, and immunohistochemical datasets. Existing malignant-cell-to-CAF CellChat results were re-ranked using a joint breadth-strength framework to identify broadly activated and high-probability signaling pathways. CAF trajectories were reconstructed independently in both cohorts using Monocle 2 and rooted according to the same biological criterion, namely enrichment of the normal-like Fib-MFAP5 population. BayesPrism was used to deconvolve CAF subtype abundance from TCGA colorectal cancer bulk transcriptomes and to evaluate its association with overall survival. MDK was consistently enriched in malignant epithelial cells across both single-cell cohorts. Within the same-platform bulk RNA cohort, median log2-normalized MDK expression increased from 7.93 in adenoma to 8.19 in carcinoma in situ and 9.02 in adenocarcinoma, supporting a significant ordered increase during colorectal cancer progression (Jonckheere-Terpstra [Formula: see text]; 10,000-permutation [Formula: see text]). Fib-WNT5A abundance likewise showed a stage-associated increase and was positioned significantly later than the normal-like Fib-MFAP5 population in patient-level pseudotime analyses of both the discovery and validation cohorts. Fib-WNT5A exhibited strong TGF-β and extracellular matrix programs, and integration of subtype-associated ECM signatures with bulk proteomics linked this population to collagen-enriched matrix remodeling. Joint breadth-strength analysis identified MK signaling as the top-ranked broadly activated malignant-cell-to-CAF pathway. CellChat further predicted COL1A1/COL1A2-CD44 interactions between Fib-WNT5A and multiple immune populations, supporting an association between Fib-WNT5A expansion and an ECM-rich, immune-restrictive microenvironment. Patient-level pseudo-bulk analyses were used to evaluate BayesPrism recovery of major CAF states. In TCGA CRC, higher Fib-WNT5A abundance was associated with poorer overall survival in the prespecified median-based univariable analysis (HR = 1.64, 95% CI 1.09-2.49; log-rank P = 0.018), whereas higher Fib-MFAP5 abundance was associated with better survival (HR = 0.54, 95% CI 0.35-0.83; log-rank P = 0.0045). Collectively, the data support a progression-linked association among tumor-cell-enriched MDK, CAF state remodeling, an ECM-high Fib-WNT5A program, and predicted collagen-mediated immune interactions in CRC. Functional perturbation studies are required to establish the direction and causality of the proposed MDK-CAF axis.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Several studies suggest that microRNA(miRNA) single-nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) are associated with colorectal cancer (CRC). However, there is very limited data on the association between miRNA SNP-SNP interactions and CRC. This study aimed to evaluate the association between miRNA SNPs, SNP-SNP interactions, and CRC risk in a Yemeni population. This study aimed to evaluate the associations of miRNA SNPs and SNP-SNP interactions with CRC risk in a Yemeni population. A case-control study was conducted in 200 patients with CRC and 200 normal participants. Genotyping of selected miRNA SNPs, miR-146a (rs2910164), miR-27a (rs895819), miR-196a-2 (rs11614913), and miR-499a (rs3746444) was performed on real-time polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR) using TaqMan allelic discrimination assays. Logistic regression was applied to estimate odds ratios (ORs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) for the associations between SNPs and CRC risk. After Bonferroni correction, the analysis revealed significant associations of miR-146a and miR-499a SNPs with CRC. Both recessive (OR = 2.1, 1.7; P = 0.0005, 0.016) and additive models (OR = 1.6, 1.3; P = 0.008, 0.037) of these SNPs showed significant associations with CRC. In contrast, SNPs in miR-27a and miR-196a-2 showed no significant association with CRC. After Bonferroni correction, the interaction between the risk genotypes, miR-146a CC and miR-499a GG, remains significantly associated with CRC risk (OR = 8.97, p = 0.01) compared with the reference group, which had both protective genotypes, miR-146a GG and miR-499a AA. The miR-146a and miR-499a polymorphisms, as well as their interaction, were associated with an increased risk of CRC in a Yemeni population. This study provides preliminary evidence for the role of miRNA SNP-SNP interactions in CRC susceptibility.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Current treat-to-target strategies for ulcerative colitis (UC) prioritize clinical remission (CR) and endoscopic remission (ER). However, whether achieving deeper remission (histologic remission [HR] or biochemical remission [BR]) confers incremental and sustained benefit beyond CR-ER endpoints remains unquantified. This study aimed to provide evidence supporting the hierarchical benefit of multidimensional remission on critical outcomes in UC. We systematically searched Medline, EMBASE, and Cochrane CENTRAL from inception to 19 May 2025 for cohort studies enrolling adults with UC in CR, with ≥ 6 months of follow-up, comparing relapse risk, corticosteroid reintroduction, hospitalization, colectomy, and colorectal cancer rates among patients achieving ER versus non-ER, HR versus non-HR, and/or BR versus non-BR. Data were synthesized using random-effects meta-analysis. The certainty of evidence was evaluated with GRADE. 94 studies (12,634 patients) were included. Compared to non-ER, ER reduced relapse risk by 44%-72% between 6 to < 60 months and corticosteroid reintroduction risk by 70% at 12 months (relative risks [RR] 0.30 [95% CI, 0.10-0.90]; very low certainty). Adding HR to CR + ER further reduced relapse risk by 51%-72% across all follow-up intervals: 12-24 months (0.46 [0.34-0.62]; moderate certainty), 24-36 months (0.48 [0.36-0.64]; moderate certainty), 48-60 months (0.28 [0.16-0.51]; low certainty), and ≥ 60 months (0.49 [0.34-0.71]; low certainty). Adding BR to CR + ER provided additional risk reduction of 71% at 12-month (0.29 [0.16-0.50]); moderate certainty), and 29% at ≥ 60 months (0.71 [0.51-0.97]; very low certainty). This meta-analysis suggests a hierarchical benefit of multidimensional remission in UC. Achieving HR or BR beyond CR-ER endpoints substantially and sustainably reduces relapse risk. These results suggest that HR and BR may be considered as potential treatment targets to optimize long-term disease control.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Missed lesions in the proximal colon are a common cause of interval colorectal cancers detected before the next surveillance colonoscopy. This study aimed to determine whether two forward-view examinations of the proximal colon could reduce the adenoma miss rate compared to a single forward-view examination. Patients undergoing screening colonoscopy were enrolled in the study. After completing the first forward-view examination of the proximal colon (pass 1), patients were randomly assigned to either the intervention group, in which the proximal colon was re-examined twice (pass 2 and 3), or the control group, in which it was re-examined once (pass 2). The primary outcome was the proximal adenoma miss rate, defined as the number of proximal adenomas detected in the final pass (pass 3 for the intervention group and pass 2 for the control group) divided by the total number of proximal adenomas detected in that group. A total of 403 patients were enrolled (intervention group, n = 202; control group, n = 201). The proximal adenoma miss rate in the intervention group was significantly lower than that in the control group (10.8%; 95% CI 6.5% - 17.2% vs. 28.1%; 95% CI 20.7% - 36.9%, P < 0.001). ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Colorectal cancer (CRC) remains a major health burden, underscoring the need for continued research to improve screening methods and treatment outcomes. The colitis-associated azoxymethane (AOM) and dextran sodium sulphate (DSS) mouse model has proven valuable for CRC research, as it closely mimics human CRC development and captures the complex interactions between the gut microbiome and immune system. However, variations in AOM/DSS dosing reported in literature can influence baseline conditions, thereby affecting the outcome and interpretation of experimental and therapeutic interventions. This study evaluated the impact of varying AOM and DSS doses on CRC development and the gut microbiome, metabolome and lipidome in mouse faeces (n = 29). Inflammation-driven CRC progression was more pronounced in mice treated with high-dose AOM (12.5 mg/kg) combined with high-dose DSS (2%) than in those receiving lower doses. Faecal 16S rRNA-based microbiome analysis revealed significant shifts in the high-dose AOM groups, which coincided with the highest tumour burden. Operational taxonomic units (OTUs) belonging to Prevotella, Turicibacter, Intestinimonas and Akkermansia muciniphila displayed patterns linked to inflammation and tumour progression, with distinct temporal abundance increases across AOM/DSS dosing groups. State-of-the-art, validated UHPLC-HRMS methodologies for faecal metabolomics and lipidomics fingerprinting (7951 features) and profiling (202 targets) identified imidazolepropionic acid, a microbe-derived metabolite, as a candidate biomarker associated with inflammation-driven CRC. In addition, mice with a high tumour burden presented elevated levels of lactic acid and γ-glutamylphenylalanine as well as decreased levels of fumaric acid, 6-deoxygalactose, glucosamine/mannosamine and L-threonine, all of which are associated with gut barrier dysfunction and inflammation. Furthermore, there was a decreased abundance of a short-chain acylcarnitine and both odd-chain and even-chain fatty acids, suggesting that altered energy metabolism may be associated with CRC progression. Multi-omics integration revealed a factor shaped by differential contributions from metabolites and lipids linked to Lachnospiraceae spp., with compounds like lactic acid, methylmalonic acid, linoleic acid and palmitoleic acid positively associated with inflammation and CRC, while hypoxanthine, nicotinic acid/2-picolinic acid, L-carnitine and deoxycarnitine, showed potential protective associations. These findings highlight the complex interplay between gut inflammation, microbiome dynamics and metabolic reprogramming in CRC and suggest that AOM/DSS dosing substantially influences these interactions.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
The incidence of early-onset colorectal cancer (EOCRC) has increased in recent decades; however, most metabolomic studies have focused on all age groups. Consequently, it remains uncertain how metabolic alterations drive EOCRC progression and whether biomarker signatures identified in older patients are valid in younger populations. We performed untargeted plasma metabolomic profiling of 791 participants, including those with colorectal cancer (CRC), colorectal adenoma (CRA), and healthy controls. Individuals were stratified by age (<50 and ≥50 years) to explore metabolic remodeling during EOCRC and late-onset CRC (LOCRC) development. A multistep feature selection process and 12 machine learning algorithms were used to establish an age-informed CRC detection model. CRC progression was associated with the suppression of caffeine and histidine metabolism and the enhancement of amino acid metabolism, particularly branched-chain amino acid, glycine-serine, and arginine-proline pathways. EOCRC showed increased phenylalanine, butanoate, and lipoic acid metabolism, whereas LOCRC was enriched in purine and fatty acid biosynthesis. A 7-metabolite panel (caffeine, ergothioneine, hypoxanthine 1, L-valyl-L-alanine, L-seryl-L-aspartic acid, cholic acid, and cycloleucine) was trained and achieved excellent detection values in all age groups (AUC > 0.95). SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) analysis highlighted metabolite-specific contributions, supporting biological interpretability. These findings delineate age-related metabolic remodeling in CRC and demonstrate that integrating plasma metabolomics with machine learning supports a robust and interpretable non-invasive detection approach. The proposed age-informed model may inform future age-tailored CRC detection strategies amid the increasing burden of early-onset cancers.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Microsatellite stable (MSS) colorectal cancer (CRC) is largely resistant to immune checkpoint blockade due to its immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment (TME). Ultrasound-targeted nanobubble destruction (UTND) offers a localized physical delivery method, but its active immunomodulatory mechanisms remain underexplored. Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) analyzed cellular changes in the TME. The activation of the NF-κB pathway was verified through western blot analysis, qPCR, and immunofluorescence staining. Intracellular ROS production was assessed using flow cytometry, confocal microscopy, and an enzyme immunoassay. Furthermore, the effects of Ccl8 on regulatory T (Treg) cells were examined by flow cytometry, qPCR and western blot. ScRNA-seq identified a CCL8-expressing macrophage subpopulation (Macro Ccl8) that was more abundant in the combination group. UTND promoted ROS production, which activated NF-κB signaling and increased Ccl8 transcription. CCL8 secreted by Macro Ccl8 modulated Treg function through the Ccl8-Ccr2 axis. Together with direct CTLA-4 checkpoint inhibition, this cascade contributed to elevated CD8 + T cell activity. In the CT26 mouse model, UTND combined with CTLA-4 antibody modulates the immunosuppressive TME partially through inducing Macro Ccl8 via the ROS-NF-κB-Ccl8 axis, in addition to direct CTLA-4 blockade. This dual mechanism attenuates Treg function and enhances antitumor immunity, providing a preclinical rationale for combining ultrasound-based physical intervention with immunotherapy in MSS CRC.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Patients with advanced colorectal cancer undergoing chemotherapy face significant physical and emotional challenges. Addressing their psychological needs is crucial for improving their quality of life. Snyder's Hope Theory, focusing on the role of hope in coping, offers a framework for enhancing nursing care. This study investigates the use of a hierarchical nursing model based on this theory to improve patient coping strategies and hope levels. 200 patients with advanced colorectal cancer undergoing chemotherapy at our center from July 2022 to July 2023 were included and randomly divided into a control group (n = 100) and an observation group (n = 100). The control group received routine nursing intervention for advanced colorectal cancer chemotherapy and routine guidance before and after chemotherapy. The observation group implemented a hierarchical nursing model based on Snyder's hope theory. The medical coping questionnaire (MCMQ) and Herth Hope Index (HHI) scores of patients in both groups before and after intervention were compared. Before the intervention, there was no statistically significant difference in MCMQ and HHI scores between the two groups (P > 0.05). After 6 cycles of chemotherapy, the observation group had higher scores in the face dimension and lower scores in the surrender and avoidance dimensions compared to the control group, with statistically significant differences (P < 0.05); the observation group had higher HHI scores than the control group, with statistically significant differences (P < 0.05). The hierarchical nursing model based on Snyder's hope theory can effectively improve the disease-coping strategies of patients with advanced colorectal cancer undergoing chemotherapy and increase their hope level, which is worthy of clinical promotion and application.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Pathological node negativity does not exclude adverse local or histopathological features in colon cancer. The ability of routinely available inflammatory-nutritional indices to identify such features specifically within pN0 disease remains uncertain. This retrospective single-center cohort used an institutional colon cancer registry covering 2022-2026. Of 234 surgical records, 105 pN-positive cases and 5 pN0 cases with synchronous metastasis were excluded, leaving 124 patients with pN0M0 disease. The primary endpoint was a composite of lymphovascular invasion, perineural invasion, bowel obstruction, or bowel perforation; pT4 disease and 30-day mortality were excluded from the primary definition and evaluated in sensitivity analyses. Eight preoperative indices were recalculated from raw laboratory values using explicit unit-specific formulas. Associations were assessed by logistic regression adjusted for age, sex, ASA class, pT4, tumor size, and emergency surgery. Among 124 patients with pN0M0 colon cancer, 71 (57.3%) had at least one composite adverse clinicopathological feature. PNI had an AUC of 0.535 (95% CI 0.433-0.637) and CALLY an AUC of 0.518 (95% CI 0.412-0.624). The clinical covariate model had an apparent AUC of 0.777, and addition of any individual index changed the AUC by no more than 0.006. In exploratory survival analysis, the composite endpoint was associated with worse overall survival (3-year OS, 68.1% vs. 94.1%; log-rank p = 0.002). Preoperative inflammatory-nutritional indices showed no clinically useful discrimination for composite adverse clinicopathological features in pN0M0 colon cancer and should not be used as stand-alone tools for this purpose. Conventional clinicopathological variables were more informative. The exploratory survival findings require external validation and do not establish treatment-predictive utility.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Colorectal cancer (CRC) remains one of the leading causes of cancer-related mortality worldwide, and resistance to conventional therapies highlights the need for novel adjunctive treatment strategies. Although Lactobacillus casei (L. casei) has shown promising anticancer potential, its poor survival under gastrointestinal conditions limits its therapeutic application. The viability of encapsulated probiotics was evaluated under simulated gastrointestinal conditions. Cytotoxic effects on HT-29 colorectal cancer cells and human dermal fibroblast (HDF) cells were evaluated using the MTT assay, and the expression of apoptosis-related genes (BAX and BCL-2) was analyzed by quantitative real-time PCR (qRT-PCR). Encapsulation efficiency reached 97.17%. Encapsulated L. casei exhibited significantly higher survival in simulated gastric (3.57 ± 0.29 log CFU/mL) and intestinal (3.65 ± 0.27 log CFU/mL) fluids, whereas free bacteria became non-viable after 120 min. Although encapsulated L. casei showed a higher IC₅₀ (1 × 10⁷ CFU/mL) than the free preparation, it retained significant selective anticancer activity by upregulating BAX and downregulating BCL-2 in HT-29 cells without affecting HDF cells. These findings demonstrate that alginate-whey protein/chitosan microencapsulation substantially enhances probiotic gastrointestinal survival while preserving apoptosis-mediated selective anticancer activity, supporting its potential as a probiotic-based adjunctive strategy for colorectal cancer and warranting further in vivo investigation.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Colorectal cancer is one of the most common malignancies worldwide and, despite recent advances in diagnosis and treatment, it remains associated with high mortality rates. Therefore, there is a growing need for novel therapeutic strategies. Medicinal plants, as natural sources of bioactive compounds, offer promising opportunities for anticancer drug development. The present study aimed to investigate the effects of Artemisia biennis L. on the SW480 colorectal cancer cell line and its impact on the expression of apoptosis-related genes (BAX and BCL-2) and metastasis-related genes (MMP1 and MMP9). Aqueous and butanolic (polar) as well as hexane and ethyl acetate (non-polar) fractions of A. biennis were evaluated at different concentrations and exposure times for their effects on cell growth and viability. The results demonstrated that polar fractions, particularly the aqueous one, significantly reduced SW480 cell viability, with stronger effects observed at longer treatment durations. IC₅₀ values of the polar fractions were lower than those of non-polar fractions. Moreover, BAX gene expression was significantly altered in the hexane fraction, while BCL-2 expression showed notable changes in the aqueous fraction. A decrease in MMP1 and MMP9 expression was also observed in the butanol and ethyl acetate fractions, suggesting reduced migratory potential. In line with these findings, the scratch assay showed that ethyl acetate and butanolic fractions significantly inhibited SW480 cell migration, with the butanolic fraction exerting the strongest anti-migratory effect. Overall, these findings indicate that bioactive compounds from A. biennis can suppress colorectal cancer cell growth through apoptosis induction and consistent with inhibition of migration-related behavior, highlighting their potential for further investigation as anticancer agents.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
The role of minimally invasive surgery (MIS) in pathological T4 colon cancer remains controversial because of the technical complexity of multivisceral resections and concerns regarding oncological adequacy. This study aimed to compare short-term postoperative outcomes following minimally invasive and open colectomy in patients with locally advanced (pT4) colon cancer. We conducted a retrospective single-centre cohort study including consecutive patients who underwent surgical resection for pathological T4 colon cancer between May 2018 and September 2025. Patients were stratified according to surgical approach (minimally invasive vs open) and pathological substage (T4a vs T4b). The primary endpoint was the occurrence of any postoperative complication within 30 days. Secondary endpoints included severe postoperative complications (Clavien-Dindo grade ≥ III) and conversion to open surgery. Multivariable and Firth-penalised logistic regression analyses were performed to identify independent predictors of postoperative morbidity. A total of 114 patients with pathological T4 colon cancer were included, of whom 79 (69.3%) underwent minimally invasive surgery and 35 (30.7%) underwent primary open surgery. Overall postoperative complications occurred more frequently after open surgery. Multivariable analysis identified surgical approach as an independent predictor of postoperative morbidity (OR 2.72, p = 0.032). Severe complications were independently associated with increasing age (OR 1.06, p = 0.010). Compared with T4a tumours, T4b lesions were associated with greater operative complexity, lower use of minimally invasive surgery, and higher postoperative complication rates. Exploratory analyses also suggested that preoperative bowel obstruction and altered bowel habits may be associated with an increased risk of conversion. In experienced colorectal centres, minimally invasive colectomy appears to be a safe and feasible option for carefully selected patients with pathological T4 colon cancer. In this consecutive real-world cohort, minimally invasive surgery was associated with lower short-term postoperative morbidity than primary open surgery. These findings should be interpreted in light of the observational study design and the potential for residual selection bias. Larger prospective multicentre studies with long-term oncological follow-up are warranted. This study was registered with the Research Registry (researchregistry11844).

The development of immune checkpoint inhibitors has improved the treatment outcomes for patients with many types of cancer. However, the clinical benefits remain limited in many patients, highlighting the need for novel therapeutic strategies to enhance antitumor immunity. Hepatocyte nuclear factor 1A (HNF1A) is a transcription factor that regulates the expression of several liver-specific genes, and its expression is increased in certain cancers, such as colon and non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), compared with normal tissue. To examine mortality risks associated with steatotic liver disease (SLD), focusing on how disease subtypes (MASLD, MetALD, ALD), and fibrosis severity shape cause-specific mortality across a broad spectrum of diseases. We analysed 486156 UK Biobank participants. Causes of death were summarised by SLD subtypes. Multivariable Cox models estimated associations between SLD, its subtypes, and fibrosis severity (FIB4 score), with cause-specific mortality outcomes across ICD10 disease categories. Compared to participants without SLD (n = 307820), those with SLD had significantly higher mortality from neoplasm (HR 1.24 (1.20, 1.28)), circulatory (1.57 (1.50, 1.64)), and digestive diseases (1.85 (1.67, 2.05)), as well as from metabolic, and genitourinary diseases, across all FIB4 score levels. Importantly, SLD subtypes exhibited distinct and unequal patterns of cause-specific mortality, with further stratification by fibrosis severity revealing graded risk differentials. SLD is associated with unequal mortality risks across a wide range of disease categories, driven by substantial heterogeneity across subtypes, fibrosis severity and outcomes. Extrahepatic cancers and circulatory diseases contribute most to overall mortality, but the magnitude of risk varies markedly. These findings highlight the need for risk-stratified, multidisciplinary management strategies that account for both subtypes and fibrosis stage, targeting liver progression, cardiometabolic burden, and cancer prevention.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Salvage surgery for local regrowth following watch-and-wait (W&W) after total neoadjuvant therapy (TNT) is perceived to be technically more difficult than immediate surgery after treatment. However, surgical difficulty lacks standardised definition and reporting. This methodological review proposes a structured minimum outcome set (MOS) to distinguish intra-operative technical complexity from surgery-related morbidity and evaluates current reporting against this framework. A predefined framework comprised two domains: (1) surgery-related morbidity (Clavien-Dindo major complications, 30- or 90-day mortality, anastomotic leak, reoperation/readmission within 30 days and stoma status) and (2) intra-operative technical complexity (surgical approach, conversion, operative time, blood loss and a predefined pelvic complexity metric). R0/R1 resection status was recorded separately as a contextual oncological measure. A systematic review identified studies reporting salvage surgery for local regrowth after TNT and W&W. Reporting of MOS variables was enumerated and risk of bias assessed using a topic-specific ROBINS-I tool. Ten studies met the inclusion criteria, comprising 569 patients managed with TNT and W&W; 198 (35%) developed local regrowth and 172 (87%) underwent salvage surgery. Only one study reported major complications with salvage-specific denominators. Mortality, anastomotic leak, reoperation and stoma outcomes were absent or pooled. R0/R1 status was reported in seven studies but often without salvage-specific denominators. No study reported objective intra-operative metrics corresponding to predefined technical complexity variables. Risk of bias ranged from moderate to serious. Current reporting is insufficient to define the safety or technical complexity of salvage surgery after TNT and W&W. The proposed MOS offers an exploratory basis for standardised reporting and may inform future consensus-driven core outcome set development.

The immune landscape of the tumor microenvironment significantly influences the development and prognosis of colorectal cancer (CRC). High intratumoral and stromal expressions of CD3+ and CD8+ T lymphocytes have been associated with a better prognosis in CRC patients. However, the prognostic role of antigen-presenting cells, such as dendritic cells and macrophages, has received less attention. In this study, we assessed the impact of CD11c expression and the disease-specific survival (DSS) in CRC patients. Thus, we evaluated the CD11c expression on tissue microarray samples via immunohistochemistry from 516 patients who underwent surgery at Helsinki University Hospital between 2000 and 2005. Samples were categorized as low expression (<5% positive stromal area) and high expression (≥5% positive). Colon and rectal cancer patients were analyzed separately using Cox regression for survival analysis. A lower CD11c expression associated with a worse DSS among rectal cancer patients (p < 0.001) and right-sided colon cancer patients (p = 0.03), but not among left-sided colon cancer patients (p = 0.41). Among rectal cancer patients, results remained consistent regardless of whether the patient received preoperative radiation (p < 0.003 and p = 0.03, respectively). In the multivariable analysis after adjusting for age, sex, stage, grade, and a mismatch repair status, a lower CD11c expression remained an independent prognostic factor among rectal cancer patients (p = 0.009), but not among colon cancer patients (p = 0.15). These results suggest that stromal CD11c expression captures the distinct immunological characteristics of rectal cancer compared to colon cancer. We conclude that CD11c could serve as a prognostic marker for rectal cancer patients. However, the immunological mechanisms differentiating colon and rectal cancers warrant further research.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Robotic right colectomy may facilitate complex intracorporeal dissection and reconstruction; however, previous comparative syntheses often combined laparoscopic extracorporeal anastomosis with robotic intracorporeal anastomosis. This imbalance makes it difficult to determine whether reported differences reflect the surgical platform or the reconstructive technique. We therefore compared robotic and laparoscopic right colectomy only in studies in which intracorporeal anastomosis was planned in both groups. PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, and Web of Science were searched from the inception to April 12, 2026. Records were deduplicated and screened in Covidence. Four non-randomized observational comparative studies were included. The primary outcome was study-defined overall postoperative morbidity, with definitions and ascertainment windows varying among studies. Secondary outcomes included operative time, conversion to open surgery, anastomotic leak, hospital stay, lymph-node harvest, and mortality. Mortality and long-term oncological outcomes were summarized narratively when comparable effect estimates were unavailable. Random-effects models, ROBINS-I, and GRADE were used for quantitative outcomes. Four studies involving 977 patients (603 robotic and 374 laparoscopic) were included. Overall postoperative morbidity occurred in 142/603 robotic and 107/374 laparoscopic patients (RR 0.84, 95% CI 0.67-1.05). No statistically significant differences were identified for conversion to open surgery (7/603 vs. 8/374; RR 0.91, 95% CI 0.13-6.33), anastomotic leak (16/603 vs. 11/374; RR 0.88, 95% CI 0.41-1.89), hospital stay (MD - 0.47 days, 95% CI - 1.00 to 0.06), or lymph node harvest (MD - 0.55 nodes, 95% CI - 3.16 to 2.06). Operative time was non-significantly longer with robotics in the primary analysis (MD 39.69 min, 95% CI - 2.19 to 81.57; I²=96%); the exploratory leave-one-out result remained heterogeneous and study-dependent. This exploratory synthesis of four non-randomized studies found no statistically significant short-term advantage of robotic over laparoscopic right colectomy when intracorporeal anastomosis was planned in both groups. These findings do not establish equivalence or exclude clinically important benefits or harms. Platform selection should therefore remain individualized according to surgeon experience, institutional workflow, resource availability, and patient and procedural complexity.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Current guidelines stratify patients with Lynch syndrome (LS) for colorectal cancer (CRC) risk and recommend colonoscopy frequency based on age and DNA mismatch repair genes with pathogenic variants. Despite following these guidelines, many patients are diagnosed with CRC after colonoscopy (i.e., postcolonoscopy CRC [PCRC]). Studying LS precancerous polyp risk rather than CRC risk could lead to more effective CRC prevention. This prospective cohort study analyzed data from patients with LS undergoing colonoscopy at Mayo Clinic from March 22, 2002, to June 20, 2025. The study included data from 143 patients with LS who underwent 557 colonoscopies. Two patients were diagnosed with CRC at their initial colonoscopy; however, no patients were diagnosed with PCRC at a subsequent colonoscopy. Precancerous polyp detection rates were 37.9% for adenomas and 11.8% for sessile serrated lesions (SSL). Predictors for identifying a precancerous polyp during colonoscopy included older age, history of prior colon adenomas, not having a previous colonoscopy at Mayo Clinic, and family history of CRC. A 6-tier LS adenoma/sessile serrated lesion (LASS) score was developed incorporating these factors. The median LASS score was 4 for lesion-positive colonoscopies and 3 for lesion-negative colonoscopies (P<.001). Adenoma and SSL detection rates increased with each additional LASS point. LASS points with corresponding adenoma and SSL detection rates were 0 (14.7%, 2.9%); 1 (17.8%, 8.9%); 2 (26.5%, 9.5%); 3 (35.0%, 12.5%); 4 (46.9%, 13.6%); 5 (57.8%, 15.5%). The LASS score is a simple prediction tool for identifying patients with LS at higher risk of developing precancerous lesions. With no cases of PCRC, the precancerous polyp detection rates reported here could serve as quality benchmarks after validation.

This study aimed to describe the clinical presentation, histopathological patterns, disease stage, and surgical management of colorectal cancer patients treated at a major tertiary hospital in Mogadishu. A retrospective observational study was conducted at Mogadishu Somali-Türkiye Recep Tayyip Erdoğan Training and Research Hospital. Medical records of all adult patients with histologically confirmed colorectal cancer who underwent surgery between January 2020 and December 2024 were reviewed. Data on demographics, clinical presentation, tumor characteristics, disease stage, surgical procedures, and postoperative complications were extracted from the hospital's electronic database and analyzed using descriptive statistics. A total of 59 patients were included, of whom 69.5% were male. The mean age was 57.44 ± 16.48 years, with 32.2% of patients aged ≤ 50 years. The most common presenting symptom was intestinal obstruction (74.6%), followed by rectal bleeding (15.3%) and perforation (8.5%). The caecum (35.6%) and sigmoid colon (32.2%) were the most frequent tumor sites. Adenocarcinoma was the predominant histological type (67.8%), followed by mucinous adenocarcinoma (15.3%) and signet-ring cell carcinoma (5.1%). Well-differentiated tumors accounted for 49.2% of cases, while 30.5% were poorly differentiated. Lymphovascular invasion and perineural invasion were present in 37.3% and 42.4% of patients, respectively. Most patients presented with advanced disease, with Stage III and Stage IV accounting for the majority of cases. Surgical management was dominated by resection and anastomosis (42.4%) and end ileostomy (30.5%), with right hemicolectomy being the most common operation (42.3%). Postoperative complications included wound infection (10.2%) and anastomotic leak (8.5%). Colorectal cancer patients in Somalia commonly present with advanced-stage disease and potentially aggressive histopathological features, leading to a high burden of emergency and palliative surgical care. Limited access to chemotherapy and the absence of radiotherapy further restrict treatment options. Strengthening early detection, diagnostic services, screening capacity, and oncology infrastructure is essential to facilitate timely diagnosis and improve colorectal cancer care in Somalia.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
In rectal cancer surgery, dissection on either side of the endopelvic fascia (EPF) determines whether this layer remains on the pelvic wall or is included with the specimen. However, its continuity with adjacent pelvic wall and rectal supporting tissues, and the anatomical meaning of these local dissection planes, remain unclear. This cadaveric study aimed to clarify the macroscopic and histological characteristics of the EPF in relation to the obturator fascia, rectal wall, and hiatal ligament. Macroscopic examination of three formalin-fixed cadavers assessed fascial architecture around the levator ani, obturator internus, and rectum. Histological analysis of eight formalin-fixed cadavers used Masson's trichrome staining and α-smooth muscle actin immunohistochemistry. EPF thickness was measured in six specimens at defined distances from the obturator fascia and rectal wall. The EPF formed a dense connective tissue layer on the superior surface of the levator ani and continued laterally into the obturator fascia without a distinct boundary. Medially, it transitioned into interfascicular connective tissue between rectal longitudinal muscle bundles and the smooth muscle-rich hiatal ligament. In four obturator-side specimens, thickness ranged from 0.03 to 0.65 mm. In two rectal side specimens, thickness at the rectal interface was 1.69 and 2.82 mm; these limited descriptive observations do not establish a regional difference. The EPF is continuous with pelvic wall and rectal supporting tissues rather than a discrete membrane. These cadaveric findings define its local morphology but do not establish implications for surgical dissection planes, circumferential resection margin status, operative or oncological outcomes, or pelvic function.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Salvage surgery is the standard of care for patients with pelvic recurrences from anorectal cancers, including rectal adenocarcinoma and anal squamous cell carcinoma (ASCC). Given the associated morbidity, some patients decline surgery, while others are considered unresectable, and controlling pelvic disease in these patients remains a major challenge. Interstitial brachytherapy (ISBT) has demonstrated efficacy in recurrent urologic and gynecologic malignancies, yet its role in the setting of recurrent anorectal cancer is undefined. A retrospective analysis on a series of consecutive patients with anorectal cancer pelvic recurrences treated with ISBT between 2018 and 2025 at a single Canadian tertiary center was performed. Cumulative incidence function was used to estimate in-field local, out-of-field pelvic and distant progression, and Kaplan-Meier was used to estimate overall survival. Fourteen patients (10 adenocarcinoma and 4 ASCC) were included, with a median target lesion size of 3.7 cm. Six (42.9%) patients were treated with external beam radiation therapy (EBRT; median 45 Gy) and ISBT (median 17.3 Gy), while 8 (57.1%) received ISBT alone (median 30 Gy). The overall response rate was 57.1% and median duration of in-field target control was 20.3 months. Median overall survival was 31 months. Out-of-field pelvic and/or distant progression were the predominant patterns of failure, with only one (7.1%) patient demonstrating isolated in-field progression and 3 (21.4%) patients dying with isolated pelvic disease. Grade 3 toxicity, including fibrotic and necrotic complications, was observed in 6 (42.9%) patients, five of whom subsequently developed progressive disease at the site of toxicity. Salvage ISBT results in durable control for anorectal cancer pelvic recurrences with acceptable toxicity profile. Distant relapse often precedes local progression in this high-risk population and death from isolated uncontrolled pelvic disease is rare using this strategy.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Defunctioning stomas are standard in low anterior resection (LAR) posttotal neoadjuvant therapy (TNT) to mitigate anastomotic complications. While loop ileostomy is common, it poses significant metabolic risks. This study investigates whether loop colostomy may reduce renal and electrolyte complications, without compromising surgical or stoma reversal outcomes. We retrospectively analyzed 97 patients with rectal cancer treated at King Hussein Cancer Center (January 2020 to November 2024) who underwent TNT followed by LAR with a defunctioning stoma (ileostomy, n = 57; colostomy, n = 40). Primary outcomes were acute kidney injury (AKI) and hyponatremia. Secondary outcomes included stoma-related and closure-related complications. Data were compared using chi-squared, Mann-Whitney U-test, and Kaplan-Meier analysis. Baseline characteristics were comparable, except for higher baseline creatinine in ileostomy patients (p = 0.002). Ileostomy was associated with more AKI (35.1% versus 2.5%, p < 0.001) and hyponatremia (57.8% versus 20.0%, p < 0.001) with greater stoma output (p < 0.001). Skin excoriation was more frequent with ileostomy (24.5% versus 5.0%, p = 0.011), while colostomy had higher stoma prolapse (22.5% versus 1.7%, p < 0.001). Other postoperative outcomes were similar. However, blood loss during stoma reversal was greater with ileostomy (p < 0.001). Kaplan-Meier analysis showed no difference in time to closure (median 84 versus 85 days, p = 0.491). In multivariate analysis, ileostomy remained associated with AKI and hyponatremia after adjustment for the included covariates. Loop colostomy may represent an alternative to loop ileostomy after LAR following TNT, with fewer metabolic complications and comparable surgical outcomes, despite a higher prolapse risk.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
In laparoscopic surgery, uninterrupted visualization is essential for efficiency and safety. Temporary laparoscope withdrawal for image-quality restoration results in "out-of-body" (OOB) time, a historically unquantified workflow disruption. Advances in artificial intelligence (AI)-based computer vision enable large-scale OOB measurement. We aimed to quantify OOB exposure across common general-surgery procedures and estimate intraoperative and economic burden. Retrospective observational study including consecutive laparoscopic procedures performed at an urban-university hospital (October 2020-October 2025), routinely video-recorded and analyzed using an AI-platform for automated OOB-intervals detection. Primary outcomes were OOB time and percentage of operative duration. Secondary outcomes included associations with operative time, intraoperative events, and operating room costs projected using a hypothetical time-driven costing model. Analyzed procedures (n = 5041) included appendectomy, cholecystectomy, hernia repair, colorectal resection, and metabolic-bariatric surgery. 49.6% of procedures exceeded 5% OOB exposure, 21.3% exceeded 10%, and 9.4% exceeded 15% of operative duration. OOB time was significantly associated with operative duration across procedures (Spearman ρ 0.58-0.74, all p < 0.001). In pooled adjusted models, each 5% increase in OOB was associated with an 8.3% operative duration increase; each additional 5 min corresponded to a 28.1% increase (both p < 0.001). OOB exposure significantly co-occurred alongside increased intraoperative events (OR 1.09, 95% CI 1.02-1.16, p = 0.012). Projected cumulative OOB-related modeled burden reached $758,829 ($143,529 annually), primarily concentrated in high-burden cases. AI-enabled OOB time quantification at large scale highlights its potential association with operative complexity and estimated operating-room resource utilization. Further studies are needed to clarify causal and clinical significance and validate true hospital cost implications.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Anal canal lesions (ACLs) represent a significant clinical challenge requiring consideration of sphincter function preservation. Endoscopic submucosal dissection (ESD) is a promising minimally invasive technique for en bloc resection, yet its application in the anal canal is technically demanding due to the narrow lumen and somatic innervation. We conducted this meta-analysis to evaluate the efficacy and safety of ESD for ACLs. Following PRISMA guidelines, we searched PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science through February 2026. Eligible studies involved adult patients undergoing ESD for lesions originating in the anal canal. Primary outcomes were en bloc and R0 resection rates. Secondary outcomes included complications and local recurrence. Pooled proportions were calculated using random-effects models. Four retrospective studies involving 150 patients were included. The pooled en bloc resection rate was 94.1% (95% CI: 89.6%-97.4%). The R0 resection rate was 84.8% (95% CI: 78.7%-90.0%). Safety analysis revealed pooled incidences of anal pain at 18.7% (95% CI: 0.0%-60.0%), delayed bleeding at 6.6% (95% CI: 1.1%-16.1%), and anal stenosis at 1.1% (95% CI: 0.0%-3.7%). The pooled local recurrence rate was 4.7% (95% CI: 0.6%-12.3%). Median follow-up for the studies ranged from 9 to 37 months. In experienced centers, ESD appears to be a feasible and promising organ-preserving approach for anal canal lesions, achieving high en bloc and R0 resection rates with low early recurrence. Comparative and longer-term data would help define its role relative to surgical excision or repeated ablative therapies.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Anal fissure is a common anorectal disorder. Despite initial conservative treatment, a considerable proportion of cases become chronic, significantly impairing quality of life. Surgical intervention, particularly lateral internal sphincterotomy (LIS), has long been the mainstay for managing sphincter spasm in chronic anal fissure (CAF). However, surgery often leads to delayed wound healing. We propose a multi-center randomized controlled trial to evaluate whether LIS combined with skin grafting can promote fissure healing. This is a multi-center, hospital-based, parallel-group randomized controlled trial conducted at three hospitals. Eligible adults (n = 104) with refractory anal fissures will be block-randomized (block size = 6) to either LIS plus skin grafting (experimental) or LIS alone (control). All surgeries will be performed by attending colorectal surgeons or senior consultants. Efficacy and safety endpoints will be systematically monitored, documented, and analyzed. LIS effectively resolves chronic anal fissures with low recurrence and acceptable safety. Adding autologous skin grafting may accelerate epithelialization and shorten healing time in refractory cases. Chinese Clinical Trial Register, ID: ChiCTR2400079420. Registered on 3 January 2024.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Distant metastasis is the leading cause of cancer-related mortality, and inflammation plays a significant role in promoting cancer metastasis. Patients undergoing surgery are generally more susceptible to bacterial infection due to surgical trauma and immunological dysfunction. However, the extent to which bacterial inflammation contributes to tumor progression remains unclear. We conducted an integrative analysis of colorectal cancer patients who underwent curative surgery and experimental animal models to investigate the impact of anastomotic leakage on oncological outcomes. Using a cecal ligation and puncture (CLP) mouse model, we analyzed NK cell infiltration and activity in peripheral blood and liver tissues under infectious inflammatory conditions, together with NET deposition in metastatic niches. Finally, we examined the efficacy of NET degradation or CTSG inhibition in restoring NK cell-mediated tumor cytotoxicity and preventing tumor metastasis in two distinct mouse models of severe infection. Postoperative infectious complications were associated with increased metastatic recurrence. In mouse models, infection-induced NETs impaired NK cell proliferation and function. Mechanistically, NET-associated CTSG contributed to reduced surface NKp46 expression, a key activating receptor on NK cells. Disruption of NETs or pharmacological inhibition of CTSG restored NK cell cytotoxicity and suppressed metastatic colonization. NET-associated CTSG undermines NK cell-mediated tumor surveillance, contributing to infection-driven metastasis. Targeting the NET-CTSG axis may offer a novel therapeutic strategy to prevent postoperative metastatic progression.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Epitranscriptomic RNA modifications have emerged as a fundamental regulatory layer linking RNA metabolism with genome maintenance, DNA damage response (DDR), and therapeutic resistance during cancer evolution. Throughout tumorigenesis, persistent oncogenic signaling, replication stress, oxidative stress, metabolic reprogramming, chronic inflammation, and anticancer treatments continuously generate DNA lesions that challenge genome integrity. Although the DDR network normally safeguards genomic stability by coordinating DNA damage sensing, checkpoint activation, and repair pathway selection, established cancer cells frequently hijack these protective mechanisms to survive radiotherapy, platinum-based chemotherapy, poly(ADP-ribose) polymerase (PARP) inhibitors, and other genotoxic therapies. Increasing evidence indicates that epitranscriptomic regulation is an integral component of the DDR rather than merely a downstream consequence of DNA damage. RNA modifications dynamically coordinate transcript stability, RNA processing, translation, alternative splicing, R-loop homeostasis, DNA: RNA hybrid dynamics, repair factor recruitment, metabolic adaptation, replication stress tolerance, and cell-cycle checkpoint activation, thereby reshaping cellular responses to genotoxic stress. Importantly, accumulating evidence suggests that RNA modifications rarely function through isolated signaling pathways. Instead, distinct epitranscriptomic marks converge on shared biological processes that collectively determine genome stability, DNA repair capacity, and therapeutic responsiveness. In this Review, we provide a comprehensive overview of how RNA modifications remodel the DDR throughout cancer evolution, with particular emphasis on cancer type-specific mechanisms rather than conventional modification-based classification. We discuss recent advances across multiple malignancies, including lung cancer, breast cancer, ovarian cancer, hepatocellular carcinoma, glioblastoma, bladder cancer, colorectal cancer, pancreatic cancer, osteosarcoma, and other solid tumors. Furthermore, we critically evaluate the current evidence supporting individual regulatory mechanisms, distinguish well-established causal pathways from observations that remain largely correlative or context-dependent, and highlight unresolved controversies that continue to limit clinical translation. Finally, we discuss the major conceptual and technical challenges facing the field and propose future directions for integrating the RNA modification-DDR axis into precision oncology.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Colorectal cancer prevention depends on detection of precursor lesions, and metabolic dysfunction may shape early colorectal neoplasia before invasive cancer develops. Evidence linking the fasting triglyceride-glucose (TyG) index with colonoscopy-defined polyp burden in younger and middle-aged diagnostic populations remains limited. This retrospective single-center cross-sectional study included 169 adults aged 18 to 59 years who underwent complete diagnostic colonoscopy and had fasting triglyceride and glucose measurements within 90 days beforehand. Patients had no polyps (n = 58), 1 to 2 polyps (n = 60), or 3 or more polyps (n = 51); the primary outcome was 3 or more polyps. Logistic regression assessed TyG continuously and by tertiles, adjusting for age, sex, body mass index category, hypertension, and ever smoking. Spline modeling, discrimination, calibration, and E-value analyses were performed. Sensitivity analyses added diet, physical activity, alcohol use, family history, and colonoscopy-quality indicators; exploratory analyses examined incremental value over conventional risk factors and 2-hour postprandial glucose. Mean TyG increased across polyp-burden groups (8.44 +/- 0.52, 8.72 +/- 0.51, and 8.90 +/- 0.49; P < 0.001). Each 1-unit increase was associated with higher adjusted odds of multiple polyps (adjusted odds ratio [aOR], 2.41; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.54 to 3.77; P = 0.002), and the highest tertile with substantially higher odds than the lowest (aOR, 4.78; 95% CI, 2.00 to 11.41; P = 0.005). Discrimination was only fair (area under the curve, 0.678). After further adjustment for diet, physical activity, alcohol use, family history, and colonoscopy-quality indicators, the association attenuated and lost significance (aOR, 1.63; 95% CI, 0.97 to 2.73; P = 0.064). Adding TyG to conventional risk factors raised discrimination only from 0.754 to 0.781. Higher fasting TyG was associated with multiple colorectal polyps in adults undergoing diagnostic colonoscopy, although much of this association was shared with dietary pattern and physical activity. TyG is best regarded as a metabolic correlate of precursor-lesion burden rather than an independent determinant, and its fair discrimination and small incremental value preclude stand-alone triage use. Prospective multiethnic validation with standardized lifestyle assessment and dynamic glycemic measures is warranted.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
The purpose of this study was to review the clinical application of cold resection for colorectal polyps and determine its efficacy and safety for polyps of different sizes. A narrative review was conducted to analyze and compare key indicators, including complete resection rate (CRR), bleeding rate, perforation rate, and recurrence rate, for polyps of different sizes undergoing cold versus hot resection. The CRR of cold snare polypectomy (CSP) for resecting colorectal polyps measuring ≤ 10 mm is comparable to that of hot resection. However, the risk of delayed bleeding and perforation is significantly lower with CSP. With nonpedunculated colorectal polyps measuring 10-19 mm, particularly sessile serrated lesions (SSLs), cold resection (e.g., piecemeal cold snare polypectomy (pCSP)) is a safe and feasible option. For colorectal adenomas, however, the risk of recurrence with cold resection may be slightly higher than with hot resection. For large (≥ 20 mm) sessile serrated lesions (L-SSLs), cold resection offers significant safety advantages; however, the risk of recurrence is higher than with hot resection. Due to the higher risk of recurrence, cold resection is not recommended for removing large (≥ 20 mm) nonpedunculated adenomatous polyps (LNPCPs). Cold resection is particularly suitable for patients taking anticoagulants and those in poor health who cannot tolerate complications. Cold resection has become the standard treatment for small polyps due to its excellent safety profile. It is now also used for some larger polyps, particularly SSLs. However, strict adherence to histology guidance is crucial for larger polyps and adenomatous lesions because of the higher rate of postoperative recurrence.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Radiotherapy resistance remains a major challenge in the clinical management of colorectal cancer (CRC), highlighting the urgent need to identify novel regulators of radiosensitivity. Here, we reveal a multi-layered mechanism whereby TICRR drives CRC radioresistance. TICRR is significantly upregulated in radioresistant CRC tissues and cell lines and is associated with poor patient survival. TICRR knockdown suppresses tumor cell proliferation, impairs DNA damage repair, and enhances radiosensitivity both in vitro and in vivo. Mechanistically, TICRR functions as an RNA-binding protein (RBP) to stabilize the mitochondrial protein C1QBP mRNA, thereby maintaining mitochondrial function and regulating AMP levels, which in turn modulate the AMPK/HIF pathway and VEGFA transcription. TICRR-high tumor cells interact with endothelial cells via the VEGFA-VEGFR1 signaling axis and transfer mitochondria to endothelial cells to enhance angiogenesis, a process disrupted by TICRR downregulation. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that TICRR promotes CRC radioresistance through a multi-layered mechanism involving mitochondrial function and tumor-endothelial cell communication, highlighting TICRR inhibition as a potential strategy for radiosensitization.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Microsatellite-stable (MSS) colorectal cancers (CRCs) are largely refractory to immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) due to immunologically "cold" tumor microenvironments (TMEs) characterized by limited T-cell infiltration. While RecQ-mediated genome instability 2 (RMI2) is known for regulating DNA repair, its role in anti-tumor immunity remains unclear. Here, we demonstrate that RMI2 deficiency impairs homologous recombination repair, causing cytosolic DNA accumulation, cGAS-STING pathway activation, and type I interferon signaling that boosts anti-tumor immunity. Notably, RMI2 knockout in mice synergizes with PD-1 blockade and fluorouracil to induce robust tumor regression and prolonged survival. Our data reveal that RMI2 loss derepresses the cGAS-STING pathway by disrupting DNA repair homeostasis, thereby reversing immune evasion. This paradigm shift converts MSS CRCs into "hot" tumors and renders them responsive to ICI therapy, establishing RMI2 inhibition as a novel therapeutic avenue.

Single-cell transcriptomics revealed UFC1 enrichment in malignant epithelial cells, and its expression correlated with DNA damage response and apoptosis pathways. A LASSO-Cox risk model incorporating UFM1 pathway genes effectively stratified patient prognosis. These findings identify UFC1 as a druggable effector of the UFMylation pathway in CRC chemotherapy stress and provide a framework integrating computational target identification, structure-based drug screening, and experimental validation for precision oncology.

The median PFS was 7.4mo in the ERBB2amp and 4.0 mo in the ERBB2mut group. The median OS was 17.2 mo in the ERBB2amp group and 14.8 mo in the ERBB2mut group, respectively. No unexpected safety signals were detected. Responses were detected in novel populations including thyroid carcinoma (n = 1) and KRAS co-mutated colon cancer (n = 1). ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Colorectal cancer (CRC) is highly treatable when diagnosed early, but screening benefit depends on completing both initial testing and follow-up colonoscopy (FU-CY) after a positive stool-based test. As quality measurements increasingly emphasize FU-CY after positive noninvasive CRC screening results, this study evaluated factors associated with multitarget stool DNA (mt-sDNA) adherence and FU-CY completion within the Providence Healthcare System in California. This retrospective cohort study linked laboratory data from Abbott with administrative claims data from Komodo Health. The study population included mt-sDNA tests shipped to patients between July 2016 and June 2023. Adherence was defined as return of a completed test with a valid result within one year of shipment. Completion of FU-CY was defined as the first eligible colonoscopy claim occurring within 1 year of a positive mt-sDNA result. Multivariable logistic regression was used to identify factors associated with mt-sDNA adherence. Among test kits with a positive mt-sDNA finding, factors associated with time to FU-CY were evaluated using Cox proportional hazards regression. Of 6191 mt-sDNA test kits, 4766 (77.0%) were completed within 1 year. Higher adjusted odds of adherence were observed among males, among patients with commercial, Medicare Advantage, or traditional Medicare insurance compared with Medi-Cal; among patients with prior mt-sDNA use; among gastroenterologist-ordered tests; and among those receiving full digital or SMS-only outreach. Among 560 patients with positive mt-sDNA results, who met the continuous enrollment requirement, 394 (70.4%) completed FU-CY within 1 year. Gastroenterologist-ordered tests were associated with shorter time to FU-CY completion (adjusted hazard ratio, 2.26; 95% CI, 1.31-3.88). High mt-sDNA screening adherence and FU-CY completion were observed in this California-based Providence cohort, although adherence varied across patient and healthcare delivery characteristics. These results suggest that both demographic and healthcare delivery factors influence the effectiveness of screening programs. These findings suggest that modifiable healthcare delivery strategies, including digital reminders, and coordinated follow-up pathways, may support participation and diagnostic continuity in stool-based CRC screening programs.

Patients with acromegaly have an increased risk of colorectal neoplasia, necessitating regular colonoscopic surveillance. However, data on bowel preparation quality in this population are limited. This study aimed to compare bowel preparation quality and colonoscopic findings between patients with acromegaly and healthy controls. Bowel preparation quality was assessed using the Aronchick Bowel Preparation Scale (ABPS), with inadequate preparation defined as ABPS scores of 4 or 5. Colonoscopic findings, including polyps, multiple polyps, diverticulosis, and hemorrhoids, were recorded. Logistic regression analysis was performed to identify independent predictors of inadequate bowel preparation. Bowel preparation quality was significantly poorer in patients with acromegaly compared with controls (p < 0.001). Excellent preparation (ABPS 1) was observed in 48.9% of controls versus only 6.5% of acromegaly patients, while poor or inadequate preparation (ABPS 4-5) was markedly more common in the acromegaly group. Polyp detection rates did not differ significantly between groups (38% vs 31.5%, p = 0.360). Hemorrhoids were significantly more prevalent in patients with acromegaly (39.2% vs 18.5%, p = 0.002). Acromegaly is independently associated with more than fivefold higher odds of inadequate bowel preparation.These findings highlight the challenges of achieving adequate bowel cleansing in patients with acromegaly and underscore the need for prospective studies to evaluate whether optimized bowel preparation strategies could improve colonoscopy quality in this population.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Colon capsule endoscopy (CCE) has emerged as a minimally-invasive alternative to colonoscopy and has in several meta-analyses shown non-inferiority in detection rates of pathology. However, CCE is a reader-dependent technique and pathology can be missed, even though images of the lesions are captured. Furthermore, misclassification of pathology can lead to erroneous conclusions, and possible delays in correct diagnosis and patient management. We present a series of cancer cases from the Danish trial CareForColon2015. All participants were recruited from the screening program with a positive fecal immunochemical test. The cancers described in this series were detected at subsequent colonoscopy and patients were treated according to the findings. We identified 4 cases of misclassified/misrepresented cancers (reported as non-neoplastic findings, such as inflammation or as a lesion significantly smaller than the actual size, as a result of suboptimal image reporting), and 1 case of a non-detected cancer (not reported by the reader, but captured in images). These cases prompt a discussion of the need for a unified terminology, reader training and implementation of artificial intelligence in the CCE reading process. This is necessary to improve the quality of CCE reporting and minimize the risk of missed pathology and misclassification of findings.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
The immune microenvironment of colorectal cancer (CRC) is characterized by pronounced cellular-state and spatial heterogeneity. B cells and macrophages bridge adaptive and innate immunity, respectively, and engage in bidirectional regulation through antibodies and immune complexes, BAFF/APRIL signaling, cytokines, chemokines, and metabolic cues. These interactions are further shaped by tumor cells, stromal components, microorganisms, and other immune populations within the tumor microenvironment. From the perspective of B cell-macrophage state coupling, this review systematically summarizes the biological foundations and reciprocal communication mechanisms underlying their interactions, with particular emphasis on their dynamic remodeling across different disease stages, tertiary lymphoid structures, distinct spatial niches within tumors, and metastatic progression. We further evaluate how established therapies and emerging experimental interventions influence this cellular network. Current evidence suggests that specific B-cell and macrophage states may form distinct functional combinations within either immune-supportive or immunosuppressive ecosystems. However, direct causal evidence remains limited, and the reproducibility of these associations across independent patient cohorts has yet to be firmly established. Future studies should integrate single-cell sequencing, B-cell receptor clonotype tracking, spatial multi-omics, and functional perturbation approaches to move beyond cellular co-occurrence and computationally inferred communication toward direct validation of functional dependencies. Such efforts will also be essential for determining whether composite state-spatial signatures can improve patient stratification, therapeutic response prediction, and treatment decision-making.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
The metabolic heterogeneity of cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs) in the colorectal cancer (CRC) microenvironment remains poorly understood. We profiled 86,142 cells from two independent CRC cohorts (GSE132465, GSE144735) using single-cell RNA-sequencing and validated findings in a public Visium dataset (GSE285505, 3,493 spots) and an external spatial cohort (GSE267401, 4 sections). Unsupervised clustering identified CAF subtypes, regulon analysis (SCENIC) mapped transcriptional drivers, and spatial deconvolution (cell2location) localized CAF populations in tissue. Unsupervised clustering of 13,003 CAFs identified a metabolically distinct subpopulation (meCAF, 4.1% of CAFs) that scored highest for glycolysis (Δ = +0.60, P < 1e-4), lactate metabolism (Δ = +0.46, P < 1e-4) and hypoxia among nine metabolic pathways compared across all three CAF subtypes. SCENIC analysis inferred HIF1A as the regulon with the highest meCAF specificity (ΔAUC = +0.111, 95% CI 0.081 to 0.134, P = 2.4e-07 by patient-paired Wilcoxon test, 23/23 patients concordant). Spatial profiling confirmed meCAF enrichment at the tumor-stroma interface with spatial concordance with lactate metabolism (Spearman ρ = 0.29-0.75). meCAF abundance was inversely correlated with distance to the cancer epithelium (ρ = -0.317, p < 3e-82), accompanied by a metabolic activity gradient. In TCGA-COADREAD (n = 410), the meCAF signature varied significantly across consensus molecular subtypes (ANOVA p = 1.9e-18), with the highest scores in CMS1 (immune subtype) and the lowest in CMS2 (epithelial subtype). These findings reveal a metabolically distinct CAF subpopulation operating within spatially restricted periepithelial micro-niches, with its clinical association to the immune-rich CMS1 subtype suggesting that stromal metabolic state may relate to the immune context of CRC.
