ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Small bowel adenocarcinoma (SBA) is a rare gastrointestinal malignancy with limited treatment options and worse outcomes than colorectal cancer. While immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) show impressive results in mismatch repair-deficient (dMMR)/microsatellite instability-high (MSI-H) tumors, microsatellite-stable (MSS) disease is traditionally considered resistant to immunotherapy. We describe a man in his 70s with recurrent duodenal adenocarcinoma who experienced disease progression after multiple systemic therapies, including cetuximab plus FOLFIRI. Molecular profiling by liquid biopsy showed MSS status with low tumor mutational burden (TMB = 1 mutation/Mb). Given the lack of standard alternatives, he was treated with nivolumab, ipilimumab, and cetuximab. Tumor regression was observed within 3 months, followed by a complete radiographic response in October 2022 and a complete metabolic response on PET/CT at 12 months. Immune-related adverse events (irAEs) included grade 2 adrenal insufficiency, vitiligo, and pneumonitis, all of which were manageable. At the latest follow-up in April 2026, the patient had maintained a complete response, approximately 42 months after the first documented radiographic complete response and 27 months after discontinuation of all anticancer therapy. This case describes an exceptional durable complete response to dual immune checkpoint blockade combined with an EGFR inhibitor in MSS duodenal adenocarcinoma. Although the relative contribution of each agent and the presence of pharmacologic synergy cannot be determined from a single case, this observation warrants further investigation in prospective trials with MSS SBA.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Extraperitoneal colostomy (EPC) following abdominoperineal resection (APR) for rectal cancer reportedly reduces stoma-related complications compared with that via transperitoneal colostomy. However, creating EPCs under laparoscopic guidance remains technically challenging. This study explored a method to create extraperitoneal tunnels using optical trocar access in 13 patients with rectal cancer undergoing laparoscopic or robotic APR. Following an incision in the posterior rectal sheath at the stoma site, a bladeless trocar with a transparent tip connected to the laparoscope was slowly propelled into the preperitoneal space under direct observation of the boundary of the preperitoneal fat and transversalis fascia. This allowed dissection of the appropriate layer and avoidance of unnecessary bleeding by visualizing the microvessels. Laparoscopic observation of the extraperitoneal route through another port facilitated optimal direction and extent of dissection. The median time to create the extraperitoneal tunnel was 8.5 min (range: 5-19). Although several studies have demonstrated methods for creating EPCs, these approaches either require additional devices or involve blunt dissection of the preperitoneal cavity, which is less ideal in terms of medical costs and safety. Methods utilizing optical trocar access may represent a simple, safe, and cost-effective alternative to previously reported techniques by requiring no additional instruments while allowing direct visualization of the dissection plane.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
The early detection and removal of colorectal polyps can help reduce colorectal cancer and mortality rates. The segmentation of colorectal polyps in colonoscopy images is difficult due to multi-scale morphology, blurred boundaries, and complex background interference.To solve this problem, we propose a network of cross-scale attention and frequency domain perception of encoder-decoder architecture.The network has two new modules: first, Scale-Aware Cross Attention Skip Connection (SCAS) uses multi-head attention mechanism and multi-scale pyramid fusion to fuse multi-scale features from encoder and decoder to enhance the model to capture polyp features of different sizes.Secondly, Dual-domain fusion (D2F) separates and assigns weights of low-frequency global information and high-frequency detail information of the feature map at bottleneck stage, improving the model to analyze spatial and frequency domains and improve polyp boundaries.Multiple public colorectal polyp segmentation datasets show that our method is competitive and performs better than existing mainstream approaches in terms of mIoU and mDice: On the CVC-ClinicDB dataset our model produces mDice of 0.922 and mIoU of 0.863, outperforming UNet, UNet++, PraNet, ACSNet, DCSAU-Net, HarDNet-CPS, ProMamba, FoBS. These results validate its strong segmentation capability and effectiveness in accurately delineating polyp regions with blurred boundaries, large size variations, and complex background interference. The proposed method provides a reliable and promising tool for clinical endoscopic assistant diagnosis. The source code is publicly available at https://github.com/si-yuan20/Robust-segmentation-of-colon-polyps-Unet.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
The validity of ILD coding in US claims data among patients with cancer remains unclear. We conducted a study to test the validity of ILD coding in claims data in patients with lung, breast, ovarian, endometrial, cervical, or colorectal cancer. We used electronic health record (EHR) data from the Mass General Brigham Health Care System linked with Medicare, Medicaid, and commercial claims data from 01/01/2017 to 12/31/2024. The base algorithm required two ICD-10-CM codes for ILD, each 7 to 180 days apart. Several nested algorithms additionally requiring ILD coding by a pulmonologist, ILD-relevant procedure, excluding autoimmune diseases, and requiring chemo/immunotherapy treatment were defined. The positive predictive values (PPVs) of each claims-based algorithm were calculated against the reference standard established through chart review by pulmonologists. The cohort consisted of 360 patients. PPV of the base algorithm was 59% (95% confidence interval: 53%-64%). The algorithm additionally requiring ILD-relevant procedure with chemo- or immunotherapy administration and excluding those with autoimmune conditions was 64% (57%-71%). The PPV of base algorithm among patients with colorectal cancer was the lowest - 38% (24%-52%). The PPVs improved meaningfully when the index diagnosis of ILD was coded by a pulmonologist, ranging from 78-88% across different algorithms. We found that, in patients diagnosed with lung, breast, gynecologic, or colorectal cancer, claims-based ILD diagnoses demonstrated moderate to low alignment with a reference standard by expert chart review. It can be improved when ILD is coded by a pulmonologist, though at the cost of substantially fewer cases of ILD identified.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Gastrointestinal (GI) malignancies account for more than one-third of cancer-related deaths worldwide, and outcomes for advanced disease remain poor despite advances in systemic therapy and immunotherapy. Chimeric antigen receptor (CAR)-engineered cellular therapies have transformed the treatment of hematologic malignancies, but their application in solid tumors has been limited by antigen heterogeneity, immunosuppressive tumor microenvironments, on-target/off-tumor toxicity, and manufacturing challenges. This narrative review examines the clinical evidence supporting chimeric antigen receptor T-cell (CAR-T) and chimeric antigen receptor natural killer (CAR-NK) therapies directed against six major targets in GI oncology: claudin 18.2 (CLDN18.2), guanylyl cyclase C (GUCY2C), mesothelin (MSLN), glypican-3 (GPC3), carcinoembryonic antigen (CEA), and human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (HER2). Among these, CLDN18.2 is the most advanced target; in the randomized phase II CT041-ST-01 trial, satricabtagene autoleucel significantly improved progression-free survival (PFS) compared with physician's choice therapy in previously treated gastric or gastroesophageal junction cancer, providing the first randomized evidence of CAR-based therapy efficacy in a solid tumor. GUCY2C and GPC3 have shown promising early-phase activity in metastatic colorectal cancer and hepatocellular carcinoma, respectively, whereas mesothelin, CEA, and HER2 continue to face important biological and safety challenges. CAR-NK cells have emerged as a complementary platform with favorable safety characteristics and off-the-shelf manufacturing potential, although clinical experience in GI malignancies remains limited. We discuss the relative clinical maturity of these targets, key barriers to implementation, and emerging strategies that may advance the role of CAR-based cellular therapies in GI cancers.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Circulating tumor cells (CTCs) are rare tumor-derived cells released from primary or metastatic lesions into the bloodstream and represent key intermediates in hematogenous dissemination. As intact cellular components of liquid biopsy, CTCs provide opportunities to investigate tumor heterogeneity, metastatic evolution, therapeutic resistance, and dynamic molecular alterations that may not be fully captured by tissue biopsy or circulating cell-free analytes. This review summarizes current advances in the biological mechanisms, detection technologies, and clinical applications of CTCs in solid tumors, with particular emphasis on their adaptive responses within the circulation. CTCs exhibit substantial phenotypic and metabolic plasticity, including epithelial-mesenchymal plasticity, altered energy metabolism, and enhanced resistance to oxidative and mechanical stress. Their interactions with platelets, neutrophils, and other immune components can further promote survival, immune evasion, and metastatic competence, particularly through the formation of homotypic and heterotypic CTC clusters. Technological advances in antigen-independent enrichment, microfluidic isolation, single-cell multi-omics, and artificial intelligence-assisted analysis are progressively extending CTC assessment beyond enumeration toward molecular and functional characterization. Emerging clinical evidence supports the potential value of CTCs for prognostic stratification, treatment monitoring, and biomarker assessment in breast, lung, prostate, colorectal, and head and neck cancers, although clinical utility varies considerably among tumor types and platforms. Further standardization and prospective validation, together with integration of metabolic, immune, and multi-omic CTC features, will be essential to establish their role in precision oncology.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Preoperative treatment is central to rectal cancer, but its benefit in elderly patients remains unclear. This study evaluated its impact on clinical outcomes in elderly patients undergoing surgery. This cohort included 5,533 patients aged ≥65 years with newly diagnosed locally advanced rectal cancer (LARC) who underwent surgical resection between January 1, 2008, and December 31, 2017. Patients were stratified into the neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy (nCRT) group (n = 1,086) and the upfront surgery group (n = 4,447). Cox proportional hazards models were used to estimate the overall survival (OS) and disease-free survival (DFS) between groups. Stratified analyses were further performed according to relevant prognostic factors. Elderly LARC patients who received nCRT were more likely to be male, younger (65-75 years), have stage III disease (clinically node-positive), and have no comorbidities (CCI = 0). These patients were also more likely to achieve significant tumor downstaging (p < 0.05), as reflected by higher rates of ypT0 and ypN0 status, along with a lower lymph node yield. nCRT was associated with improved OS in univariable analysis (p=0.0002), but this association was no longer significant after multivariable adjustment (p=0.5645). No significant associations were observed for DFS. Consistent with the adjusted analysis, stratified analyses across relevant prognostic factors showed no significant associations between nCRT and either OS or DFS. The use of nCRT was associated with increased pathological tumor downstaging but not improved survival outcomes in elderly patients with locally advanced rectal cancer. Individualized treatment decisions are therefore warranted.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
This study aims to investigate the occurrence of chemotherapy-induced diarrhea (CID) in patients with colorectal cancer and analyze its associated influencing factors. Based on this, a random forest model was introduced to screen and model potential influencing factors. Combined with feature importance ranking and interpretability analysis, the contribution of each factor to the occurrence of CID was further explored, thereby improving the accuracy of high-risk population identification, supporting future individualized risk assessment and nursing management. This was a retrospective study using convenience sampling. A total of 508 patients with colorectal cancer who received chemotherapy at a tertiary first-class hospital in Gansu Province from February 2025 to September 2025 were selected as the study subjects. Data on general information, disease-related information, and laboratory indicators were collected. The occurrence of chemotherapy-induced diarrhea was used as the outcome variable. Univariate analysis was used to screen relevant factors. Based on this, the random forest recursive feature elimination (RF-RFE) method was applied to select the optimal feature subset, and a random forest-based risk identification model was developed. Five-fold cross-validation was used to evaluate model performance. The SHAP method was used for interpretability analysis of the model. Among the 508 patients, some developed CID during chemotherapy. Univariate analysis showed that BMI, ECOG score, hemoglobin, albumin, total bilirubin, serum creatinine, diabetes, permanent stoma, and irinotecan use were associated with the occurrence of CID (P < 0.05). The random forest model selected seven optimal features (total bilirubin, irinotecan use, albumin, ECOG score, BMI, serum creatinine, and diabetes). The model achieved an AUC of 0.88, accuracy of 0.85, sensitivity of 0.65, and specificity of 0.93 in the test set. SHAP analysis indicated that total bilirubin and irinotecan use contributed the most to the occurrence of CID. The incidence of CID is relatively high in patients with colorectal cancer during chemotherapy. Its occurrence is closely related to factors such as liver function status, chemotherapy regimen, nutritional status, and underlying diseases. The random forest-based prediction model demonstrated good predictive performance and may provide a potential tool for early identification of patients at higher risk of CID and support future individualized nursing management.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Preoperative chronic corticosteroid use has been associated with an increased risk of postoperative complications. However, its association with postoperative outcomes following gastrointestinal surgery remains unclear. This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to evaluate this association. PubMed, Embase, and the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials (CENTRAL) were searched from inception to September 1, 2026. Eligible observational cohort studies compared patients with and without preoperative chronic corticosteroid exposure; studies restricted to inflammatory bowel disease were excluded. Adjusted estimates were pooled using random-effects models with restricted maximum likelihood and Hartung-Knapp confidence intervals after outcome-specific exclusion of potentially overlapping cohorts. Risk of bias and certainty of evidence were assessed using the Risk of Bias in Non-randomized Studies of Exposures (ROBINS-E) tool and the Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation (GRADE) approach, respectively. Fourteen retrospective cohort studies were included, seven of which contributed to quantitative synthesis. Bariatric surgery accounted for 65.2% of reported participants. The primary mortality analysis included five studies comprising 776,681 patients after overlap exclusions. Preoperative exposure was associated with higher odds of 30-day mortality (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 1.51, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.26-1.81), readmission (aOR 1.26, 95% CI 1.07-1.48), reoperation (aOR 1.32, 95% CI 1.10-1.59), sepsis (aOR 1.40, 95% CI 1.36-1.43), and organ-space surgical site infection (SSI; aOR 1.26, 95% CI 1.16-1.37). No statistically significant associations were found for superficial or deep SSI. Mortality and sepsis associations persisted in corticosteroid-specific analyses; readmission, reoperation, and organ-space SSI findings were less consistent across sensitivity analyses. Individual SSI analyses included only two studies and predominantly reflected colorectal surgery. Composite outcomes were summarized narratively. Evidence certainty was low or very low. Preoperative chronic corticosteroid exposure, as defined in the included studies, was associated with higher odds of adverse postoperative outcomes. The associations with mortality and sepsis were more consistent across sensitivity analyses. Given the mixed exposure definitions and residual confounding, the observed associations cannot be attributed to corticosteroids alone or generalized to all gastrointestinal procedures. These findings may support careful perioperative risk stratification and postoperative monitoring in these patients. https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD420261359719, identifier CRD420261359719.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Ileostomy reversal is associated with substantial postoperative morbidity despite being considered a relatively minor surgical procedure. Although glutamine supplementation has been investigated in gastrointestinal surgery, evidence regarding its role in patients undergoing ileostomy reversal remains limited. This study evaluated the association between postoperative glutamine supplementation and short-term outcomes following ileostomy reversal in patients with colorectal cancer. This retrospective cohort study included consecutive patients with colorectal cancer who underwent elective ileostomy reversal between January 2015 and December 2025. Patients were classified into the glutamine group, who received postoperative intravenous glutamine supplementation, and the control group. Postoperative outcomes within 30 days, including complications, gastrointestinal recovery, and length of hospital stay, were compared between groups. A total of 183 patients were included, comprising 103 patients in the glutamine group and 80 in the control group. After 1:1 propensity score matching (PSM), 74 matched pairs were identified. Compared with the control group, the glutamine group had a significantly lower incidence of overall postoperative complications (14.9% vs. 29.7%, P = 0.043) and infectious complications (9.5% vs. 23.0%, P = 0.041). The glutamine group also had shorter times to first flatus, first defecation, and initiation of oral diets, as well as lower incidences of postoperative nausea and vomiting and abdominal distension. Hospital stay was shorter in the glutamine group. No significant between-group differences were observed in postoperative serum prealbumin, total protein, or albumin levels. In this PSM study, postoperative glutamine supplementation was associated with fewer postoperative complications, faster gastrointestinal recovery, and shorter hospital stay following ileostomy reversal in patients with colorectal cancer. These findings indicate a potential association between glutamine supplementation and favorable short-term postoperative outcomes and warrant confirmation in prospective randomized studies.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Colorectal cancer liver metastasis (CRLM) is favored by portal anatomy but determined by a sequence of organ-selective bottlenecks: sinusoidal arrest, early survival, immune escape, metabolic accommodation, and growth-pattern-specific expansion. This Review integrates direct human CRLM evidence, mechanistic models, and organoid studies to define what is established, what remains inferential, and what next-generation models must test. Paired primary-tumor and liver-metastasis organoids preserve inter- and intrapatient heterogeneity and can reproduce selected chemotherapy responses, but epithelial-only cultures cannot model hepatic receptivity. Liver-containing systems should therefore be built as question-specific modules that add hepatocytes, liver sinusoidal endothelial cells, hepatic stellate cells, Kupffer or recruited myeloid cells, extracellular matrix, and flow only when required by the hypothesis. We propose an evidence-linked experimental framework combining longitudinal single-cell transcriptomics, chromatin profiling, metabolomics, isotope tracing, spatial readouts, and perturbation-rescue experiments. Particular emphasis is placed on extracellular-vesicle-mediated premetastatic niche formation, clinically observed microenvironmental evolution, and context-dependent vulnerabilities such as vessel co-option and liver-restricted immune-metabolic dependencies. We also define minimum reporting and validation standards required before organoid results can influence clinical decisions. The central conclusion is that organoids become models of hepatic tropism only when liver context is treated as a controlled causal variable rather than as the site from which tumor epithelium was sampled.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Premature ovarian insufficiency (POI), defined as loss of ovarian function before 40 years with elevated gonadotropins and oligo/amenorrhea, is increasingly recognized as a systemic condition with long-term health consequences. While cardiovascular, skeletal, and neurocognitive risks are well established, the relationship between POI and cancer risk remains less clearly understood. This mini-review summarizes current evidence on site-specific malignancy risks in women with POI and evaluates the influence of hormone replacement therapy (HRT) on cancer outcomes. Available epidemiological studies, cohort analyses, and guideline recommendations addressing cancer incidence in POI were reviewed, with emphasis on breast, ovarian, endometrial, colorectal, and autoimmune-associated malignancies. Women with spontaneous POI generally demonstrate a reduced risk of breast, ovarian, and endometrial cancers, largely attributed to lower lifetime estrogen exposure and fewer ovulatory cycles. However, cancer risk may vary by etiology: autoimmune POI is associated with increased thyroid cancer incidence, while genetic subgroups such as fragile X mental retardation 1 premutation carriers may exhibit altered ovarian cancer susceptibility. Importantly, physiological HRT in POI differs fundamentally from postmenopausal hormone therapy and does not appear to increase overall cancer risk when continued until the average age of natural menopause. POI is typically associated with lower risks of hormone-dependent malignancies, though subgroup-specific variations exist. Individualized counseling, appropriate progestin opposition, and further POI-specific cohort studies are essential to refine cancer surveillance strategies.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Colorectal cancer (CRC) remains one of the most prevalent and lethal malignancies worldwide. Current clinical interventions, including surgery, chemotherapy, and immunotherapy, are limited by metastasis and unsatisfactory therapeutic outcomes. Saikosaponin D (SSD), a bioactive constituent isolated from SSD-NPs were fabricated via a thin-film hydration method. The physicochemical properties, pH stability, and colon-responsive release behavior of the nanoparticles were characterized. In vitro anti-proliferative, anti-migrative, anti-invasive, calcium-mitochondrial stress, and biosafety profiles were evaluated. A subcutaneous HCT-116 xenograft nude mouse model was employed for in vivo biodistribution and antitumor studies. Proteomics-metabolomics analyses, qRT-PCR, and inhibitor rescue experiments were conducted to elucidate the underlying mechanisms. SSD-NPs exhibited uniform spherical morphology, favorable colloidal stability, and colon-pH-responsive release. SSD-NPs suppressed CRC cell proliferation, migration, and invasion, and triggered intracellular calcium overload, mitochondrial ROS burst, and mitochondrial dysfunction. Self-assembly markedly attenuated SSD-associated hemolysis and conferred a broad therapeutic window. In vivo, SSD-NPs preferentially accumulated in tumors and inhibited xenograft tumor growth with a favorable biosafety profile. Multi-omics analyses suggested that TSP1 upregulation may promote calcium influx through CD47, leading to mitochondrial stress, sphingolipid metabolic perturbation, and potential necroptosis, which was supported by Nec-1 rescue assays and qRT-PCR analysis of necroptosis-associated genes. Carrier-free SSD-NPs mitigate the intrinsic hemolytic toxicity of SSD and elicit potent anti-CRC effects both in vitro and in vivo. This study provides a facile carrier-free nanoplatform for SSD delivery and offers mechanistic insights for natural-product-derived nanomedicines against colorectal cancer.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Tertiary lymphoid structures (TLS) are inducible, organized lymphoid clusters that recapitulate key functions of secondary lymphoid organs within chronically inflamed tumor tissue. In colorectal, gastric, and esophageal cancers, the most common luminal gastrointestinal (GI) malignancies, surgical resection preserves the spatial relationship between TLS and the tumor core, invasive margin, and surrounding mucosa, making the resected specimen a uniquely informative anchor for studying antitumor immunity. This narrative review synthesizes evidence from human cohorts, single-cell and spatial genomics, and perioperative immunotherapy trials. We trace the developmental continuum from loose lymphocytic clusters to germinal center-bearing follicles, contrast germinal center-dependent humoral immunity with germinal center-independent B-cell responses, and examine how regulatory T and B cells can turn TLS into immunosuppressive niches. We then analyze proposed inductive circuits, including chemokine-stromal organization, microbial and mutational antigenic pressure, and innate immune sensing, and discuss how desmoplasia, mechanical compression, hypoxia, and metabolic competition may arrest TLS maturation. A tumor-by-tumor comparison of colorectal, gastric, and esophageal cancers shows that TLS density, maturity, and anatomic localization carry divergent prognostic information; and diffuse gastric cancer, peritoneal metastases, and chemoradiated esophageal tumors illustrate states of TLS disruption. We also appraise neoadjuvant checkpoint trials (NICHE, NICHE-2, NEONIPIGA, CheckMate 577, MATTERHORN), consider TLS as complements to TNM staging for adjuvant decision-making and as candidate correlates of pathologic response, and outline experimental strategies for TLS induction and the technical prerequisites for translating TLS into surgical biomarkers. We hypothesize that mature, margin-positioned TLS are promising development- and location-dependent markers of organized antitumor immunity, but routine clinical use awaits standardized, multicenter validation. We therefore propose a minimum reporting framework to accelerate this translation.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Colorectal cancer (CRC) remains a major global health burden, with recurrence, metastasis, and therapeutic resistance limiting durable treatment responses. Tanshinone IIA (Tan IIA), a bioactive diterpene quinone derived from Salvia miltiorrhiza Bunge, has shown broad antitumor activity in preclinical CRC models. This review summarizes its major mechanisms, therapeutic-sensitization effects, and translational potential, while evaluating mechanistic evidence using a three-tier framework encompassing association, functional evidence, and mechanistically supported causality. Tan IIA inhibits proliferation, promotes apoptosis, disrupts mitochondrial and redox homeostasis, suppresses glycolytic adaptation, and modulates autophagy, ferroptosis, invasion, angiogenesis, and the inflammatory tumor microenvironment. It also enhances sensitivity to 5-fluorouracil and oxaliplatin in selected resistant models. Despite these preclinical findings, a substantial exposure gap exists between the nominal concentrations commonly used in CRC cell studies (5-40 μM) and the total plasma peak concentrations reported after oral Danshen administration in healthy volunteers (1.75-25.76 ng/mL). Clinical translation remains challenged by poor aqueous solubility, limited systemic exposure, metabolic clearance, and insufficiently defined exposure-response relationships and safety windows. Future studies should prioritize mechanistic validation and the assessment of pharmacologically active intratumoral exposure, alongside formulation optimization, structural modification, and systematic safety evaluation.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Neoadjuvant treatment is associated with reduced lymph-node yield in rectal cancer, but the accompanying changes in tumor-draining lymph nodes (TDLNs) remain incompletely characterized. We analyzed Surveillance, Epidemiology, and End Results data, a 178-patient institutional cohort, quantitative histopathology of 447 histologically negative TDLNs from 159 patients, and bulk RNA sequencing of 30 nodes from 24 patients. Institutional comparisons distinguished a radiotherapy-containing treatment pathway (RT) from management without preoperative radiotherapy (NRT); in the institutional clinical cohort, all 105 RT patients and 10 of 73 NRT patients received neoadjuvant chemotherapy. Pathology models accounted for patient clustering, and RNA counts were aggregated within patients. Recorded preoperative radiotherapy was associated with lower examined-node counts in Surveillance, Epidemiology, and End Results (SEER). In the institutional cohort, the expanded pretreatment-adjusted incidence-rate ratio was 0.83 [95% confidence interval (CI), 0.67-1.02]; pretreatment-covariate overlap weighting yielded 0.80 (95% CI, 0.66-0.96). RT-group nodes were more fibrotic and smaller, with lower germinal-center and lymphoid-tissue area fractions. Patient-level RNA-seq identified 4,446 differentially expressed genes, with higher extracellular-matrix and angiogenic programs and lower antigen-receptor and B-cell-receptor signaling. Selected pathway directions were retained across sensitivity analyses. Computational deconvolution provided supportive estimates of relative cell composition. A radiotherapy-containing neoadjuvant treatment pathway, including chemoradiotherapy in the institutional clinical, pathology, and RNA-seq cohorts, was associated with lower node yield and structural and transcriptional differences in TDLNs. These findings characterize the nodal structural and transcriptional phenotype associated with neoadjuvant treatment.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
The role of bacteria in causing cancer has been emerging as an increasingly important yet complex factor in tumor formation and proliferation, predominantly through indirect mechanisms, including chronic inflammation, immune modulation, and metabolic genotoxicity. Although only a handful of bacteria have been reported to contribute to specific types of cancers, for example, Chlamydia pneumoniae in lung carcinoma and Streptococcus bovis in colon cancer, their association with tumors is not specific and relies predominantly on chronic inflammatory processes. Nevertheless, the mouth offers a distinct and fragile niche because of its rich and complex microflora, biofilms, and exposure to environmental carcinogens. Specifically, patients with Oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC) present with a high colonization rate for bacterial pathogens like Streptococcus anginosus, Prevotella melaninogenica, and Capnocytophaga gingivalis. The main mechanisms driving tumor growth include cytokine network promotion, inhibition of apoptosis and cell cycle control, and production of carcinogenic metabolites like acetaldehyde, which is formed by alcohol metabolism. Moreover, microbial nitrosation produces N-nitroso compounds that can induce DNA alterations and mutations. The complex relationship involving microbial dysbiosis, biofilm formation, and immune system activity is further complicated by poor oral health practices and periodontitis. Overall, while roles of bacteria in cancers like melanoma or lung carcinoma are variable and indirect, the mouth is a highly relevant example of carcinogenic processes involving the microbiome, making it an important target for future cancer research and treatment. These findings underscore the need for continued investigation into oral biofilm-immune interactions as a foundation for novel cancer prevention and treatment strategies.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Colorectal cancer (CRC) is the third most common malignancy worldwide and poses a significant clinical challenge owing to its high morbidity and mortality rates. Despite ongoing improvements in comprehensive treatment regimens and early detection, the 5-year survival rate of patients has not substantially increased. Ferroptosis is a novel form of regulated cell death that is context dependent and can exert either tumor-suppressive or tumor-promoting effects depending on cellular context and microenvironmental factors. Its therapeutic induction must balance tumor-cell killing against potential effects on normal intestinal epithelium and ferroptosis-sensitive immune populations. Therefore, this review aimed to synthesize the molecular characteristics of ferroptosis and its regulatory mechanisms, focusing on the potential value of traditional Chinese medicine in targeting ferroptosis for the treatment of CRC. Our review suggests that targeting ferroptosis is a promising but context-dependent strategy requiring further validation.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Appendiceal adenocarcinoma (AA) is a rare cancer characterized by high incidences of mucinous histology, peritoneal metastasis, and a good prognosis. However, its chemotherapeutic efficacy and prognostic factors are unclear. To evaluate real-world clinical outcomes and explore prognostic factors in patients with metastatic AA treated with chemotherapy. Retrospective study. We reviewed the clinical courses of patients with metastatic AA receiving first-line chemotherapy between February 2005 and March 2023. We also explored prognostic factors using multivariate analysis. In the 66 identified patients, incidences of mucinous histology and peritoneal metastasis were 41% and 90%, respectively. Forty patients (60.6%) received an oxaliplatin-based regimen combined with bevacizumab. Median progression-free survival (PFS) was 10.9 months, and median overall survival (OS) was 23.0 months. The response rate was 22.0%, and the disease control rate was 87.8% in 41 patients with target lesions. Subsequent chemotherapy was administered to 77.4% of patients. Multivariate analysis showed that presence of the primary tumor, Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status (PS) ≥1, moderate to massive ascites, and elevated pretreatment carcinoembryonic antigen and carbohydrate antigen 19-9 levels were significantly associated with shorter OS. There were significant differences in OS among the three groups classified by the number of poor prognostic factors (none versus [vs.] 1-2 vs. 3-4). Patients with metastatic AA showed comparable PFS and OS to those with common colorectal cancer despite a high incidence of peritoneal metastasis and a low response rate. Elevated tumor marker levels, presence of the primary tumor, ECOG PS ≥1, moderate to massive ascites were poor prognostic factors for OS. The number of these risk factors may allow exploratory prognostic stratification; however, this model is hypothesis-generating and requires external validation before clinical application.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Small bowel obstruction (SBO) is a recognized complication after colorectal surgery. We report an early postoperative mechanical SBO caused by non-migrated Hem-O-Lok clips after laparoscopic low anterior resection (LAR). A 65-year-old man presented eight days after laparoscopic LAR with recurrent vomiting and obstipation. Examination showed abdominal distension, decreased bowel sounds, tympany, and minimal tenderness without peritoneal signs. Computed tomography (CT) demonstrated dilated small-bowel loops and a discrete transition point without radiological features of ischemia, necrosis, or perforation. Because the patient remained clinically stable and no urgent operative indication was identified, a monitored trial of non-operative management was undertaken with nasogastric decompression, bowel rest, serial abdominal examinations, and interval imaging. Persistent obstruction, failed contrast progression, an unchanged transition point, and increasing bowel dilatation prompted reoperation on hospital day five. Exploratory laparotomy demonstrated a band-like tethering point involving Hem-O-Lok clips that remained attached to the inferior mesenteric vessel stump and entrapped a small-bowel loop. The clips were removed, the vascular stump was secured with Vicryl sutures, and the obstruction resolved. The patient recovered without postoperative complications and was discharged on postoperative day four. Unlike previously reported colorectal cases in which clips dislodged and became embedded in the small-bowel wall, the clips in this case remained attached to the inferior mesenteric vessel stump and produced extrinsic focal entrapment. The histological nature of the band-like tissue could not be established because no specimen was obtained. This case illustrates that clip-related obstruction can occur without migration and that CT may not establish the clip-bowel relationship. Its clinical contribution is to draw attention to the clipped vascular pedicle during exploration of persistent focal SBO and to the need to consider vascular control when releasing the entrapped bowel.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Colonoscopy diagnosis is conventionally the first step for the treatment of colorectal cancer (CRC); however, not all patients can be immediately transferred into surgery after such an examination, and a delay is very common in clinical practice. Nonetheless, the prognostic value of such delay has not been thoroughly addressed. A retrospective cohort study was conducted and consecutive patients who underwent colonoscopy diagnosis after the occurrence of symptoms and received subsequent radical surgery were enrolled. The delay from the examination to surgery was calculated, and its predictive value for disease-free survival (DFS) and overall survival (OS) was determined. Clinical data, including the acceptance of adjuvant chemotherapies (ADTs) among different delayed subgroups, were compared; and a Cox model was used to examine the risk factors for both DFS and OS. Taking 15 days (d) as the cutoff point (median, range: 0-956 d), patients were divided into delay-short (Ds<15 d, n=241) or delay-long (Dl≥15 d, n=262) subgroups, patients with bowel obstruction would be more likely to present Ds. No difference was found for the delay in patients who accepted ADTs or not (P=0.251). No significant differences were found for DFS (log-rank=0.13, P=0.710) and OS (log-rank=0.23, P=0.635) among Dl or Ds subgroup. Finally, the delay was not identified as a risk factor for the outcome. Certain delay from colonoscopy diagnosis to surgery was less likely to be associated with the survival in stage I-III CRC patients who received radical resection; however, taking into consideration of the limitations of present study, additional studies with prolonged delay and enlarged sample size are of particular important to validate our results in future.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Metastatic colorectal cancer (mCRC) remains a major cause of cancer-related morbidity and mortality worldwide. Its systemic treatment has evolved from conventional cytotoxic chemotherapy toward biomarker-driven targeted therapy and immunotherapy. Advances in molecular profiling have refined patient selection for anti-EGFR and anti-VEGF therapies and have enabled the development of treatments directed against BRAF V600E, KRAS G12C, HER2 amplification, and other actionable alterations. In parallel, immune checkpoint inhibitors have transformed the management of microsatellite instability-high/mismatch repair-deficient mCRC, whereas microsatellite-stable disease remains largely resistant to immunotherapy and continues to require rational combination strategies. Despite these advances, primary and acquired resistance, dynamic clonal evolution, and the immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment remain major barriers to durable disease control. Circulating tumor DNA and multidimensional molecular profiling are increasingly being explored to monitor treatment response, identify emerging resistance, and guide sequential therapy. This review summarizes recent advances in targeted therapy and immunotherapy for mCRC and discusses priorities for developing adaptive, biomarker-driven treatment strategies.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
The Gulf Cooperation Council countries face converging demographic aging and a rising cancer burden. By 2040, new cancer cases are projected to increase by approximately 143%, and deaths by 188%; among adults aged ≥70 years, projected increases reach 540% in men and 357% in women relative to 2018. Despite advanced oncology infrastructure, routine comprehensive geriatric assessment and dedicated geriatric oncology services remain absent as a system-level standard, limiting toxicity-minimizing care for vulnerable older patients. To map the current status of comprehensive geriatric assessment (CGA) and geriatric oncology (GO) services across the six GCC countries, synthesize demographic and cancer-burden projections, identify implementation gaps, and propose a pragmatic, culturally adapted, stepwise roadmap with measurable performance targets for integrating CGA into routine oncology care. This narrative review followed the SANRA framework. A structured search of PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, and Google Scholar (inception to June 2026) used predefined terms covering geriatric oncology, CGA, GCC countries, cancer burden, and implementation science. Sources were supplemented with GLOBOCAN 2022, UN World Population Prospects 2022, national registry reports (UAE-NCR 2021-2023; QNCR 2020), and international guidelines, including the 2025 ASCO Global Guideline and 2014 SIOG consensus. In 2020, the GCC reported 42,475 new cancer cases and 19,895 deaths; breast, colorectal, and thyroid cancers comprised approximately 40% of incidence. Routine G8 screening, dedicated GO clinics, geriatric domain registry capture, and actionable CGA-guided interventions were absent across all six countries. Pilot programs at King Faisal Specialist Hospital and Tawam Hospital lack EHR integration, standardized follow-up, and performance monitoring. Indian nurse-led G8 models demonstrated feasible reductions in grade 3-5 chemotherapy toxicity (15%), offering a scalable benchmark. The integration of CGA into GCC oncology is strongly supported by demographic, epidemiological, and clinical evidence. This first GCC-wide synthesis proposes a pragmatic, stepwise roadmap with ten domain-specific performance targets adapted from Western and Indian models. These targets were extrapolated from non-GCC evidence, and prospective GCC pilot studies are needed for validation.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Colon capsule endoscopy (CCE) is a patient-friendly, minimally invasive alternative to conventional colonoscopy, but its value depends on pathway performance rather than diagnostic accuracy alone. This narrative review examines the cost-effectiveness of CCE across colorectal cancer screening, symptomatic investigation, incomplete colonoscopy, post-polypectomy surveillance, inflammatory bowel disease monitoring, and AI-supported implementation. Targeted literature searches were performed in PubMed and official guidance sources through 6 July 2026. Across broad screening populations, CCE is not yet cost-effective compared with biennial faecal immunochemical testing (FIT) or 10-yearly colonoscopy; contemporary Dutch MISCAN modelling found all CCE screening strategies dominated at full adherence, largely because unit cost and follow-up colonoscopy burden remained high. The dominant economic problem is pathway duplication: a 2025 meta-analysis found a pooled follow-up endoscopy rate of 42%, and contemporary UK/Scottish service data showed that about half of patients required further optical endoscopy or sigmoidoscopy. CCE may offer conditional value after incomplete colonoscopy, in lower-risk symptomatic triage, and in carefully selected surveillance pathways where a negative or low-risk capsule result may avoid, defer, or focus colonoscopy. Evidence from Crohn's disease and ulcerative colitis monitoring is encouraging but should not be extrapolated uncritically to colorectal cancer screening or dysplasia surveillance, where biopsy and therapy remain decisive. AI-assisted CCE may reduce reading time and improve polyp detection, but robust lifetime cost-effectiveness models are still needed. The current evidence supports CCE as a pathway-dependent filter, not a universal substitute for colonoscopy.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Juvenile polyps are benign hamartomatous lesions usually seen in children, most often in the colorectal region. Solitary gastric juvenile polyps in adults without features of polyposis syndromes are exceedingly rare, with fewer than five cases reported in the literature. We describe a 31-year-old male presenting with weight loss and intermittent painless rectal bleeding. Upper endoscopy revealed a solitary pedunculated polyp in the gastric antrum, which was removed via endoscopic mucosal resection. Colonoscopy showed internal hemorrhoids and a solitary rectal ulcer, which were likely the source of bleeding, while small bowel imaging was unremarkable. Histopathology confirmed a juvenile polyp. This case emphasizes the importance of recognizing this rare entity and the role of endoscopy in diagnosis and management.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Colorectal cancer (CRC) exhibits substantial intratumoral heterogeneity, yet the molecular mechanisms that maintain aggressive epithelial cell states remain incompletely understood. Here, we combined single-cell RNA sequencing, weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA), metabolic profiling, and experimental validation to investigate the functional diversity of malignant epithelial populations in CRC. We identified EPC3 as a highly proliferative malignant epithelial population with pronounced metabolic activity and features associated with tumor progression. Transcriptomic network analysis revealed a proliferation-associated gene module (M23), within which DDX39A emerged as a key candidate associated with the EPC3 phenotype. Clinical analysis revealed that DDX39A was significantly upregulated in CRC tissues and was associated with advanced tumor stage, metastasis, and poor prognosis. Functional experiments demonstrated that DDX39A promotes CRC cell proliferation, migration, invasion, and tumor growth in vivo, while modulating glycolytic activity and mitochondrial respiration, suggesting its involvement in regulating metabolic adaptation in CRC cells. Mechanistically, DDX39A was found to promote glycolytic reprogramming through regulation of HIF-1α expression, thereby influencing cell cycle progression and maintaining the malignant epithelial phenotype to facilitate CRC progression. Collectively, these findings identify DDX39A as a potential regulator linking metabolic remodeling with malignant cell-state maintenance and suggest its potential value as a biomarker and therapeutic target for colorectal cancer.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
In colorectal cancer the most frequently analyzed markers are RAS/RAF mutations which have negative predictive role for anti-EGFR antibody therapy. Although the hotspot mutations of the K- and NRAS exon 2-4 are well defined, the predictive role of rare mutations of other codons are questionable and the current guidelines are less precise in this respect. We have retrospectively re-analyzed the full spectrum of RAS/RAF mutations by next-generation sequencing (NGS) in a small cohort of nineteen cetuximab treated metastatic colorectal cancer patients whose enrollment was based on KRAS exon 2 mutation analysis. We have detected 13 rare RAS/RAF mutations where 5 occurred together with hotspot (HSP) mutations. In the five non-HSP mutant cases we have detected 8 rare/non-HSP RAS/RAF mutations: KRAS-E37.,C51Y, NRAS-D57N,E62K,G60E/V14I, HRAS-P34L and BRAF-G464R. Kaplan-Meier analysis indicated that the progression free survival (PFS) of non-HSP cases ran parallel with wild type (WT) cases separately from the HSP mutant cases without statistical significance (p = 0.156). However, the combination of WT group with non-HSP cases resulted in a near significant survival difference from HSP cases (p = 0.057, HR = 3.501). Kaplan-Meier analysis of the overall survival (OS) again demonstrated that the survival curve of WT cases ran parallel with non-HSP cases, clearly separated from the HSP cases (p = 0.024). Overall survival of WT cases was significantly different as compared to HSP cases (p = 0.005) with HR of 6.362 (CI 1.496-27.055) as expected, while it was not statistically different from non-HSP cases (p = 0.092) with a HR of 0.891 (CI 0.248-3.205). In this small retrospective study we showed that the analyzed non-HSP mutations of RAS/RAF in colorectal cancer treated with cetuximab do not have negative effect on the efficacy. Since our cohort is very small and do not have accordingly the necessary statistical power of the survival analyses, therefore can only be considered as hypothesis generating one of the issue of the predictive role of non-hotspot RAS mutations on cetuximab efficacy.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
The human gut microbiome has gradually moved from the margins of physiology to something much closer to the centre of the conversation. It shapes how food is broken down, helps train the immune system, nudges metabolic balance, and even appears to influence brain function, though exactly how remains open to debate. New tools, especially high-throughput sequencing, multi-omics workflows, and increasingly sophisticated computational models, have made it possible to look beyond who is there and begin asking what these microbes might be doing. Even so, working with human microbiomes is rarely straightforward. No two people carry the same microbial community, and small differences in diet, medication, or lifestyle can produce large shifts in composition and function. Add to that the lack of standardisation across studies, and it becomes difficult to draw firm causal links rather than correlations. Still, the associations keep accumulating. Altered microbial communities have been linked to conditions as varied as type 2 diabetes, colorectal cancer, neurodegenerative disorders, and chronic gut inflammation. These connections have naturally pushed interest towards ways of deliberately reshaping the gut ecosystem. Rather than treating microbiome modulation as a simple add-on, this chapter approaches it as a form of ecosystem management guided by precision data. Traditional strategies such as probiotics, prebiotics, and synbiotics are placed alongside newer ideas, including modulation driven by microbial metabolites, targeted mineral supplementation, engineered probiotic strains, synthetic microbial consortia, and even attempts to edit microbial communities in situ. The underlying argument is that these interventions make the most sense when paired with predictive metagenomic and metabolic models, which can help anticipate how a given microbiome might respond, or resist change altogether. That said, the path from concept to practice is not smooth. Long-term clinical evidence is still sparse, microbial engraftment remains unpredictable, and scaling personalised approaches beyond small cohorts poses obvious logistical challenges. Regulation is another unresolved piece of the puzzle, particularly when interventions blur the line between food, supplement, and therapy. There are also broader ecological questions. Introducing or reshaping microbial communities may have consequences that extend beyond individual patients. By keeping these constraints in view, the chapter aims to temper optimism with realism and to sketch a future in which precision microbiome interventions are developed carefully, tested rigorously, and applied where they are most likely to make a meaningful difference, especially for nutritionally vulnerable groups.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
The microbiota of the human gastrointestinal tract plays a vital role in overall well-being, influencing metabolic pathways, immune responses, and even brain function. Dysbiosis, disrupted microbial balance, is linked to disorders like IBD, obesity, and colorectal cancer. Conventional gut microbiome investigation approaches are limited by their restricted specificity, error, and failure to address functional diversity, as well as their reliance on gene-marker surveys, which often overlook rare microbes. Recent developments in artificial intelligence (AI) have significantly enhanced the accuracy of gut health diagnosis and prediction through the large-scale analysis of complex microbiome datasets, enabling the identification of patterns and connections that traditional statistical methods cannot. Tools including MiCoDe, GMWI2, CRCpred, DeepMicro, MicrobiomeAnalyst, GutBug, and QIIME 2 are built using AI methods, such as random forest modelling, Support Vector Machine (SVM), and network-based inference. These tools are revolutionising predictive gut microbiome analysis by allowing for early disease detection, risk evaluation, and personalised recommendations to therapies such as probiotics or dietary adjustments. Nonetheless, these developments in AI-based technologies encounter issues related to data standards, confidentiality, sample variety, and regional bias, which hinder the potential of these AI-driven tools in clinical practice. Further research on employing federated learning and the use of hybrid AI technologies can improve the transparency and reliability of these tools, since these tools can transform gut microbiome research into effective diagnostics and therapeutics for improving and optimising human gut health. This chapter explores the most recent advances in AI-powered approaches for predicting gut health, focusing on their procedures, effectiveness, and future medical implications.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Human microbiome which is a dynamic ecosystem of trillions of microorganisms is important in health and disease, especially in the establishment of cancer in ways such as through inflammation, generation of genotoxins, and immune modulation. This report aims to discuss the concept of microbiome modulation as a preventive and curative approach to cancer along with personalized nutrition and precision medicine. Dysbiosis is also associated with several types of cancers, such as colorectal, breast, and pancreatic whereby pathobionts, such as Fusobacterium nucleatum contribute to tumorigenesis, and beneficial taxa induce protective metabolites such as short-chain fatty acids. Eubiosis is restored through modulation methods such as probiotics, prebiotics, synbiotics, fecal microbiota transplantation, selective antibiotics, and dietary interventions and increase the efficacy of immunotherapy and decrease immunotherapy resistance. Anticancer properties of natural products, including curcumin, resveratrol, and berberine, can be summed up by their capacity to moderate microbiota in terms of achieving anti-inflammatory phenotypes. Gut microbes metabolically modify the food substances to produce bioactive metabolite, which affects the host immunity and epigenetics. Precision nutrition is a system that directs individuals to make diets based on multiomics data, microbiomics included, thereby predicting reactions and avoiding chronic diseases. Genome-scale reconstructions of metabolic models and machine learning computational models mimic these interactions to make personalized predictions. The problems are variability of microbiomes, standardization of data, ethical issues, and causality. In sum, this synthesis provides evidence that the microbiome can help make oncology a treatment centered on reaction to health issues but prevention based on individual needs and subjected to artificial intelligence personalization to allow administering the highest quality health to all the patients.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
ObjectiveColorectal cancer (CRC) develops through somatic genomic alterations, but panel-detected alteration counts across pathological stages and tumor locations remain incompletely characterized.MethodsIn this exploratory observational study, tumor lesions and adjacent normal mucosa from two patients with multiple colorectal lesions were analyzed using a 1,021-gene targeted sequencing panel. An exploratory cohort of 23 sporadic CRC patients was assessed using the same workflow. One MSI-H case was retained descriptively but excluded from alteration-count subgroup comparisons, leaving 22 patients. The metric was the unnormalized number of qualifying somatic alteration events per sample, not conventional mutations-per-megabase tumor mutational burden.ResultsIn both patients, analyzed separately, alteration counts increased descriptively across lesions with more advanced pathological features. Among 22 sporadic CRC patients, counts did not differ between conventional and mucinous adenocarcinoma (P=1.000), but were higher in T4 versus T2/T3 tumors (P=0.017), M1 versus M0 tumors (P=0.044), and right-versus left-sided CRC (P=0.038). Right-sided tumors were also larger (P=0.046), while T-stage distribution did not differ in the molecular sidedness comparison (P=1.000). These findings may be confounded by clinical and pathological factors. In a separate cohort of 2,471 CRC patients, right-sided tumors more often presented as T3-T4 disease (90% vs 82%, P<0.001).ConclusionsThese hypothesis-generating findings suggest that panel-derived somatic alteration counts may increase with pathological advancement and differ by tumor location. Small sample size, separate Lynch syndrome analysis, MSI-H exclusion, unnormalized counts, and cross-sectional design limit inference. Larger independent cohorts with standardized metrics and confounder adjustment are needed.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
This study aims to investigate the multi-target molecular mechanisms through which synthetic phenolic antioxidants (SPAs) may contribute to colorectal cancer (CRC) progression using an integrated approach of network toxicology, molecular docking, and molecular dynamics (MD) simulation. A representative library of traditional and novel SPAs was selected, and their toxicity profiles and carcinogenicity were predicted via ADMETlab 3.0. Potential targets of SPAs were retrieved from SwissTargetPrediction, SEA, PharmMapper, and ChEMBL. CRC-related targets were collected from GeneCards, TTD, and OMIM. Intersecting targets were analyzed for protein-protein interactions (PPI) and functional enrichment (GO and KEGG) using STRING, Cytoscape, and the clusterProfiler R package. Differential expression and diagnostic potential of hub genes were validated using TCGA (COAD and READ) and GEO (GSE271719) datasets. Molecular docking and 100 ns MD simulations were performed using CB-Dock2 and Gromacs 2025 to evaluate binding stability. We identified 222 shared targets between SPAs and CRC. Ten hub genes (SRC, MAPK1, HSP90AA1, EGFR, ESR1, AKT1, KRAS, JUN, SHC1, and HRAS) were identified, with JUN, SRC, HSP90AA1, AKT1, SHC1, and HRAS significantly overexpressed in CRC tissues. Enrichment analysis showed these targets are primarily involved in PI3K-Akt, MAPK, TNF, and VEGF signaling pathways. ESR1, HSP90AA1, and HRAS exhibited high diagnostic value (AUC > 0.8). Molecular docking identified favorable predicted docking scores for several SPA-hub protein pairs, with AO245-AKT1 showing the lowest predicted docking score (-9.7 kcal/mol). MD simulations suggested relatively limited conformational fluctuations of the predicted AO245-AKT1 complex under the simulated conditions. SPAs may be mechanistically associated with CRC‑related hub genes and oncogenic pathways involved in cell proliferation, inflammation, and oxidative stress, providing hypothesis‑generating evidence that requires further experimental validation. AKT1 was identified as a critical intervention target, while genes such as ESR1 and HSP90AA1 serve as potential diagnostic biomarkers. These findings provide a theoretical framework for understanding the environmental health risks of SPAs and offer new insights into CRC pathogenesis under pollutant exposure.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
The purpose of this study was to compare health-related quality of life (QoL), ostomy self-care ability, and influencing factors among persons with permanent colostomies in 2 cities located in eastern versus western China. Cross-sectional study. Five hundred and fifteen patients with rectal cancer and a permanent colostomy were recruited from September 2013 to February 2016. Data were collected in the ostomy outpatient clinics of 3 grade A tertiary hospitals in Guangzhou, China (eastern China) and 2 grade A tertiary hospitals in Lanzhou, China (Western China). Participants completed a questionnaire that asked for demographic and pertinent stoma-related items designed for purposes of this study. They also completed the Stoma-QoL and Stoma Self-care Scale instruments. Participants were divided into 2 groups according to eastern and western geographical locations for intergroup comparative analysis. There were significant differences between mean scores of Stoma-QoL (52.53 ± 12.72 vs. 41.86 ± 12.20; P < .001) and ostomy self-care abilities (38.03 ± 6.86 vs. 30.25 ± 9.84; P < .001) between patients in eastern and western China, respectively. Age, employment status, body image loss, acceptance of ostomy by patients themselves and their spouses, professional support from enterostomal/WOC nurses, and ostomy self-care ability were significant factors associated with Sitoma-QoL, accounting for 51.8% of the variance. Stoma-QoL and ostomy self-care ability among patients with permanent colostomy in eastern China were generally better than those in western China. Effective measures should be taken to improve the QoL of patients with colostomy in western China.

Individual genetic polymorphisms can exert a modifier effect on splicing. With about one single-nucleotide polymorphism per 250 bases, we hypothesized that consideration of splice haplotypes will improve the accuracy of spliceogenic variant annotation, as current methods mainly assess single DNA variants and in a single reference genome. We describe Panthera for high-throughput pangenomic analysis of splice haplotypes, available as an open-source on GitHub (https://github.com/CherWeiYuan/Panthera). It accepts user-input variants and uses a deep learning model to predict their combinatorial effect on splice site probabilities under 64 non-redundant genetic backgrounds derived from five human super populations. The 874,587-parameter model is designed based on splicing mechanisms where multiple functional motifs, spliceosomal and auxiliary elements, interact with the sequential implementations of convolutional neural network (CNN) and Transformer blocks to simulate local and full-sequence motif interactions respectively. ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Spontaneous regression (SR) of colorectal cancer (CRC) is extremely rare. Recently, an association between SR of CRC and deficient mismatch repair (dMMR) has been increasingly reported. Here, we report a rare case of 2 distinct dMMR ascending colon cancers that consecutively regressed in a single patient, potentially associated with biopsy procedures, and we discuss the surgical indications for T1b CRC with dMMR. A 71-year-old female underwent a screening colonoscopy, which revealed a sessile lesion (Lesion 1) and an adjacent erosion (Lesion 2) in the ascending colon. A superficially elevated lesion (Lesion 3) was visible proximally but was not biopsied. She underwent endoscopic mucosal resection for Lesion 1 and a biopsy for Lesion 2, which revealed moderately differentiated adenocarcinoma. One month later, Lesion 2 had completely scarred over without malignant cells on repeat biopsy. Meanwhile, the unbiopsied Lesion 3 persisted. A biopsy of Lesion 3 confirmed adenocarcinoma, and deep submucosal invasion was suspected. Laparoscopic ileocecal resection with D2 lymph node dissection was performed. Histopathologically, no residual cancer cells were identified in the resected specimen. An adjacent SSLD was identified without carcinoma. No lymph node metastasis was detected. Immunohistochemistry of the initial biopsies for Lesions 2 and 3 showed a loss of MLH1 and PMS2, indicating dMMR status. We encountered an exceptional case wherein 2 independent dMMR ascending colon cancers consecutively disappeared following biopsies. This case may provide evidence that localized physical stimulation combined with dMMR-driven high immunogenicity can induce SR. While assessing the MMR status of T1 CRC provides vital information, the decision to omit surgical bowel resection should be made cautiously, considering the potential coexistence of flat precancerous lesions, such as SSLDs, even after SR. Careful evaluation and further case accumulation are needed to optimize treatment guidelines.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Colorectal cancer (CRC) remains a major contributor to the global cancer burden, with approximately 555,000 new cases and 286,000 deaths annually in China, where most patients are still diagnosed at intermediate or advanced stages. This narrative review synthesizes recent evidence on the evolution of CRC screening technologies and their health economic evaluation, with the aim of informing resource-adapted screening strategies for China and comparable settings. PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, the Cochrane Library, and three major Chinese databases (CNKI, Wanfang Data, and VIP) were searched from database inception to 7 November 2025, with emphasis on studies published within the past five years. The evidence supports three principal findings. First, noninvasive molecular testing has substantially improved diagnostic performance: next-generation multitarget stool DNA testing achieves a sensitivity of 93.9% for CRC (versus 67.3% for the fecal immunochemical test [FIT] in the same head-to-head cohort), and stool syndecan-2 methylation testing outperforms FIT for advanced colorectal neoplasia, although sensitivity for advanced precancerous lesions remains below 50% for all currently available noninvasive assays. Second, health economic analyses consistently identify FIT as the most cost-effective primary screening tool under real-world adherence conditions, whereas structured risk-stratified and opportunistic screening models achieve higher benefit-cost ratios (9.29 for opportunistic screening versus 6.43 for population-based screening in a representative Chinese community program, although these ratios derive from a single community program, are subject to selection bias, and are not incremental comparisons). Third, artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted colonoscopy-specifically computer-aided detection (CADe), as distinct from computer-aided diagnosis (CADx)-reduces adenoma miss rates in randomized tandem studies; in a single-center diagnostic study, combined AI and conventional colonoscopy showed high agreement with histopathology, although this finding derives from an enriched symptomatic cohort rather than an average-risk screening population. Most pivotal trials of emerging molecular assays were industry-sponsored, which may inflate reported performance. Building on this evidence, we propose a conceptual dual-cycle optimization framework with illustrative, author-proposed thresholds: an outer cycle that matches the population coverage of emerging high-cost technologies to regional per-capita gross domestic product and budget constraints, and an inner cycle that recalibrates individual risk annually through a four-dimensional assessment system integrating the Asia-Pacific Colorectal Screening score, serial molecular monitoring, AI-derived imaging features, and genetic susceptibility. Neither a single highly sensitive test nor a low-cost primary screening tool alone can simultaneously maximize early detection and contain health expenditure; tiered, risk-stratified, and economically graded strategies are required to reduce the CRC burden in resource-heterogeneous settings. The framework is hypothesis-generating, and its thresholds require prospective calibration before implementation.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Mitochondria are indispensable organelles in the center of cellular bioenergetics, coupling oxidative phosphorylation to ATP production while also influencing processes such as cellular metabolism, oxidative stress regulation, reactive oxygen species (ROS) signaling, calcium buffering and apoptosis induction. Mitochondrial plasticity and remodeling shape the processes of cell differentiation, immune activation, senescence, and cancerogenesis. Their functional state is shaped by dynamic remodeling and frequently altered by pharmacological treatments, genetic mutations, aging, and cell dysfunction in association with diseases. Key parameters reflecting mitochondrial status include membrane potential (MMP), mitochondrial reactive oxygen species (mitoROS) and mitochondrial biomass. Here, we describe a unified, flow cytometry-based protocol for sequential quantification of these parameters in a single cell preparation using three fluorescent probes: MitoTracker Green FM for mitochondrial biomass, JC-1 for ratiometric measurement of MMP, and MitoSOX Red for mitoROS. The method is compatible with both adherent and suspension cells, provides single-cell resolution, and enables high-throughput profiling across high number of conditions and treatments. We demonstrate its utility in colorectal cancer cell lines with contrasting metabolic phenotypes (OXPHOS-reliant SW1417 and glycolytic COLO-320) exposed to chemotherapeutics and metabolic inhibitors. This parallel assay provides an efficient and scalable approach to interrogate mitochondrial functionality under diverse conditions. It is particularly valuable for studies of metabolic remodeling and cell stress responses, offering a practical alternative or complement to respirometry-based assays.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
There has been increasing interest in the potential efficacy of a ketogenic diet in the treatment of cancer. One of the proposed rationales for this is that cancer cells, unlike normal cells, lack the ketolytic enzymes required to utilize ketone bodies for energy, causing selective death to cancer cells under low glucose conditions. In this study, we asked whether cancer cells uniformly lack ketolytic enzymes and whether this correlated with their ability to utilize ketone bodies for survival under low-glucose conditions. In addition, we determined if these in vitro assays could predict the efficacy of a ketogenic diet in vivo using preclinical mouse models. We screened multiple cancer cell lines for their expression of 3-oxoacid CoA-transferase 1 (OXCT1) and β-hydroxybutyrate dehydrogenase (BDH1), and evaluated their survival under β-hydroxybutyrate (βHB)-supplemented glucose free conditions. We also determined the extent by which βHB is depleted in the cell culture media. The expression of OXCT1 and BDH1 varies between cancer cell lines, and did not always correspond to functional ketone utilization. Furthermore, when tested in vivo using tumor-implanted mouse models, many cancer cells grew regardless of their predicted ketolytic capacity, highlighting the limited ability of these in vitro findings to predict in vivo efficacy. The growth of SW480 colon cancer cells, shown in vitro to be a user of βHB, was slowed to a greater extent when implanted in vivo to mice fed a ketogenic diet, when compared to H1299 lung cancer cells, which were not a user of βHB in vitro. Further investigations suggest that H1299 is a greater producer of lactate, which we hypothesize is being converted back to glucose in the liver via gluconeogenesis, causing the observed higher blood glucose and plasma insulin. This in turn, supports the growth of the H1299 cells in vivo, that could not be predicted by our in vitro assays. Taken together, we show that while it is not possible to predict the efficacy of a ketogenic diet using in vitro assays, it may be possible to identify which cancer cells may be impacted under low glucose conditions based on its propensity to produce lactate via glycolysis.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Disinfection of drinking water is essential for preventing waterborne infectious diseases. However, disinfectants can react with natural organic matter, bromide, iodide, ammonia, and other precursors to form disinfection byproducts (DBPs). Because DBPs are widely detected in drinking-water systems and may differ substantially in toxicity, persistence, and exposure potential, their possible contribution to cancer remains an important public-health concern. This systematic review summarizes epidemiological and experimental evidence concerning the relationship between drinking-water DBPs and cancer. Literature searches were conducted in PubMed, Web of Science, and Scopus using predefined combinations of terms related to DBPs, drinking-water exposure, cancer, epidemiology, genotoxicity, oxidative stress, and carcinogenic mechanisms. Eligible studies included population-based epidemiological studies, toxicological and mechanistic studies, systematic reviews, and meta-analyses. The evidence was synthesized narratively because of substantial heterogeneity in exposure metrics, study populations, cancer outcomes, and effect measures. The methodological limitations of the included studies were considered with particular attention to exposure misclassification, residual confounding, selection bias, outcome ascertainment, and publication bias. Trihalomethanes (THMs) and haloacetic acids (HAAs) were the most frequently investigated DBP groups and therefore provided the principal epidemiological evidence in this review. However, the review also considered emerging nitrogen-containing, brominated, iodinated, aromatic, alicyclic, and inorganic DBPs. For these emerging compounds, evidence was evaluated primarily on the basis of occurrence, toxicological potency, genotoxicity, and mechanistic plausibility. The most consistent epidemiological evidence concerned bladder cancer, for which several case-control and cohort studies reported positive associations with long-term exposure to total THMs or specific THM constituents. Associations with colorectal, kidney, ovarian, and selected hematological cancers were less consistent and should be considered suggestive rather than conclusive. Evidence for causal interpretation was limited by difficulties in reconstructing long-term individual exposure, insufficient characterization of inhalation and dermal exposure, regional variability in DBP composition, and incomplete adjustment for tobacco smoking, occupational exposures, diet, socioeconomic status, and other potential confounders. Experimental studies indicate that some DBPs, particularly brominated and nitrogen-containing compounds, can induce oxidative stress, DNA adduct formation, DNA strand breaks, chromosomal damage, altered DNA methylation, histone modification, mitochondrial dysfunction, inflammatory signaling, and dysregulation of cell-cycle and apoptosis pathways. These mechanisms provide biological plausibility for some epidemiological observations but do not establish that all DBPs or DBP mixtures cause cancer in humans. Overall, the evidence supports a relatively stable association between long-term drinking-water DBP exposure and bladder cancer, whereas evidence for other cancer sites remains limited or inconsistent. Future studies should prioritize prospective cohort designs, improved individual-level exposure assessment, biomonitoring, mixture-based analysis, evaluation of multiple exposure routes, preregistered protocols, and transparent risk-of-bias assessment. Regulatory frameworks should progressively incorporate unregulated and emerging DBPs while maintaining adequate microbial protection. The greater emphasis on THMs and HAAs reflects the availability of epidemiological evidence rather than a conclusion that these compounds are more toxic than all emerging DBPs. Emerging DBPs, particularly N-nitrosamines, haloacetonitriles, iodinated DBPs, halogenated benzoquinones, and halofuranones, warrant further occurrence monitoring, toxicological evaluation, and mixture-based risk assessment.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Situs inversus totalis (SIT) is a rare congenital anomaly characterized by a complete mirror-image reversal of organs. Especially in a minimally invasive surgery, care must be taken to avoid misidentification because of reversed anatomical landmarks. Robot-assisted surgery (RAS) may be a feasible surgical option and may facilitate precise surgical manipulation in anatomically challenging situations. Although there are several reports of RAS using the da Vinci surgical robot system (Intuitive Surgical, Sunnyvale, CA, USA) for colorectal cancer (CRC) in patients with SIT, the optimal robot platform, port settings, and procedures have not been determined. In a 74-year-old woman with SIT referred to our department for treatment of advanced rectal cancer, preoperative examinations showed cancer invasion beyond the intestinal walls and multiple lymph node swelling within the mesentery. After completing 4 cycles of preoperative chemotherapy, robot-assisted low anterior resection using the hinotori™ surgical robot system (hinotori; Medicaroid, Kobe, Hyogo, Japan) was planned. Prior to the surgery, we conducted meticulous simulation with other medical staff using the hinotori, instruments, monitors, and a dry box. During the operation, port placements and instruments were set in a completely left-right reversed position from the standard configuration. From the medial approach through mesenteric vessel division and dissection of the left-sided colon and rectosigmoid junction, the cockpit surgeon smoothly operated monopolar curved scissors with the non-dominant left hand with reversed procedures. In the operating room, a monitor displaying a left-right flipped image was placed alongside the original-image monitor, and surgery proceeded while the patient-side surgeons confirmed anatomical accuracy. As the hinotori has no sealing devices or linear staplers, vessel ligation, division of the mesorectum, and rectal transection were performed by the patient-side surgeons. The patient was discharged without major complications. To our knowledge, this is the first report of a surgical robot system other than the da Vinci system used to perform surgery for CRC in a patient with SIT. Sufficient preoperative simulation and display of flipped images contributed to the safe operation of robot-assisted low anterior resection in the patient. It is necessary to understand the characteristics of each surgical robot platform and perform surgery by leveraging the system's individual features.
