ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Opioid overprescribing remains a major public health concern. Prior work in our colorectal surgery group demonstrated adequate pain control with fewer opioids than prescribed. To evaluate opioid prescribing before and after implementation of a procedure-specific prescribing support tool for outpatient anorectal surgery. We performed a retrospective before-and-after study of adult patients undergoing outpatient anorectal surgery between January and July 2024. Prescribing patterns during a pre-intervention period (January-March 2024) were compared with those during a post-intervention period (May-July 2024). The intervention consisted of standardized prescribing recommendations, clinician education, badge reference cards, and posted guidance materials. The primary outcome was prescribed opioid quantity measured in morphine milligram equivalents (MMEs). A total of 219 patients were included, with 70 patients in the pre-intervention cohort and 149 patients in the post-intervention cohort. Mean prescribed MME decreased slightly from 83.1 ± 34.8 to 79.9 ± 32.7 following implementation. Median prescribed MME remained unchanged at 90 MME (IQR 60-90). Patient-level analysis demonstrated no statistically significant difference in prescribed MME between study periods (p=0.53). When stratified by procedure opioid-prescribing tier, prescribing remained stable among low- and mid-opioid prescribing procedures, while high-opioid prescribing procedures had lower mean prescribed MMEs following implementation, although statistical significance was not reached. Follow-up survey data demonstrated high awareness of the prescribing guidance but inconsistent routine use. Implementation of procedure-specific opioid prescribing guidance was not associated with a statistically significant reduction in overall opioid prescribing. Despite widespread awareness of the recommendations, reported utilization was inconsistent, suggesting that passive dissemination strategies alone may be insufficient to change prescribing behavior. Broader, multifaceted strategies may be required to achieve meaningful change.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Respiratory sarcopenia (RS) is a recognized comorbidity in elderly patients with colorectal cancer (CRC). This study evaluated the associations between preoperative diaphragmatic ultrasound parameters and RS in elderly patients with CRC. This retrospective analysis of prospectively collected data included patients aged ≥ 60 years with stage I-III CRC who underwent laparoscopic surgery between February 2023 and February 2024. All underwent preoperative pulmonary function testing, computed tomography, and diaphragmatic ultrasound. Sarcopenia was defined as low muscle strength (reduced handgrip strength) and low skeletal muscle mass (the skeletal muscle index at the third lumbar vertebra level, L3 SMI). RS was operationally defined in patients with sarcopenia by the additional presence of low peak expiratory flow rate (PEFR). Among 210 patients (58.1% men; median age, 69 years [IQR, 66-73]), 104 (49.5%) had no sarcopenia (NS), 42 (20.0%) had sarcopenia with preserved PEFR (SPP), and 64 (30.5%) had RS. Postoperative pulmonary complications, hospital stay, and 2-year disease-free survival worsened across the three groups (all Preoperative diaphragmatic ultrasound parameters were associated with RS in elderly patients with CRC. These findings suggest that the combined Df-DTdi model yields discriminative ability for RS in this cohort and may have potential utility in preoperative risk assessment. Prospective multicenter studies are needed for validation.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Dihydroorotate dehydrogenase (DHODH) is a mitochondrial enzyme involved in de novo pyrimidine biosynthesis and has emerged as a potential target in cancer metabolism and therapy. This study integrated transcriptomic analysis with structure-based drug discovery to investigate the biological significance and therapeutic potential of DHODH in colorectal cancer (COAD and READ). TCGA-COAD and TCGA-READ RNA-seq data were analyzed for differential expression, clinical association, survival, pathway enrichment, immune infiltration, and therapeutic relevance, with GSE44076 used for external validation. DHODH was significantly elevated in colorectal cancer, while its expression showed limited association with overall survival. Enrichment and immune analyses suggested that DHODH may be associated with immune-related processes and the tumor immune microenvironment. CCLE/DepMap analysis further indicated DHODH dependency in a subset of colorectal cancer cell lines. Structure-based virtual screening identified several promising compounds, including (+)-Luguine, Benzyl 2-[(2-cinnamylidene-3-oxo-1-benzofuran-6-yl)oxy]acetate, 2,3,5-trimethyl-6-(3-(4-methylpiperazin-1-yl)-3-oxopropyl)-7H-furo[3,2-g]chromen-7-one, and N-[2-(4-methylphenyl)ethyl]-2-(2-oxo-1,2-dihydroquinolin-3-yl)acetamide. Molecular docking and 100 ns molecular dynamics simulations supported stable ligand-DHODH interactions. MM/PBSA analysis showed favorable binding free energies ranging from -4.98 to -7.69 kcal/mol, with the DHODH-(+)-Luguine complex exhibiting the most favorable predicted binding energy. ADMET analysis further indicated generally acceptable drug-like and pharmacokinetic properties, although compound-specific toxicity concerns were identified. Overall, DHODH may represent a promising therapeutic target in colorectal cancer, while the identified compounds provide potential candidates for further experimental validation as DHODH inhibitors.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Early tumor shrinkage (ETS) and depth of response (DpR) are increasingly recognized as early efficacy endpoints and potential surrogate markers of long-term outcomes in metastatic colorectal cancer (mCRC). However, determinants of ETS and DpR in patients receiving intensive first-line chemotherapy remain insufficiently characterized, particularly in Asian populations. We retrospectively analyzed patients with histologically confirmed mCRC treated with first-line mFOLFOXIRI plus bevacizumab at Hanoi Medical University Hospital between January 2020 and June 2025. ETS was defined as a ≥20% reduction in target lesion diameters at the first radiological assessment (8 weeks), and DpR as the maximum percentage reduction from baseline. Logistic and linear regression were used to identify factors associated with ETS and DpR. PFS was analyzed according to ETS and DpR. Seventy-two patients were included. ETS was observed in 56.9%, with a median DpR of 40% and median time to maximal response of 4.9 months. Primary tumor resection showed a trend toward higher ETS rates in multivariable analysis, whereas no patient with a BRAF V600E mutation achieved ETS, although the number of BRAF-mutant tumors was limited. ETS was significantly associated with greater DpR. In multivariable analysis, ETS, completion of 12 treatment cycles, and ≥50% CEA reduction at week 8 were associated with greater DpR. RAS, BRAF, and PIK3CA mutations were not independently associated with DpR. Median PFS was 14.5 months, with significantly longer PFS in patients achieving ETS or higher DpR. In patients with metastatic colorectal cancer treated with first-line mFOLFOXIRI plus bevacizumab, ETS and early CEA reduction were associated with greater tumor shrinkage. Both ETS and DpR were also associated with longer progression-free survival, supporting their potential role as early markers of treatment response.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Iron is essential for cellular metabolism, oxygen transport, and redox homeostasis; however, disturbances in iron handling, rather than absolute iron excess alone, are increasingly recognized as contributors to tissue injury in chronic disease. Expansion of the labile iron pool promotes oxidative stress, mitochondrial dysfunction, inflammation, and ferroptosis, an iron-dependent form of regulated cell death characterized by lipid peroxidation, thereby linking iron dysregulation to multisystem pathology. This narrative review integrates experimental, clinical, and epidemiological evidence examining the role of iron dysregulation in colorectal cancer, metabolic dysfunction, cardiovascular, pulmonary, renal, hepatic, neurodegenerative, and reproductive disorders. Emphasis is placed on ferroptosis, whose biological effects vary according to tissue environment and disease type. In neoplastic conditions such as colorectal cancer, ferroptosis may represent a therapeutic vulnerability that can be exploited to induce tumor cell death. In contrast, in non-neoplastic chronic diseases, ferroptosis predominantly acts as a mediator of oxidative injury, inflammation, fibrosis, and progressive organ dysfunction. These observations support a systems-level model in which iron functions not as a uniformly toxic or protective factor, but as a selective amplifier of redox imbalance and tissue susceptibility. At the population level, current evidence highlights the complexity of defining safe iron exposure and the limitations of indiscriminate supplementation, particularly in iron-replete individuals. These findings support a shift from exposure-based interpretations of iron excess toward mechanism-based, tissue-specific, and risk-stratified approaches integrating biomarkers of iron metabolism, oxidative stress, and inflammation.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Microbiome data analysis demands customized workflows tailored to specific biological questions, sequencing modalities, and data properties. However, constructing and executing these workflows requires navigating heterogeneous software dependencies, reference databases, and multi-step parameter tuning. Here, we present MicroBioAgent, an autonomous, domain-specific agent framework that translates high-level biological queries into executable, study-specific pipelines across 16S rRNA amplicon, reference-based shotgun, and de novo assembly-based metagenomics. Rather than relying on static pipeline templates, MicroBioAgent employs a closed-loop execution architecture: it dynamically selects and runs bioinformatics tools within user-controlled environments while iteratively inspecting intermediate outputs to adapt downstream analytical decisions. Furthermore, to address the long-running nature of metagenomic computation, we introduce an asynchronous background task-management mechanism that reduces LLM token consumption by over 50% while enabling real-time plan adjustment and automated workflow resumption. We systematically evaluated MicroBioAgent across three benchmarks of increasing complexity: (1) paired amplicon and shotgun profiling of tomato rhizosphere microbiomes, (2) taxonomic and functional profiling coupled with machine-learning classification in a colorectal cancer cohort, and (3) de novo metagenomic assembly, metagenome-assembled genome (MAG) binning, and metabolic pathway reconstruction in a polyethylene degradation study. Across all benchmarks, MicroBioAgent faithfully recapitulated the primary biological findings of the original studies, exhibiting high analytical concordance despite expected tool- and database-dependent variations. In systematic robustness evaluations across 27 independent runs spanning three backbone large language models and three prompt-complexity tiers, MicroBioAgent achieved a 98.8% task completion rate and yielded highly reproducible diversity and differential-abundance estimates. MicroBioAgent establishes a scalable, adaptive paradigm for end-to-end computational microbiome research.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Introduction Most colorectal cancers (CRCs) are detected after symptomatic presentation in primary care. Because CRC shares symptoms with benign disorders, managing the risk of a missed diagnosis is challenging, and many patients are referred unnecessarily for urgent colonoscopy. As a result, colonoscopy resources cannot keep pace with increasing demand. Simple triage tools that can help prioritise patients for referral are urgently needed. Methods ColoSTAT measures the concentration of five protein biomarkers in a single multiplexed ELISA and was validated in a case control study enriched for cancer cases. Serum samples from two prospective cross-sectional studies and retrospective biobanked samples were combined into training (300) and validation (200) cohorts, matched for sex, age and clinical diagnosis. Overall, 56% of participants were male, and the median age at sampling was 64 years (range, 28 to 91 years). The validation cohort was supplemented with an additional 100 serum samples from patients with advanced adenoma (AA) (50.0% female; median age 63 years, range 44 to 84 years). Results Compared with colonoscopy, ColoSTAT detected CRC of all stages with a sensitivity of 89% and a specificity of 54% (90.3% and 54.3% in patients aged 45 to 84 years). Modelled at an intended-use CRC population prevalence of 4%, the negative predictive value (NPV) was >99% and the positive predictive value (PPV) was >7%. Sensitivity was 90.7% for early-stage and 89.4% for late stage cancers, and 58% for AA. Discussion ColoSTAT is a potential blood based alternative for the triage of patients with symptoms of CRC. By helping to prioritise symptomatic patients according to their CRC risk, it could improve triage to colonoscopy and support more effective patient management. Keywords: biomarkers, early detection of cancer, colonoscopy, colorectal cancer, triage

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Colorectal cancer (CRC) genomic studies have largely underrepresented African populations, limiting understanding of disease biology in these groups. This study addressed this gap by generating integrated genomic and transcriptomic data from South African (SA) CRC patients, establishing a foundation for future cancer studies. Bulk RNA sequencing of 32 samples identified several differentially expressed genes between tumour and normal samples, with AGAP3, AMPD2, ANKRD10, and SALL4 showing strong diagnostic performance (average sensitivity 99.9%, specificity 94.22%, PPV 99.9%, NPV 89.5%). SALL4 performed best and was validated using TCGA data and Kaplan-Meier survival analysis. Consensus Molecular Subtype classification revealed a distinct distribution, with enrichment of metabolic (CMS3, 30%) and mesenchymal (CMS4, 30%) subtypes and under-representation of canonical CMS2 (21%). APC mutation rates were lower than in European patients (~55% vs ~75%). Functional analysis identified inflammatory pathways as primary drivers of carcinogenesis, with viral influences exacerbating the inflammatory tumour microenvironment. Altered neural pathways in tumour samples suggested a consequential gut-brain axis loop as cancer infiltrates enervated tissue, an increasingly relevant field to which these data contribute. Whole-genome sequencing of 12 samples revealed pathogenic and likely pathogenic variants with transcriptomic differential expression; SMPD1, PERM1, PRRT2, and RP1 emerged as potential multi-omics markers, while novel mutations (KDM6A, C2CD2, TAF2, SLC6A16, OR5M10, PITRM1, TRIM64B, CARD11) were identified as previously unrecognised contributors to CRC progression in African samples. These findings expand genomic resources for African cancer research and provide new insights into the molecular landscape and tumourigenesis mechanisms of CRC in SA patients, supporting the development of population-specific precision oncology approaches.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
**Background:** Colorectal cancer (CRC) is a public health concern in sub-Saharan Africa, where the molecular landscape of the disease remains poorly characterised. In particular, genomic studies of resident Black African populations are limited, and the contribution of population-specific mutational processes and potential infectious exposures remains insufficiently understood. The Molecular, Somatic and Infectious Drivers of Colorectal Cancer in Africa (MOSAIC) collaboration aims to address these gaps by generating population-specific genomic data. This pilot study aimed to assess the feasibility of paired tumour-normal whole-genome sequencing (WGS) and to provide an initial characterisation of somatic mutations and mutational signatures in South African patients with CRC. **Methods:** We recruited five Black South African patients with newly diagnosed, treatment-naive CRC through the CoRecT Cancer study at Chris Hani Baragwanath Academic Hospital and Wits University Donald Gordon Medical Centre, Johannesburg. Fresh-frozen colorectal tumour tissue and matched peripheral blood samples were subjected to paired-end WGS (2 x 151 bp) using the Illumina NovaSeq X Plus platform. Somatic variants were identified using CaVEMan and Strelka2, followed by functional annotation using the Ensembl Variant Effect Predictor (VEP). Protein-altering variants were characterised using the R package maftools. Mutational signature contributions were estimated using SigProfilerAssignment and the COSMIC v3 reference catalogue. **Results:** All ten sequencing samples, comprising five tumour-blood pairs, passed quality control. Estimated sequencing depth ranged from 49.2X to 82.4X for tumour samples and from 22.7X to 40.7X for matched blood samples, with a median of 96.3% well-aligned reads. Following somatic variant calling and filtering, the number of retained mutations ranged from 1,106 to 65,379 per tumour. Three of the five tumours harboured at least one predicted protein-altering variant, comprising seven missense and four splice-site variants across eleven genes. Mutational signature analysis of single base substitutions (SBS) revealed inter-individual heterogeneity. SBS1 and SBS5 were detected across all five tumours, while additional signatures included SBS18, SBS20, SBS26 and SBS44, among others. Several tumours exhibited signatures associated with mismatch repair-related mutational processes. **Conclusions:** This pilot study demonstrates the feasibility of paired tumour-normal WGS and preliminary somatic mutation profiling in Black South African patients with CRC. The findings provide initial insights into the heterogeneous mutational landscape of CRC in this underrepresented population. However, the small sample size and incomplete clinical and molecular characterisation necessitate cautious interpretation. Larger studies incorporating comprehensive mismatch repair assessment, copy-number and structural variant analysis, germline susceptibility profiling and investigation of infectious exposures will be essential to validate these preliminary observations and better understand the molecular and environmental drivers of CRC in African populations.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Colorectal cancer (CRC) remains a leading cause of cancer deaths worldwide. GPA33, expressed on 95% of CRC, has been extensively targeted by IgG-attached payloads in conventional radioimmunotherapy (RIT), but toxicity was dose-limiting. A 2-step pretargeted radioimmunotherapy (PRIT) regimen using Self-Assembling-Disassembling antibody (SADA) specific for GPA33 (10 mg/kg) intravenous (IV) in step #1 and 24 h later [86Y]Y-ABD (9 nmole) IV in step #2, avoided normal gut uptake in non-human primates. Dosimetry results based on tissue counting in murine models using GPA33-SADA IV in step #1 and [225Ac]Ac-Pr in step #2, were 30.88, 0.1 and 2.56 Gy/uCi (Gy/37 kBq; RBE= 1), respectively for subcutaneous (sq) SW1222 tumor, blood and kidney, demonstrating favorable therapeutic ratios (309 for blood; 12 for kidney). Established sq SW1222 xenografts treated with 225Ac-SADA-PRIT showed dose dependent improvement in median survival (MS). Using one cycle of 2 doses 7 days apart (74kBq + 74kBq of 225Ac), majority of mice had complete tumor volumetric responses of sq SW1222, LS174T, LOVO and intraperitoneal SW1222 xenografts. Complete response was confirmed histologically at 180 days, accompanied by statistically significant improvements in MS. All treatments were well tolerated, with transient reversible weight loss (<15%), minimal hematologic, and no acute (within 30 days post 225Ac) chemical toxicities. At necropsy, kidneys showed minimal to marked subclinical tubular injury. The ability of a single cycle of 225Ac-SADA-PRIT to induce major CRC response and durable remission with minimal acute toxicities in multiple xenograft models while avoiding on-target off-tumor gut toxicity is encouraging, although subclinical histologic renal and ovarian damage remain a concern.

意义与启示：COMET框架从bulk长读长数据解析细胞类型特异性甲基化，揭示结肠肿瘤中成纤维细胞扩增及上皮细胞癌基因启动子高甲基化，为肠癌表观遗传研究提供新视角。

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
DNA methylation shapes cellular identity and changes with aging and disease, but most human methylomes come from bulk tissue, which mixes signal across many cell types. A methylation change at the bulk tissue level can reflect a change in cellular composition or an intrinsic shift within a cell type, and the two cannot be separated from bulk data. Single-cell and sorted-cell methods resolve cell types directly, but their cost and workflow complexity pose challenges to large studies. Long-read sequencing of single DNA molecules can directly detect DNA methylation on each read. We built COMET (Cell-of-Origin from METhylation), a framework that uses cell-type-specific methylation to assign individual long reads to cell types from standard bulk long-read sequencing. COMET detects changes in cell-type composition robustly even from shallow bulk long-read data, quantifies methylation level of repetitive DNA within each cell type, and, with deeper sequencing, resolves methylation differences between health and disease in individual cell types. We applied COMET to 140 human blood samples, 104 human brain samples and 59 human colon samples. In blood, we found epigenetic aging clock is primarily driven by shifts in cell-type composition, and that APOE4 carriers have myeloid-specific methylation changes. In brain, we found sex-biased change in cell-type composition with age, resolved methylation and hydroxymethylation separately within each cell type. In colon, we found a consistent expansion of fibroblasts in tumors relative to matched normal tissue, localized methylation loss at LINE-1 in fibroblast cells, and identified tumor- and cell-type-specific hypermethylation in epithelial cells at the promoters of known colorectal cancer genes. By resolving cell-type-specific methylation directly from bulk long-read data, this approach opens broad study of cell-type epigenetics across human tissues in aging and disease.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Cancer subtyping increasingly relies on both tumor mutational status and the spatial organization of the tumor microenvironment (TME). In colorectal cancer (CRC), mismatch repair deficient tumors (dMMR) are generally more immune infiltrated than mismatch repair proficient (pMMR) tumors, have better prognosis following resection, and respond to immune checkpoint inhibitors. Whether some pMMR tumors also harbor tumor-engaged T cells is unknown. Integrating spatial profiling with genomic analysis, we find that ~20% of pMMR tumors exhibit similar levels of T cell infiltration as dMMR tumors but without any specific somatic driver mutation or higher tumor mutational burden. These T cell-infiltrated pMMR (tipMMR) tumors contain abundant cytotoxic PD1+ Granzyme B+ CD8+ T cells in direct contact with tumor epithelium and immune clusters enriched for TCF1+ precursor exhausted T cells. tipMMR CRC tumors are similar in frequency as dMMR tumors and their immunologically active state suggests that immunotherapy should be considered in this population.

意义与启示：LUCID可同时进行细胞分型并校正邻域RNA污染，提升空间转录组数据质量，为肠癌及肝转移微环境解析提供更可靠工具。

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Cell profiles in segmented spatial transcriptomics are contaminated by RNA of neighbouring cells and by segmentation errors that merge two cells. LUCID is a multinomial mixture model that jointly assigns a type to each cell, tests whether its profile mixes two types and estimates the fraction of counts coming from its neighbours. An external reference is adapted to the platform, an identifiability rule protects a cell's own signal and the test is calibrated by parametric bootstrap. LUCID works with or without a reference, runs on CPUs and returns integer counts for all genes. On three public Visium HD datasets (mouse brain, human colorectal cancer, mouse liver) and in simulations built on them, LUCID removed contamination from other cell types as well as a two-step baseline, flagged fewer contaminated cells as mixed, emptied no cell and preserved minority lineages where one cell type dominates.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
BackgroundColorectal cancer is the third most common cancer in men and women, and the fifth most common cancer overall, in South Africa. A previous report by the South African National Cancer Registry (SANCR) established that colorectal cancer incidence is rising in all South African population groups but rising fastest in Black South Africans. However, whether incidence increases by age at onset, as observed in many upper-income countries worldwide, remains unknown. In the present study, we assessed changes in colorectal cancer incidence (2002-2023) and mortality (2002-2019) in South Africa by sex, population group and age at onset. MethodsWe calculated incidence from SANCR case counts and mortality from Stats SA death records, using Stats SA mid-year population estimates, standardised to the Segi world standard population. We defined age at onset as early (<50 years) or late ([≥]50 years). We described trends using joinpoint regression and annual percentage changes (APCs) over 2002-2023 and 2011- 2023, the period after private-laboratory reporting became mandatory. ResultsA total of 70,467 histologically confirmed primary colorectal cancers were registered with the SANCR over 2002-2023; 53.7% were in men. The overall age-standardised incidence rate (ASIR) was 6.61 per 100,000 (95% CI 6.32-6.89) in 2002 and 8.23 (7.99-8.46) in 2023. Overall incidence fell from 2002 to 2007 (not significant), rose from 2007 to 2015 and showed no significant change from 2015 to 2023. The first two segments coincide with the withdrawal of some private laboratories from reporting in 2005-2007 and with mandatory reporting from 2011. From 2011 to 2023, incidence fell in White South Africans (APC -1.0%, 95% CI -1.9 to -0.04), rose in Black African South Africans (+3.1%, 2.0 to 4.2) and did not change significantly in Coloured (-1.0%, -2.3 to 0.3) or Indian/Asian (+0.3%, -2.2 to 2.7) South Africans. Early-onset incidence rose by 1.6% per year (95% CI 1.1 to 2.1) over 2002-2023, similar to late-onset incidence (1.8%, 1.0 to 2.5). After 2011, neither changed significantly (early-onset +0.3%, -0.3 to 0.9; late-onset 0.0%, -1.0 to 1.0). Over 2002-2023, the early-onset APC was highest in White South Africans (+3.9%, 2.9 to 4.9), followed by Black African (+1.7%, 1.1 to 2.4), Coloured (+1.6%, 1.0 to 2.3) and Indian/Asian (+1.5%, 0.4 to 2.7) South Africans. The late-onset APC was +4.1% (3.4 to 4.9) in Black African, +1.3% (0.1 to 2.5) in White, +1.3% (0.1 to 2.5) in Indian/Asian and +0.7% (-0.3 to 1.6) in Coloured South Africans. After 2011, early-onset incidence rose in White (+1.2%, 0.3 to 2.2), Coloured (+1.7%, 0.4 to 3.1) and Black African (+1.1%, 0.4 to 1.8) South Africans. Late-onset incidence fell in White South Africans (-1.5%, -2.6 to -0.4) and rose in Black African South Africans (+3.7%, 2.4 to 5.0). Early-onset mortality rose by 1.2% per year (0.5 to 2.0) over 2002-2019, and late-onset mortality by 0.9% (0.3 to 1.4). ConclusionEarly-onset colorectal cancer incidence in South Africa rose over 2002-2023, and much of the rise coincided with mandatory private-laboratory reporting from 2011. Since 2011, early-onset incidence has risen modestly in White, Coloured and Black African South Africans, while late-onset incidence has fallen in White South Africans. In Black African South Africans, late-onset incidence and mortality continue to rise faster than early-onset.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Colibactin is a mutagen produced by bacterial strains in the colorectal microbiomes of some healthy people. It generates somatic mutations characterised by the mutational signatures SBS88 and ID18 in normal human colorectal epithelial cells in vivo. Increasing prevalence of colibactin mutagenesis during the 20th century is hypothesised to have caused recent international increases in early-onset colorectal cancer incidence. Here, we establish the early-life prevalence, timing, mutation burdens and distribution through the colon of colibactin mutagenesis by sequencing normal colorectal epithelial cell genomes to detect SBS88 and ID18 in 90 healthy and inflammatory bowel disease affected children and adolescents. Colibactin-induced mutagenesis was present in ~43%, with or without inflammatory bowel disease. It usually begins shortly after birth and ceases by age five years. Mutation burdens are higher in the left than right colon and show substantial variation, with some children displaying mutation burdens comparable to those of healthy non-exposed individuals greater than 60 years of age. The future public health implications of this common early life mutagen exposure will depend on clarification of its role in colorectal cancer causation.

意义与启示：发现LisH衍生肽通过隔离Taf5实现转录抑制，并抑制结直肠癌细胞生长，为靶向转录共激活因子的抗癌策略提供新思路。

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Squelching is an indirect inhibition of transcription that results from redistribution of cofactors away from DNA. Here, we describe a class of Lis homology (LisH)-derived peptides that act as transcriptional squelchers. LisH domains are a highly conserved motif found in 10s of thousands of proteins and are composed of ~30 amino acids in a helix-turn-helix fold. By examining a phylogenetically diverse subset of LisH domains in a synthetic Saccharomyces cerevisiae assay, we identified a small number of hydrophobic residues within the first helix that are required for effective inhibition of reporter expression. In addition, squelching required binding to the general transcriptional cofactor Taf5, a subunit of the TFIID complex. Transcriptome-level impacts were largely correlated in yeast expressing two distinct LisH sequences, consistent with a model that LisH-based squelching results from a shared mechanism of sequestering Taf5. Consistent with that inference, overexpression of Taf5 partially reversed the squelching effect. Given the interest in squelching as a potential area for anti-cancer therapies, we also tested whether our shortest squelching sequence called YC5C-H1 had any effect on the human colorectal cancer cell line HCT-15. In addition to preferentially squelching high expression genes, YC5C-H1 sharply slowed growth of HCT-15 cells.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Stress granule (SG) gene-set scores summarize transcription associated with stress-response machinery, but their stability across scoring definitions is uncertain. We compared fibroblast-epithelial expression contrasts for four fixed SG lists in two colorectal cancer single-cell cohorts containing 195,527 cells from 85 donors. Analyses used donor pairing, gene-wise standardized expression, within-cell ranks and raw-count pseudobulk summaries, with tissue and sequencing-depth sensitivities. At least 20 tumor cells per compartment were available for 15 and 29 paired donors. Pseudobulk SG-A contrasts were negative in both cohorts: median differences in mean log2 counts per million were -0.383 (95% confidence interval -0.493 to -0.319) and -0.493 (-0.614 to -0.384). Rank-based SG-B contrasts were also negative in both cohorts. In a post hoc comparison using identical depth-retained cells and weights, the second cohort had positive gene-Z estimates and negative rank-based estimates; the positive estimates did not meet the eight-test false-discovery threshold. Spatial comparisons depended on the fibroblast reference subtype, and the CosMx panel measured only 11 of 27 SG-B genes. RNA-protein correlations varied across genes, while organoid depletion calls were more frequent for selected translation-associated members than for the four core members. These findings establish reproducible relative-expression contrasts under specified definitions and show that their direction can change across scoring and depth conditions. Reporting the scoring definition, retained donor population, depth sensitivity and gene coverage together identifies the contrasts that reproduce and provides a defined basis for testing their relationship to SG formation.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Guanylin (GUCA2A) and uroguanylin (GUCA2B) are paracrine hormone ligands of the tumor-suppressor receptor guanylyl cyclase C (GUCY2C). In early colorectal tumorigenesis, expression of GUCA2A and GUCA2B is silenced through transcriptional repression by APC-regulated {beta}-catenin/TCF signaling, a pathway activated early in malignant transformation. This repression depends on a locus control region (LCR) 1,000-3,683 bp upstream of GUCA2A. Here, we used dCas9-APEX2 biotinylation at genomic elements by restricted spatial tagging (C-BERST) in colorectal cancer (CRC) cell lines with inducible suppression of {beta}-catenin/TCF signaling to identify {beta}-catenin/TCF-regulated proteins associated with the GUCA2A regulatory region that mediate repression of GUCY2C ligand transcription. Guide RNAs were used to direct dCas9-APEX2 for locus-specific proximity biotinylation of proteins. Quantitative mass spectrometry identified p38 (MAPK14) as a candidate regulator enriched near the GUCA2A promoter following {beta}-catenin/TCF suppression. Loss-of-function and rescue experiments established that p38 supports GUCA2A and GUCA2B induction following {beta}-catenin/TCF suppression. Importantly, GATA2 was identified as a p38-dependent activator of GUCA2A and GUCA2B transcription that remained enriched near the GUCA2A promoter independent of {beta}-catenin/TCF signaling. Indeed, GATA2 S192 phosphorylation was reduced by p38 loss and by active {beta}-catenin/TCF signaling. Thus, a p38/GATA2 axis links oncogenic {beta}-catenin/TCF signaling to repression of GUCY2C hormone expression in CRC.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Gene regulation is commonly modeled at the gene level, yet genes express multiple isoforms from distinct transcription start sites whose regulatory architecture is not resolved by current approaches. Here we introduce FULL-seq, a scalable single-cell multiomic platform that jointly profiles chromatin accessibility and full-length transcript coverage from the same cell, enabling direct coupling of regulatory elements to alternative first exon (AFE) usage. FULL-seq achieves high sensitivity for both transcriptome and chromatin accessibility while providing transcript-wide coverage across mRNAs up to 15 kb with precise exon-level mapping. We uncover diverse promoter-AFE regulatory architectures, revealing distinct transcription factor programs across alternative first exons of the same gene, and show that gene-level annotation frameworks can obscure regulatory relationships in multi-promoter genes. Applying FULL-seq to human cancer cells further reveals metastasis-associated AFE programs that are not apparent from gene-level expression. These AFE programs were reproduced in independent colorectal cancer cell-line datasets, and CALB1 AFE activation was observed in a subset of liver metastases from an independent patient cohort. Furthermore, CRISPRi-mediated repression of metastasis-associated CALB1 AFEs reduced colorectal cancer cell migration. Together, our findings establish alternative promoter and first-exon usage as a functionally relevant layer of gene regulation and demonstrate that FULL-seq enables regulatory relationships and cellular phenotypes to be connected at the promoter-isoform level.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Interactions among cells and their local microenvironments shape tissue organization and function, while their dysregulation can contribute to disease. In Alzheimer's disease (AD), the complex responses of glial cells and neurons to amyloid-{beta} pathology can both mitigate and exacerbate neuronal injury. Spatial transcriptomics enables investigation of these relationships in situ, but recovering interpretable transcriptional programs and their interactions from spatial transcriptomics remains challenging, in part because conventional nonlinear models are non-identifiable. Here we present CIRCA (Causal Interaction Representation for Cellular Architectures), a self-supervised causal representation learning framework that jointly learns identifiable cell- and neighborhood-level transcriptional programs and the directed interactions among them under explicit assumptions. It can also be extended to incorporate additional modalities such as pathology. Benchmarked against five existing methods across seven cell-resolution datasets, CIRCA achieved the highest biological accuracy in six and the highest overall score in all five multi-section datasets, while recovering higher-order anatomical organization. In an AD mouse model, incorporating amyloid-{beta} pathology revealed four region-specific plaque niches enriched for microglia. Plaque-associated microglia shared a core disease-associated response whose strength varied by region, and AD genetic risk was preferentially enriched in hippocampal and cortical plaque-associated microglia. Reproducible latent factors linked to cell-level amyloid burden separated phagocytic from inflammatory microglial programs. Applied to a human colorectal cancer dataset, CIRCA resolved patient-specific tumor niches, conserved stromal remodeling niches, and distinct macrophage states, highlighting its versatility. Together, these results establish CIRCA as a methodological advance over existing approaches, enabling deeper insights into tissue organization and the molecular dependencies linking cells to their local environments.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
The DNA damage response governs genomic integrity, and abnormal DNA repair can drive tumorigenesis. We previously identified a Rac1-Abi-1 signaling pathway in which Rac1 activates protein phosphatase 5, leading to Abi-1-S323 dephosphorylation and enhanced non-homologous end joining (NHEJ). Given the error-prone nature of NHEJ and its potential to promote genomic instability, we sought to determine whether Rac1-Abi-1-mediated regulation of NHEJ contributes to tumorigenesis. Here, we demonstrate the tumorigenic role of Abi-1-S323 dephosphorylation in nonmalignant cell models and multiple tumorigenesis models established using a newly generated genetically engineered Abi-1 mouse model. We first found that the dephospho-mimetic Abi-1-S323A mutant promoted transformation-associated phenotypes in nonmalignant human cells and enhanced orthotopic glioblastoma growth under unperturbed conditions. To further investigate its tumorigenic potential in vivo, we generated CRISPR/Cas9-mediated Abi-1-S296A knock-in mice, in which S296 corresponds to human S323. Abi-1-S296A mouse embryonic fibroblasts exhibited increased proliferation, while mutant mice developed spontaneous tumors involving lymphoid tissues and organs under unperturbed conditions. Furthermore, Abi-1-S296A increased susceptibility to tumorigenesis following DNA damage. In a low-dose whole-body irradiation model, Abi-1-S296A mice showed a trend toward shortened survival and increased tumor development, with lesions including Harderian gland papillary cystadenomas, round-cell neoplasms, and anaplastic sarcomas. In addition, in an azoxymethane/dextran sulfate sodium (AOM/DSS)-induced colorectal tumor model, Abi-1-S296A mice developed significantly more tumors and had a greater tumor burden. These findings identify Abi-1-S323 dephosphorylation as a previously unrecognized regulator of tumorigenesis and establish a new mouse model for investigating the physiological and pathological consequences of constitutive activation of upstream NHEJ-regulatory signaling.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Microbiome modulation can augment responses to immunotherapy in advanced cancer. Early studies of anti-PD-1 therapies in combination with fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT) reported efficacy in immunotherapy-naive and -refractory settings. However, FMTs are variable in composition, difficult to scale, and risk the transfer of emerging pathogens. VE800 is a consortium of 11 strains of commensal bacteria derived from healthy donors and grown from clonal cell banks. VE800 increased anti-PD-1 efficacy in preclinical models of cancer. CONSORTiUM-IO was a first-in-human, open-label phase 1 study that evaluated safety and efficacy of VE800 with nivolumab in advanced PD-1-refractory melanoma, PD-1-naive gastric/gastroesophageal junction (G/GEJ) adenocarcinoma and PD-1-naive microsatellite-stable colorectal cancer (MSS CRC). VE800 plus nivolumab was well tolerated but offered no improvement over historic response rates. Exploratory analyses in patients with melanoma revealed that VE800 strain engraftment was associated with greater progression-free survival (PFS) and increased immune activation peripherally. STATEMENT OF SIGNIFICANCEThe first-in-human study of the safety and efficacy of a defined bacterial consortium in combination with anti-PD-1 treatment in various solid tumors demonstrated the safety of the combination, albeit with low clinical efficacy. The results provide important knowledge and considerations about microbiome modulation in cancer, to help design future trials.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Faecalibacterium prausnitzii is a prominent member of the human gut microbiota whose depletion is associated with various intestinal and metabolic disorders. While multiple mechanisms have been proposed to explain how F. prausnitzii promotes host health, the molecular determinants underlying these activities remain elusive. Here, we show that F. prausnitzii is a prolific producer of the human metabolite N-butyrylglycine, which we find accumulates to millimolar concentrations in bacterial culture and is readily detectable in the feces of conventional wildtype mice. We establish an enzymatic basis of N-butyrylglycine production by identifying and biochemically validating an F. prausnitzii N-acyltransferase that catalyzes the conjugation of butyryl-CoA and glycine. Despite being derived from butyrate, N-butyrylglycine exhibits distinct bioactivity from its precursor, including reduced histone deacetylase inhibitory activity, an altered inflammatory profile, and enhanced suppression of cellular proliferation across multiple cancer cell lines. Furthermore, transcriptomic profiling revealed N butyrylglycine coordinates repression of G2/M checkpoint-associated programs and downregulation of the colorectal cancer associated gene AOC1. Together, these findings suggest that specialized metabolites produced by F. prausnitzii contribute to its beneficial effects and may underlie its protective role in colorectal cancer.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Chimeric antigen receptor (CAR)-T-cell therapy remains limited in solid tumors by the scarcity of suitable target antigens and an immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment. Here, we developed a tumor-responsive recombinant adeno-associated virus (rAAV) strategy that harnesses aberrant NF-{kappa}B activity to establish a shared synthetic CAR target across tumor types. Using an NF-{kappa}B-responsive decoy minimal promoter (DMP), rAAV-SA drove tumor-preferential surface expression of a synthetic antigen (SA), enabling antigen-dependent CAR-T-cell activation, degranulation, and cytotoxicity. Systemic rAAV-SA delivery combined with CAR-T cells produced antitumor activity in triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) and colorectal cancer xenograft models. We subsequently engineered rAAV-ARMS (antigen redirection and multifunctional secreted effectors), integrating SA expression with tumor-local production of an IL-15/IL-15R sushi-domain fusion, CXCL10, and IFN-{gamma}. Compared with antigen redirection alone, rAAV-ARMS enhanced CAR-T-cell-mediated killing in three-dimensional tumor spheroids and, in a TNBC xenograft model, increased intratumoral T-cell accumulation and improved the efficacy of intravenously administered CAR-T cells, without overt systemic toxicity under the conditions examined. These findings establish a tumor-programmed platform for target-redirected universal CAR-T-cell therapy in solid tumors.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Accurate discrimination between tumour and non-tumour cells is essential for interpreting spatial transcriptomics data and identifying spatially resolved therapeutic targets. Existing tumour-cell annotation approaches were primarily developed for single-cell RNA sequencing and do not explicitly incorporate the spatial organization of cells. Here, we introduce SpaceMACE, an extension of the MACE tumour-cell annotation framework for sequencing-based and imaging-based spatial transcriptomics. SpaceMACE first combines reference-based cell-type classification with copy-number-variation-based tumour classification. The resulting consensus annotations are subsequently refined using spatial proximity and gene-expression similarity. We evaluated SpaceMACE across multiple spatial transcriptomics platforms, including Stereo-seq, Visium HD, CosMx and Xenium, and across colorectal, hepatocellular and ovarian cancer datasets. SpaceMACE retained the high precision of the original MACE framework while improving the spatial coherence of tumour-cell annotations. Together, these results demonstrate that SpaceMACE provides a scalable and platform-independent framework for tumour-cell annotation in spatial transcriptomics and supports the spatial investigation of tumour-specific molecular targets.

bioRxiv (预印本) · 2026-11-17 · Lu, X.; Tlais, H.; Rehman, H.; Olson, C. P.; Hartz, A. L.; O'Tain, N. R.; Martens, A. N.; Ju, T.; Figueiredo, V. C.; Markworth, J. F.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Colorectal cancer (CRC) cachexia induces skeletal muscle dysfunction, impeding quality of life and worsening cancer prognosis. Multiple preclinical models, including the widely used mouse model of subcutaneous inoculation with the C26 colorectal carcinoma cell line, have been developed to study the biological mechanisms of CRC cachexia and elucidate potential new treatments. It has been proposed that a distinct cell line of the same origin, namely CT26, is relatively non-cachectic. However, studies evaluating the relative potential of C26 and CT26 cells to induce cancer cachexia in parallel have been limited. The differences in the biological mechanisms by which C26 and CT26 impact skeletal muscle mass and function have also not been fully elucidated. In the current study, we investigated the differential capacity of C26 and CT26 to induce cancer cachexia using both an in vitro cancer-muscle cell co-culture and an in vivo syngeneic mouse model. Our results show that both C26 and CT26 cells induced significant atrophy of murine C2C12 skeletal myotubes. In the mouse model, while C26 and CT26 both reduced skeletal muscle mass and fat mass, only C26 tumors led to loss of body weight and impaired skeletal muscle force output. We further show that C26 tumors express a higher level of interleukin-6 and C26 tumor-bearing mice exhibit greater muscle inflammation than CT26 tumor-bearing mice. In addition, mice bearing C26 and CT26 tumors showed differential regulation of the innate immune responses and muscle protein turnover. Overall, our data suggests that although both C26 and CT26 cells do exhibit cachectic effects, C26 cells induce greater loss in body weight, fat mass, skeletal muscle mass, and physical function via promoting chronic inflammation and deregulating protein balance of skeletal muscle.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Single-cell transcriptome sequencing has been widely applied across the life sciences. It enables accurate and robust identification of cell types in heterogeneous biological tissues through unsupervised clustering, shallow learning, and deep learning. While deep learning does not outperform shallow learning in classification performance, it streamlines cell type identification by eliminating cumbersome preprocessing procedures. However, the availability of training datasets with comprehensive cell type annotations is always limited, so new datasets inevitably contain cell populations that are not pre-defined in the training data. To address this limitation, we integrated unsupervised clustering with transformer-based models to identify cell populations unrecognized by classical methods. Specifically, we developed the Nankai GeneRank Classifier by fine-tuning the pre-trained Geneformer-V1 model, and then clustered cells based on its softmax-normalized class probability matrix (SCPM). Applied to a public colorectal cancer dataset, the new method, named SCPM-based clustering, resolved cell populations that cannot be unambiguously identified by classical methods alone and led to the discovery of novel candidate markers of colorectal cancer stem cells, demonstrating its utility.

Sisyphus at the splenic flexure: sidedness in colorectal cancer
bioRxiv (预印本) · 2026-11-16 · Ke, L.; Cecchini, M.; Cannataro, V. L.; Townsend, J. P.
意义与启示：该研究通过分解突变供给与癌症效应，揭示左右侧二分法对多数驱动基因足够，但APC和PIK3CA存在异质性，提示需精细记录肿瘤部位以优化分析。
展开英文原题摘要与原文链接
ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Colorectal cancer is divided into left and right to guide prognosis and therapy, yet a precise definition of left vs right sided colorectal cancer is still not fully agreed upon. The published conventions place it anywhere between the cecum and the rectosigmoid junction. The dichotomy assumes side homogeneity, i.e., that colorectal subsites within a side add limited information once the side is known. That assumption has been examined primarily through mutation prevalence, a quantity that confounds how often a driver arises with how strongly it is selected once it has. Analyzing 1,027 whole-exome and whole-genome sequenced colorectal tumors, we decomposed the prevalence of six driver groups into mutation supply and cancer effect, and asked whether a binary side label captures how each of their prevalence, mutation supply, and cancer effect vary along the colorectum. Mostly it does: the mutational input behaves as two blocks, and even the more than thirty-fold strengthening of cancer effect on BRAF V600E from sigmoid colon to cecum is adequately captured by side. But APC shows nominal evidence against side homogeneity in both prevalence and cancer effect while showing little net left-right difference, and PIK3CA H1047 rejects it in supply. The evidence for finer resolution is real but partial, and the failures do not announce themselves. We recommend additional research recording primary tumor location at the finest practicable resolution--at minimum, International Classification of Diseases for Oncology, 3rd Edition (ICD-O-3) topography. Such well-annotated datasets would enable the left-right boundary to be a reversible analytic choice rather than an irreversible annotation.

沙特阿拉伯结直肠癌筛查国家指南（2026更新版）
National guidelines for colorectal cancer screening in Saudi Arabia: Recommendations from the multi-society guideline development task force.
Saudi Journal of Gastroenterology : Official Journal of the Saudi Gastroenterology Association · 2026-11 · Almadi MA, Alkhiari R, Alotaibi A, Alsohaibani F, Bazarbashi A, Alghamdi A, et al.
要点与启示：该指南基于GRADE系统制定，推荐45-75岁人群每两年FIT筛查，为中东地区CRC筛查提供本土化范本，对我国筛查策略优化亦有参考价值。
展开英文原题摘要与原文链接
ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
These updated national guidelines were developed jointly by the Saudi Gastroenterology Association, Saudi Society of Colon and Rectal Surgery, Saudi Society of Gastrointestinal Oncology, and Saudi Society of Family and Community Medicine, and provide evidence-based recommendations for colorectal cancer (CRC) screening in Saudi Arabia, superseding the 2015 national guidelines. This update incorporates new epidemiological data from Saudi Arabia, including updated incidence estimates, polyp prevalence studies, colonoscopy quality audit data, and national screening uptake surveys, to provide a comprehensively evidence-anchored and locally contextualized framework. A national multidisciplinary group formulated 25 key Population, Intervention, Comparison, Outcome (PICO) questions across seven domains. Systematic literature searches were performed from inception to March 2026. Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation (GRADE) evidence profiles were prepared for critical outcomes, and recommendations were developed through an iterative consensus process requiring ≥80% agreement for strong recommendations. The Task Force strongly recommends implementing an organized national CRC screening program for all asymptomatic average-risk adults aged 45 to 75 years. Biennial fecal immunochemical testing (FIT) is recommended as the primary population-based screening modality. Colonoscopy every 10 years is a recommended alternative. All positive FIT results must be followed by timely, high-quality colonoscopy. Specific recommendations are provided for high-risk groups. High-certainty evidence from multiple randomized trials and large-scale implementation studies demonstrates that organized CRC screening substantially reduces CRC-specific mortality and incidence. A phased, FIT-based national implementation strategy is recommended, tailored to Saudi epidemiology, population preferences, and healthcare infrastructure, with iterative quality improvement as new evidence emerges.

基于理论域框架的伊朗结直肠手术抗生素预防不依从行为机制研究
Beyond guideline deviation: understanding surgical antibiotic prophylaxis nonadherence in Iranian surgical practice using the theoretical domains framework.
Antimicrobial Resistance and Infection Control · 2026-08 · Salami H, Salehi M, Tafti SMA, Khalili H
要点与启示：揭示抗生素预防不依从主要源于术后延长用药而非适应证选择，提示肠癌围手术期抗菌管理需聚焦停药流程与文化变革。
展开英文原题摘要与原文链接
ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Surgical antibiotic prophylaxis (SAP) is essential for preventing surgical site infections, yet inappropriate perioperative antibiotic use remains a persistent stewardship challenge. Although SAP non-adherence is well documented, the behavioral and organizational mechanisms sustaining it remain poorly understood in Iranian surgical settings. This study assessed SAP adherence and explored factors shaping perioperative antibiotic prescribing and implementation. This explanatory mixed-methods study included a three-month retrospective assessment of SAP adherence followed by qualitative interviews. Adult patients undergoing elective colorectal and urologic surgeries in a tertiary university-affiliated hospital were included. SAP adherence was assessed using routinely collected hospital data based on indication, antibiotic selection, dose appropriateness, and duration. Antibiotic exposure was measured using length of therapy (LOT), days of therapy (DOT), and defined daily dose (DDD). Semi-structured interviews were then conducted with healthcare professionals to explore factors underlying the observed patterns of SAP non-adherence. Interview data were analyzed using directed content analysis guided by the Theoretical Domains Framework (TDF). Among 109 patients, only 10 (9.2%) met all SAP adherence criteria. Although indication was appropriate in all patients and dosing was appropriate in 105 patients (96.3%), non-adherence was mainly driven by inappropriate antibiotic selection and prolonged postoperative continuation. Antibiotics were continued beyond 24 h in 93 patients (85.3%), beyond 48 h in 82 (75.2%), and prescribed at discharge in 66 (60.6%). Antibiotic exposure was substantial, with median LOT, DOT, and total DDD of 4.0, 6.0, and 6.3, respectively. Fifteen interviews were conducted to explain these adherence patterns, identifying perceived infection risk, broad-spectrum prescribing norms, unclear responsibilities, workflow disruptions, professional responsibility concerns, patient expectations, and lack of structured antibiotic review as key drivers of persistent non-adherence. SAP non-adherence was common and extended beyond the decision to prescribe prophylaxis. Improving SAP practice requires stewardship interventions that address prescribing culture, perioperative workflow, and structured postoperative antibiotic discontinuation.

本周热点与趋势总结

由本期文献提炼的课题组可执行信号
  1. 【肝转移机制：坏死周边微环境与NETs成为可干预靶点】Cancer Discovery 报道肿瘤坏死与结直肠癌转移独立于肿瘤大小相关，原发灶与肝转移灶的单细胞与空间转录组显示坏死周边程序富集于转移进展，患者循环中NET预激活及CD177低表达中性粒细胞增多且外渗能力下降；该研究提示靶向中性粒细胞胞外诱捕器（NETs）可抑制肿瘤坏死与转移，将“坏死”从被动结局提升为肝转移干预靶点。
  2. 【肝转移代谢机制：乳酸化修饰驱动转移】Advanced Science 通过对肝转移灶与配对原发灶的乳酸化组+蛋白组整合分析，鉴定 GLUD1 K503 乳酸化为关键事件，AARS1 介导的该修饰通过转录后重编程驱动结直肠癌转移；这为 Warburg 效应—乳酸蓄积—非组蛋白乳酸化轴提供了直接的人体标本证据，提示 AARS1/GLUD1 轴可作为抗转移候选靶点。
  3. 【辅助治疗策略外延：阿司匹林与结构化运动降低复发】European Journal of Cancer 综述指出，两项 III 期随机试验支持在细胞毒化疗之外扩展辅助策略：ALASCCA 中低剂量阿司匹林用 3 年使携带 PI3K 通路变异的切除后结肠/直肠癌复发风险降低约 50%；结合运动干预的随机证据，提示基于分子分型与生活方式干预的辅助治疗组合有望成为 II–III 期 CRC 的新标准组成。
  4. 【局部治疗与免疫微环境：HFRT 通过 APOC2 重塑髓系免疫】Advanced Science 研究显示，大分割放疗（HFRT）诱导肿瘤来源 APOC2，驱动炎性单核细胞分化并增强抗肿瘤免疫，治疗后血清 APOC2 升高与 MSS 局部晚期直肠癌接受 HFRT 为基础的新辅助免疫化疗的 pCR 相关；该结果为 MSS 直肠癌“放疗+免疫”联合提供了可检测的疗效预测标志物与机制依据。
  5. 【免疫逃逸与联合靶向：FOLR1 ADC 与 VEGF/PD-(L)1 双靶策略】Science Translational Medicine 通过 FACS 为基础的全基因组 CRISPR 激活筛选，将 FOLR1 鉴定为 MHC-I 抗原提呈缺失所致免疫逃逸的关键负调控因子，抗 FOLR1 ADC 可增强抗 PD-1 疗效，且 FOLR1 高表达预示 ICB 应答差；Cancer Treatment Reviews 同期系统梳理 GI 肿瘤中 VEGF 驱动免疫排斥微环境的生物学与临床证据，支持抗血管生成与 PD-(L)1 协同作为克服 ICB 耐药的前沿方向。
  6. 【治疗相关毒性机制：肿瘤来源 KRT16 促心房颤动】Advanced Science 回顾性分析发现，未经抗肿瘤治疗的女性乳腺癌、肺癌与结直肠癌患者房颤患病率已显著升高，原位荷瘤小鼠模型显示房颤诱发率增加并伴心房重构，机制涉及肿瘤来源 KRT16 经内皮—间质转化诱导心房重塑；提示 CRC 患者房颤风险部分独立于抗癌治疗，需在围治疗期加强心律监测与机制导向的心血管保护研究。
